title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
嘉靖己酉天下士屬當大比
仰惟
皇上致理作人于兹三紀而登進
者凡十科矣猗與盛哉福建
試事屆期巡按御史陳宗夔
始被
===
命司監臨祗奉
德意兼程而南旣至則益嚴前御
史楊九澤所聘文學與諸遴
簡執事者以學正寇韋敎諭
趙文翰主試以敎諭黎天啟
蔣仲哲學正龍旆敎諭馮璠
方輅費增胡然分試提調則
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

嘉靖己酉，天下士屬當大比。仰惟皇上致理作人，于兹三紀，而登進者凡十科矣。猗與盛哉！福建試事屆期，巡按御史陳宗夔始被命司監臨，祗奉德意，兼程而南。旣至，則益嚴前御史楊九澤所聘文學與諸遴簡執事者，以學正寇韋、敎諭趙文翰主試，以敎諭黎天啟、蔣仲哲、學正龍旆、敎諭馮璠、方輅、費增、胡然分試。提調則
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549], scholars throughout the realm were due to take the triennial examination. Reverently reflecting upon His Majesty’s achievement of good government and cultivation of talent, we have now reached three twelve-year cycles, during which candidates have been advanced through ten examinations. Ah, how flourishing!

When the time came for the Fujian examination, Regional Inspector Chen Zongkui received orders to serve as Supervising Official. Reverently carrying out the imperial benevolent intent, he traveled south at an accelerated pace. Upon arriving, he imposed still stricter requirements upon the scholars engaged by the preceding Regional Inspector, Yang Jiuze, and the various personnel selected to administer the examination. Instructors Kou Wei and Zhao Wenhan served as Examiners; Instructors Li Tianqi, Jiang Zhongzhe, Long Pei, Feng Fan, Fang Lu, Fei Zeng, and Hu Ran served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
左布政使屠大山右布政使
張鏊監試則按察副使柯喬
僉事鄭炯旣鑰院御史矢言
曰惟兹求賢鉅典仰廑
淵衷形之
詔令屢矣肆吾二三譾劣執事者
其何以對揚之其惟勤惟愼
===
惟公無私惟進端純而黜浮
靡衆唯唯籲於
天神乃合士之選於提學副使周
琉者三千有奇三試之拔其
尤得九十人乃鍥其名氏弁
文之優者二十一篇爲錄以
獻韋首序之曰昔閩東南荒服
punctuated:
左布政使屠大山、右布政使張鏊，監試則按察副使柯喬、僉事鄭炯。旣鑰院，御史矢言曰：「惟兹求賢鉅典，仰廑淵衷，形之詔令屢矣。肆吾二三譾劣執事者，其何以對揚之？其惟勤惟愼，惟公無私，惟進端純而黜浮靡。」衆唯唯，籲於天神。乃合士之選於提學副使周琉者三千有奇，三試之，拔其尤，得九十人。乃鍥其名氏，弁文之優者二十一篇，爲錄以獻。
韋首序之曰：「昔閩東南荒服
translation_en:
…the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, Tu Dashan, and the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, Zhang Ao. Examination oversight was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ke Qiao and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zheng Jiong. Once the examination compound had been locked, the censor solemnly declared: “This great undertaking of seeking worthy men has engaged His Majesty’s profound concern, repeatedly expressed in imperial edicts. How, then, can we few shallow and unworthy men charged with this duty requite and uphold his intentions? Only by diligence and caution, by impartiality without private bias, and by advancing the upright and pure while rejecting the superficial and extravagant.” All voiced their assent and invoked Heaven’s spirits. Thereupon, more than three thousand candidates selected by Zhou Liu, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, were assembled. They were examined in three sessions, and the most outstanding were chosen, yielding ninety men. Their names were then engraved for printing, with twenty-one of the finest essays placed at the beginning, to make a record for presentation to the throne.
Wei wrote the opening preface, saying: “In former times, Min was a remote southeastern region…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也在宋稱人文其俗為鄒魯
其出者多名碩有行業聞望
皆儒先倡明理學之餘也然
理學在天地猶元氣也其盛
衰一繫乎時諸儒先雖倡明
之然未甞嚮用尤未能彰顯
如我
===
國家如
今日也蓋帝王心傳之失也久矣
自我
聖祖崇儒肇學
文皇帝建極乃裒經傳而頒示之
於是理學明備暨我
皇上統壹聖真又以帝王躬行之
punctuated: 也。在宋稱人文，其俗為鄒魯，其出者多名碩，有行業聞望，皆儒先倡明理學之餘也。然理學在天地，猶元氣也，其盛衰一繫乎時。諸儒先雖倡明之，然未甞嚮用，尤未能彰顯如我國家、如今日也。蓋帝王心傳之失也久矣。自我聖祖崇儒肇學，文皇帝建極，乃裒經傳而頒示之，於是理學明備。暨我皇上統壹聖真，又以帝王躬行之
translation_en: …was such a region. In the Song, Fujian became renowned for its cultural attainments, and its customs were likened to those of Zou and Lu. Many who emerged from it were eminent scholars, distinguished by their conduct, accomplishments, and reputation. All this was the enduring legacy of earlier Confucian masters who championed and elucidated the Learning of Principle. Yet the Learning of Principle is to Heaven and Earth as primordial vital energy: its flourishing and decline depend entirely upon the times. Although those earlier masters championed and elucidated it, it had never been accorded acceptance and put into practice, still less made manifest as under our dynasty and in our own day. For the transmission of the heart-mind among the sage emperors and kings had long been lost. Our sagely founding ancestor honored Confucian learning and established schools; Emperor Wen established the supreme standard, then gathered the classics and commentaries and promulgated them. Thus the Learning of Principle became fully elucidated and complete. Now our emperor has unified the authentic teachings of the sages and has further taken what emperors and kings personally put into practice…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
理揭之
訓詞
振德之功垂于萬世豈惟一鄉
已哉然則士之盛於閩與主
司之望士皆於是乎在蓋甞
論之儒之功用大矣而有所
遇以行所學則儒先大願之
===
而不能獲也然必屬諸後人
後之人居其鄉蒙其教澤而
生
聖人之世乃寓於文也舉千百年
之大願而欲售之感慨乎殊
昔奮庸於
清朝其可以厚望也明矣顧主
punctuated: 理揭之訓詞，振德之功垂于萬世，豈惟一鄉已哉？然則士之盛於閩，與主司之望士，皆於是乎在。蓋甞論之：儒之功用大矣，而有所遇以行所學，則儒先大願之而不能獲也，然必屬諸後人。後之人居其鄉，蒙其教澤，而生聖人之世，乃寓於文也，舉千百年之大願而欲售之。感慨乎殊昔，奮庸於清朝，其可以厚望也明矣。顧主
translation_en: … principles, proclaiming them in admonitory pronouncements. The achievement of promoting virtue will endure for ten thousand generations: how could it benefit only a single province? Thus both the flourishing of scholars in Fujian and the examination officials’ expectations of them rest upon this. I have considered the matter: the practical contributions of Confucian scholars are great. Yet to obtain an opportunity to put their learning into practice was something earlier Confucian masters earnestly desired but could not attain; they therefore had to entrust it to later generations. Those later generations dwell in their native places, receive the beneficent influence of their teaching, and live in the age of a sage ruler. They now embody in their writing the great aspiration cherished for hundreds and thousands of years, seeking to bring it to fulfillment. Moved by thoughts of bygone days and striving to render service at our illustrious court, they clearly warrant high expectations. Yet the presiding…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
司惴惴然猶且曰知人難以
言知人尤難言之以一日之
長而庸弗違則尤難之至如
是而曰得士則不明之咎誰
其逭之是以懼抑
國家之待士也重矣待之重則
責之不容不重士何以自責
===
乎矧惟儒先之繼免於□棄
恥為鄉人焉是可懼尤大也
雖然士先志夫志孰大於道
之行哉然以一物為心則累
於一物累斯怠怠斯畫而求
不負於所學得乎士惟責志
焉耳矣乃若主司之需乎士
punctuated:
司惴惴然，猶且曰：「知人難，以言知人尤難；言之以一日之長，而庸弗違，則尤難之至。」如是而曰得士，則不明之咎，誰其逭之？是以懼。抑國家之待士也重矣，待之重，則責之不容不重。士何以自責乎？矧惟儒先之繼，免於□棄，恥為鄉人焉，是可懼尤大也。

雖然，士先志。夫志孰大於道之行哉？然以一物為心，則累於一物；累斯怠，怠斯畫，而求不負於所學，得乎？士惟責志焉耳矣。乃若主司之需乎士
translation_en:
…the examining officials remain apprehensive and still say: “Knowing men is difficult; knowing men through their words is harder still. To judge a man by the excellence he displays on a single day, and then have his conduct in office accord with that judgment [?], is the very height of difficulty.” If, under such circumstances, we claim to have found worthy scholars, who can escape blame for a lack of discernment? This is why we are afraid. Moreover, the state treats scholars with great esteem. Since it esteems them so highly, its demands upon them must necessarily be correspondingly weighty. What demands, then, should scholars place upon themselves? Furthermore, as successors to the earlier Confucian masters, they must avoid being □ cast aside [?] and be ashamed to remain mere ordinary men of their native place. Here there is even greater cause for apprehension.

Nevertheless, for a scholar, resolve comes first. What resolve could be greater than that of putting the Way into practice? Yet if one fixes one’s mind upon a single thing, one becomes encumbered by it; encumbrance leads to indolence, and indolence to setting limits upon oneself. Can one then hope not to betray what one has learned? Scholars need only hold themselves accountable for their resolve. As for what the examining officials require of scholars…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也以世道也不以空言也夫
士不務空言而爲世道所賴
必能脫去恆習粹然於吾儒
之學明體而達用以答
聖功以明
文治無忝先正之鄕而主司亦
附於事
===
君以人者所以交懼而相成也然
非志焉曷爲之孔子曰大道
之行三代之英丘未之逮也
而有志焉夫孔子之志何遠
哉蓋所不能必慰者時也爾
諸士以時自慶矣其尚責志
於終焉是舉也提督軍務右
punctuated:
也，以世道也，不以空言也。夫士不務空言，而爲世道所賴，必能脫去恆習，粹然於吾儒之學，明體而達用，以答聖功，以明文治，無忝先正之鄕，而主司亦附於事君以人者，所以交懼而相成也。然非志焉，曷爲之？孔子曰：「大道之行，三代之英，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」夫孔子之志何遠哉！蓋所不能必慰者，時也。爾諸士以時自慶矣，其尚責志於終焉！
是舉也，提督軍務右
translation_en:
…what the presiding examiners seek from scholars concerns the moral order of the world, not empty words. Scholars who shun empty words and become a mainstay of that order must be able to cast off habitual ways and attain purity in our Confucian learning, illuminating its substance and comprehending its practical application. They thereby repay the sage emperor’s achievements and make manifest his civil governance, bringing no disgrace upon this native land of former worthies. The presiding examiners, too, may thus rank among those who serve their ruler by providing worthy men. In this way, their mutual apprehension leads each to help the other succeed. Yet without setting their resolve upon this, how could they accomplish it? Confucius said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, did not live to see them, yet I aspire to them.” How far-reaching was Confucius’s aspiration! What could not assuredly bring him consolation [?] was the age in which he lived. You scholars congratulate yourselves upon the age in which you live; may you hold yourselves to your resolve through to the end!
For this examination, the Superintendent of Military Affairs and Right …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
副都御史喻智遹觀人文右
叅政朱憲章左叅議吳源按
察副使秦鰲僉事余爌桂榮
張恕顧翀都指揮僉事盧鏜
路正均範理於外左叅政汪
大受僉事楊大章都指揮僉
事田耕顧邦重皆預用
===
賀按察使周采以遷秩副使張
謙以上績皆先行蓋嘗與勞
書之
直隸真定府趙州儒學學正
寇韋謹序
punctuated:
副都御史喻智，遹觀人文；右叅政朱憲章、左叅議吳源、按察副使秦鰲、僉事余爌、桂榮、張恕、顧翀、都指揮僉事盧鏜、路正，均範理於外。左叅政汪大受、僉事楊大章、都指揮僉事田耕、顧邦重，皆預用賀。按察使周采以遷秩，副使張謙以上績，皆先行，蓋嘗與勞，書之。
直隸真定府趙州儒學學正寇韋謹序。
translation_en:
…Vice Censor-in-chief Yu Zhi surveyed the flourishing of literary culture. Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Xianzhang, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Wu Yuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qin Ao, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Yu Kuang, Gui Rong, Zhang Shu, and Gu Chong, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Lu Tang and Lu Zheng all supervised and managed affairs outside the examination compound. Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Dashou, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Yang Dazhang, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Tian Geng and Gu Bangzhong all participated in offering congratulations [?]. Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Cai had departed earlier because of a promotion, as had Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Qian to report his administrative achievements. Since they too had contributed to the work, their names are recorded here.
Preface respectfully composed by Kou Wei, School Director of the Confucian School of Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史陳宗夔〔惟一湖廣通山縣人戊戌進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使屠大山〔國望浙江鄞縣人癸未進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使張鏊〔濟甫江西南昌縣人丙戌進士〕

福建等處提刑按察司副使柯喬〔遷之直隸青陽縣人己丑進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司僉事鄭炯〔□□□□餘姚縣人乙未□□〕
===
考試官
直隸眞定府趙州儒學學正寇韋〔自絃湖廣鄖縣人丁酉貢士〕
山東濟南府武定州陽信縣儒學教諭趙文翰〔叔煥河南信陽州人丁酉貢士〕
同考試官
江西贛州府雩都縣儒學教諭黎天啓〔允忠廣東順德縣人癸卯貢士〕
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教諭蔣仲哲〔汝鑑廣西全州人丁酉貢士〕
湖廣靖州儒學學正龍旆〔時揚廣西融縣人丁酉貢士〕
直隸揚州府儀眞縣儒學教諭馮璠〔美中貴州永寧衛籍浙江錢塘縣人丙午貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方輅〔朝錫江西樂平縣人庚子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試

監臨官
巡按福建監察御史陳宗夔〔惟一，湖廣通山縣人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使屠大山〔國望，浙江鄞縣人，癸未進士〕。
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使張鏊〔濟甫，江西南昌縣人，丙戌進士〕。

監試官
福建等處提刑按察司副使柯喬〔遷之，直隸青陽縣人，己丑進士〕。
福建等處提刑按察司僉事鄭炯〔□□□□，餘姚縣人，乙未□□〕。

考試官
直隸眞定府趙州儒學學正寇韋〔自絃，湖廣鄖縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
山東濟南府武定州陽信縣儒學教諭趙文翰〔叔煥，河南信陽州人，丁酉貢士〕。

同考試官
江西贛州府雩都縣儒學教諭黎天啓〔允忠，廣東順德縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教諭蔣仲哲〔汝鑑，廣西全州人，丁酉貢士〕。
湖廣靖州儒學學正龍旆〔時揚，廣西融縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
直隸揚州府儀眞縣儒學教諭馮璠〔美中，貴州永寧衛籍，浙江錢塘縣人，丙午貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方輅〔朝錫，江西樂平縣人，庚子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Fujian Provincial Examination, the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing (1549)

Supervising Official
Chen Zongkui, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Fujian. His courtesy name was Weiyi; he was from Tongshan County, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuxu year.

Proctors
Tu Dashan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian. His courtesy name was Guowang; he was from Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.
Zhang Ao, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian. His courtesy name was Jifu; he was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Examination Monitors
Ke Qiao, Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian. His courtesy name was Qianzhi; he was from Qingyang County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Zheng Jiong, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian. [Four characters illegible.] He was from Yuyao County; the annotation gives the yiwei year, followed by two illegible characters identifying his qualification [?].

Examiners
Kou Wei, Instructor at the Confucian School of Zhao Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Zixian; he was from Yun County, Huguang, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the dingyou year.
Zhao Wenhan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. His courtesy name was Shuhuan; he was from Xinyang Subprefecture, Henan, and was a tribute student of the dingyou year.

Associate Examiners
Li Tianqi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yudu County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Yunzhong; he was from Shunde County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student of the guimao year.
Jiang Zhongzhe, Instructor at the Confucian School of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Rujian; he was from Quan Subprefecture, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Long Pei, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jing Subprefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Shiyang; he was from Rong County, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Feng Fan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yizhen County, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Meizhong; his registration was in Yongning Guard, Guizhou, and he was originally from Qiantang County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student of the bingwu year.
Fang Lu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yingshang County, Ying Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Chaoxi; he was from Leping County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute student of the gengzi year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
山東兖州府滋陽縣儒學教諭費增〔公美江西德化縣人丁酉貢士〕
湖廣漢陽府漢川縣儒學教諭胡然〔性夫雲南左衛籍直隸鳳陽縣人丙午貢士〕
印卷官
福建等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷戴鱘〔子魚直隸桃源縣人監生〕
福建等處提刑按察司經歷司知事方宗善〔公一江西鉛山縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾與回言終日不違如愚退而省其
私亦足以發回也不愚
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也明乎郊社之禮禘嘗之義
治國其如示諸掌乎
未有義而後其君者也
易
===
夫大人者與天地合其德
凡益之道與時偕行
是故闔戶謂之坤闢戶謂之乾一闔一闢
謂之變往來不窮謂之通見乃謂之象
形乃謂之器制而用之謂之法利用出
入民咸用之謂之神是故易有太極是
生兩儀兩儀生四象四象生八卦
百官以治萬民以察
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「吾與回言終日，不違如愚。退而省其私，亦足以發，回也不愚。」

郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。明乎郊社之禮、禘嘗之義，治國其如示諸掌乎！

未有義而後其君者也。

易

夫大人者，與天地合其德。

凡益之道，與時偕行。

是故闔戶謂之坤，闢戶謂之乾，一闔一闢謂之變，往來不窮謂之通，見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器，制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。是故易有太極，是生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦。

百官以治，萬民以察。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “I have spoken with Hui all day, and he has raised no objection, as though he were stupid. Yet when he withdraws and I examine his conduct in private, it too suffices to elucidate what I have taught. Hui is not stupid.”

The rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil are the means by which one serves the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple are the means by which one sacrifices to one’s ancestors. For one who understands the rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil, and the meaning of the di and chang sacrifices, would governing a state not be like looking at something displayed on one’s palm?

There has never been a righteous person who put his ruler last.

Book of Changes

The great man harmonizes his virtue with Heaven and Earth.

Every way of bringing increase proceeds in step with the times.

Thus, closing the door is called kun; opening the door is called qian. One closing and one opening are called change; coming and going without exhaustion are called free passage. Becoming manifest is called an image; taking shape is called a vessel. Fashioning things and putting them to use is called a method; making their use beneficial in coming and going, so that all the people employ them, is called spiritual efficacy. Thus, in the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate, which generates the Two Modes. The Two Modes generate the Four Images; the Four Images generate the Eight Trigrams.

Through this, the hundred officials are brought into order, and the myriad people are kept under scrutiny.

Book of Documents

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:

凡厥庶民有猷有爲有守汝則念之不協

之極

之

善無常主，協于克一。

凡厥庶民，有猷、有爲、有守，汝則念之；不協于極，不罹于咎，皇則受之。而康而色，曰：「予攸好德。」汝則錫之福，時人斯其惟皇之極。

春秋
translation_en:
The emperor then spread his civil virtue far and wide, having dancers perform with shields and feathers between the two stairways. After seventy days, the Miao submitted.

Goodness has no constant possessor; it accords with those who can remain single-minded.

Among the common people, those who have plans, accomplishments, or steadfast principles—you should keep them in mind. Those who do not conform to the supreme standard, yet have incurred no blame—the sovereign should receive them. If, with composed countenances, they say, “What we love is virtue,” you should bestow blessings upon them. These people will then adhere to the sovereign’s supreme standard.

Reverently serve the Lord on High, and establish leaders and chiefs for the people.

BOOK OF ODES

Uneven grows the water-fringe: to left and right we gather it. The gentle, virtuous maiden: with zithers large and small we show her affection. Uneven grows the water-fringe: to left and right we select it. The gentle, virtuous maiden: with bells and drums we gladden her.

Like the luxuriant pine and cypress, may there be none who fail to sustain you.

He was laid in a narrow lane; cattle and sheep sheltered and nurtured him. He was laid in a level woodland; woodcutters happened to be felling trees there. He was laid upon cold ice; birds covered him with their wings. The birds then departed, and Hou Ji cried. Long and loud was his cry; his voice filled the road.

He has presented offerings to his illustrious deceased father, and likewise to his cultured mother.

translation_en:
Third Session
Policy questions〔five〕
Question: The Changes speaks of harmonious intercourse between above and below, and the Documents records the enlightened ruler and his worthy ministers. Thus, a meeting of ruler and ministers suited to one another occurs perhaps once in a thousand years. The tradition of exchanging songs at the court of Shun is ancient indeed. Since the Han and Tang dynasties, instances of mutual understanding between rulers and ministers have been fully recorded in the histories. Were there also instances that approached the spirit of those answering songs?
We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao placed the phrase “ruler and ministers touring together” at the very beginning of the Third Compilation of the Great Pronouncements. How grand these imperial words are! Truly, they shine resplendently through the ages. Reading now the Record of the River-Viewing Tower and the Song of the Drunken Academician, we can still envision the flourishing relationship between the enlightened ruler and his worthy ministers at that time. Yet the imperial intent was profound and far-reaching: can those living ten thousand generations later fathom even a small part of it?
The successive sage emperors inherited this tradition, with ruler and subjects forming a single body. Can we also learn the broad outlines of their imperial summons, banquets, and excursions from the Records of Imperial Instructions and the accounts left by scholarly officials? Coming now to our present Emperor, whose reign has coincided with an age of flourishing and who has availed himself of an era of peace, he once, during …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
萬幾之暇
召見輔臣及
賜同遊西苑真媲美唐虞同符
聖祖矣
宸翰天章皆昭播寰宇諸士子能仰窺其萬一
歟其鋪張揚厲之以鳴
國家之盛
問甞聞聖人之精因畫以示故書也者所
以畫聖人之心法者也自伏羲始畫八
===
卦而書契聿興嗣後群聖授受心法相
因故帝王之書代有作者其詳可歷指
而言歟黃帝命倉頡作六書而字文肇
立至周宣變為大篆而文字寖備矣於
群聖心法之微抑有所傳歟秦弗師古
書法漸滅自漢而降十札之書頒及方
國飛白之字賚及近臣勒孝經於碑陰
賜吏治於棘寺書非不善也不知果有
得於聖人之心法否乎洪惟我

萬幾之暇，召見輔臣，及賜同遊西苑，真媲美唐虞，同符聖祖矣。宸翰天章，皆昭播寰宇，諸士子能仰窺其萬一歟？其鋪張揚厲之，以鳴國家之盛。
問：甞聞聖人之精，因畫以示，故書也者，所以畫聖人之心法者也。自伏羲始畫八卦，而書契聿興。嗣後群聖授受，心法相因，故帝王之書，代有作者，其詳可歷指而言歟？黃帝命倉頡作六書，而字文肇立；至周宣變為大篆，而文字寖備矣。於群聖心法之微，抑有所傳歟？秦弗師古，書法漸滅。自漢而降，十札之書頒及方國，飛白之字賚及近臣，勒《孝經》於碑陰，賜《吏治》於棘寺。書非不善也，不知果有得於聖人之心法否乎？洪惟我
translation_en:
…in moments of leisure from the myriad affairs of government, he summoned his grand secretaries to an audience and graciously allowed them to accompany him on an excursion through the Western Park. This truly rivaled the splendor of the reigns of Tang and Yu and accorded with the example of the sagely ancestor. His imperial calligraphy and august compositions have been illustriously disseminated throughout the realm. Can you examination candidates reverently discern even a ten-thousandth part of their significance? Expound and extol these achievements, giving voice to the flourishing grandeur of the state.
Question: We have heard that the essential spirit of the sages is revealed through drawn strokes. Thus, writing is the means by which the sages’ teachings of the mind are depicted. Beginning when Fu Xi first drew the Eight Trigrams, written signs came into being. Thereafter, the sages transmitted and received these teachings of the mind in succession; hence, in every age there were emperors and kings who produced works of calligraphy. Can you enumerate these in detail and discuss them? The Yellow Emperor commanded Cang Jie to devise the Six Principles of Writing, and written characters were first established. By the time of King Xuan of Zhou, the script had changed into Greater Seal script, and the forms of writing gradually became complete. Did this also transmit something of the subtle teachings of the sages’ minds? Qin failed to take antiquity as its model, and the methods of writing gradually disappeared. From the Han onward, writings on ten slips [?] were distributed to the regional states; characters in ‘flying-white’ script were bestowed upon close ministers; the Classic of Filial Piety was engraved on the reverse of a stele; and ‘The Governance of Officials’ was bestowed upon the Court of Judicial Review. Such calligraphy was certainly accomplished, but we do not know whether it truly embodied an understanding of the sages’ teachings of the mind. Reverently considering our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝
聖神天縱凡
誥諭臣民對越
郊廟者皆親灑
宸翰又甞
特命儒臣勒成洪武正韻一書盡合古文之本
旨頓洗千古之陋習誠萬世不刊之典
也然書法之或因或革當時儒臣果何
所取正歟迨我
===
皇上聖思神授
睿藻天成甞以一夜註釋五箴或揮灑千言
頃刻立就勒之
陵寢播之訓告形之咏歌者多出自
奎畫今固已炳燭丹書而粃稃倉史矣然我
皇上心法之傳遠紹羲皇媲休
聖祖者則固不在點畫翰墨之間也多士涵濡
同文之化久矣請敬陳之
問仁智性之德也合内外者也而說者不
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝，聖神天縱，凡誥諭臣民、對越郊廟者，皆親灑宸翰。又甞特命儒臣勒成《洪武正韻》一書，盡合古文之本旨，頓洗千古之陋習，誠萬世不刊之典也。然書法之或因或革，當時儒臣果何所取正歟？迨我皇上，聖思神授，睿藻天成，甞以一夜註釋五箴，或揮灑千言，頃刻立就。勒之陵寢、播之訓告、形之咏歌者，多出自奎畫。今固已炳燭丹書，而粃稃倉史矣。然我皇上心法之傳，遠紹羲皇，媲休聖祖者，則固不在點畫翰墨之間也。多士涵濡同文之化久矣，請敬陳之。
問：仁智，性之德也，合内外者也，而說者不
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagely and divine qualities, personally wielded the imperial brush for all proclamations to officials and commoners and all writings addressing the spirits at the suburban altars and ancestral temples. He also once specially commanded Confucian officials to compile the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu Zhengyun). Entirely consonant with the original principles of ancient writing, it swept away at a stroke the defective practices of ages past. Truly, it is an authoritative work that shall stand unaltered for ten thousand generations. Yet, in retaining some conventions of writing and changing others, what standards did those Confucian officials actually follow?
Coming down to our present emperor, his sagely thoughts are divinely inspired, and his discerning literary compositions are naturally accomplished. Once, in a single night, he annotated the Five Admonitions; on other occasions, a thousand words flowed from his brush, completed in an instant. Many of the writings engraved at the imperial mausoleums, disseminated as instructions and proclamations, or expressed in songs originate from his imperial brush. Indeed, he has already illuminated the Cinnabar Writings and reduced the work of the scribe Cang Jie to mere chaff. Yet the transmission of the teaching of the mind through our emperor, reaching back to Emperor Fuxi and matching the glory of the sagely founding ancestor, assuredly does not reside merely in brushstrokes and ink. You candidates have long been steeped in the civilizing influence of a shared written culture. Respectfully set forth your views.
Question: Benevolence and wisdom are virtues of human nature, uniting the inner and the outer. Yet those who explain them do not …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
同何歟孔子曰智者動仁者靜固矣至
傳易論陰陽之道别言仁智所見之異
而朱子釋之曰仁陽智陰則又以仁爲
動而智爲靜何也子思子曰成己仁也
成物智也固矣及子貢稱夫子之聖則
以學言智以教言仁而朱子釋之曰智
所以自明仁所以𠄢物則又以成己爲
智成物爲仁何也程子云仁包四德是
智在仁之中也朱子謂四德之智如四
===
時之冬萬物成始而成終則仁又在智
之中矣抑又何耶孔子以智屬乎天仁
屬乎地而後人有智圓仁方之說孔子
以智仁勇爲三達德而後人有仁明武
之言果能皆得其旨否乎玆欲即用明
體而析之有以極其精會偏求全而合
之有以體其大果何如而後爲至當協
一之論也學者因聖賢之立言而求端
用力指歸果安在哉訂證千古詔示方
punctuated: 同，何歟？孔子曰：「智者動，仁者靜。」固矣。至傳易，論陰陽之道，别言仁智所見之異，而朱子釋之曰：「仁陽，智陰。」則又以仁爲動而智爲靜，何也？子思子曰：「成己，仁也；成物，智也。」固矣。及子貢稱夫子之聖，則以學言智，以教言仁，而朱子釋之曰：「智所以自明，仁所以𠄢物。」則又以成己爲智，成物爲仁，何也？程子云：「仁包四德。」是智在仁之中也。朱子謂四德之智，如四時之冬，萬物成始而成終，則仁又在智之中矣。抑又何耶？孔子以智屬乎天，仁屬乎地，而後人有智圓仁方之說；孔子以智仁勇爲三達德，而後人有仁明武之言。果能皆得其旨否乎？玆欲即用明體而析之，有以極其精；會偏求全而合之，有以體其大。果何如而後爲至當協一之論也？學者因聖賢之立言而求端，用力指歸，果安在哉？訂證千古，詔示方
translation_en:
…differ: why is this? Confucius said, “The wise are active; the benevolent are still.” This is certainly so. Yet in his commentary on the Book of Changes, when discussing the Way of yin and yang, he distinguishes what the benevolent and the wise perceive. Zhu Xi explains this by saying, “Benevolence is yang; wisdom is yin.” This, however, makes benevolence active and wisdom still. Why is this? Master Zisi said, “Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom.” This is certainly so. Yet when Zigong praised the sageliness of Confucius, he spoke of wisdom in terms of learning and benevolence in terms of teaching. Zhu Xi explains this by saying, “Wisdom is the means of enlightening oneself; benevolence is the means of [acting upon?] things.” This, however, makes perfecting oneself wisdom and perfecting things benevolence. Why is this?

Master Cheng said, “Benevolence encompasses the four virtues.” Thus wisdom is contained within benevolence. Zhu Xi says that wisdom among the four virtues is like winter among the four seasons: through it the myriad things complete their beginning and their end. Thus benevolence is, in turn, contained within wisdom. Why, then, is this? Confucius associated wisdom with Heaven and benevolence with Earth, and later thinkers spoke of wisdom as round and benevolence as square. Confucius regarded wisdom, benevolence, and courage as the three universally applicable virtues, and later thinkers spoke of benevolence, discernment, and martial prowess. Did all these formulations truly capture his meaning?

We now wish to elucidate substance through function, analyzing these matters so as to reach their utmost subtlety; and to bring partial perspectives together in pursuit of completeness, synthesizing them so as to embody their full scope. How, indeed, can we arrive at an account that is entirely fitting, harmonious, and unified? When learners seek a starting point in the pronouncements of the sages and worthies, where, precisely, should they direct their efforts? Critically examine and substantiate the teachings of the ages, and give instruction to those …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
來不徒泛然口耳而已試以心得者陳
之
問昔人言天下政平訟理惟良二千石又
曰宰天下不如爲縣令之樂以其親民
也故守令賢否係生民休戚而天下之
治因之漢之循吏史冊所載盛矣或文
學化俗或敎化安全或勸民農桑樹畜
或疏鑿灌溉而防禁奢靡似矣然埒之
治蒲宰莒諸賢亦可以並駕歟然有稱
===
治行第一而政績罔聞且弁其名而失
之又或偽增戸數而蒙旌賞豈當時所
謂循吏者亦未可盡信歟我
國朝遴選守令屢廑
詔旨特加優重百八十年來民安物阜厥有由
然其人亦可以殫述歟其最著者如況
之治蘇劉之治雄王之治維揚林之治
潤顧之治莊浪許之治樂陵皆守令之
卓異者也其遺風善政孰可以爲法歟
punctuated:
來，不徒泛然口耳而已，試以心得者陳之。

問：昔人言：「天下政平訟理，惟良二千石。」又曰：「宰天下不如爲縣令之樂。」以其親民也。故守令賢否，係生民休戚，而天下之治因之。漢之循吏，史冊所載盛矣：或文學化俗，或敎化安全，或勸民農桑樹畜，或疏鑿灌溉而防禁奢靡，似矣。然埒之治蒲、宰莒諸賢，亦可以並駕歟？然有稱治行第一而政績罔聞，且弁其名而失之，又或偽增戸數而蒙旌賞，豈當時所謂循吏者亦未可盡信歟？我國朝遴選守令，屢廑詔旨，特加優重。百八十年來，民安物阜，厥有由然。其人亦可以殫述歟？其最著者，如況之治蘇、劉之治雄、王之治維揚、林之治潤、顧之治莊浪、許之治樂陵，皆守令之卓異者也。其遺風善政，孰可以爲法歟？
translation_en:
…those to come, rather than merely engaging in superficial talk and hearsay. Set forth what you have grasped for yourselves.

Question: An ancient said, “For equitable government and the proper adjudication of lawsuits throughout the realm, all depends on worthy officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank.” Another said, “Administering the realm does not match the pleasure of serving as a district magistrate,” because the latter is close to the people. Thus, whether prefects and magistrates are worthy determines the people's well-being or suffering, and the good government of the realm depends upon this. The historical records contain abundant accounts of the conscientious officials of the Han: some transformed customs through literary learning; some brought security through moral instruction; some encouraged farming, sericulture, planting, and livestock raising; and some dredged and dug irrigation works while restraining extravagance. These seem worthy achievements. Yet, measured against the worthies who governed Pu and administered Ju, could they stand alongside them? Some, however, were acclaimed as foremost in administrative performance, yet no achievements in government are known of them; moreover, placing their names at the head of the list was mistaken [?]. Others fraudulently inflated household counts and received commendations and rewards. Might the accounts of those called conscientious officials at the time therefore not be wholly trustworthy?

Our dynasty has carefully selected prefects and magistrates, repeatedly making this a concern of imperial edicts and treating these officials with particular favor and esteem. There are indeed reasons why, over the past hundred and eighty years, the people have enjoyed peace and material abundance. Could all these men be enumerated? Among the most renowned are Kuang, who governed Su; Liu, who governed Xiong; Wang, who governed Weiyang; Lin, who governed Run; Gu, who governed Zhuanglang; and Xu, who governed Leling. All were outstanding prefects or magistrates. Which of the traditions and good administrative practices they left behind can serve as models?

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫吏治得失古今炳然司民牧者追跡
循良固有不必遠慕而得者然願治君
子往往有遺慨焉豈所持未得其要歟
抑致此别有道歟諸士子行將有民物
之寄幸以槩於中者言之以爲時政之
一助
問
國家經世利用莫善於飛輓之制則鹽法固
今日之大猷也試以閩中鹽法商之夫建官轉
===
運竝峙淮浙其責維鈞而鹽法之詳略
迥異其究可得聞歟淮浙之產鹽也恒
難而課獨有餘八閩之產鹽也恒易而
課每不足果行鹽之地有未廣食鹽之
戶有未蕃歟抑經畫之無方禁令之未
壹歟均一場司也而徵納有本折之異
同爲引鹽也而析引有大小之殊辦鹽
爲竈丁之業乃又得以米折價額課爲
邊餽之需復分給內地軍餉報中則姦
punctuated:
夫吏治得失，古今炳然。司民牧者追跡循良，固有不必遠慕而得者。然願治君子往往有遺慨焉，豈所持未得其要歟？抑致此别有道歟？諸士子行將有民物之寄，幸以槩於中者言之，以爲時政之一助。
問：國家經世利用，莫善於飛輓之制，則鹽法固今日之大猷也。試以閩中鹽法商之。夫建官轉運，竝峙淮浙，其責維鈞，而鹽法之詳略迥異，其究可得聞歟？淮浙之產鹽也恒難，而課獨有餘；八閩之產鹽也恒易，而課每不足。果行鹽之地有未廣、食鹽之戶有未蕃歟？抑經畫之無方、禁令之未壹歟？均一場司也，而徵納有本折之異；同爲引鹽也，而析引有大小之殊。辦鹽爲竈丁之業，乃又得以米折價；額課爲邊餽之需，復分給內地軍餉。報中則姦
translation_en:
The successes and failures of official administration stand clearly revealed, both past and present. Those charged with governing the people can follow the example of upright and capable officials without necessarily seeking models in the distant past. Yet gentlemen intent on good government often find cause for lingering regret. Is this because their approach fails to grasp the essentials? Or is there some other reason for this outcome? You candidates will soon be entrusted with the people and their affairs. Please state what is in your hearts, thereby contributing to the government of the day.
Question: For ordering the realm and making effective use of resources, no state institution surpasses the system of rapid provision transport. The salt administration is therefore surely a major policy of our day. Let us examine it through the salt administration of Fujian. Offices for salt distribution have been established here alongside those of Huai and Zhe, with equal responsibilities; yet their salt regulations differ markedly in detail and scope. May we hear a thorough explanation? Salt production in Huai and Zhe is consistently difficult, yet their tax receipts yield a surplus; salt production in the eight prefectures of Fujian is consistently easy, yet their receipts repeatedly fall short. Is the territory in which their salt may be sold really insufficiently extensive, or are the households consuming it insufficiently numerous? Or does the fault lie in inadequate planning and inconsistent prohibitions? All are alike saltworks offices, yet some collect dues in kind and others in commuted payments. All handle salt issued against certificates, yet the quantities allotted per certificate differ in size. Producing salt is the occupation of registered salt workers, yet they are also allowed to commute its value in rice [?]. The assessed revenue is intended to supply the frontier, yet portions are also allocated to military provisions in the interior. When subscriptions for salt certificates are reported, dishonest …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
商土著自操贏縮之權賦役則刁竈滑
胥巧爲影射之計是豈立法之舊歟近
於潯浯沋三場有欲別立抽分以助海
防之用者有欲輕價召中以免轉輸之
艱者議孰爲優於福寧福安地方有欲
添委掣摯以增額外之稅者有欲嚴捕
私販以資軍門之需者說孰爲當其運
鹽也一母二子之名似與額定正餘者
不侔其榷鹽也圍量抽掣之法擬之懸
===
衡秤較者有間東路細鹽之規當矣或
有議其競利南路官鹽之立似矣或有
病其多事將何所折衷歟玆皆鹺政之
大都也今欲使其法盡復
祖宗之舊而又不拂乎時宜使其課盡歸軍國
之資而又不爲小民之病果何施而後
可請備言之以觀用世之學
punctuated: 商土著自操贏縮之權；賦役則刁竈滑胥巧爲影射之計。是豈立法之舊歟？近於潯、浯、沋三場，有欲別立抽分以助海防之用者，有欲輕價召中以免轉輸之艱者，議孰爲優？於福寧、福安地方，有欲添委掣摯以增額外之稅者，有欲嚴捕私販以資軍門之需者，說孰爲當？其運鹽也，一母二子之名似與額定正餘者不侔；其榷鹽也，圍量抽掣之法擬之懸衡秤較者有間。東路細鹽之規當矣，或有議其競利；南路官鹽之立似矣，或有病其多事。將何所折衷歟？玆皆鹺政之大都也。今欲使其法盡復祖宗之舊，而又不拂乎時宜；使其課盡歸軍國之資，而又不爲小民之病，果何施而後可？請備言之，以觀用世之學。
translation_en:
…merchants and local residents themselves control increases and reductions; in taxes and labor service, crafty salt producers and unscrupulous clerks devise clever schemes of concealment under others’ names. Can this be the original intent of the regulations? Recently, at the three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and You, some have proposed instituting a separate levy in kind to help meet coastal-defense expenses, while others have proposed offering salt at a lower price to attract merchants to take up contracts and avoid the difficulties of transport. Which proposal is preferable? In Funing and Fu’an, some have proposed appointing additional officers to inspect and levy salt [?], thereby increasing revenue beyond the established quota; others have proposed rigorously apprehending illicit salt dealers to meet the needs of the military command. Which view is appropriate?

In salt transport, the designation “one mother and two sons” seems inconsistent with the prescribed quotas for regular and surplus salt. In administering the salt monopoly, the method of measuring by enclosure and extracting a levy differs from weighing and checking with suspended scales. The regulations for fine salt on the eastern route seem appropriate, yet some criticize them for competing for profit. The establishment of government salt on the southern route seems reasonable, yet some fault it for creating too much administrative business. How should these views be reconciled?

These are all major aspects of salt administration. Now, if we wish to restore its regulations fully to the ancestral emperors’ precedents without running counter to present circumstances, and to ensure that all its revenues go toward military and state expenses without burdening the common people, what measures must be taken to accomplish this? Please explain fully, so that we may assess your learning for practical service in the world.
