title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾與回言終日不違如愚退而省其
私亦足以發回也不愚
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批此章語本照應而作者
多欠體貼是篇辭簡意完迥異衆作錄之不獨以文也
同考試官學正龍批孔顏授受之蘊而以舉
業排比之文發之難矣哉錄此以示作論語義者
===
考試官教諭趙批此亦似足以發者
考試官學正寇批善發聖人之蘊
聖人與大賢之悟教而有得於其獨焉夫學以
心悟而不以言求顏子之自得者深矣聖人驗
於其獨而樂與之有以哉昔吾夫子之意蓋謂
君子之學以致道也而君子之教以言傳也故
吾與回言終日要之無非教也而亦無非以明
乎道也夫言以終日則其言已多而其時亦久
矣吾見回也言斯聽之未甞因言而有疑聽斯
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「吾與回言終日，不違如愚。退而省其私，亦足以發。回也不愚。」

黃士觀

同考試官教諭馮批：「此章語本照應，而作者多欠體貼。是篇辭簡意完，迥異衆作，錄之不獨以文也。」

同考試官學正龍批：「孔顏授受之蘊，而以舉業排比之文發之，難矣哉！錄此以示作論語義者。」

考試官教諭趙批：「此亦似足以發者。」

考試官學正寇批：「善發聖人之蘊。」

聖人與大賢之悟教，而有得於其獨焉。夫學以心悟，而不以言求，顏子之自得者深矣。聖人驗於其獨而樂與之，有以哉！昔吾夫子之意，蓋謂君子之學以致道也，而君子之教以言傳也。故吾與回言終日，要之無非教也，而亦無非以明乎道也。夫言以終日，則其言已多，而其時亦久矣。吾見回也，言斯聽之，未甞因言而有疑；聽斯
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “I have spoken with Hui all day, and he has raised no objections, as though he were foolish. Yet when he withdraws and I examine his private conduct, it too is sufficient to elucidate what I have taught. Hui is not foolish.”

Huang Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “The wording of this chapter has correspondences throughout, but writers often fail to grasp its meaning closely. This essay is concise in expression and complete in meaning, markedly different from the other compositions. It is selected for more than its literary merit alone.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, School Director: “How difficult it is to bring out the profound meaning of what Confucius transmitted and Yan Hui received through the parallel prose of examination compositions! This is selected to show those composing essays on the meaning of the Analects.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “This, too, seems sufficient to elucidate the teaching.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Director: “It brings out the sage’s profound meaning well.”

The sage approved the great worthy’s understanding of his teaching, finding confirmation in his conduct when alone. Learning rests on understanding with the mind rather than seeking through words: Master Yan’s understanding attained for himself was profound indeed. The sage verified it in his conduct when alone and gladly approved him—with good reason! What our Master meant on that occasion was, surely, that the gentleman studies to attain the Way, while the gentleman teaches by transmitting it through words. Thus: “When I speak with Hui all day, in sum, everything I say is instruction, and everything serves to clarify the Way. Now, when one speaks for an entire day, the words are already many and the time is long. I observe that whenever I speak, Hui listens, never entertaining doubts because of what I say; having listened, he…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
受之未甞因疑而有問是吾言以終日而其不
違亦終日也斯不亦無所於可無所於否而呐
然如愚者耶使其退也而無以發也則亦何取
於回也及因其宴居之暇而考其體驗之真則
又見其非有師友之臨也而坦然見乎日用其
於吾所言者無一而不體會焉非有啟沃之資
也而沛然措諸躬行其與終日語者無一而不
發明焉是其時之靜也見其涵道之體也其感
而通也見其順應之妙也相悅以解而無所於
===
疑相悟以心而無俟於問玆回之所以為明也
而可以愚目之乎是知不違如愚者乃其迹之
似而亦足以發者固其學之幾於化也夫子豈
真不知回者哉樂與之意深是故反覆其詞以
表見之爾雖然夫子亦以回之愚而警諸子之
才辯也孔門之能悟者回之下其次莫如子貢
然子貢之多識其失也以達回之得也以愚至
論其傳則又在參之魯焉嗟乎有子貢之達而
不足於愚魯尚未之有得而况無子貢之達者
punctuated: 受之，未甞因疑而有問。是吾言以終日，而其不違亦終日也。斯不亦無所於可、無所於否，而呐然如愚者耶？使其退也而無以發也，則亦何取於回也？及因其宴居之暇，而考其體驗之真，則又見其非有師友之臨也，而坦然見乎日用，其於吾所言者，無一而不體會焉；非有啟沃之資也，而沛然措諸躬行，其與終日語者，無一而不發明焉。是其時之靜也，見其涵道之體也；其感而通也，見其順應之妙也。相悅以解，而無所於疑；相悟以心，而無俟於問。玆回之所以為明也，而可以愚目之乎？是知不違如愚者，乃其迹之似，而亦足以發者，固其學之幾於化也。夫子豈真不知回者哉？樂與之意深，是故反覆其詞以表見之爾。雖然，夫子亦以回之愚而警諸子之才辯也。孔門之能悟者，回之下，其次莫如子貢。然子貢之多識，其失也以達；回之得也以愚。至論其傳，則又在參之魯焉。嗟乎！有子貢之達而不足於愚魯，尚未之有得，而况無子貢之達者
translation_en:
…he accepted it, never raising a question on account of doubt. Thus, as I spoke throughout the day, he likewise went throughout the day without dissent. Did he not seem to approve of nothing and disapprove of nothing, remaining inarticulate, like a fool? If, after withdrawing, he had been unable to bring anything forth, what would there have been to value in Hui? Yet when I examined the genuineness of his understanding and practice in his hours of private leisure, I saw that, even without teachers or friends present, he manifested it freely in daily life: there was nothing I had said that he did not grasp and embody. Without the assistance of further instruction, he put it abundantly into personal practice: there was nothing in our whole day’s conversation that he did not bring to light. In his stillness, one could see how he inwardly nurtured the Way; when moved by things and responding to them, one could see the subtlety of his fitting responses. We delighted in one another through understanding, with no room for doubt; we understood one another in our hearts, without waiting for questions. This is what made Hui discerning. Could he be regarded as foolish?

We thus know that his seeming foolishness in never dissenting was merely the outward appearance of his conduct, whereas his capacity to bring the teaching to light showed that his learning had indeed approached effortless transformation. Could the Master really have failed to understand Yan Hui? His delight in approving of him was profound; therefore he turned the matter over repeatedly in his words to make it manifest. Nevertheless, the Master also used Hui’s apparent foolishness to admonish the other disciples for their cleverness and eloquence. Among those in Confucius’s school capable of insight, none ranked next below Hui more highly than Zigong. Yet, for all Zigong’s extensive knowledge, his failing lay in his intellectual facility; Hui’s attainment lay in his apparent foolishness. As for the transmission of the teaching, that rested instead with the apparent dullness of Zeng Shen. Alas! Even someone possessing Zigong’s intellectual facility, if insufficiently endowed with such foolishness and dullness, would still have attained nothing. How much more so someone without Zigong’s intellectual facility…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎求聖人之道者於此可以辨其幾矣
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也明乎郊社之禮禘嘗之義
治國其如示諸掌乎
丘行義
同考試官教諭方批講治國示掌處異乎諸
子之作似甞於禮制而有得者
同考試官教諭費批作者多勦說浮詞獨是
篇據理敷衍略不作一時俗語是可與言禮矣
===
考試官教諭趙批文有理致
考試官學正寇批發揮精到
中庸推祀禮之大者而君道無不備焉蓋君道
莫大於事神治人也禮之大者有以該之其盡
制何如哉中庸舉武王周公制禮以明道而終
言之如此蓋曰聖人制禮非徒備王制之隆寔
以寓王道之大誠以王者為上帝所寵綏其事
之不可不重也于是乎郊社之禮制焉語精誠
則致其通也語功德則大其報也參一人於兩
punctuated:
乎？求聖人之道者，於此可以辨其幾矣。

郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。明乎郊社之禮、禘嘗之義，治國其如示諸掌乎！

丘行義

同考試官教諭方批：講治國示掌處，異乎諸子之作，似甞於禮制而有得者。

同考試官教諭費批：作者多勦說浮詞，獨是篇據理敷衍，略不作一時俗語，是可與言禮矣。

考試官教諭趙批：文有理致。

考試官學正寇批：發揮精到。

中庸推祀禮之大者，而君道無不備焉。蓋君道莫大於事神治人也，禮之大者有以該之，其盡制何如哉！中庸舉武王周公制禮以明道，而終言之如此。蓋曰：聖人制禮，非徒備王制之隆，寔以寓王道之大。誠以王者為上帝所寵綏，其事之不可不重也，於是乎郊社之禮制焉。語精誠，則致其通也；語功德，則大其報也。參一人於兩
translation_en:
…could they? Those who seek the Way of the sage can here discern its subtle workings.

“The rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil are those by which one serves the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple are those by which one sacrifices to one’s ancestors. If one understood the rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil, and the meaning of the di and chang sacrifices, would governing a state not be like displaying something on one’s palm?”

Qiu Xingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “Its discussion of governing a state as though displaying something on one’s palm differs from the other candidates’ compositions. The author seems to have gained some understanding through studying ritual institutions.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: “Most writers offer borrowed explanations and empty phrases. This essay alone develops its argument on the basis of principle, without the slightest resort to the fashionable language of the day. Here is someone with whom one can discuss ritual.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The composition has reasoned depth.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: “Its exposition is precise and thorough.”

The Doctrine of the Mean expounds the greatest sacrificial rites, in which the Way of the ruler is fully embodied. For nothing in the ruler’s Way is greater than serving the spirits and governing the people. The greatest rites encompass these: how completely their institutions provide for them! The Doctrine of the Mean cites the establishment of rites by King Wu and the Duke of Zhou to illuminate the Way, and concludes with these words. Their meaning is this: when sages established rites, they did not merely provide for the grandeur of royal institutions; they embodied within them the greatness of the kingly Way. Truly, since the king is favored and protected by the Lord on High, he must attach the utmost importance to serving him. Thus the rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil were instituted. In terms of pure sincerity, they bring communion to its fullest realization; in terms of meritorious beneficence, they magnify the repayment of it. They place the One Man as a third alongside the two…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
間夫固有以憑藉而奉承之矣率仁以饗帝禮
之制不其大乎王者爲祖宗所付託其祀之不
可不隆也于是乎宗廟之禮行焉以尊崇則人
情之極也以薦享則天道之經也自一世以萬
世夫固可以率循而對越之矣致孝以饗親禮
之義不其精乎夫斯禮也斯義也制之而仁孝
全擴之而治化備焉者也誠使有聖者作於郊
社而測其微焉於禘嘗而研其蘊焉則其於治
國也何有乎蓋神人雖異用而感通之者惟一
===
心禮政雖殊途而推行之者惟一理由其仁以
仁天下而化吾見其易孚也由其孝以教天下
而恩吾見其易洽也是卽天地吾奠位于上下
祖宗吾昭假於宗祊者也謂之曰其如示諸掌
信乎王制之明而王道特易易矣是則禮制極
乎天親而經制達乎天下此武王周公所以爲
盡道而其達孝亦足徵焉矣抑有虞氏禘黃帝
而郊嚳則郊禘之禮自夏殷以上皆行之而尊
尊親親仁至義盡則至武周而後大備也是故
punctuated: 間，夫固有以憑藉而奉承之矣。率仁以饗帝，禮之制不其大乎？王者爲祖宗所付託，其祀之不可不隆也。于是乎宗廟之禮行焉：以尊崇，則人情之極也；以薦享，則天道之經也。自一世以萬世，夫固可以率循而對越之矣。致孝以饗親，禮之義不其精乎？夫斯禮也，斯義也，制之而仁孝全，擴之而治化備焉者也。誠使有聖者作，於郊社而測其微焉，於禘嘗而研其蘊焉，則其於治國也何有乎？蓋神人雖異用，而感通之者惟一心；禮政雖殊途，而推行之者惟一理。由其仁以仁天下，而化吾見其易孚也；由其孝以教天下，而恩吾見其易洽也。是卽天地吾奠位于上下，祖宗吾昭假於宗祊者也。謂之曰「其如示諸掌」，信乎王制之明，而王道特易易矣。是則禮制極乎天親，而經制達乎天下。此武王周公所以爲盡道，而其達孝亦足徵焉矣。抑有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，則郊禘之禮自夏殷以上皆行之，而尊尊親親、仁至義盡，則至武周而後大備也。是故
translation_en: …between Heaven and Earth, he surely has a basis on which to rely in reverently serving them. Following benevolence in offering sacrifice to the Supreme Lord—is not this ritual institution great? The king has been entrusted with his charge by his ancestors, and his sacrifices to them must therefore be grand. Thus the rites of the ancestral temple are performed: in honoring and exalting the ancestors, they bring human feelings to their fullest expression; in presenting sacrificial offerings, they embody the constant order of Heaven’s Way. From one generation through ten thousand generations, there is assuredly a pattern to follow in reverently responding to them. Fulfilling filial devotion through offerings to one’s parents—is not the meaning of these rites profound? These rites and their meaning, when instituted, bring benevolence and filial devotion to completion; when extended, they fully provide for government and moral transformation. If a sage should indeed arise, fathom the subtleties of the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and the sacrifices to the soil, and investigate the deep significance of the di ancestral sacrifice and the autumn sacrifice, what difficulty would he have in governing the state? For although dealings with spirits and human beings differ, it is the same heart that responds to and communes with them; although ritual and government take different paths, it is the same principle that is carried into practice. By extending his benevolence to treat all under Heaven benevolently, he would, I believe, readily secure their trust in his transforming influence. By extending his filial devotion to instruct all under Heaven, he would, I believe, readily spread his gracious influence everywhere. This is precisely what is expressed in saying: ‘For Heaven and Earth, I establish their positions above and below; to the ancestors, I reverently draw near.’ To describe this as ‘like showing something on one’s palm’ is indeed apt: royal institutions are clear, and the kingly Way becomes exceedingly easy to practice. Thus ritual institutions reach their fullest expression in serving Heaven and one’s parents, while the established order extends throughout all under Heaven. This is why King Wu and the Duke of Zhou are said to have fulfilled the Way; their universally exemplary filial devotion is also sufficiently demonstrated here. Yet the ruler of Yu, Shun, offered the di sacrifice to Huangdi and the suburban sacrifice to Ku. Thus the suburban and di sacrifices were already practiced in the Xia and Yin dynasties and before. But honoring the honored and cherishing one’s kin, with benevolence brought to its utmost and righteousness fully realized, attained complete fulfillment only with King Wu and the Duke of Zhou. For this reason…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
孔子亟稱之而又推極其道正以見繼述之善
有在耳先儒曰舜爲人道之極萬世仰之不可
加周爲王制之備萬世由之不能易噫其亦深
知聖人者乎
未有義而後其君者也
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批義必急君是就性分上
說出不可已處此作盡之矣
同考試官教諭黎批詞嚴義正孟子義之絕
===
佳者宜錄以式
考試官教諭趙批發揮忠與義無二道文
字大見筆力佳士也
考試官學正寇批親切有味
大賢决言懷義者必能忠乎其君也夫義以行
忠則忠根諸性矣曾謂懷義而有不忠其君者
哉於此見義之爲利而君人者當審所尚也孟
子開導惠王之意如此蓋曰志莫同於上下之
交治莫先於義利之辨吾謂王亦有仁義者豈
punctuated:
孔子亟稱之，而又推極其道，正以見繼述之善有在耳。先儒曰：「舜爲人道之極，萬世仰之不可加；周爲王制之備，萬世由之不能易。」噫！其亦深知聖人者乎！

未有義而後其君者也。
鄭元韶

同考試官教諭蔣批：「義必急君，是就性分上說出不可已處，此作盡之矣。」
同考試官教諭黎批：「詞嚴義正，孟子義之絕佳者，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭趙批：「發揮忠與義無二道，文字大見筆力，佳士也。」
考試官學正寇批：「親切有味。」

大賢决言懷義者必能忠乎其君也。夫義以行忠，則忠根諸性矣。曾謂懷義而有不忠其君者哉？於此見義之爲利，而君人者當審所尚也。孟子開導惠王之意如此。蓋曰：志莫同於上下之交，治莫先於義利之辨。吾謂王亦有仁義者，豈
translation_en:
…Confucius repeatedly praised them and further expounded their Way to its fullest extent, precisely to show wherein lay their excellence in carrying on and fulfilling their predecessors’ work. An earlier Confucian scholar said: “Shun represented the pinnacle of the human Way: ten thousand generations look up to him, unable to surpass him. The Zhou brought royal institutions to completeness: ten thousand generations follow them, unable to alter them.” Ah! Surely he deeply understood the sages!

“There has never been a righteous man who put his ruler last.”
By Zheng Yuanshao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Righteousness necessarily makes service to the ruler an urgent priority. This explains, in terms of one’s innate moral endowment, what one cannot desist from doing. This composition exhaustively expresses it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The language is rigorous and the meaning correct. An outstanding exposition of the meaning of Mencius [?]; it should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It elaborates how loyalty and righteousness are not two separate ways. The writing amply displays the force of his brush. A fine scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: “Closely pertinent and rich in meaning.”

The great worthy declared unequivocally that one who cherishes righteousness must be capable of loyalty to his ruler. When righteousness guides the practice of loyalty, loyalty is rooted in human nature. Could one possibly claim that someone who cherishes righteousness might yet be disloyal to his ruler? Here we see that righteousness brings benefit, and that a ruler of men should carefully examine what he esteems. Such was Mencius’s intention in enlightening King Hui. His point was this: nothing brings intentions into greater accord than communication between those above and those below; nothing takes precedence in government over distinguishing righteousness from profit. When I say that Your Majesty need only have benevolence and righteousness, could it be that…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
誠無利於上而言乎彼仁不遺親仁之利也而
於義亦有焉蓋義也者本諸心則爲敬敬君敬
之大者也裁之事則爲宜事君事之急者也人
惟大義之不明是故不知大者之爲急容有之
矣苟使忠愛之誠根於天性而以之效職也必
知尊主之爲恭篤棐之念切於由衷而以之從
上也必知體國之爲急責之所在身先殉之爲
任不同而同於精白以承德者固其情之不能
自已者也事之所在身先任之爲分不同而同
===
於夙夜以在公者固其職之不容自懈者也蓋
未有君臣之義無所逃於天地者既洞然決擇
於我矣而於公私之際所當辨其上下者乃漠
然不加之意焉忘國家之急以自便其私圖計
利害之私而罔先乎國是是後君矣是不知制
命之義矣則不忠莫大乎是而謂義者有之乎
是知義以爲忠未有忠而不激於義者忠由乎
義未有義而不永其忠者此性之所不已而亦
事之所以相成也人患不明乎義耳而患不忠
punctuated:
誠無利於上而言乎？彼仁不遺親，仁之利也，而於義亦有焉。蓋義也者，本諸心則爲敬，敬君，敬之大者也；裁之事則爲宜，事君，事之急者也。人惟大義之不明，是故不知大者之爲急，容有之矣。苟使忠愛之誠根於天性，而以之效職也，必知尊主之爲恭；篤棐之念切於由衷，而以之從上也，必知體國之爲急。責之所在，身先殉之，爲任不同，而同於精白以承德者，固其情之不能自已者也；事之所在，身先任之，爲分不同，而同於夙夜以在公者，固其職之不容自懈者也。
蓋未有君臣之義無所逃於天地者，既洞然決擇於我矣，而於公私之際所當辨其上下者，乃漠然不加之意焉。忘國家之急以自便其私，圖計利害之私而罔先乎國是，是後君矣，是不知制命之義矣。則不忠莫大乎是，而謂義者有之乎？是知義以爲忠，未有忠而不激於義者；忠由乎義，未有義而不永其忠者。此性之所不已，而亦事之所以相成也。人患不明乎義耳，而患不忠
translation_en:
…could I truly have said this because it brings no benefit to those above? That the benevolent do not forsake their parents is the benefit of benevolence; righteousness likewise has its benefits. Rooted in the heart, righteousness becomes reverence, and revering one’s ruler is the greatest expression of reverence. Applied to affairs, it becomes fitting conduct, and serving one’s ruler is the most urgent of affairs. Only because people fail to understand this great righteousness can they fail to recognize that what is greatest is also most urgent. If sincere loyalty and love are rooted in one’s Heaven-given nature and brought to the performance of one’s duties, one will surely understand that honoring the ruler constitutes respect. If the resolve to give devoted assistance comes earnestly from the heart and guides one in obeying superiors, one will surely understand that attending to the state’s concerns is urgent. Wherever responsibility lies, one takes the lead in devoting oneself to it, even at the cost of one’s life. Though their responsibilities differ, all alike receive their ruler’s beneficence with pure sincerity: their feelings cannot allow them to do otherwise. Wherever there is work to be done, one takes the lead in undertaking it. Though their allotted duties differ, all alike attend to public service morning and night: their offices do not permit them to slacken their efforts.
Surely no one, having clearly discerned and chosen for himself the righteousness binding ruler and minister—a bond from which there is no escape anywhere between Heaven and earth—could then remain indifferent to the precedence that must be distinguished at the boundary between public and private interests. To forget the state’s urgent needs for one’s own private convenience, calculating personal gains and losses without putting affairs of state first, is to place the ruler second. It is to fail to understand the righteous obligation governing the commitment of one’s life [?]. No disloyalty could be greater: could one say that a righteous person would act thus? Thus we know that righteousness gives rise to loyalty: no loyalty is unstirred by righteousness. Loyalty proceeds from righteousness: no righteousness fails to make loyalty enduring. This is the ceaseless working of human nature, and also the way these qualities complete one another in practice. What people should worry about is merely their failure to understand righteousness; why worry about disloyalty …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉噫於此可以見義之爲利矣於此可以見君
當躬行乎義以爲之倡矣抑義利之辨王伯之
分也孟子之在戰國急於明道術以正人心者
而於仁義亦以利言何耶蓋時方功利入人不
有以正之則其機溺而不返不因而誘之則其
志沮而未信利在君親救時之微意也要之行
之以誠抑孰非王道哉故曰仁義固所以利之
又曰王道本於誠意噫合而觀之則得矣
易
===
夫大人者與天地合其德
鄭元韶
同考試官敎諭蔣批發揮天地合德之旨殆
無餘蘊蓋深於易者
同考試官敎諭黎批雄深雅健讀其文不覺
蹶然起敬
考試官敎諭趙批說合德處最盡
考試官學正寇批爾雅可愛
文言賛聖德之至協諸天地者也夫天地至大
punctuated:
哉？噫！於此可以見義之爲利矣，於此可以見君當躬行乎義以爲之倡矣。抑義利之辨，王伯之分也。孟子之在戰國，急於明道術以正人心者，而於仁義亦以利言，何耶？蓋時方功利入人，不有以正之，則其機溺而不返；不因而誘之，則其志沮而未信。利在君親，救時之微意也。要之，行之以誠，抑孰非王道哉？故曰：「仁義固所以利之。」又曰：「王道本於誠意。」噫！合而觀之，則得矣。

易

夫大人者，與天地合其德。

鄭元韶

同考試官敎諭蔣批：發揮天地合德之旨，殆無餘蘊，蓋深於易者。

同考試官敎諭黎批：雄深雅健，讀其文，不覺蹶然起敬。

考試官敎諭趙批：說合德處最盡。

考試官學正寇批：爾雅可愛。

文言賛聖德之至，協諸天地者也。夫天地至大
translation_en:
…need one fear disloyalty? Ah! Here we can see that righteousness brings benefit; here we can see that the ruler should personally practice righteousness to set an example. Yet the distinction between righteousness and profit is the dividing line between true kingship and hegemony. During the Warring States period, Mencius urgently sought to clarify the Way and its methods so as to rectify people’s hearts. Why, then, did he also speak of benevolence and righteousness in terms of benefit? At that time, the pursuit of achievement and profit was taking hold of people. Without something to correct them, their impulses would sink into it beyond recovery; without using those impulses to guide them, their resolve would falter and they would remain unconvinced. To locate benefit in serving one’s ruler and parents expressed his subtle intention to remedy the troubles of the age. Ultimately, when practiced with sincerity, what among these would not be the kingly Way? Thus it is said, “Benevolence and righteousness are indeed the means of benefiting them.” It is also said, “The kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere.” Ah! Consider these together, and their meaning becomes clear.

Book of Changes

“As for the great man, his virtue accords with that of Heaven and Earth.”

Zheng Yuanshao

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: His exposition of the meaning of virtue according with Heaven and Earth leaves almost nothing unexplored. He is evidently deeply versed in the Book of Changes.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Powerful, profound, elegant, and vigorous. Reading his writing, one cannot help being suddenly stirred to respect.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: His explanation of how virtue accords with Heaven and Earth is exceptionally thorough.

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: Refined and pleasing.

The Commentary on the Words and Phrases praises the perfection of the sage’s virtue, which accords with Heaven and Earth. Now Heaven and Earth are supremely great…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也而聖德同之德斯至矣其爲物所利見也宜
哉文言申乾九五爻義如此今夫道必體而後
可與語天德之純德必至而後可以建天下之
極然則其惟九五之大人乎剛健中正其心純
矣而太極之全體不虧基命宥密其敬至矣而
天命之本眞不鑿存神以立本則廓然而大公
者无非天地之心也知化以達用則物來而順
應者无非天地之事也是天地生人之理其在
大人也既兼體而不遺則大人造德之純其於
===
天地也自配合而无間大生廣生德固至矣而
无私者其本也大人无私則帝德之廣運有以
協上下以同流誠通誠復德云大矣而无私者
其運也大人无私則至德之淵微有以參兩儀
而並運以其在天地者而視之乎聖人焉則命
之所以不已者即誠之所以不息也蓋不可以
形器觀矣以其在聖人者而配之乎天地焉則
情順萬事而无情者即心普萬物而无心者也
又可以彼此論耶是何也道之一也衆人梏於
punctuated: 也，而聖德同之，德斯至矣，其爲物所利見也宜哉！文言申乾九五爻義如此。今夫道必體而後可與語天德之純，德必至而後可以建天下之極。然則其惟九五之大人乎？剛健中正，其心純矣，而太極之全體不虧；基命宥密，其敬至矣，而天命之本眞不鑿。存神以立本，則廓然而大公者，无非天地之心也；知化以達用，則物來而順應者，无非天地之事也。是天地生人之理，其在大人也，既兼體而不遺，則大人造德之純，其於天地也，自配合而无間。大生廣生，德固至矣，而无私者其本也。大人无私，則帝德之廣運，有以協上下以同流。誠通誠復，德云大矣，而无私者其運也。大人无私，則至德之淵微，有以參兩儀而並運。以其在天地者而視之乎聖人焉，則命之所以不已者，即誠之所以不息也，蓋不可以形器觀矣。以其在聖人者而配之乎天地焉，則情順萬事而无情者，即心普萬物而无心者也，又可以彼此論耶？是何也？道之一也。衆人梏於
translation_en:
…yet the sage’s virtue accords with it: his virtue has thus reached its utmost perfection. How fitting that beings should benefit from seeing him! Such is the way the Commentary on the Words (Wenyan) elaborates the meaning of the nine in the fifth place of the Qian hexagram. Now, only after embodying the Way can one speak of the purity of Heaven’s virtue; only after bringing virtue to perfection can one establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. Is this not precisely the great man of the nine in the fifth place? Firm and vigorous, central and correct, his mind is pure, and the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate remains unimpaired. Establishing the Mandate in profound stillness, his reverence is consummate, and the original authenticity of Heaven’s Mandate remains unaltered by artifice. By preserving the spiritual to establish the foundation, his expansive and utterly impartial disposition is wholly the mind of Heaven and Earth. By understanding transformation to realize its operation, his fitting responses to things as they come are wholly the affairs of Heaven and Earth. Since the great man fully embodies, without omission, the principle by which Heaven and Earth generate human beings, the purity of the virtue he has attained naturally accords with Heaven and Earth without any separation.

In their great and far-reaching generation of things, their virtue is indeed consummate, and selflessness is its foundation. The great man is selfless; thus the far-reaching operation of his sovereign virtue enables him to accord with what is above and below and flow together with them. In sincerity’s outward passage and return, virtue may be called great, and selflessness is its operation. The great man is selfless; thus the profound subtlety of his consummate virtue enables him to form a triad with the Two Powers, Heaven and Earth, and operate alongside them. If we take what is present in Heaven and Earth and consider it in the sage, that by which the Mandate continues without cease is precisely that by which sincerity never rests. Surely this cannot be viewed in terms of physical forms and concrete objects. If we take what is present in the sage and match it with Heaven and Earth, his feelings’ accommodation to every affair without partial feeling is precisely their mind’s encompassing all things without a partial mind. How, then, can one speak of them as separate? Why is this so? Because the Way is one. Ordinary people are shackled by…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
有我而不能相通是以見其異聖人體之至公
而无所間隔是以見其同要之豈誠出於斯道
之外而强合也哉是則德之純也旣參天地而
不違則聖之作也宜乎其繼天地以立極矣物
所利見夫豈无自也哉雖然聖人豈惟合德天
地而已其彌綸參贊之妙實則範圍之以成其
能是天地之位萬物之育皆不能无待於聖人
者然則聖人之功之德其可易易言耶是故觀
合德而可以得聖德之純觀位育而可以得聖
===
功之極
百官以治萬民以察
楊珂
同考試官教諭蔣 批 說出聖人書契之利且
文意詳整易義之優者未能先於子矣
同考試官教諭黎 批 其旨遠其辭文非有得
於同文之妙者不能到此
考試官教諭趙 批 精潔渾成
考試官學正寇 批 治察是如此說
punctuated:
有我而不能相通，是以見其異；聖人體之至公，而无所間隔，是以見其同。要之，豈誠出於斯道之外而强合也哉？是則德之純也。旣參天地而不違，則聖之作也，宜乎其繼天地以立極矣。物所利見，夫豈无自也哉？雖然，聖人豈惟合德天地而已？其彌綸參贊之妙，實則範圍之以成其能。是天地之位、萬物之育，皆不能无待於聖人者。然則聖人之功之德，其可易易言耶？是故觀合德，而可以得聖德之純；觀位育，而可以得聖功之極。
百官以治，萬民以察。
楊珂
同考試官教諭蔣批：說出聖人書契之利，且文意詳整，易義之優者未能先於子矣。
同考試官教諭黎批：其旨遠，其辭文，非有得於同文之妙者不能到此。
考試官教諭趙批：精潔渾成。
考試官學正寇批：治察是如此說。
translation_en:
…by attachment to the self and thus unable to communicate with one another, they perceive differences. The sage embodies the Way with perfect impartiality, with nothing intervening or separating, and thus perceives unity. Ultimately, could sincerity stand outside this Way and be forcibly joined to it? This, then, is the purity of virtue. Since the sage participates with Heaven and Earth without departing from them, it is fitting that his activity should carry on their work and establish the supreme standard. How could the benefit that all beings derive from beholding him be without a source? Yet does the sage merely unite his virtue with Heaven and Earth? Through the wondrous workings by which he encompasses all things and assists their transformation, he gives them order and fulfills their capacities. Thus Heaven and Earth taking their proper places, and the myriad things receiving their nourishment, all depend upon the sage. Can the sage’s achievement and virtue, then, be spoken of lightly? By observing his union in virtue with Heaven and Earth, one can apprehend the purity of sagely virtue; by observing their proper positioning and the nourishment of things, one can apprehend the utmost extent of sagely achievement.

“Through this the hundred officials are governed, and the myriad people are scrutinized.”

Yang Ke

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “You bring out the benefits of the sage’s introduction of writing and written contracts. Moreover, the essay’s ideas are fully developed and well ordered. Even the finest essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes cannot surpass yours.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Its purport is far-reaching, its language refined. No one who had not grasped the subtle workings of a common written language could attain this.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Precise and clean, seamlessly composed.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: “This is how ‘governed’ and ‘scrutinized’ should be explained.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖人同文之化而有以徵諸臣民焉夫臣職脩
而民志定是固合同而化矣自非聖人通變而
考之以文其孰能與於此今夫聖人不先天以
開人每因時而立政其以書契易結繩者豈不
欲與天下相安於无事而爲是更變哉時之所
會有不能違耳是故布列庶位而佐王以出治
者有百官焉罔不欲其各脩其職也但風教日
移相沿而飾治者亦多矣復可以上古之簡例
之乎惟書契有作則紀法定而旌别之義昭功
===
罪明而勸懲之典著庶寮之肅遵王度也有位
之儆守官箴也君執要以馭臣而臣明徵以脩
職朝無倖位揖讓之風行矣百官有弗治乎百
官治是上焉者誠於書契焉有賴矣至於生聚
萬方而遵王以會極者有萬民焉罔不欲其各
得其情也但風會日流相率而爲偽者亦衆矣
復可以上古之淳待之乎惟書契有作則綜覈
詳於約劑之明簡稽得於品式之具以登民數
則多寡有程也以察民故則是非有辨也君脩
punctuated: 聖人同文之化，而有以徵諸臣民焉。夫臣職脩而民志定，是固合同而化矣。自非聖人通變而考之以文，其孰能與於此？今夫聖人不先天以開人，每因時而立政。其以書契易結繩者，豈不欲與天下相安於无事而爲是更變哉？時之所會，有不能違耳。是故布列庶位而佐王以出治者，有百官焉，罔不欲其各脩其職也。但風教日移，相沿而飾治者亦多矣，復可以上古之簡例之乎？惟書契有作，則紀法定而旌别之義昭，功罪明而勸懲之典著。庶寮之肅遵王度也，有位之儆守官箴也，君執要以馭臣，而臣明徵以脩職，朝無倖位，揖讓之風行矣。百官有弗治乎？百官治，是上焉者誠於書契焉有賴矣。至於生聚萬方而遵王以會極者，有萬民焉，罔不欲其各得其情也。但風會日流，相率而爲偽者亦衆矣，復可以上古之淳待之乎？惟書契有作，則綜覈詳於約劑之明，簡稽得於品式之具。以登民數，則多寡有程也；以察民故，則是非有辨也。君脩
translation_en:
…The sage’s transforming influence in unifying writing can thus be verified among his ministers and people. When ministers discharge their duties and the people’s minds are settled, this indeed constitutes unity and transformation. Unless the sage comprehended changing circumstances and established standards through writing, who could have achieved this? The sage does not anticipate Heaven in enlightening the people, but always establishes government in accordance with the times. In replacing knotted cords with written documents, was he not making this change because he wished to enjoy peace and freedom from trouble together with all under Heaven? What the times bring about simply cannot be resisted.

Thus there are the hundred officials, arrayed in their various posts, who assist the king in carrying out government; he wishes every one of them to discharge his duties. Yet as customs and moral instruction change daily, many follow established practices merely to give an appearance of good government. Can they still be judged by the simplicity of high antiquity? Once written documents are instituted, regulations and laws are fixed, and the principles for recognizing and distinguishing officials become clear; merits and offenses are made evident, and the rules for encouragement and punishment become manifest. The various officials reverently observe royal standards, and those holding office vigilantly abide by official admonitions. The ruler grasps the essentials by which to govern his ministers, while the ministers make the evidence clear in discharging their duties. At court, no one holds a post through undeserved favor, and a spirit of deference prevails. Could any of the hundred officials fail to be well governed? That the hundred officials are well governed shows that those above do indeed depend upon written documents.

As for those who live and multiply throughout the realm and follow the king in uniting around the supreme standard, these are the myriad people; he wishes the true circumstances of every one of them to be duly recognized. Yet as prevailing customs shift daily, many follow one another into deceit. Can they still be treated with the trust appropriate to the simplicity of high antiquity? Once written documents are instituted, comprehensive scrutiny becomes thorough through clearly drawn contracts, and inspection and verification become possible through fully specified classifications and forms. When these are used to register the population, its numbers have a definite measure; when they are used to investigate the people’s affairs, right and wrong can be distinguished. The ruler cultivates…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
文以立極而民遵道以作乂比屋可封於變之
化成矣萬民有弗察乎萬民察是下焉者亦於
書契焉有賴矣是則書契一易而百官萬民罔
不賴之以順治聖人通變考文之功何其大哉
抑邃古之風遠矣後世疑心志而信耳目疑耳
目而信簡書法愈煩民愈詐而書契適足以滋
偽而聖人之心至是亦戚矣然則若之何而可
曰捄詐存乎朴御物存乎誠然則通變宜民之
術又當得諸書契之外而後可
===
書
凡厥庶民有猷有為有守汝則念之不協
于極不罹于咎皇則受之而康而色曰
予攸好德汝則錫之福時人斯其惟皇
之極
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批箕子演極之意模寫殆
盡當是作手
同考試官學正龍批造詞精切且正大典則
punctuated:
文以立極，而民遵道以作乂，比屋可封，於變之化成矣。萬民有弗察乎？萬民察，是下焉者亦於書契焉有賴矣。是則書契一易，而百官萬民罔不賴之以順治，聖人通變考文之功何其大哉！抑邃古之風遠矣，後世疑心志而信耳目，疑耳目而信簡書，法愈煩，民愈詐，而書契適足以滋偽，而聖人之心至是亦戚矣。然則若之何而可？曰：「捄詐存乎朴，御物存乎誠。」然則通變宜民之術，又當得諸書契之外而後可。

書
凡厥庶民，有猷、有為、有守，汝則念之。不協于極，不罹于咎，皇則受之。而康而色，曰：「予攸好德。」汝則錫之福，時人斯其惟皇之極。

黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批：「箕子演極之意，模寫殆盡，當是作手。」
同考試官學正龍批：「造詞精切，且正大典則。」
translation_en:
…cultural forms to establish the supreme standard, while the people follow the Way and bring about good order. Every household becomes worthy of enfeoffment, and the transforming influence that changes the people is fulfilled. Could any of the myriad people remain beyond scrutiny? When all are scrutinized, those below likewise have written documents to thank. Thus, once written documents were adopted as a change, the hundred officials and the myriad people all relied on them to achieve orderly government. How great was the sages’ achievement in adapting to change and establishing standards of writing!

Yet the customs of remote antiquity have long vanished. In later ages, people distrusted intentions and trusted what they heard and saw; then they distrusted what they heard and saw and trusted written records. The more elaborate the laws became, the more deceitful the people grew, so that written documents served only to multiply falsehood. At this, even the hearts of the sages would grieve. What, then, should be done? The answer is: “The remedy for deceit lies in simplicity; the governance of affairs lies in sincerity.” Thus, the art of adapting to change for the people’s benefit must also be sought beyond written documents before it can succeed.

Book of Documents
“Among the common people, those who have plans, accomplishments, or steadfast principles—you should keep them in mind. Those who do not conform to the supreme standard but have not incurred blame—the sovereign should receive them. Compose your countenance. If they say, ‘What I love is virtue,’ you should bestow blessings upon them. Such people will then turn to the sovereign’s supreme standard.”

Huang Shiguan
Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: “He has reproduced almost fully the meaning of Jizi’s exposition of the supreme standard. Surely an accomplished writer.”

Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor, comments: “His phrasing is precise and apt, and also upright, dignified, and in keeping with classical models…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
可以爲式矣
考試官教諭趙批平實之文
考試官學正寇批整潔可誦
王者務成人以善則天下之善成矣蓋天下之
才不皆善而所賴以成之者君也苟能成之而
不已焉民其有不協於極哉箕子演皇極之疇
以告武王及此若曰王旣建極以端天下之本
矣而納民於極當何如哉誠以天之生才難矣
庶民之中不可以語成德也然亦有精於方物
===
者焉有優於幹理者焉有秉執不撓者焉此則
質之可以語上者也王其存而念之咸造之以
錫類之仁又有弗協於休復之吉亦不淪於迷
復之凶者焉此則行之可導而上下者也王其
矜而受之亦成之以容保之度苟斯人也果能
感慕以圖成進修以無倦觀其色粹乎其安和
也聽其言確乎其好德也此其志專矣然未協
於克一也王豈惟念受而已哉必也福以勸之
或旌其賢也有匪頒之典或馭其幸也有賚予
punctuated:
可以爲式矣。
考試官教諭趙批：平實之文。
考試官學正寇批：整潔可誦。
王者務成人以善，則天下之善成矣。蓋天下之才不皆善，而所賴以成之者君也。苟能成之而不已焉，民其有不協於極哉？箕子演皇極之疇以告武王，及此若曰：王旣建極以端天下之本矣，而納民於極當何如哉？誠以天之生才難矣，庶民之中，不可以語成德也。然亦有精於方物者焉，有優於幹理者焉，有秉執不撓者焉，此則質之可以語上者也。王其存而念之，咸造之以錫類之仁。又有弗協於休復之吉，亦不淪於迷復之凶者焉，此則行之可導而上下者也。王其矜而受之，亦成之以容保之度。苟斯人也，果能感慕以圖成，進修以無倦，觀其色，粹乎其安和也；聽其言，確乎其好德也。此其志專矣，然未協於克一也。王豈惟念受而已哉？必也福以勸之，或旌其賢也，有匪頒之典；或馭其幸也，有賚予
translation_en:
…It may serve as a model.
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: A plain and substantial composition.
Examiner Kou, School Instructor, comments: Orderly and polished, worthy of recitation.
When a king strives to bring people to fulfillment through goodness, the goodness of all under Heaven is brought to fulfillment. For the talents of all under Heaven are not uniformly good; it is upon their ruler that people depend to bring them to fulfillment. If he can accomplish this without ceasing, will any among the people fail to accord with the supreme standard? When Jizi expounded the section on the Royal Ultimate to King Wu, at this point it was as though he said: The king has already established the supreme standard to set right the foundation of all under Heaven. But how should he bring the people into accord with that standard?
Truly, Heaven does not readily produce people of talent. Among the common people, one cannot speak of perfected virtue. Yet there are those skilled in discerning things, those adept at managing affairs, and those who hold firmly to their principles without yielding. These are people whose native qualities admit of higher attainments. Let the king keep them in mind and attend to them, bringing them all to fulfillment through a benevolence that extends blessings to their kind. There are also those who do not accord with the good fortune of an auspicious return, yet do not sink into the ill fortune of a misguided return. These are people whose conduct can be guided upward or downward. Let the king show them compassion and receive them, likewise bringing them to fulfillment through his capacity to embrace and protect them.
If such people can indeed be moved to admiration and aspire to fulfillment, advancing in self-cultivation without weariness, then, when one observes their countenances, their composure and harmony are unalloyed; when one listens to their words, their love of virtue is assured. Their resolve is now single-minded, yet they have not attained constancy in it. How could the king merely attend to them and receive them? He must encourage them with blessings. To honor their worthiness, there are prescribed distributions of gifts; or, to guide them through his favor [?], there are grants of rewards…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之施夫然則進善之機既發於其始而為善之
力又輕於其終吾見承王之錫者皆曰大君養
人以善也吾何為不善莫不益勵於王道之歸
焉泳王之化者皆曰王者域民以中吾何為不
中莫不益安於帝則之順焉夫以王者成人如
是其難用心如是其至以其為建極而代天也
王可不知所務哉抑箕子既以錫福告王矣下
文又曰凡厥正人既富方穀夫待教而善必賞
而後勸者中才也聖人之意豈不以豪傑待天
===
下歟蓋帝王之道必本於人情養而後善固理
之不可易者臣民之馭庸非所當先哉若夫自
修以協極者則固有本末耳夫知本則義義則
協極矣是故知協極之為義而後知錫福之為
仁
以敬事上帝立民長伯
陳道基
同考試官教諭馮批文武用三宅三俊而責
任之重於是作見之
punctuated:
之施。夫然，則進善之機既發於其始，而為善之力又輕於其終。吾見承王之錫者皆曰：「大君養人以善也，吾何為不善？」莫不益勵於王道之歸焉。泳王之化者皆曰：「王者域民以中，吾何為不中？」莫不益安於帝則之順焉。夫以王者成人如是其難，用心如是其至，以其為建極而代天也，王可不知所務哉？抑箕子既以錫福告王矣，下文又曰：「凡厥正人，既富方穀。」夫待教而善、必賞而後勸者，中才也。聖人之意，豈不以豪傑待天下歟？蓋帝王之道，必本於人情；養而後善，固理之不可易者。臣民之馭，庸非所當先哉？若夫自修以協極者，則固有本末耳。夫知本則義，義則協極矣。是故知協極之為義，而後知錫福之為仁。
以敬事上帝，立民長伯。
陳道基。
同考試官教諭馮批：「文武用三宅三俊，而責任之重，於是作見之。」
translation_en:
…the bestowal of gifts. Thus, once the impulse to advance toward goodness has been awakened at the outset, the effort required to practise goodness becomes lighter in the end. I see that all who receive the king’s gifts say, “The great sovereign nurtures people through goodness. Why should I fail to be good?” All become still more earnest in turning toward the kingly Way. Those immersed in the king’s transforming influence all say, “The king guides the people within the bounds of the mean. Why should I fail to accord with the mean?” All become still more at ease in following Heaven’s standard. The difficulty with which a king brings people to fulfilment, and the utmost care he devotes to it, arise from his establishing the supreme standard and acting on Heaven’s behalf. Can the king fail to understand what he must attend to?
Moreover, after Jizi had instructed the king about bestowing blessings, the text goes on to say, “As for all your upright men, once enriched, they will become good.” Those who await instruction before becoming good, and must receive rewards before being encouraged, are people of middling ability. Could the sage’s intention have been anything other than to treat the people of the realm as men of outstanding capacity? Yet the Way of emperors and kings must be rooted in human feelings. That people become good after being nurtured is indeed an unalterable principle. In governing subjects and people, should this not take priority? As for those who cultivate themselves to accord with the supreme standard, there are certainly roots and branches to their endeavour. Understanding the root leads to righteousness, and righteousness brings accord with the supreme standard. Thus, only after understanding that according with the supreme standard constitutes righteousness does one understand that bestowing blessings constitutes benevolence.
“Thereby reverently to serve the Lord on High and establish leaders and chiefs for the people.”
Chen Daoji.
Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “Kings Wen and Wu employed the holders of the three offices and the three groups of outstanding men; the weight of the responsibilities entrusted to them is here brought out [?].”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正龍批叙敬事立民有許多曲
折意思
考試官教諭趙批詞理詳盡可取
考試官學正寇批意足詞暢
二聖於宅俊之賢而以天人之任責之焉夫人
君事天治民任莫有重焉者也而皆於宅俊兼
之文武任人之專為何如哉昔周公以知恤之
道啓成王及此意謂天下之治天下之賢為之
也知之既真固可以語推心之誠而任之不重
===
又豈足以盡其用哉文武之於宅俊也蓋盡任
使之道者矣何也人君為天之宗子仰有事天
之道然而一日萬幾豈能獨事也惟以宅俊之
賢與天合德者也于是用以敬事上帝焉或因
其道而裁成也夙夜惟寅以盡夫彌綸參賛之
務或因其宜而輔相也朝夕有恪式竭夫左右
宣力之勞承天以理事而敬以凝庶績也承天
以守法而敬以清刑獄也承天以子民而敬以
助康和也天道不言而成化臣道無成以代終
punctuated:
同考試官學正龍批：叙敬事立民，有許多曲折意思。
考試官教諭趙批：詞理詳盡，可取。
考試官學正寇批：意足詞暢。

二聖於宅俊之賢，而以天人之任責之焉。夫人君事天治民，任莫有重焉者也，而皆於宅俊兼之。文武任人之專，為何如哉！昔周公以知恤之道啓成王，及此，意謂天下之治，天下之賢為之也。知之既真，固可以語推心之誠，而任之不重，又豈足以盡其用哉？文武之於宅俊也，蓋盡任使之道者矣。何也？人君為天之宗子，仰有事天之道，然而一日萬幾，豈能獨事也？惟以宅俊之賢，與天合德者也，于是用以敬事上帝焉。或因其道而裁成也，夙夜惟寅，以盡夫彌綸參賛之務；或因其宜而輔相也，朝夕有恪，式竭夫左右宣力之勞。承天以理事，而敬以凝庶績也；承天以守法，而敬以清刑獄也；承天以子民，而敬以助康和也。天道不言而成化，臣道無成以代終。
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor, comments: “The exposition of reverently serving Heaven and establishing leaders for the people contains many subtle turns of thought.”
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “The wording and reasoning are thorough and merit acceptance.”
Examiner Kou, School Instructor, comments: “The ideas are fully developed and the language flows freely.”

The two sage kings entrusted the worthy men whom they placed in office with responsibilities toward both Heaven and the people. For a ruler, no responsibilities are weightier than serving Heaven and governing the people; yet both were combined in the charge given to these appointed worthies. How complete was the trust with which Kings Wen and Wu employed men! Long ago, when the Duke of Zhou instructed King Cheng in the way of understanding what should concern him, he touched upon this point. His meaning was that the governance of All under Heaven is accomplished by the worthy men of All under Heaven. Once a ruler truly understands this, one may indeed speak of his sincerity in giving them his wholehearted trust. Yet unless he entrusts them with weighty responsibilities, how can he make full use of their abilities? In their treatment of the worthies they appointed, Wen and Wu fully realized the proper way of entrusting duties and employing men. Why was this so? As Heaven’s principal son, the ruler has, above him, the duty of serving Heaven. Yet with myriad affairs arising in a single day, how could he perform this service alone? It was precisely because the worthies they appointed possessed virtue in accord with Heaven that they employed them to serve the Lord on High reverently. Some followed Heaven’s Way and brought its workings to proper fulfillment, remaining reverent day and night to discharge fully the task of ordering all things and assisting Heaven’s transforming work. Others provided assistance in accordance with what was fitting, remaining respectful morning and evening and exerting themselves to the utmost in service at their ruler’s side. Upholding Heaven’s will in managing affairs, they reverently brought all achievements to completion; upholding Heaven’s will in maintaining the laws, they reverently ensured clarity and justice in punishments and legal proceedings; upholding Heaven’s will in caring for the people as their children, they reverently promoted peace and harmony. Heaven’s Way accomplishes transformation without speaking; the way of a minister is to claim no achievement as his own, but to bring the work to completion on another’s behalf…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
天工亮而帝載熈文武代天理物之責始可以
無愧矣人君爲民之父母俯有治人之道然而
惟惠之懷不能以獨治也惟以宅俊之賢宜于
人民者也于是用以立民長伯焉位乎民極也
提綱挈領以成天下之務處乎具瞻也統宗會
元以安天下之民理事以先天下而期無叢脞
也守法以先天下而期無寃民也子民以先天
下而期無弊俗也宅俊妙倡率之機天下被咸
和之澤下民協而萬邦休文武宅中圖治之責
===
始可以無歉矣夫以一宅俊之任而道極於天
人功光於上下此文武所以開我周有道之長
也王其知所法哉抑論知人則哲惟帝其難此
周公告成王知恤之道大旣以夏商告之矣而
復懇懇以文武爲言無非欲其遠稽近述以盡
道也厥後成王果得之周官之訓精微蘊奥著
於言辭禮樂文章形於訓誥然則成王果知恤
乎先儒有言純心要矣用賢急焉抑以是而知
成王之能純心
punctuated:
天工亮而帝載熈，文武代天理物之責始可以無愧矣。人君爲民之父母，俯有治人之道，然而惟惠之懷，不能以獨治也。惟以宅俊之賢，宜于人民者也，于是用以立民長伯焉。位乎民極也，提綱挈領以成天下之務；處乎具瞻也，統宗會元以安天下之民。理事以先天下而期無叢脞也，守法以先天下而期無寃民也，子民以先天下而期無弊俗也。宅俊妙倡率之機，天下被咸和之澤，下民協而萬邦休，文武宅中圖治之責始可以無歉矣。
夫以一宅俊之任，而道極於天人，功光於上下，此文武所以開我周有道之長也。王其知所法哉！抑論知人則哲，惟帝其難。此周公告成王知恤之道，大旣以夏商告之矣，而復懇懇以文武爲言，無非欲其遠稽近述以盡道也。厥後成王果得之，《周官》之訓，精微蘊奥著於言辭，禮樂文章形於訓誥。然則成王果知恤乎？先儒有言：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」抑以是而知成王之能純心。
translation_en:
…Heaven’s work is accomplished and the sovereign’s undertakings flourish; only then can Kings Wen and Wu discharge without shame their responsibility to order all things on Heaven’s behalf. The ruler is father and mother to the people, and in looking down upon them has a Way by which to govern them. Yet, though he cherishes benevolence, he cannot govern alone. It is precisely because the worthy men whom he appoints are suited to serving the people that he establishes them as the people’s leaders. Standing as the people’s standard, they grasp the guiding principles and essential points to accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. Occupying positions to which all look up, they bring together the governing principles and fundamental purposes to secure the people’s peace. They take the lead throughout the realm in managing affairs, seeking to prevent confusion over petty details; they take the lead in upholding the laws, seeking to ensure that no one suffers injustice; and they take the lead in caring for the people as their children, seeking to eliminate corrupt customs. Appointing eminent men brings the workings of leadership to perfection, and all under Heaven receive the blessings of universal harmony. The common people live in concord and the myriad states enjoy well-being. Only then can Kings Wen and Wu discharge without regret their responsibility to occupy the center and devise good government.
Through the single responsibility of appointing eminent men, the Way reaches its utmost realization in Heaven and humanity, and achievements shine above and below. This is how Kings Wen and Wu inaugurated the long succession of our Zhou’s possession of the Way. May the king recognize what he should emulate! Yet, as for the saying that to know men is wisdom, even the sage emperor found this difficult. Here the Duke of Zhou was telling King Cheng how to understand what he must be concerned about. Having already instructed him broadly through the examples of Xia and Shang, he again spoke earnestly of Kings Wen and Wu. His sole purpose was to have the king examine distant precedents and follow recent ones, thereby fully realizing the Way. Subsequently, King Cheng did indeed grasp this. In the instructions entitled “Offices of Zhou” (Zhouguan), subtle insights and profound meanings are manifest in the language, while ritual, music, and the forms of civilized order find expression in the admonitions and proclamations. Did King Cheng, then, truly understand what he must be concerned about? An earlier Confucian scholar said: “Purifying the heart is essential; employing the worthy is urgent.” From this, indeed, we can recognize King Cheng’s ability to purify his heart.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
詩
參差荇菜左右采之窈窕淑女琴瑟友之
參差荇菜左右芼之窈窕淑女鍾鼓樂
之
丘行義
同考試官教諭費批簡而文典而雅詩人好
德之意正如此
同考試官教諭方批其意切其辭莊蓋一唱
三歎而有餘音焉
===
考試官教諭趙批得風人之旨
考試官學正寇批就性情上說來良是
詩人兩興既得聖配而深致夫好德之情焉蓋
莫難於聖配之得也宮人好之而無不用其情
焉有以哉關雎詩人於文王既得太姒而興言
之蓋曰參差乎荇菜也苟為吾筐筥之盛者必
左右以取之而一莖一葉咸為明信之需矣况
我淑女窈窕之德幸而見焉匪致吾之慇懃不
可也蓋必以琴瑟之在御者而是搏是拊於以
punctuated:
詩

參差荇菜，左右采之。窈窕淑女，琴瑟友之。參差荇菜，左右芼之。窈窕淑女，鍾鼓樂之。

丘行義

同考試官教諭費批：簡而文，典而雅，詩人好德之意正如此。

同考試官教諭方批：其意切，其辭莊，蓋一唱三歎而有餘音焉。

考試官教諭趙批：得風人之旨。

考試官學正寇批：就性情上說來，良是。

詩人兩興既得聖配，而深致夫好德之情焉。蓋莫難於聖配之得也，宮人好之而無不用其情焉，有以哉！關雎詩人於文王既得太姒而興言之，蓋曰：參差乎荇菜也，苟為吾筐筥之盛者，必左右以取之，而一莖一葉咸為明信之需矣。况我淑女窈窕之德，幸而見焉，匪致吾之慇懃不可也。蓋必以琴瑟之在御者，而是搏是拊，於以
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Uneven grows the water plantain; to left and right we gather it. The graceful, virtuous maiden—with qin and se zithers we befriend her. Uneven grows the water plantain; to left and right we select it. The graceful, virtuous maiden—with bells and drums we gladden her.”

Qiu Xingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: “Concise yet polished, classically grounded and elegant: precisely such is the poet’s intention in cherishing virtue.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “Its meaning is earnest and its language dignified. Like one singing phrase answered by three sighs of admiration, it leaves lingering echoes.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It captures the intent of the poet of the Airs.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: “To explain it in terms of innate nature and feelings is indeed right.”

Through two evocative comparisons, the poet speaks of having obtained a sage consort and gives profound expression to the feeling of cherishing virtue. Nothing, indeed, is harder than obtaining a sage consort. That the palace women cherish her and express their feelings to the utmost surely has its reason! Once King Wen had obtained Tai Si as his consort, the poet of ‘Guan ju’ (‘The Calling Ospreys’) voiced this through evocative comparison, saying in effect: Uneven grows the water plantain. If it is to fill our square and round baskets, we must gather it to left and right, so that every stem and every leaf may serve to manifest our sincerity. How much more, then, when we are fortunate enough to behold our virtuous maiden’s graceful virtue, must we express our devoted solicitude! We must take the qin and se zithers set ready for use and strike and pluck them, thereby to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
依炙而戀慕之庶同牢合卺之辰而聞此優柔
平中之奏亦爲之一慶焉豈以綢繆而爲瀆耶
參差乎荇菜也苟爲吾錡釡之湘者必無方以
薦之而或菹或茹咸爲馨香之助矣况我淑女
德之窈窕幸而見焉匪將吾之誠篤不可也又
必以鍾鼓之在懸者而載考載擊於以歡洽而
悅懌之庶洽陽渭涘之顧而聞此諧和雝肅之
音尤爲之一慰焉豈以繾綣而爲煩耶是何也
有不世之德如淑女以配聖人以成内治蓋願
===
於昔而酬於今鬱於前而舒於後者也一時喜
樂尊奉之極奚容已哉吁詩人可謂得於性情
之正矣大抵天下之化始於閨門而感人尤莫
速於德太姒之聖德能使宮人形於憂樂者如
此蓋已協天人之心備諸福之本矣由是而樛
木而螽斯而麟趾莫非德之徴應而王化昭焉
豈偶然哉及觀之易之坤則以代終爲訓噫此
其爲文王脩齊之明效而孔子取以冠乎詩也
歟
punctuated: 依炙而戀慕之，庶同牢合卺之辰，而聞此優柔平中之奏，亦爲之一慶焉，豈以綢繆而爲瀆耶？參差乎荇菜也，苟爲吾錡釡之湘者，必無方以薦之，而或菹或茹，咸爲馨香之助矣。况我淑女，德之窈窕，幸而見焉，匪將吾之誠篤不可也。又必以鍾鼓之在懸者，而載考載擊，於以歡洽而悅懌之，庶洽陽渭涘之顧，而聞此諧和雝肅之音，尤爲之一慰焉，豈以繾綣而爲煩耶？是何也？有不世之德如淑女，以配聖人，以成内治，蓋願於昔而酬於今，鬱於前而舒於後者也。一時喜樂尊奉之極，奚容已哉！吁！詩人可謂得於性情之正矣。大抵天下之化始於閨門，而感人尤莫速於德。太姒之聖德，能使宮人形於憂樂者如此，蓋已協天人之心，備諸福之本矣。由是而《樛木》，而《螽斯》，而《麟趾》，莫非德之徴應，而王化昭焉，豈偶然哉？及觀之《易》之《坤》，則以代終爲訓。噫！此其爲文王脩齊之明效，而孔子取以冠乎《詩》也歟！
translation_en:
…to draw close to her [?] and express their affectionate admiration, hoping that, on the day when the bridal couple share the sacrificial meat and drink from paired gourd cups, hearing this gentle, balanced music will give her further cause for celebration. How could such loving attentiveness be considered disrespectful?

Uneven in length are the water plants! If they are to be cooked in our tripods and cauldrons, we must employ every means to present them; whether pickled or cooked as vegetables, all contribute their fragrance. How much more, then, when we are fortunate enough to behold our virtuous lady, whose virtue is so retiring and refined: we cannot fail to offer our sincere devotion. We must also sound and strike the suspended bells and drums, expressing our joy and delight in her. We hope that, when she comes from the southern bank of the Qia and the banks of the Wei, hearing these harmonious, solemn sounds will give her still greater comfort. How could such devoted affection be considered troublesome?

Why is this so? A virtuous lady possessed of virtue rarely seen in any age has become the sage’s consort and perfected the governance of the inner quarters. What was wished for in the past is fulfilled today; feelings once pent up can now find release. How could the utmost joy and reverence of that moment possibly be restrained? Ah! The poet may truly be said to have attained correctness in human nature and feeling.

The moral transformation of the world generally begins within the household, and nothing moves people more swiftly than virtue. That the sagely virtue of Tai Si could bring the palace women’s sorrow and joy to expression in this way shows that she had already accorded with the hearts of Heaven and humankind and established the foundation of every blessing. Hence the poems “Drooping Trees,” “Locusts,” and “The Qilin’s Hoof”: all are manifestations answering to virtue, through which the king’s transforming influence becomes evident. Could this be mere coincidence?

When we turn to the Kun hexagram in the Book of Changes, its teaching is to bring matters to completion on another’s behalf. Ah! Is this not the clear effect of King Wen’s cultivation of himself and ordering of his family, and the reason Confucius selected this poem to stand at the head of the Book of Odes?

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
如松柏之茂無不爾或承
林應揚
同考試官教諭費批觀此猶可想見有周臣
子忠愛氣象
同考試官教諭方批文從字順敷陳祝君之
意宛然
考試官教諭趙批舂容典雅
考試官學正寇批寫得人臣祝君的意思出
詩人頌君之福取諸物之常盛者焉夫福以盛
===
為難也福之不已而常盛斯其福之至乎天保
臣子之荅君如此其意蓋曰吾君之福以進盛
則日月矣以悠久則南山矣而其常盛也何如
哉彼天下之物二儀煦而榮悴生焉有時而或
悴者非所貴也四時變而盛衰異焉有時而或
衰者不足取也惟松柏之茂造化之栽培獨至
氣機之生育特隆而吾君之福如之其必洪休
之踵至而循環不已多福之駢集而日新罔渝
舊者固已邁矣而其新者又於是乎來焉何其
punctuated:
如松柏之茂，無不爾或承。
林應揚
同考試官教諭費批：觀此，猶可想見有周臣子忠愛氣象。
同考試官教諭方批：文從字順，敷陳祝君之意宛然。
考試官教諭趙批：舂容典雅。
考試官學正寇批：寫得人臣祝君的意思出。
詩人頌君之福，取諸物之常盛者焉。夫福以盛為難也，福之不已而常盛，斯其福之至乎！《天保》臣子之荅君如此。其意蓋曰：吾君之福，以進盛則日月矣，以悠久則南山矣，而其常盛也何如哉？彼天下之物，二儀煦而榮悴生焉，有時而或悴者，非所貴也；四時變而盛衰異焉，有時而或衰者，不足取也。惟松柏之茂，造化之栽培獨至，氣機之生育特隆，而吾君之福如之。其必洪休之踵至而循環不已，多福之駢集而日新罔渝。舊者固已邁矣，而其新者又於是乎來焉，何其
translation_en:
“Like the luxuriance of pines and cypresses, may there always be that which carries on for you.”

Lin Yingyang

Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor, comments: “Reading this, one can still envision the loyal and loving spirit of the subjects of Zhou.”

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “The prose flows and the wording is apt; the wish to bless the ruler is vividly expressed.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Measured, ample, and classically elegant.”

Examiner Kou, School Director, comments: “It brings out a subject’s intention in invoking blessings upon his ruler.”

In praising his ruler’s blessings, the poet draws upon things that flourish perpetually. For blessings, attaining abundance is difficult; surely blessings that never cease and remain forever abundant are blessings at their utmost! Such is the subjects’ response to their ruler in “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao). Its meaning is, in effect: Our ruler’s blessings, in their increasing fullness, resemble the sun and moon; in their enduring length, they resemble the Southern Mountain. But what is their perpetual flourishing like? Among the things of the world, the warmth of Heaven and Earth brings forth both flourishing and withering. Whatever may sometimes wither is not what we prize. As the four seasons change, flourishing and decline alternate. Whatever may sometimes decline is unworthy of selection. Only in the luxuriance of pines and cypresses does the nurturing of creative transformation reach an exceptional perfection, and the generative workings of vital energy display particular abundance. Our ruler’s blessings are like these. Surely great blessings will arrive one after another in an unending cycle, and manifold blessings will gather together, renewed daily without fail. The old have already passed, and now the new arrive. How…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
相續而不絕已乎新者未之往矣而其後者又
於是乎至焉何其相繼而無息已乎斂其福於
一身則緝熈純嘏衍而爲眉壽萬年之休布其
福於天下則德化昭明流而爲宗社無疆之慶
保太和以培其根萃百順以達其枝時有推移
而福無隆替其與松柏之舊葉將落而新葉已
生者其理不亦同哉必如是而後臣子之心乃
能答君恩於萬一也抑書稱幾康弼直繼以昭
受上帝申命用休若以福爲德應而詩人盡託
===
之天何也蓋君臣之體分懸絕言不可以直遂
況事之戩穀神之孝享民之徧德皆古帝王之
要道而祈天永命之本有周臣子雖頌禱君福
託名於天而陳善之敬亦於是乎寓矣故曰美
不忘規天保有焉
春秋
夏齊人伐我北鄙〔僖公二十六年〕晉欒書
帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕公會晉侯宋公衛
侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世子光滕子薛伯
punctuated:
相續而不絕已乎？新者未之往矣，而其後者又於是乎至焉，何其相繼而無息已乎？斂其福於一身，則緝熈純嘏，衍而爲眉壽萬年之休；布其福於天下，則德化昭明，流而爲宗社無疆之慶。保太和以培其根，萃百順以達其枝，時有推移，而福無隆替。其與松柏之舊葉將落而新葉已生者，其理不亦同哉？必如是，而後臣子之心乃能答君恩於萬一也。抑《書》稱「幾康弼直」，繼以「昭受上帝，申命用休」，若以福爲德應，而詩人盡託之天，何也？蓋君臣之體分懸絕，言不可以直遂。況事之戩穀、神之孝享、民之徧德，皆古帝王之要道，而祈天永命之本。有周臣子雖頌禱君福，託名於天，而陳善之敬亦於是乎寓矣。故曰：「美不忘規，《天保》有焉。」

春秋

夏，齊人伐我北鄙。〔僖公二十六年〕晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯，
translation_en:
…how continuously they follow, without ever ending! Before the new blessings have passed, those that follow arrive in turn: how unceasingly they succeed one another! Gathered into the ruler’s own person, these blessings become an ever-brightening abundance of great good fortune, extending into the felicity of venerable longevity for ten thousand years. Spread throughout the world, they make his virtuous influence shine forth, flowing into boundless blessings for the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain. He preserves supreme harmony to nourish their roots and gathers every favorable influence to extend their branches. Times change, but his blessings neither wax nor wane. Is this not the same principle seen in pines and cypresses, whose new leaves have already grown before the old ones fall? Only thus can his subjects fulfill their heartfelt wish to repay even a ten-thousandth part of their ruler’s kindness.

Yet the Book of Documents speaks of vigilance, good order, and upright assistance, continuing with “Manifestly receive Heaven’s favor; its mandate is renewed with blessings.” This seems to treat blessings as a response to virtue. Why, then, does the poet attribute them entirely to Heaven? The respective stations of ruler and minister are separated by an immense distance, so words cannot simply proceed without restraint. Moreover, bringing affairs to a good outcome, serving the spirits with filial offerings, and extending virtue to all the people are essential principles of the ancient sage-kings’ rule and the foundation for beseeching Heaven to perpetuate its mandate. Although the subjects of Zhou praised their ruler’s blessings and prayed for them in Heaven’s name, their reverent duty to set goodness before him was also embodied in these words. Thus it is said: “To praise without forgetting admonition—this is found in ‘Heaven Protects’ [Tianbao].”

Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, the men of Qi attacked our northern borderlands. 〔The twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.〕 Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔The sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, and the Earl of Xue …

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “He integrates the Classic and its commentaries, leaving nothing unaddressed in his judgments. Reading this is refreshing.”
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Accords with the meaning of the commentary.”
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: “Achieves a careful and rigorous style.”
By observing the different ways in which our own state and other states subdued their enemies, the guilt of those skilled in warfare becomes clear. For subduing an enemy, nothing equals reliance on righteousness; mere strength and power have no part in it. Thus, when we consider how Lu and Jin dealt with their enemies, is there not a vast difference between their successes and failures? I have heard that maintaining awe-inspiring might and displaying virtue are sound principles of military affairs, while relying on strength to oppress the weak is the great danger against which warfare demands vigilance. This is why the gentleman values putting an end to conflict and dares not bring harm upon the multitude: it is entirely because the lives of the people must be held dear. Among the great officers recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, few understood virtue. Hence those skilled in governing a state do not resort to arms. In Lu, I find one such man, Liuxia Hui. title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
好勝者孰不快於一逞惠也展喜之遣文告脩
焉申之以王命魯有所恃而不恐數之以廢職
齊有所怍而弗為卒之師旅不勤甲兵不頓而
民命賴焉謂非聖之和者哉下此者其惟善師
乎是故欒書之救鄭也一聞申息之起遂下旋
旆之令其於不陣似矣然繞角之役桑隧之遇
溱洧之往來寧不念悄悄之征夫耶擬之善為
國者事固不逮矣下此者其惟善陣乎是故知
罃之駕楚也運謀還師以敝之三分四軍以逆
===
之其於不戰似矣然牛首之師北林之會東門
之觀兵寧弗勞耽耽之大眾耶較之善師者其
德愈衰矣乃若荀吳之善戰猶有異焉夫狄人
之侵至于大原攘之可也而乃聽魏舒之詐謀
廢司馬之成法五乘為三伍也多方以誘其狎
五陳以相離也未列而薄其師喜功生事變制
多殺非惟下惠之罪人抑亦書罃之罪人矣是
則善戰者服上刑善陣者次之善師者又次之
而皆不若不師之為尤愈也春秋備書其望天
punctuated: 好勝者，孰不快於一逞？惠也，展喜之遣，文告脩焉，申之以王命，魯有所恃而不恐；數之以廢職，齊有所怍而弗為。卒之師旅不勤，甲兵不頓，而民命賴焉，謂非聖之和者哉？下此者，其惟善師乎？是故欒書之救鄭也，一聞申息之起，遂下旋旆之令，其於不陣似矣。然繞角之役、桑隧之遇、溱洧之往來，寧不念悄悄之征夫耶？擬之善為國者，事固不逮矣。下此者，其惟善陣乎？是故知罃之駕楚也，運謀還師以敝之，三分四軍以逆之，其於不戰似矣。然牛首之師、北林之會、東門之觀兵，寧弗勞耽耽之大眾耶？較之善師者，其德愈衰矣。乃若荀吳之善戰，猶有異焉。夫狄人之侵，至于大原，攘之可也，而乃聽魏舒之詐謀，廢司馬之成法。五乘為三伍也，多方以誘其狎；五陳以相離也，未列而薄其師。喜功生事，變制多殺，非惟下惠之罪人，抑亦書罃之罪人矣。是則善戰者服上刑，善陣者次之，善師者又次之，而皆不若不師之為尤愈也。《春秋》備書，其望天
translation_en:
… those eager for victory: who would not delight in an opportunity to vent their anger? Yet when Zhan Xi was dispatched, Liu Xiahui had the diplomatic declaration carefully prepared. By reiterating the king’s command, he gave Lu something to rely upon, so that it had no fear; by reproaching Qi for abandoning its duties, he gave Qi cause for shame, so that it desisted. In the end, the troops were not wearied, arms and armor were not worn down, and the people’s lives were preserved. Could one deny that he was the harmonious one among the sages?

Below this, would there not be those skilled in conducting campaigns? Thus, when Luan Shu went to rescue Zheng, as soon as he heard that the forces of Shen and Xi had mobilized, he ordered his banners turned back. In this he approached the ideal of not drawing up battle formations. Yet in the campaign at Raojiao, the encounter at Sangsui, and the movements to and fro across the Zhen and Wei rivers, did he never think of the anxious men on campaign? Compared with those skilled in governing a state, his deeds certainly fell short.

Below this, would there not be those skilled in deploying battle formations? Thus, when Zhi Ying sought to overawe Chu, he devised a strategy of returning with his forces to wear it down, dividing the four armies into three contingents to confront it. In this he approached the ideal of not fighting. Yet in the expedition to Niushou, the meeting at Beilin, and the display of troops at the eastern gate, did he not exhaust his formidable host? Compared with those skilled in conducting campaigns, his virtue was weaker still.

As for Xun Wu’s skill in fighting, there was a further difference. When the Di invaded as far as Dayuan, repelling them would have been permissible. But instead he listened to Wei Shu’s deceptive scheme and discarded the established regulations of the Minister of War. In reorganizing five chariot units into three infantry squads, he used various means to lure the enemy into overconfidence; in having five formations separate from one another, he pressed upon the enemy’s troops before they had drawn up their ranks. Delighting in achievements and provoking trouble, changing the military organization and killing great numbers, he stood condemned not only by the standard of Liu Xiahui, but also by those of Luan Shu and Zhi Ying.

Thus those skilled in fighting should receive the severest punishment; those skilled in deploying battle formations, the next; and those skilled in conducting campaigns, the next again. All fall short of the still better course of not sending out an army. The Spring and Autumn Annals records these matters fully, in the hope that all under Heaven …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
下以王者之事也而用兵禦敵之略不具見哉
抑古之以車戰也謂以正相加不幸而失捷猶
無以重衂成乎民也至春秋則以詐覆敵後世
沿習不已如孫吳之爲將秦隋之爲君則失之
愈遠而生民之禍極矣豈惟毒乎一世而已哉
噫此下惠所以師於百世而君子尚論夫王道
也
公孫歸父會齊人伐莒 秋晉侯會狄于
攢函〔宣公十一年〕
===
楊嶷

愈讀愈有滋味
考試官教諭趙 批 曲盡聖人書法之妙
考試官學正寇 批 詞義嚴正
春秋紀内外之兵好有所以謹大防者有所以
明大義者攷莒之伐攢函之會外狄而貶魯晉
聖人於夷夏君臣之際其嚴矣乎且魯之會齊
伐莒以其不恭也晉之會狄于攢函以其求成
punctuated:
下以王者之事也，而用兵禦敵之略不具見哉？抑古之以車戰也，謂以正相加，不幸而失捷，猶無以重衂成乎民也。至春秋，則以詐覆敵，後世沿習不已。如孫吳之爲將，秦隋之爲君，則失之愈遠，而生民之禍極矣，豈惟毒乎一世而已哉？噫！此下惠所以師於百世，而君子尚論夫王道也。
