translation_en:
…all under Heaven through the deeds of a true king. Are not the strategies for employing troops and resisting enemies fully revealed therein? In ancient times, warfare with chariots meant confronting one another by upright means. Even if an army unfortunately failed to win, it would still not inflict further grievous losses upon the people [?]. By the Spring and Autumn period, however, deception was used to overthrow the enemy, and later generations continually followed this practice. With generals such as Sun Wu and Wu Qi, and rulers such as those of Qin and Sui, the departure grew ever greater, and the calamities suffered by the people reached their utmost extent. How could the harm have been confined to a single age? Alas! This is why Liu Xiahui serves as a teacher for a hundred generations, and why the gentleman esteems discussion of the Kingly Way.
Gongsun Guifu joined men of Qi in attacking Ju. In autumn, the Marquis of Jin met the Di at Zanhan. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xuan〕
Yang Yi
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The narration is careful and disciplined, and the writing vigorous and forceful. The more one reads it, the more rewarding it becomes.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: It brings out in full the subtle excellence of the Sage’s manner of recording events.
Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: Its language and meaning are rigorous and upright.
In recording warfare and friendly relations involving Lu and other states, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes safeguards the great boundaries and sometimes clarifies the great principles of righteousness. Examining the attack on Ju and the meeting at Zanhan, we find that it treats the Di as outsiders and censures Lu and Jin. How strict the Sage is concerning the distinctions between the Yi and the Xia, and between ruler and minister! Now, Lu joined Qi in attacking Ju because Ju had been disrespectful; Jin met the Di at Zanhan because they sought peace…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也夫伐則小國以懲會則夷狄以懷矣曷言乎
外狄而責魯晉耶蓋内夏外夷天下之大防也
蠻夷戎狄族類之異明矣邈然要荒止其所焉
可也惟兹以求成之故而並登乎壇壝之上假
服屬之名而混列於會同之間尚謂有别也乎
吾聞先王之御夷也正朔之不加禮教之不及
朝聘之不通凡以懲淫慝一内外也匪是之由
而遂悻悻於禮文之接玉帛之好焉向使挾詐
以逞伺隙而動斯則盛世之所憂者能無懼乎
===
聖人以謂寧無泉狄之會而不可無族類之分
是故略詞以外之其以謹華夷之辨與若禁亂
誅暴天下之大義也廐矢竊發徵舒之惡著矣
魯晉協力請而戮之可也乃者懲細過於小弱
而廢天討之所當加求外比於遠夷而遺王法
之所不貸尚謂知類也乎吾聞先王之敕法也
有甲兵之威有軍旅之伐有鈇鉞之誅凡以治
姦惡正典刑也匪是之圖而顧汲汲於一莒之
伐泉狄之會焉致使三綱以淪九法以斁斯則
punctuated:
也。夫伐則小國以懲，會則夷狄以懷矣。曷言乎外狄而責魯晉耶？蓋内夏外夷，天下之大防也。蠻夷戎狄，族類之異明矣。邈然要荒，止其所焉可也。惟兹以求成之故，而並登乎壇壝之上；假服屬之名，而混列於會同之間，尚謂有别也乎？吾聞先王之御夷也，正朔之不加，禮教之不及，朝聘之不通，凡以懲淫慝，一内外也。匪是之由，而遂悻悻於禮文之接、玉帛之好焉。向使挾詐以逞，伺隙而動，斯則盛世之所憂者，能無懼乎？聖人以謂寧無泉狄之會，而不可無族類之分。是故略詞以外之，其以謹華夷之辨與？
若禁亂誅暴，天下之大義也。廐矢竊發，徵舒之惡著矣。魯晉協力，請而戮之可也。乃者懲細過於小弱，而廢天討之所當加；求外比於遠夷，而遺王法之所不貸，尚謂知類也乎？吾聞先王之敕法也，有甲兵之威，有軍旅之伐，有鈇鉞之誅，凡以治姦惡，正典刑也。匪是之圖，而顧汲汲於一莒之伐、泉狄之會焉，致使三綱以淪，九法以斁，斯則
translation_en:
…was the reason. A punitive expedition chastises a small state, while a meeting wins over the Yi and Di. Why, then, speak of excluding the Di and censuring Lu and Jin? To place the Xia within and the Yi outside is the great boundary under Heaven. The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di plainly belong to different peoples. It is fitting that they remain in their own places, far away in the outermost domains. Yet here, merely because they sought peace, they were allowed to ascend the covenant altar together with the Chinese rulers; under the pretext of submission, they were indiscriminately ranked among those attending interstate assemblies. Could this still be called maintaining distinctions? I have heard that, in governing the Yi, the former kings did not impose their calendar upon them, extend ritual instruction to them, or exchange court visits and diplomatic missions with them. All this served to restrain excess and wickedness and maintain a consistent distinction between inside and outside. Instead of following this course, they obstinately pursued ceremonial intercourse and friendly exchanges of jade and silk. Should these peoples use deceit to pursue their ambitions and seize an opening to act, this would be a source of anxiety even in a flourishing age. Could one have no fear? The Sage held that one could dispense with the meeting with the Di [?], but could not dispense with distinctions between peoples. He therefore used abbreviated wording to place them outside. Was this not to safeguard the distinction between Hua and Yi?
As for suppressing disorder and punishing violence, these are great obligations under Heaven. An arrow was secretly loosed at the stables, and Zhengshu’s wickedness became manifest. Lu and Jin ought to have joined forces, sought authorization, and executed him. Instead, they punished a minor fault in a small and weak state while neglecting the proper object of Heaven’s chastisement; they sought an external alliance with distant Yi while overlooking one whom the king’s law could not pardon. Could this still be called understanding how to distinguish cases? I have heard that, when the former kings enforced the law, they employed the威 of armed forces, military expeditions, and execution with the axe. All these served to punish the treacherous and wicked and uphold the established penal order. Instead of planning for this, they busied themselves with nothing more than an expedition against Ju and a meeting with the Di [?], allowing the Three Bonds to founder and the Nine Standards to fall into ruin. This, then, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
人心之當正者可無幾乎聖人以謂寧無莒狄
之謀而不可無徵舒之討是故直書以貶之其
以治亂賊之黨與此義行則華夷辨而貴賤殊
君臣嚴而天地泰矣謂春秋之成為世道一治
不其然與雖然宣也奪嫡頃也忘親是固宜其
無意於陳也獨惜晉景主伯林父新將而舉動
若此是亦可謂無制中夏之略矣卒之栗門轘
而京觀建致使王室懿親奔走於蛇豕之國又
將誰咎也哉君子是以嗟桓文之早而悼悼之
===
晚也
禮記
天垂象聖人則之郊所以明天道也
鄧原玉
同考試官教諭馮批郊以明天道與社以
神地道同意作者類不知此獨子能發明美報
之義是用錄出
考試官教諭趙批渾厚爾雅得聖人明天
道之意
punctuated:
人心之當正者，可無幾乎？聖人以謂寧無莒狄之謀，而不可無徵舒之討。是故直書以貶之，其以治亂賊之黨與？此義行，則華夷辨而貴賤殊，君臣嚴而天地泰矣。謂《春秋》之成為世道一治，不其然與？雖然，宣也奪嫡，頃也忘親，是固宜其無意於陳也。獨惜晉景主伯，林父新將，而舉動若此，是亦可謂無制中夏之略矣。卒之栗門轘而京觀建，致使王室懿親奔走於蛇豕之國，又將誰咎也哉？君子是以嗟桓文之早，而悼悼之晚也。

禮記

天垂象，聖人則之。郊所以明天道也。

鄧原玉

同考試官教諭馮批：郊以明天道，與社以神地道同意。作者類不知此，獨子能發明美報之義，是用錄出。

考試官教諭趙批：渾厚爾雅，得聖人明天道之意。
translation_en:
…could the matters in human hearts that require correction be few [?]? The Sage held that plans concerning Ju and the Di could be dispensed with, but the punitive action against Zhengshu could not. Thus he recorded the events directly to censure them: was this not intended to punish the accomplices of rebels and traitors? When this principle prevails, the distinction between the Chinese and the outsiders is clear, noble and lowly are differentiated, the relationship between ruler and minister is strictly maintained, and Heaven and Earth are at peace. Is it not indeed true that the completion of the Spring and Autumn Annals brought a measure of order to the world?

Nevertheless, Duke Xuan usurped the rightful heir’s position, and Duke Qing forgot his kin; it was therefore only to be expected that they would have no concern for Chen. What is especially regrettable is that Duke Jing of Jin held the hegemonic leadership and Linfu had newly assumed military command, yet their conduct was like this. They too may be said to have lacked a strategy for governing the central states. In the end came dismemberment by chariots at Limen and the erection of a mound of enemy corpses, leaving close kin of the royal house fleeing about in a land of serpents and swine. Whom else could they blame? Thus the gentleman sighs that Dukes Huan and Wen lived too early and laments that Duke Dao came too late.

Record of Rites

“Heaven displays its signs, and the sage takes them as his model. The suburban sacrifice serves to make manifest the Way of Heaven.”

Deng Yuanyu

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “Making manifest the Way of Heaven through the suburban sacrifice has the same meaning as revealing the numinous efficacy of the Way of Earth through the sacrifice to the soil. Writers generally fail to understand this. You alone have been able to elucidate the meaning of praising and requiting Heaven’s bounty; for this reason, your essay has been selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Substantial, dignified, and refined: it grasps the sage’s intention in making manifest the Way of Heaven.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正寇批不鑿不浮發揮聖人則
天處明盡
觀郊祭法天以備物而聖人崇祀之義著矣蓋
天以生物爲功者也聖人備物以崇祀則其明
天之道者義獨至矣特牲詳論郊祀之禮而結
言其意也蓋謂盡物以致飾者聖王祀天之文
因物以致義者聖王祀天之實循文以究其實
郊之所觀者深矣彼法象莫大乎天雖化工之
默運也而懸象著明者已昭垂於冲穆之表禮
===
制莫善於聖人固經制之悉具也而備物致用
者皆殽法乎制作之原日月相推而明生焉十
二月相推而歲成焉袞冕於是乎放其文也天
道無爲而質具焉乾道變化而龍生焉車旂於
是乎尚其象也郊祀之法天備物者如此豈徒
極觀美之具哉亦以明天道焉耳蓋乾元資始
品物流形天地間無非法象無非道也聖人備
物以崇祀則太和保合之體假物采以闡其微
而含萬物以化光者皆昭晰於明禋之際化育
punctuated:
考試官學正寇批：不鑿不浮，發揮聖人則天處明盡。

觀郊祭法天以備物，而聖人崇祀之義著矣。蓋天以生物爲功者也，聖人備物以崇祀，則其明天之道者，義獨至矣。特牲詳論郊祀之禮，而結言其意也。蓋謂盡物以致飾者，聖王祀天之文；因物以致義者，聖王祀天之實。循文以究其實，郊之所觀者深矣。彼法象莫大乎天，雖化工之默運也，而懸象著明者，已昭垂於冲穆之表。禮制莫善於聖人，固經制之悉具也，而備物致用者，皆殽法乎制作之原。日月相推而明生焉，十二月相推而歲成焉，袞冕於是乎放其文也。天道無爲而質具焉，乾道變化而龍生焉，車旂於是乎尚其象也。郊祀之法天備物者如此，豈徒極觀美之具哉？亦以明天道焉耳。蓋乾元資始，品物流形，天地間無非法象，無非道也。聖人備物以崇祀，則太和保合之體，假物采以闡其微，而含萬物以化光者，皆昭晰於明禋之際。化育
translation_en:
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: “Neither strained nor superficial; it explains clearly and fully how the sage takes Heaven as his model.”

Observe how the suburban sacrifice models itself on Heaven in providing its ritual objects: the meaning of the sage’s reverent worship thereby becomes manifest. For Heaven’s achievement lies in giving life to things. When the sage provides ritual objects for reverent worship, the significance of his making manifest the Way of Heaven reaches its fullest extent. “The Single Victim” (Tesheng) [?] discusses the rites of the suburban sacrifice in detail and concludes by stating their meaning. Its point is that employing objects to the fullest to furnish adornment constitutes the outward form of the sage king’s sacrifice to Heaven; using those objects to convey meaning constitutes its substance. Following the outward form to investigate its substance, one finds profound things to contemplate in the suburban sacrifice.

Among models and images, none is greater than Heaven. Although the work of transformation proceeds silently, the luminous images suspended above are already manifest beyond its deep stillness. Among ritual institutions, none surpass those of the sage. His established arrangements are indeed complete, and the objects provided for use all imitate the source of his ritual creations. The sun and moon succeed one another, producing light; the twelve months succeed one another, completing the year. The ceremonial robe and cap accordingly reproduce their patterns. Heaven’s Way acts without deliberate effort, yet its substance is fully present; the Way of Qian transforms, and dragons are born. The carriage and banners accordingly honor these images.

Such is the suburban sacrifice’s provision of objects in imitation of Heaven. Could these merely be furnishings that bring visual splendor to its utmost? They also serve to make manifest the Way of Heaven. For all things derive their beginnings from the primal power of Qian, and the myriad kinds of beings unfold into form. Between Heaven and Earth, nothing is without a model or image, and nothing is without the Way. When the sage provides ritual objects for reverent worship, the underlying reality that preserves and unites supreme harmony borrows the colors and ornament of these objects to disclose its subtle workings. That which embraces the myriad things and transforms them with radiance thus becomes fully clear at the offering of the pure sacrifice. The transforming and nourishing…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
流行之機因效法以章其蘊而幹歲功於不忒
者悉顯示於昭假之餘夫如是而後見上天生
物之功爲不可掩聖人美報之禮爲不可已也
否則衮冕車旂之設者皆文焉而已豈聖人崇
祀之意哉是其始也法天以制禮其終也用禮
以顯天至教至德之相須爲用也如此抑聞之
易曰乾始能以美利利天下而不言所利大
矣哉則無心成化者天道之自然而有心無爲
聖人之所以合德於天者惟聖人合德於天而
===
後能以明乎天之道此又郊祀之微義也嗚呼
非天下之至仁孰能與於此
樂由中出故靜禮自外作故文大樂必易
大禮必簡
張孔脩
同考試官教諭馮批言醇而和蓋知學禮樂
而有得者足以占所蘊矣
考試官教諭趙批只順題講去而於先王
制禮樂之意提掇明甚是之取爾
punctuated:
流行之機，因效法以章其蘊，而幹歲功於不忒者，悉顯示於昭假之餘。夫如是，而後見上天生物之功爲不可掩，聖人美報之禮爲不可已也。否則衮冕車旂之設者，皆文焉而已，豈聖人崇祀之意哉？是其始也，法天以制禮；其終也，用禮以顯天。至教至德之相須爲用也如此。抑聞之，《易》曰：「乾始能以美利利天下，而不言所利。」大矣哉！則無心成化者，天道之自然；而有心無爲，聖人之所以合德於天者。惟聖人合德於天，而後能以明乎天之道。此又郊祀之微義也。嗚呼！非天下之至仁，孰能與於此？

樂由中出故靜，禮自外作故文，大樂必易，大禮必簡。
張孔脩

同考試官教諭馮批：言醇而和，蓋知學禮樂而有得者，足以占所蘊矣。

考試官教諭趙批：只順題講去，而於先王制禮樂之意，提掇明甚，是之取爾。
translation_en:
…the workings of its flowing activity have their hidden substance revealed through imitation, and that which unfailingly brings the year's labors to fruition is fully manifested through the luminous approach to the spirits. Only thus do we see that Heaven's achievement in bringing forth living things cannot be concealed, and that the sage's rites of splendid recompense cannot cease. Otherwise, the provision of embroidered robes, ceremonial caps, carriages, and banners would be mere ornament. Could this be the sage's intention in honoring the sacrifices? At the outset, he models himself on Heaven to establish ritual; in the end, he uses ritual to reveal Heaven. Such is the mutual dependence of supreme teaching and supreme virtue in their operation.

Moreover, I have heard it said in the Book of Changes: “Qian's initiating power can benefit all under Heaven with its excellent benefits, yet does not speak of what it benefits.” How great this is! Accomplishing transformation without conscious intent is the spontaneity of Heaven's Way; possessing conscious intent yet acting without contrivance is how the sage accords his virtue with Heaven. Only after the sage accords his virtue with Heaven can he illuminate Heaven's Way. This is another subtle meaning of the suburban sacrifice. Ah! Who but one possessing the utmost benevolence under Heaven could participate in this?

“Music issues from within and therefore is still; ritual arises from without and therefore has outward form. Great music must be easy; great ritual must be simple.”
Zhang Kongxiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: His language is pure and harmonious. He evidently knows how to study ritual and music and has gained an understanding of them. This is sufficient to discern what he holds within.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: He simply follows the topic in developing his exposition, yet brings out very clearly the intention of the former kings in establishing ritual and music. This is why I selected his essay.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正寇批發揮大樂必易二句最
為得旨敬羡敬羡
記者推禮樂之妙而贊其體天地之撰焉蓋天
地之撰易簡而已也禮樂為能體之則其靜文
之妙可識矣想昔記者之意若謂禮樂之道和
序焉盡之矣始之發於身心極之合乎天地夫
豈有二乎哉彼樂者聲容具陳若難乎其為靜
矣惟樂由中出則心也者樂之本也審一定和
者既有以涵主靜之源則順成和動者自有以
===
安至靜之體以五聲則成文也以八音則從律
也以百度則得數也蓋不必外和以求靜而靜
即妙於和之中矣何靜如之禮者經曲異宜若
難乎其為文矣惟禮自外作則身也者禮之原
也比類成行者既有以端人文之本則嘉會合
禮者自有以煥人道之華以容貌則得莊也以行
列則得正也以進退則得齊也蓋不必舍序以
求文而文不出於序之外矣何文如之夫天下
之道靜者或隱而難惟大樂與天地同和則其
punctuated:
考試官學正寇批：發揮「大樂必易」二句，最為得旨。敬羡！敬羡！

記者推禮樂之妙，而贊其體天地之撰焉。蓋天地之撰，易簡而已也。禮樂為能體之，則其靜文之妙可識矣。想昔記者之意，若謂禮樂之道，和序焉盡之矣。始之發於身心，極之合乎天地，夫豈有二乎哉？彼樂者，聲容具陳，若難乎其為靜矣。惟樂由中出，則心也者，樂之本也。審一定和者，既有以涵主靜之源，則順成和動者，自有以安至靜之體。以五聲則成文也，以八音則從律也，以百度則得數也。蓋不必外和以求靜，而靜即妙於和之中矣。何靜如之？禮者，經曲異宜，若難乎其為文矣。惟禮自外作，則身也者，禮之原也。比類成行者，既有以端人文之本，則嘉會合禮者，自有以煥人道之華。以容貌則得莊也，以行列則得正也，以進退則得齊也。蓋不必舍序以求文，而文不出於序之外矣。何文如之？夫天下之道，靜者或隱而難，惟大樂與天地同和，則其
translation_en:
Examiner Kou, an Instructor, comments: “The exposition of the two clauses beginning ‘Great music must be easy’ captures their meaning exceptionally well. Admirable! Admirable!”

The author of the Record explores the subtle workings of ritual and music and praises their embodiment of the operations of Heaven and Earth. For the operations of Heaven and Earth are simply ease and simplicity. Since ritual and music can embody these, we may understand the subtle workings of their stillness and patterned expression. We may imagine that the ancient author meant that harmony and order encompass the entire Way of ritual and music. Beginning in their expression through the body and mind, and culminating in their accord with Heaven and Earth, how could they follow two different principles?

Music presents sounds and bodily movements together, so it might seem difficult for it to be still. Yet music comes forth from within: the mind is its foundation. That which examines unity and establishes harmony [?] already nurtures the source of the primacy of stillness; that which brings things to completion in accord with their nature and moves harmoniously consequently settles into the substance of utmost stillness. Through the five tones it achieves pattern; through the eight classes of instruments it accords with the pitch standards; through its manifold measures it attains proper numerical proportions. There is no need to seek stillness outside harmony: stillness works subtly within harmony itself. What stillness could equal this?

Ritual has different appropriate forms in its general principles and particular observances, so it might seem difficult for it to possess patterned expression. Yet ritual arises from without: the body is its source. That which groups like things and arranges them in ranks already sets right the foundation of human culture; auspicious gatherings conducted in accordance with ritual consequently bring the splendor of the human Way to full brilliance. In bearing and appearance it achieves dignity; in ranks and files it achieves correctness; in advancing and withdrawing it achieves uniformity. There is no need to abandon order to seek patterned expression: patterned expression does not lie outside order. What patterned expression could equal this?

Now, among the ways of the world, those characterized by stillness may be hidden and difficult to grasp. Great music alone shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth, and thus its…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
靜者非有事於强也自吾心之至和者充之聲
得之而爲聲焉音得之而爲音焉度得之而爲
度焉各順其自然而已矣擬諸乾知大始而確
然示人易者何異哉天下之道文者或彙而煩
惟大禮與天地同節則其文者非徒事於末也
舉吾身之至序者推之時乎莊而莊焉時乎正
而正焉時乎齊而齊焉皆行所無事而已矣擬
諸坤作成物而隤然示人簡者何異哉是惟易
而靜也而後見其靜者爲和之至惟簡而文也
===
而後見其文者爲序之極禮樂之道斯其至矣
抑論天地設位聖人成能則禮樂易簡之妙豈
惟合諸天地而已哉要之易簡之道在我則禮
樂參贊之化皆不外此故曰易簡而天下之理
得天下之理得而成位乎其中矣學者能合而
觀之則天地也禮樂也身心也其一貫矣乎
第貳場
論
聖人先得我心之同然
punctuated:
靜者非有事於强也，自吾心之至和者充之，聲得之而爲聲焉，音得之而爲音焉，度得之而爲度焉，各順其自然而已矣。擬諸乾知大始而確然示人易者，何異哉？天下之道，文者或彙而煩，惟大禮與天地同節，則其文者非徒事於末也。舉吾身之至序者推之，時乎莊而莊焉，時乎正而正焉，時乎齊而齊焉，皆行所無事而已矣。擬諸坤作成物而隤然示人簡者，何異哉？是惟易而靜也，而後見其靜者爲和之至；惟簡而文也，而後見其文者爲序之極。禮樂之道，斯其至矣。抑論天地設位，聖人成能，則禮樂易簡之妙，豈惟合諸天地而已哉？要之，易簡之道在我，則禮樂參贊之化皆不外此。故曰：「易簡而天下之理得，天下之理得而成位乎其中矣。」學者能合而觀之，則天地也，禮樂也，身心也，其一貫矣乎！

第貳場

論

聖人先得我心之同然
translation_en:
…its stillness does not involve forcing anything. Extend the utmost harmony within my heart: individual sounds receive it and become sounds; musical tones receive it and become tones; measures receive it and become measures. Each merely follows what is natural to it. How does this differ from Qian, which presides over the great beginning and, in its firmness, shows people ease? Among the ways of the world, patterned forms may become crowded and cumbersome. Yet great ritual shares the articulation of Heaven and Earth, so its patterned forms do not merely concern themselves with superficial details. Extend the utmost order embodied in my person: when solemnity is called for, be solemn; when correctness is called for, be correct; when uniformity is called for, be uniform. All this is simply acting without contrivance. How does this differ from Kun, which brings things to completion and, in its yielding nature, shows people simplicity? Only when there is ease together with stillness do we see that this stillness is harmony at its utmost; only when there is simplicity together with patterned form do we see that this form is order at its fullest. Here the Way of ritual and music reaches its culmination.

Moreover, consider how Heaven and Earth establish their positions and the sage fulfills his capacities: can the subtle workings of ease and simplicity in ritual and music merely accord with Heaven and Earth, and nothing more? In essence, when the Way of ease and simplicity resides in me, the transforming work of ritual and music, participating in and assisting the processes of Heaven and Earth, lies entirely within it. Thus it is said: “Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. When those principles are grasped, one establishes one’s place in their midst.” If students can view these things together, will they not find Heaven and Earth, ritual and music, and body and mind united by a single thread?

The Sage Was the First to Grasp What Our Hearts Commonly Affirm

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
大也蓋嘗觀之天地間之至貴者謂之人人之
至靈者謂之心心之生生者謂之性性之括萬
善而不遺者謂之理義故理義之在人也發之
親而孝長而敬事君而忠臨民而仁親疎貴賤
厚薄而別聲色臭味嗜慾而節五常百行千變
萬化皆明覺而有倫理是皆不學而知不慮而
能者也非以堯存非以桀亡非以賢知而通非
以愚不肖而塞何也所謂性之善而心之同然
者本如此其妙也而聖人獨先得之豈天之獨
===
厚聖人耶嘗求其故矣試語於衆曰人之有心
異於耳目口鼻乎曰無以異也心之同然異於
耳之同聽目之同美口之同嗜鼻之同臭乎曰
無以異也夫於耳目口鼻吾皆通之而於心則
蔽焉豈非得之天者同而所以事其心者未至
與夫人生而靜天之性也感於物而動性之欲
也聖人知動之爲害而心以制之去其所本無
而復其所固有故曰盡心之學所以爲大也盡
之也者存之也孳孳於善存而不失慎獨以研
punctuated:
大也。蓋嘗觀之，天地間之至貴者謂之人，人之至靈者謂之心，心之生生者謂之性，性之括萬善而不遺者謂之理義。故理義之在人也，發之親而孝，長而敬，事君而忠，臨民而仁；親疎貴賤，厚薄而別；聲色臭味，嗜慾而節。五常百行，千變萬化，皆明覺而有倫理，是皆不學而知、不慮而能者也。非以堯存，非以桀亡，非以賢知而通，非以愚不肖而塞。何也？所謂性之善而心之同然者，本如此其妙也。而聖人獨先得之，豈天之獨厚聖人耶？嘗求其故矣。試語於衆曰：「人之有心，異於耳目口鼻乎？」曰：「無以異也。」「心之同然，異於耳之同聽、目之同美、口之同嗜、鼻之同臭乎？」曰：「無以異也。」夫於耳目口鼻，吾皆通之，而於心則蔽焉，豈非得之天者同，而所以事其心者未至與？

夫人生而靜，天之性也；感於物而動，性之欲也。聖人知動之爲害，而心以制之，去其所本無，而復其所固有。故曰：「盡心之學所以爲大也。」盡之也者，存之也。孳孳於善，存而不失，慎獨以研
translation_en:
…is great. I have considered this: what is most precious between Heaven and Earth is called the human being; what is most spiritually perceptive in the human being is called the heart-mind; the ceaseless generative activity of the heart-mind is called human nature; and that in human nature which encompasses every goodness without omission is called principle and righteousness. Thus, principle and righteousness within people manifest themselves as filial devotion toward parents, respect toward elders, loyalty in serving the ruler, and benevolence in governing the people. They distinguish degrees of generosity according to closeness or distance in relationship and high or low station, and moderate appetites and desires for sounds, sights, smells, and tastes. Throughout the five constant virtues and the hundred forms of conduct, amid a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations, there is clear awareness and moral order. All these are known without learning and accomplished without deliberation. They do not exist because of Yao, nor perish because of Jie; they do not become accessible because someone is worthy and wise, nor become blocked because someone is foolish and unworthy. Why is this? What we call the goodness of human nature and the common assent of the heart-mind is inherently wondrous in just this way. Yet sages alone apprehend it first: can Heaven favor sages alone? I have sought the reason. Let us put this question to people: “Does possessing a heart-mind differ from possessing ears, eyes, a mouth, and a nose?” They reply: “There is no difference.” “Does the common assent of the heart-mind differ from the ears’ shared responses to sounds, the eyes’ shared appreciation of beauty, the mouth’s shared preferences in taste, and the nose’s shared responses to smells?” They reply: “There is no difference.” In the case of ears, eyes, mouth, and nose, we all apprehend this commonality, yet in the case of the heart-mind we are obscured. Is this not because what we receive from Heaven is the same, while our efforts to tend the heart-mind remain insufficient?

When people are born and are still, this is their Heaven-given nature; when they are affected by things and stirred into activity, these are the desires of that nature. Sages understand the harm arising from such activity and use the heart-mind to control it, removing what was not originally there and restoring what was inherently theirs. Thus it is said: “This is why the learning that fully realizes the heart-mind is great.” Fully realizing it means preserving it. Diligently pursuing goodness, preserving it without loss, and remaining watchful over oneself when alone in order to investigate…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其幾親師友以致其助識前言往行以畜其德
而吾之學始精一矣窮理盡性而天下之道始
備矣此聖人所以得我心之同然而衆人不能
也夫衆人之不能何也蓋以純駁雜擾之資加
之以或輟或作之學於其心之蔽者未能祛而

激則溺於卑污紛紛籍籍不爲異物者亦希矣
至是而人心之同然安得不爲聖人之獨有哉
聖人從事於心旣有以致其精而物之紛然者
===
又不能爲吾動是以同寂而異感同體而異發
同蘊而異用親也而先得我心之孝焉兄也而
先得我心之敬焉君也而先得我心之忠焉民
也而先得我心之仁焉親疎貴賤厚薄也而先
得我心之别焉食色臭味也而先得我心之節
焉五常百行千變萬化而先得我心之明覺條
理焉有天下以爲是而吾矯以爲非得我心之
公非焉有天下以爲非而吾矯以爲是得我心
之公是焉其存主曰德吐詞曰經用世曰業無
punctuated: 其幾，親師友以致其助，識前言往行以畜其德，而吾之學始精一矣。窮理盡性，而天下之道始備矣。此聖人所以得我心之同然，而衆人不能也。夫衆人之不能何也？蓋以純駁雜擾之資，加之以或輟或作之學，於其心之蔽者未能祛而復之。是故不迷於意見，則惑於聲利；不騖於亢激，則溺於卑污。紛紛籍籍，不爲異物者亦希矣。至是而人心之同然，安得不爲聖人之獨有哉？聖人從事於心，旣有以致其精，而物之紛然者又不能爲吾動，是以同寂而異感，同體而異發，同蘊而異用。親也，而先得我心之孝焉；兄也，而先得我心之敬焉；君也，而先得我心之忠焉；民也，而先得我心之仁焉；親疎貴賤厚薄也，而先得我心之别焉；食色臭味也，而先得我心之節焉；五常百行，千變萬化，而先得我心之明覺條理焉。有天下以爲是，而吾矯以爲非，得我心之公非焉；有天下以爲非，而吾矯以爲是，得我心之公是焉。其存主曰德，吐詞曰經，用世曰業，無
translation_en:
…its incipient stirrings; draw close to teachers and friends to obtain their help; and learn the words and deeds of the past to nurture one’s virtue. Only then does my learning become refined and single-minded. By thoroughly investigating principle and fully realizing one’s nature, one comes to comprehend the Way in its entirety. This is how sages apprehend what our hearts acknowledge in common, while ordinary people cannot.

Why can ordinary people not do so? Their endowments mingle purity and impurity in confused disorder, and to these they add learning pursued by fits and starts. They cannot remove what obscures their hearts and restore them. Thus, if they are not led astray by their own opinions, they are beguiled by reputation and profit; if they do not pursue arrogant extremes, they sink into baseness and corruption. Amid such turmoil and confusion, few avoid becoming something other than human. At this point, how could what human hearts acknowledge in common fail to become the exclusive possession of sages?

Sages devote themselves to the heart, having found the means to attain its refinement, while the bewildering multitude of external things cannot disturb it. Thus, there is a common stillness but differing responses to stimuli, a common substance but differing manifestations, a common inner store but differing applications. In relation to parents, the sage first apprehends the filial devotion in my heart; in relation to elder brothers, the respect in my heart; in relation to the ruler, the loyalty in my heart; and in relation to the people, the benevolence in my heart. In relations of closeness and distance, nobility and lowliness, and greater and lesser regard, the sage first apprehends the distinctions in my heart. In food, sexual desire, smells, and tastes, the sage first apprehends the restraint in my heart. Throughout the five constant virtues and the hundred forms of conduct, amid a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations, the sage first apprehends the clear awareness and ordered principles in my heart.

There are things the whole world deems right that I, correcting its judgment, deem wrong: here the sage apprehends my heart’s impartial disapproval. There are things the whole world deems wrong that I, correcting its judgment, deem right: here the sage apprehends my heart’s impartial approval. What the sage preserves within and takes as master is called virtue; what is expressed in words is called the classics; what is put into practice in the world is called achievement; what is without…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
過不及曰中約而言之曰天下古今同然之理
義嗟乎至矣吾嘗求之古昔而嘆先得我心之
難也得之而繼天者堯舜禹湯文武之爲君也
得之而佐命者臯夔伊周之爲臣也得之而明
道者孔孟之爲師也戰國之季人之陷溺其心
如碩果不食者亦至矣而孟子惓惓性善而取
證於人心之同然將何從而得之耶延平李子
有言曰人理義之心未嘗無惟持守之卽在爾
夫不失之謂得不亡之謂存持守也者存之也
===
存則大大則廣廣則塞是故至大配天至廣配
地至塞配萬化學而至是其孰爲得耶孰爲先
得耶孰爲我耶孰爲聖人耶善學者求之心性
焉盡矣請以是足孟子之意

詞反堆積可厭惟此作明淨可誦錄之

punctuated:
過不及曰中，約而言之，曰天下古今同然之理義。嗟乎，至矣！吾嘗求之古昔，而嘆先得我心之難也。得之而繼天者，堯舜禹湯文武之爲君也；得之而佐命者，臯夔伊周之爲臣也；得之而明道者，孔孟之爲師也。戰國之季，人之陷溺其心，如碩果不食者，亦至矣。而孟子惓惓性善，而取證於人心之同然，將何從而得之耶？延平李子有言曰：「人理義之心未嘗無，惟持守之卽在爾。」夫不失之謂得，不亡之謂存。持守也者，存之也。存則大，大則廣，廣則塞。是故至大配天，至廣配地，至塞配萬化。學而至是，其孰爲得耶？孰爲先得耶？孰爲我耶？孰爲聖人耶？善學者求之心性焉盡矣。請以是足孟子之意。

translation_en:
…neither exceeding nor falling short is called the Mean. In brief, it is the moral principle and rightness universally acknowledged throughout the world, past and present. Ah, this is perfection! I have sought it among the ancients and sighed at how difficult it is to apprehend before others what is shared by my own heart. Those who apprehended it and carried on Heaven’s work were the rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Those who apprehended it and assisted in fulfilling the heavenly mandate were the ministers Gao, Kui, Yi, and Zhou. Those who apprehended it and illuminated the Way were the teachers Kongzi and Mengzi. By the end of the Warring States period, people’s hearts had become utterly submerged, with what survived resembling a great fruit left uneaten [?]. Yet Mengzi remained earnestly devoted to the goodness of human nature and sought evidence in what human hearts universally acknowledge. By what means, then, can one apprehend it? Master Li of Yanping said: “People have never lacked a heart endowed with moral principle and rightness. Simply hold fast to it, and it is present.” To apprehend it means not to lose it; to preserve it means not to let it perish. Holding fast to it is preserving it. Preserved, it becomes great; great, it becomes expansive; expansive, it fills all things. Thus, in its utmost greatness it matches Heaven; in its utmost expansiveness it matches Earth; in its utmost fullness it matches the myriad transformations. When learning reaches this point, who apprehends it? Who apprehends it first? Who is the self? Who is the sage? Those who learn well seek it in the heart and human nature: that is all. Allow me to supplement Mengzi’s meaning with this.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
有遐思焉是不可以風多士乎
考試官敎諭趙批是善言聖人者
考試官學正寇批義理之文
心統天下之道者也聖人所以立人極者亦惟
盡其心而已天以太極之理畀諸人蘊之爲性
廓之爲理義而心統之者也外心以言理義非
以語性也外心以立人極非以合天也百姓日
用而不知盡心之道鮮矣夫聖人者豈異人哉
不過卽夫人心之同以成能耳蓋降衷之恆厥
===
賦鈞焉天無心也盡心之極同然者取足焉聖
人無異也以人合天而心極盡心極盡而人極
立矣此盡心之學所以爲大歟今夫天地之大
德曰生是故陰陽寒暑之動盪也四時日月之
推移也根荄蝡息蠕動之竝育竝行也其生不
息其化不窮其理謂之道其用謂之神其主宰
謂之帝其實則一元始之也元者何天地之心
是已故曰復其見天地之心乎天地匪心無以
斡萬化聖人匪心無以裁天地別之爲聖狂賢
punctuated:
有遐思焉，是不可以風多士乎？
考試官敎諭趙批：是善言聖人者。
考試官學正寇批：義理之文。
心統天下之道者也。聖人所以立人極者，亦惟盡其心而已。天以太極之理畀諸人，蘊之爲性，廓之爲理義，而心統之者也。外心以言理義，非以語性也；外心以立人極，非以合天也。百姓日用而不知，盡心之道鮮矣。夫聖人者，豈異人哉？不過卽夫人心之同以成能耳。蓋降衷之恆，厥賦鈞焉，天無心也；盡心之極，同然者取足焉，聖人無異也。以人合天而心極盡，心極盡而人極立矣。此盡心之學所以爲大歟！今夫天地之大德曰生。是故陰陽寒暑之動盪也，四時日月之推移也，根荄蝡息蠕動之竝育竝行也，其生不息，其化不窮。其理謂之道，其用謂之神，其主宰謂之帝，其實則一元始之也。元者何？天地之心是已。故曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」天地匪心，無以斡萬化；聖人匪心，無以裁天地。別之爲聖狂賢

Examiner Kou, School Instructor, comments: An essay on moral principle.
The mind unifies the Way of all under Heaven. The means by which the sage establishes the ultimate standard for humanity likewise consists simply in fully realizing his mind. Heaven bestows upon human beings the principle of the Supreme Ultimate. Held within, it constitutes human nature; expanded, it constitutes principle and righteousness. The mind unifies them. To discuss principle and righteousness apart from the mind is no way to speak of human nature; to establish the ultimate standard for humanity apart from the mind is no way to accord with Heaven. The common people use it daily without knowing it; rare indeed is the way of fully realizing the mind. Is the sage, then, different from other people? He merely develops his capacities on the basis of what human minds share. For the constant moral nature bestowed from above is equally allotted to all: Heaven has no deliberate intent. At the utmost realization of the mind, what all alike recognize supplies everything needed: the sage is no different from others. By bringing the human into accord with Heaven, the mind is realized to the utmost; when the mind is realized to the utmost, the ultimate standard for humanity is established. Is this not why the learning of fully realizing the mind is so great!
Now, the great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving. Thus, in the stirring of yin and yang, cold and heat; in the progression of the four seasons, sun, and moon; and in the concurrent growth and activity of rooted plants and breathing, crawling creatures [?], their generation never ceases and their transformation is inexhaustible. Their principle is called the Way; their operation is called the numinous; their governing power is called the Lord. In substance, however, it is the single primal origin that initiates them. What is this primal origin? It is precisely the mind of Heaven and Earth. Hence the saying: “In Return, do we not see the mind of Heaven and Earth!” Without mind, Heaven and Earth could not direct the myriad transformations; without mind, the sage could not regulate Heaven and Earth. Distinguished as sages, madmen, the worthy…

統之者心敘之爲君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友倫
也而統之者心以人物則表裏焉以古今則進
退焉以造化則出入焉而心管之矣口於味目
於色耳於聲其形同也獨心異乎哉夫太極生
人之初一而已粹然其性渾然其理燦然其義
皆人心之所同有也而聖人何以先得之蓋天
以統元氣也地以統元形也人以統元識也吾
以一身中天地固將會天地之心以立心相似
===
而不違者也而形生神發之後始有役於形昏
於氣溺於慾鑿於情與聖人大相遠者天之所
降安所繆盭若是哉不能盡其心而已聖人所
以與天地參者其諸盡心乎聖人之心何心也
天地之心也藏於密而不溷之以形會於精而
不雜之以氣誠於幾而不欥之以慾通於靈而
不滑之以情夫藏於密則靜深而心之淵源者
無不盡矣會於精則昭曠而心之廣大者無不
盡矣誠於幾而通於靈則大公順應而吾心之
punctuated: 愚，形也，而統之者心；秩之爲仁義禮智，性也，而統之者心；敘之爲君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友，倫也，而統之者心。以人物則表裏焉，以古今則進退焉，以造化則出入焉，而心管之矣。口於味，目於色，耳於聲，其形同也，獨心異乎哉？夫太極生人之初，一而已。粹然其性，渾然其理，燦然其義，皆人心之所同有也，而聖人何以先得之？蓋天以統元氣也，地以統元形也，人以統元識也。吾以一身中天地，固將會天地之心以立心，相似而不違者也。而形生神發之後，始有役於形、昏於氣、溺於慾、鑿於情，與聖人大相遠者。天之所降，安所繆盭若是哉？不能盡其心而已。聖人所以與天地參者，其諸盡心乎？聖人之心何心也？天地之心也。藏於密而不溷之以形，會於精而不雜之以氣，誠於幾而不欥之以慾，通於靈而不滑之以情。夫藏於密，則靜深而心之淵源者無不盡矣；會於精，則昭曠而心之廣大者無不盡矣；誠於幾而通於靈，則大公順應而吾心之
translation_en:
…and foolish: these are distinctions of embodied form, yet what unifies them is the heart-mind. Ordered as benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, they constitute human nature, yet what unifies them is the heart-mind. Arranged as ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend, they constitute human relationships, yet what unifies them is the heart-mind. In relation to people and things, it encompasses outer and inner; in relation to past and present, it advances and retreats; in relation to creation and transformation, it issues forth and enters in. The heart-mind governs all these. The mouth’s relation to flavors, the eyes’ to colors, and the ears’ to sounds are alike in their bodily constitution. Could the heart-mind alone differ?

When the Supreme Ultimate first gives birth to human beings, there is only unity. The purity of their nature, the wholeness of their principle, and the brilliance of their moral rightness are shared by all human heart-minds. How, then, does the sage apprehend them first? Heaven unifies primordial vital energy; earth unifies primordial form; humanity unifies primordial awareness. Standing with my own body between heaven and earth, I must surely comprehend their heart-mind in order to establish my own, resembling them and never departing from them. Only after bodily form comes into being and spirit begins to operate do some become enslaved by form, benighted by vital energy, submerged in desires, and distorted by feelings, thus becoming greatly estranged from the sage. How could what Heaven bestows be so perverse? It is simply that they fail to realize their heart-minds fully.

Is it not through fully realizing the heart-mind that the sage forms a triad with heaven and earth? What heart-mind does the sage possess? The heart-mind of heaven and earth. He stores it in the hidden depths without letting bodily form pollute it; gathers it in its essential purity without letting vital energy adulterate it; makes it sincere at the first stirrings without letting desires disturb it [?]; and opens it to spiritual responsiveness without letting feelings confuse it. Stored in the hidden depths, it is still and profound, and the heart-mind’s deepest sources are fully realized. Gathered in its essential purity, it is luminous and expansive, and the heart-mind’s vastness is fully realized. Sincere at the first stirrings and open to spiritual responsiveness, it responds with utter impartiality and accord, and my heart-mind’s…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
體用又一以貫之矣由是而踐形由是而盡性
由是而惇倫由是而經天綱奠地維陳藝極著
話言以知覺天下後世而彌綸參賛舉之矣孰
非盡心之功哉故曰心之精爽是謂聖人此付
形受質之始聖人衆人無以異也而踐形盡性
聖人雖欲不異于人不可也夫其所以爲人者
非外心以成身不能不與人同所以先得者非
外盡心以成聖不能不與人異同異之間人自
爲之低昂之機天曷故焉若要其始則桀可使
===
語命也跖可使語道也塗人可使爲堯舜也容
聖愚豐嗇哉然則心之所在聖人以能盡而成
聖衆人以不能盡之而爲衆人使夫人而皆知
盡心也則夫人而聖賢矣性善之說此其章章
著者也故曰聖人所以立人極者盡心而已是
故舉其類則位之所在堯舜以其盡心者垂而
爲時雍風動之休矣道之所在夫子以其盡心
者寄而爲刪述垂憲之功矣故曰得中數者立
於上焉得窮數者立於下焉道化無紀極聖人
punctuated: 體用又一以貫之矣。由是而踐形，由是而盡性，由是而惇倫，由是而經天綱、奠地維、陳藝極、著話言，以知覺天下後世，而彌綸參賛舉之矣。孰非盡心之功哉？故曰：「心之精爽，是謂聖人。」此付形受質之始，聖人衆人無以異也；而踐形盡性，聖人雖欲不異于人，不可也。夫其所以爲人者，非外心以成身，不能不與人同；所以先得者，非外盡心以成聖，不能不與人異。同異之間，人自爲之；低昂之機，天曷故焉？若要其始，則桀可使語命也，跖可使語道也，塗人可使爲堯舜也，容聖愚豐嗇哉？然則心之所在，聖人以能盡而成聖，衆人以不能盡之而爲衆人。使夫人而皆知盡心也，則夫人而聖賢矣。性善之說，此其章章著者也。故曰：「聖人所以立人極者，盡心而已。」是故舉其類，則位之所在，堯舜以其盡心者垂而爲時雍風動之休矣；道之所在，夫子以其盡心者寄而爲刪述垂憲之功矣。故曰：「得中數者立於上焉，得窮數者立於下焉。道化無紀極，聖人
translation_en:
…the substance and functioning of the mind, too, are unified by a single thread. Through this one fulfills one’s bodily form, fully realizes one’s nature, strengthens human relationships, orders Heaven’s guiding cords, establishes Earth’s supporting bonds, sets forth the standards of the arts, and records instructive sayings, thereby awakening understanding throughout the world and in later generations. The work of comprehensively ordering things and assisting the transforming powers of Heaven and Earth is thus accomplished. Which of these is not an achievement of fully realizing the mind? Thus it is said: “The purest intelligence of the mind—this is what is called a sage.” At the outset, when bodily form and material constitution are bestowed, sages and ordinary people are no different. Yet in fulfilling their bodily form and fully realizing their nature, sages could not be indistinguishable from others even if they wished.

What makes them human does not lie outside the mind through which they fulfill their persons; in this they cannot but be the same as others. What they apprehend before others does not lie outside fully realizing the mind through which they become sages; in this they cannot but differ from others. Whether they are alike or different is something people bring about themselves. What responsibility does Heaven bear for the workings by which they sink or rise? If we trace matters back to their beginning, then Jie could be made to discuss Heaven’s mandate, Zhi could be made to discuss the Way, and a person on the road could be made into a Yao or Shun. Could there be a lavish endowment for sages and a scant one for fools? Thus, as regards the mind, sages become sages because they can fully realize it, while ordinary people remain ordinary because they cannot. If everyone knew how to fully realize the mind, everyone would be a sage or worthy. Here is conspicuous evidence for the teaching that human nature is good. Thus it is said: “The means by which sages establish the ultimate standard for humanity is simply to fully realize the mind.”

To illustrate this by its different manifestations: where political position was theirs, Yao and Shun handed down what they had achieved by fully realizing their minds, bringing about the blessings of universal harmony and transforming influence like the wind. Where the Way was his, the Master, Confucius, embodied what he had achieved by fully realizing his mind in the work of editing and transmitting the classics and bequeathing enduring standards. Thus it is said: “Those who obtain a central allotment of destiny stand above; those who obtain an exhausted allotment stand below. The transforming power of the Way knows no limit; sages …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
不虛生大造生成之功用其賴此以成能乎天
地生人之心至是亦甚慊矣雖然心者天之理
也無心則天矣聖人之心與天合一其次未至
於聖者亦求盡心而已本其靜而養之之謂豫
研其幾而察之之謂精持其心而守之之謂一
而又集義以存之知言養氣以培植之勿忘勿
助以默成之則聖人先得我心之同而吾又先
得聖心之同矣奈何性晦道裂曲學淫詞籍籍
然起贅疣天地幻妄吾心防決瀾倒害如洪水
===
非孟子公言排斥不遺餘力則聖人之聖取諸
人心之同然者又孰得而知之哉說者以為孟
軻功不在禹下蓋謂此也
表
擬宋賜直講孫復五品服謝表〔慶曆四年〕
陳道基
同考試官教諭馮批用事造語俱精練不凡
殆工於四六者
同考試官學正龍批表語渾厚且有警策與
punctuated:
不虛生，大造生成之功用，其賴此以成能乎？天地生人之心，至是亦甚慊矣。雖然，心者天之理也，無心則天矣。聖人之心與天合一，其次未至於聖者，亦求盡心而已。本其靜而養之之謂豫，研其幾而察之之謂精，持其心而守之之謂一。而又集義以存之，知言養氣以培植之，勿忘勿助以默成之，則聖人先得我心之同，而吾又先得聖心之同矣。奈何性晦道裂，曲學淫詞籍籍然起，贅疣天地，幻妄吾心，防決瀾倒，害如洪水！非孟子公言排斥，不遺餘力，則聖人之聖，取諸人心之同然者，又孰得而知之哉？說者以為孟軻功不在禹下，蓋謂此也。
表
擬宋賜直講孫復五品服謝表〔慶曆四年〕
陳道基

同考試官學正龍批：表語渾厚，且有警策，與
translation_en:
…do not come into the world in vain. Does the great creative process of bringing things into being and nurturing them depend upon this to fulfill its capacities? Heaven and Earth's intention in giving birth to human beings is thereby amply satisfied. Nevertheless, the mind is Heaven's principle; without deliberate intention, it is Heaven itself. The sage's mind is one with Heaven. Those below this level, who have not yet attained sagehood, likewise need only seek to realize their minds fully. To nurture the mind on the basis of its stillness is called preparedness; to investigate its incipient movements and scrutinize them is called refinement; to hold fast to the mind and preserve it is called single-mindedness. Further, one preserves it by accumulating righteousness, cultivates it by understanding words and nourishing vital energy, and silently brings it to fulfillment by neither neglecting it nor forcing its growth. Thus the sage first apprehends what is common to my mind, and I in turn first apprehend what is common to the sage's mind [?]. Yet how has human nature become obscured and the Way fragmented, with distorted learning and licentious speech arising in noisy profusion—excrescences upon Heaven and Earth, deluding our minds, breaking through embankments and pouring forth in waves, as harmful as a flood! Had Mengzi not openly repudiated these teachings, sparing no effort, who could have known that the sage's sageliness derives from what human minds alike acknowledge? Those who say that Meng Ke's achievement was no less than Yu's presumably mean this.

Memorial

A Model Memorial of Thanks on Behalf of Sun Fu, Lecturer, upon Being Granted Robes of the Fifth Rank under the Song Dynasty 〔Fourth Year of Qingli〕

Chen Daoji

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
場中只具謝體者不同矣
考試官教諭趙批寓忠悃於陳謝之中得
宋表體
考試官學正寇批駢麗中寫出忠愛之意
可嘉
慶曆四年某月某日國子監直講臣孫復
伏蒙
聖恩賜以五品服者
帝德中虛式廣論心之益
===
皇恩下賚爰推同體之仁仰承衣被之自
天俯愧服庥之無地光榮罕儷踴躍奚勝臣誠
惶誠恐稽首頓首竊以君臣道合若股肱
心膂以相資上下志同如黼黻玄黃而共
濟煥天章以成帝服備物彩以肅臣工司
服詔於司勳儀禮謹有功之報玄衮昭乎
玄德周王隆丕享之誠蓋天命所存而等
威之攸辨寔王章是正而頒賚之有經苟
以加于無良疇足稱乎作勸自羔羊之委
punctuated:
場中只具謝體者不同矣。
考試官教諭趙批：寓忠悃於陳謝之中，得宋表體。
考試官學正寇批：駢麗中寫出忠愛之意，可嘉。
慶曆四年某月某日，國子監直講臣孫復，伏蒙聖恩賜以五品服者。
帝德中虛，式廣論心之益；皇恩下賚，爰推同體之仁。仰承衣被之自天，俯愧服庥之無地。光榮罕儷，踴躍奚勝！臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以君臣道合，若股肱心膂以相資；上下志同，如黼黻玄黃而共濟。煥天章以成帝服，備物彩以肅臣工。司服詔於司勳，儀禮謹有功之報；玄衮昭乎玄德，周王隆丕享之誠。蓋天命所存，而等威之攸辨；寔王章是正，而頒賚之有經。苟以加于無良，疇足稱乎作勸？自羔羊之委
translation_en:
…different from those examination compositions that merely observe the form of a thanksgiving memorial.
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: It conveys heartfelt loyalty through expressions of thanks and captures the style of Song thanksgiving memorials.
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: Amid its elegant parallel prose, it expresses loyalty and devotion. Commendable.
On a certain day of a certain month in the fourth year of Qingli [1044], your servant Sun Fu, Lecturer in the Directorate of Education, having humbly received the imperial favor of robes of the fifth rank, submits this memorial.
Your Majesty’s virtue is receptive and open, thereby extending the benefit of exchanges of heartfelt counsel; your imperial grace bestows gifts upon those below, thus extending the benevolence that regards ruler and ministers as one body. Looking upward, I receive the clothing and protection that descend from Heaven; looking downward, I am so ashamed to enjoy this favor that I can find no place for myself. This glory has few equals: how can I contain my leaping joy! Your servant, in utter fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows.
I humbly consider that when ruler and ministers are united in the Way, they sustain one another like legs and arms, heart and backbone; when those above and below share one purpose, they complement one another like the axe and interlaced emblems, and the black and yellow colors, of ceremonial robes. Resplendent heavenly patterns constitute the emperor’s robes; the full array of emblematic colors lends solemn dignity to his officials. The official in charge of vestments receives directions from the official in charge of merit [?]: the rules of ceremonial propriety carefully provide for rewarding meritorious service. Dark ceremonial robes manifest profound virtue: the king of Zhou displayed utmost sincerity in his magnificent offerings. For these are where Heaven’s mandate resides and where distinctions of rank and majesty are made clear. Indeed, royal regulations are thereby set aright, and the bestowal of gifts follows established rules. If such gifts were conferred upon the unworthy, how could this be called encouragement to good service? Since the unhurried bearing celebrated in “The Lamb’s Fleece” …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
蛇既邈而梁鵜之濡翼斯張漢高衣解淮
陰武功粗定孝宣寵加黃霸吏治用登賜
三公而去襜帷猶寓禮賢之悃歷四時而
稱仕宦莫逃曠位之譏奪錦龍門燕豫終
乖於雅道賜衣虎觀誇恩何補於人文是
非彰德於身豈曰祗承于帝茲蓋伏遇
○○○○
恭已守文
凝神體道
===
經天緯地淵微肇尚絅之
聖修
玉色金聲英美發黃中之峻德服靡厭乎三
澣儉以永圖武不試於五兵治綿保大匪
頒有式禮嚴在笥之將職授非宜法信終
朝之褫篤緇衣之好賢雋彙征嘉赤舄之
忠疑丞協輔謂仲尼乃斯道宗祖而太學
寔王化所關爰修釋菜之上儀迺幸辟雍
之重地橋門觀聽信三王四代之維師爼
punctuated:
蛇既邈，而梁鵜之濡翼斯張。漢高衣解淮陰，武功粗定；孝宣寵加黃霸，吏治用登。賜三公而去襜帷，猶寓禮賢之悃；歷四時而稱仕宦，莫逃曠位之譏。奪錦龍門，燕豫終乖於雅道；賜衣虎觀，誇恩何補於人文？是非彰德於身，豈曰祗承于帝？
茲蓋伏遇○○○○，恭已守文，凝神體道，經天緯地，淵微肇尚絅之聖修；玉色金聲，英美發黃中之峻德。服靡厭乎三澣，儉以永圖；武不試於五兵，治綿保大。匪頒有式，禮嚴在笥之將；職授非宜，法信終朝之褫。篤緇衣之好，賢雋彙征；嘉赤舄之忠，疑丞協輔。謂仲尼乃斯道宗祖，而太學寔王化所關，爰修釋菜之上儀，迺幸辟雍之重地。橋門觀聽，信三王四代之維師；爼
translation_en:
…that unhurried bearing has long since receded, while the spectacle of the pelican on the weir wetting its wings has become prevalent. Emperor Gao of Han took off his robe for Huaiyin, and military achievements were largely secured; Emperor Xiaoxuan extended his favor to Huang Ba, and civil administration thereby improved. Bestowing gifts upon the Three Dukes and removing carriage curtains still expressed sincere respect for worthy men; yet to count oneself an officeholder merely by passing through the four seasons could not escape the charge of neglecting one’s post. Competing for brocade at Longmen was festive amusement ultimately at odds with the proper Way; bestowing robes at the Tiger Pavilion—what could such a display of favor contribute to cultural accomplishment? These acts did not make virtue manifest in the person: how could they be called reverent service to the Lord on High?
Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty, ○○○○, who reverently maintains established institutions and concentrates your spirit upon embodying the Way. You order Heaven and Earth; profound and subtle, your sage self-cultivation begins with the modesty of wearing a plain outer garment over brocade. With the countenance of jade and the resonance of metal, your excellence expresses the lofty virtue of inward equilibrium. You do not disdain robes washed three times, practicing frugality with an enduring purpose; you do not put military might to the test with the five weapons, and your governance perpetuates the preservation of greatness. The distribution of gifts follows established forms, and ritual strictly governs the bestowal of robes kept in the chest. When an office is improperly conferred, the law assures that its insignia may be stripped away before the morning is over. You deepen the love of worthy men celebrated in “Black Robes,” and talented men advance together; you commend the loyalty represented by the red slippers, and the Advisers and Aides assist you in concert.
Deeming Zhongni the ancestral master of this Way, and the Directorate of Education’s Imperial University truly essential to royal transformation, you performed the exalted ceremony of presenting vegetable offerings and visited the august precincts of the Biyong. Those gathered at the bridge gates to see and hear witnessed, indeed, the teacher of the Three Kings and Four Dynasties [?]; the sacrificial stands…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
並輝煌昭千聖萬賢之一道似此斯文之
幸慶洽儒流豈意衰陋之軀特承
寵賚竊念臣復學未通方志惟信古以聖人
之心不可復見著春秋尊王發微以君子
之節在有不為居泰山安貧俟命自分
明時之永逸不圖
休命之荐臨石介颺言本出門墻師友之義
輔臣聯薦深慚道德經術之褒濫竽講筵
厠員胄學豈有康侯之望特紆晉錫之蕃
===
使後大夫載叨緋服今趨
禁闥乃佩銀魚敢云儒者之榮竊忝縉紳之
盛臣敢不益堅晚節自勵初心服美而思
瞻就
日望雲之悃佩華而玩達潜淵在渚之機啓
乃心以沃心闡一德以輔德奉謀謨而補
衮用輸韈線之能陳仁義以彌縫上徹
宸旒之聽伏願
滋休純嘏
punctuated:
並輝煌，昭千聖萬賢之一道。似此斯文之幸，慶洽儒流。豈意衰陋之軀，特承寵賚！
竊念臣復，學未通方，志惟信古。以聖人之心不可復見，著春秋，尊王發微；以君子之節在有不為，居泰山，安貧俟命。自分明時之永逸，不圖休命之荐臨。石介颺言，本出門墻師友之義；輔臣聯薦，深慚道德經術之褒。濫竽講筵，厠員胄學。豈有康侯之望，特紆晉錫之蕃！使後大夫，載叨緋服；今趨禁闥，乃佩銀魚。敢云儒者之榮，竊忝縉紳之盛。
臣敢不益堅晚節，自勵初心！服美而思瞻就日望雲之悃，佩華而玩達潜淵在渚之機。啓乃心以沃心，闡一德以輔德。奉謀謨而補衮，用輸韈線之能；陳仁義以彌縫，上徹宸旒之聽。伏願滋休純嘏。
translation_en:
…shine brilliantly together, illuminating the single Way shared by the thousand sages and myriad worthies. Such good fortune for our cultural tradition spreads rejoicing throughout the ranks of scholars. Who could have imagined that this aged and humble person would receive Your Majesty’s special favor and gifts!
I humbly reflect that I, your servant Fu, have not attained comprehensive learning; my aspiration has been only to trust antiquity. Because the sage’s mind could no longer be seen directly, I wrote on the Spring and Autumn Annals, honoring royal authority and elucidating its subtle meanings. Because a gentleman’s integrity lies in refusing certain actions, I dwelt on Mount Tai, content in poverty and awaiting my allotted fate. I assumed that I would remain forever in retirement under this enlightened reign, never expecting Your gracious commands to arrive repeatedly. Shi Jie’s outspoken praise arose from the obligations binding teachers and friends within the scholarly community. Your assisting ministers jointly recommended me, and their praise of my moral character and classical learning leaves me deeply abashed. Unworthily filling a place at the imperial lectures, I joined the staff of the Directorate of Education. How could I possess the prestige of the lord of Kang? Yet Your Majesty has graciously bestowed abundant gifts, as in the Changes’ hexagram Jin, “Advance.” “An envoy, then a grand master” [?]—I again undeservedly received crimson robes; now, entering the palace gates, I wear a silver fish-shaped insignia. Dare I call this an honor to a scholar? I merely feel ashamed to occupy a place among the splendid ranks of officials.
How could your servant fail to strengthen his integrity in his later years and renew his original resolve! Wearing these fine robes, I contemplate the sincere devotion expressed in looking toward the sun and gazing at the clouds; bearing this splendid insignia, I ponder the circumstances governing advancement and withdrawal, whether hidden in the depths or resting by the islet. I shall open my heart to nourish Your Majesty’s heart and expound undivided virtue to assist Your virtue. Offering counsel to mend the imperial robe, I shall contribute my meager ability, no more than thread for stockings; setting forth benevolence and righteousness to remedy deficiencies, I shall seek to reach Your imperial hearing. I humbly wish that Your blessings and abundant good fortune may increase…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
典學緝熈
挈綱領以整齊萬方
美黼冕而懷柔羣祀
恩弘挾纊小民毋曰怨咨
化廣素絲有官皆以安吉斯民樂樂利利均
荷燠衣之歡惟
皇子子孫孫丕振垂裳之治臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第參塲
策
第一問
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批我
皇上君臣同遊上之媲美
punctuated:
典學緝熈，挈綱領以整齊萬方，美黼冕而懷柔羣祀。恩弘挾纊，小民毋曰怨咨；化廣素絲，有官皆以安吉。斯民樂樂利利，均荷燠衣之歡；惟皇子子孫孫，丕振垂裳之治。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第參塲
策
第一問
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批：我皇上君臣同遊，上之媲美
translation_en:
…may Your Majesty steadfastly pursue learning and continue in increasing brilliance, grasp the essential principles to bring order to all regions, and adorn the embroidered robes and ceremonial crown while propitiating all the spirits receiving sacrifice. May your bounty spread the warmth of silk padding, so that the common people voice no resentment or lament; may your transforming influence extend the integrity symbolized by white silk, so that all officials enjoy peace and good fortune. These people rejoice in their joys and benefit from their benefits, all sharing the delight of receiving warm clothing. May the imperial sons and grandsons magnificently perpetuate the effortless rule symbolized by letting the robes hang down. Your servant cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling reverence as he gazes toward Heaven and looks up to the Sage. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zheng Yuanshao
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Our emperor and his ministers delight together [?]; in matching the excellence of …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖遠之超邁唐虞子能一一敷揚使天下傳而誦之是必涵濡
聖化久矣可以科目士盡子哉
同考試官教諭黎批是篇氣昌詞偉志遠謀恭
聖天子中興之治所以望於臣下者不在是哉
考試官教諭趙批歷叙唐虞賡歌之盛而
聖祖
皇上實遠紹之此作能道其實且厚望焉是堯舜吾
君之志也得士如此良以自慶矣
考試官學正寇批君臣同遊之盛夫人能
===
言之至於治道之所由成則鮮克知者子能及此
可以為天下士矣
世之隆也其運之相乘乎治之興也其道
之相成乎蓋機會之相乘者運也而世之
隆污繫之矣上下之相成者道也而治之
興替繫之矣夫惟乘間世之運則上下之
道不期而自合夫惟協相成之道則雍熈
之化不戒而自孚此有虞之風所以獨盛
於前我
punctuated:
聖祖，遠之超邁唐虞。子能一一敷揚，使天下傳而誦之，是必涵濡聖化久矣，可以科目士盡子哉？
同考試官教諭黎批：是篇氣昌詞偉，志遠謀恭。聖天子中興之治，所以望於臣下者，不在是哉？
考試官教諭趙批：歷叙唐虞賡歌之盛，而聖祖、皇上實遠紹之。此作能道其實，且厚望焉，是堯舜吾君之志也。得士如此，良以自慶矣。
考試官學正寇批：君臣同遊之盛，夫人能言之；至於治道之所由成，則鮮克知者。子能及此，可以為天下士矣。
世之隆也，其運之相乘乎？治之興也，其道之相成乎？蓋機會之相乘者，運也，而世之隆污繫之矣；上下之相成者，道也，而治之興替繫之矣。夫惟乘間世之運，則上下之道不期而自合；夫惟協相成之道，則雍熈之化不戒而自孚。此有虞之風所以獨盛於前，我
translation_en:
…the Sage Founder and, reaching further back, surpassing Tang and Yu. You have expounded each point, enabling all under Heaven to pass it on and recite it. Surely you have long been steeped in the sage ruler’s transforming influence. Could the designation of an examination scholar encompass all that you are?
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: This essay has abundant spirit and magnificent diction; its aspirations are lofty and its counsels reverent. Is this not what the sage Son of Heaven expects of his subjects in his work of restoring flourishing government?
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: The essay recounts in detail the flourishing exchange of songs under Tang and Yu, whose distant legacy the Sage Founder and His Majesty have truly continued. This composition expresses the reality of this achievement and also sets high hopes upon it: it manifests the aspiration to make our ruler a Yao or a Shun. To obtain a scholar such as this is truly cause for congratulating ourselves.
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: Anyone can speak of the splendor of ruler and ministers enjoying excursions together. Yet few can understand how the Way of government is brought to fulfillment. Your ability to reach this understanding qualifies you as a scholar of all under Heaven.
When an age flourishes, is it because its favorable circumstances build upon one another? When good government arises, is it because its guiding principles bring one another to fulfillment? For the convergence of opportunities constitutes the fortunes of an age, and upon these depend its flourishing or decline. Mutual fulfillment between those above and those below constitutes the Way, and upon this depend the rise or fall of good government. Only when the rare favorable fortunes of an age are seized do the ways of those above and below accord spontaneously, without prior arrangement. Only when they harmonize in the Way of mutual fulfillment does the transforming influence of harmony and prosperity spontaneously inspire trust, without admonition. This is why the influence of Youyu flourished preeminently in antiquity, and why our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
祖宗
聖皇所以嗣響於今而非漢唐以下所得彷彿
其萬一也執事策諸生而欲鋪張揚厲以
鳴
國家之盛顧愚何足以知之蓋甞讀易而得
君臣相與之道矣上天下澤曰履孔子傳
之曰君子以辯上下定民志而其傳履之
彖則曰履帝位而不疚光明也乾下坤上
曰泰孔子傳之曰后以裁成天地之道輔
===
相天地之宜以左右民而其傳泰之彖則
曰天地交而萬物通也上下交而其志同
也蓋上下之分不定無以示光明不疚之
履而上下之志不交又何以成裁成輔相
之治哉粤昔唐虞二帝中天而興應運以
生廣四聰於畢達孚庶尹於允諧臣鄰弼
直藹都俞吁咈之風明良遭逢慶元首股
肱之盛然勅天時幾之儆不忘於喜起賡
歌之中蓋運之相乘至有虞而特隆故道
punctuated:
祖宗、聖皇所以嗣響於今，而非漢唐以下所得彷彿其萬一也。執事策諸生，而欲鋪張揚厲，以鳴國家之盛，顧愚何足以知之？

蓋甞讀易而得君臣相與之道矣。上天下澤曰履，孔子傳之曰：「君子以辯上下，定民志。」而其傳履之彖則曰：「履帝位而不疚，光明也。」乾下坤上曰泰，孔子傳之曰：「后以裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」而其傳泰之彖則曰：「天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。」蓋上下之分不定，無以示光明不疚之履；而上下之志不交，又何以成裁成輔相之治哉？

粤昔唐虞二帝，中天而興，應運以生。廣四聰於畢達，孚庶尹於允諧。臣鄰弼直，藹都俞吁咈之風；明良遭逢，慶元首股肱之盛。然勅天時幾之儆，不忘於喜起賡歌之中。蓋運之相乘，至有虞而特隆，故道
translation_en:
…and why our imperial ancestors and our sage emperor have continued its resonance down to the present—something of which the Han, Tang, and subsequent dynasties could not approximate even one ten-thousandth. You, honored examiners, have posed policy questions to us students, wishing us to expound and extol the dynasty’s flourishing. Yet how could someone as ignorant as I adequately comprehend it?

I have, however, read the Book of Changes and gained an understanding of the Way by which ruler and ministers engage with one another. Heaven above and the lake below constitute Treading (Lü). Confucius’s commentary says: “The noble man thereby distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people’s aspirations.” His commentary on the judgment of Treading says: “He treads the imperial position without fault: this is luminous clarity.” Qian below and Kun above constitute Peace (Tai). Confucius’s commentary says: “The sovereign thereby shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting to Heaven and Earth, and thus guides and aids the people.” His commentary on the judgment of Peace says: “Heaven and Earth interact, and the myriad things communicate; those above and those below interact, and their purposes are united.” If the distinctions between those above and below are not established, there is no way to manifest the luminous and faultless conduct of Treading. Yet if their purposes do not communicate, how can government accomplish this work of shaping, completing, and assisting?

Long ago, the two emperors of Tang and Yu rose to the zenith, born in response to the destined course of their age. They extended their hearing in all four directions until everything reached them, and inspired trust among the many officials in true harmony. Their ministers and close attendants assisted and corrected them; an atmosphere of frank assent and dissent prevailed. Enlightened rulers and worthy ministers encountered one another, rejoicing in the flourishing partnership of the head with its arms and legs. Yet amid their joy in rising to service and their exchanges of song, they did not forget the admonitions to heed Heaven and attend to the timing and first stirrings of affairs [?]. The convergence of favorable circumstances reached particular fullness under Youyu; therefore, the Way…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之相成至有虞而特著也嗣是如湯之於
伊尹則一德之咸有也高宗之於傅說則
麴糱鹽梅之交修也周室之盛君歌鹿鳴
以燕其臣臣歌天保以答其君而卷阿之
詩則召公從遊之作也然周行之求遂歌
之矢猶有虞廷時幾之意焉要皆運之會
也道之成也漢唐以還風斯下矣洛陽宴
會讓三傑之不如漢祖所以興炎劉之業
丹霄侍從諒魏徵之踈慢唐宗所以成貞
===
觀之治若夫杯酒猜疑之釋藝祖之優功
臣也賞花釣魚之賦仁宗之宴近僚也要
其君臣之遇亦足以稱一時之盛然宴遊
之儀雖侈飭戒之實或踈蓋其運寢微故
其道寢降仰窺賡歌之風則旣遠矣彼善
於此其惟丹霄之宴猶庶幾存交儆之遺
乎君子未可以停仆一事病之也宋祚旣
移胡元竊偕天運積否而開泰人心厭亂
而思治此其時矣洪惟我
punctuated:
之相成，至有虞而特著也。嗣是，如湯之於伊尹，則一德之咸有也；高宗之於傅說，則麴糱鹽梅之交修也。周室之盛，君歌《鹿鳴》以燕其臣，臣歌《天保》以答其君，而《卷阿》之詩，則召公從遊之作也。然周行之求、遂歌之矢，猶有虞廷時幾之意焉。要皆運之會也，道之成也。
漢唐以還，風斯下矣。洛陽宴會，讓三傑之不如，漢祖所以興炎劉之業；丹霄侍從，諒魏徵之踈慢，唐宗所以成貞觀之治。若夫杯酒猜疑之釋，藝祖之優功臣也；賞花釣魚之賦，仁宗之宴近僚也。要其君臣之遇，亦足以稱一時之盛。然宴遊之儀雖侈，飭戒之實或踈。蓋其運寢微，故其道寢降，仰窺賡歌之風，則旣遠矣。彼善於此，其惟丹霄之宴，猶庶幾存交儆之遺乎？君子未可以停仆一事病之也。
宋祚旣移，胡元竊偕，天運積否而開泰，人心厭亂而思治，此其時矣。洪惟我
translation_en:
…the mutual fulfillment of the Way became especially manifest under Shun of Youyu. Thereafter, in the relationship of Tang to Yi Yin, both possessed a single virtue; in that of Gaozong to Fu Yue, they cultivated one another like yeast and malt in brewing, or salt and plums in seasoning. At the height of the Zhou house, the ruler sang “The Deer Call” to feast his ministers, and the ministers sang “Heaven Protects” in reply to their ruler. The poem “The Winding Hill” was composed by the Duke of Shao while accompanying the king on an excursion. Yet its seeking men to fill the Zhou ranks and its offering of a song [?] still conveyed the spirit of the court of Shun: vigilance over each moment and the first stirrings of events. All these, in essence, were conjunctions of historical fortune and fulfillments of the Way.
From the Han and Tang onward, this ethos declined. At the banquet in Luoyang, the Han founder acknowledged that he did not equal his three outstanding ministers: this was how he established the enterprise of the Liu house, whose dynastic virtue was fire. At Danxiao, the Tang emperor excused Wei Zheng’s apparent negligence and lack of deference while attending him: this was how he brought about the good government of the Zhenguan reign. As for dispelling suspicion over cups of wine, this was the Song founder’s generous treatment of meritorious ministers; composing verses while admiring flowers and fishing was Emperor Renzong’s way of feasting his close officials. Taken together, these encounters between rulers and ministers were sufficient to be called the glories of their respective times. Yet although the ceremonies of feasting and excursions were lavish, the substance of admonition and warning was sometimes neglected. As their historical fortune gradually weakened, their Way gradually declined; looking back to the ethos of exchanging songs at Shun’s court, they were already far removed from it. If one was better than another, was it not the banquet at Danxiao that perhaps still preserved something of the legacy of mutual admonition? A gentleman should not condemn the emperor solely for the incident of “stopping and toppling” [?].
Once the Song’s dynastic mandate had passed away and the non-Han Yuan had usurped it [?], Heaven’s course, after accumulated obstruction, opened into flourishing. People’s hearts had grown weary of disorder and longed for good government. This was precisely the moment. Reverently considering our …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝挺生淮甸肇創函夏扶綱常於再
造廓宇宙於重新是蓋乗撥亂反正之運
啓旋乾轉坤之業劉基天授之說已識
帝王之有眞矣一時明良之盛振古罕儷
大誥三篇首冠以君臣同遊之言其虞廷賡歌
之遺響乎拾失搏過不忘上下交修之念
其勅天時幾之微意乎觀其於儒臣宋濂
也或閱江有樓而
特命為之記以紀其事非但侈登臨之勝蓋欲
===
藉遊覽以動保治之思也或賜飲至醉而
親為之賦又
命侍臣皆為醉學士歌非徒示優老之恩蓋欲
使後世知同遊之樂也寓交儆之意於豫
逸之中篤不忘之懷於晉接之頃他如
召見賜坐之歡下逮不一經史時事之訪聽
納惟虛豈非我
聖祖以相成之道開統天之業以為貽謀燕翼
之圖耶
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝挺生淮甸，肇創函夏，扶綱常於再造，廓宇宙於重新，是蓋乗撥亂反正之運，啓旋乾轉坤之業。劉基天授之說，已識帝王之有眞矣。一時明良之盛，振古罕儷。《大誥》三篇，首冠以君臣同遊之言，其虞廷賡歌之遺響乎？拾失搏過，不忘上下交修之念，其勅天時幾之微意乎？觀其於儒臣宋濂也，或閱江有樓，而特命為之記，以紀其事，非但侈登臨之勝，蓋欲藉遊覽以動保治之思也。或賜飲至醉，而親為之賦，又命侍臣皆為《醉學士歌》，非徒示優老之恩，蓋欲使後世知同遊之樂也。寓交儆之意於豫逸之中，篤不忘之懷於晉接之頃。他如召見賜坐之歡，下逮不一；經史時事之訪，聽納惟虛。豈非我聖祖以相成之道，開統天之業，以為貽謀燕翼之圖耶？
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao arose preeminent in the Huai region and founded anew the Chinese realm. He restored the cardinal relationships and constant moral norms as he rebuilt the polity, and brought order throughout the world as he renewed it. He thus took advantage of the destined moment to quell disorder and restore proper rule, inaugurating an enterprise that turned Heaven and Earth about. Liu Ji’s account of Heaven’s bestowal had already recognized that here was a true emperor. The flourishing partnership of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers at that time had scarcely an equal in all antiquity. The three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) open with words about ruler and ministers enjoying excursions together: was this not an echo of the responsive songs at Shun’s court? Remedying omissions and correcting faults [?], he never forgot that those above and below should cultivate one another. Was this not the subtle intent of reverently attending to Heaven’s commands, the proper times, and the incipient signs of affairs [?]?

Consider his treatment of the Confucian minister Song Lian. When there was a tower for viewing the river, he specially commanded Song to compose an account recording the undertaking. This was not merely to extol the splendid prospect from its heights: he wished to use sightseeing to stir reflection on preserving good government. On another occasion, he bestowed wine upon Song until he became drunk and personally composed a rhapsody for him; he also commanded all his attendant ministers to compose a “Song of the Drunken Academician.” This was not merely a display of favor toward an elderly minister: he wished later generations to know the pleasure of ruler and ministers enjoying excursions together. Amid ease and recreation, he embedded the intention of mutual admonition; in receiving his ministers, he deepened his enduring affection for them. Other instances, such as the pleasure of being summoned to an audience and granted a seat, extended to many below him. When consulting them about the Classics, histories, and current affairs, he listened and accepted their counsel with an open mind. Was this not our sagely founder employing the principle of mutual assistance to inaugurate an enterprise of universal rule, thereby devising plans to leave to his descendants for their peace and security?

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承運祚寢隆上下一體相得益章如幾
密之商夜分乃退則
成祖之於七臣也協心之戒
誥詞親增則
仁廟之於五臣也或推心置腹而從容咨訪於
燕見之時或
禁苑賜遊而商議可否於裁决之際則
宣廟
英廟之遇臣猶可想見也如楊士奇李賢諸臣
===
之所紀錄傳播海宇歷歷若覩此其道之
相成而治日以興有由然矣賡歌卷阿之
風其再振乎肆我
皇上聖神天縱嗣纂丕圖宣
累葉之重光冠百王而獨盛是蓋當世道一新
之會適禮樂百年之期
中興全盛之運夫固天啓於
今日矣一時弼理之臣翕然響應
萬幾之暇或
punctuated:
列聖相承，運祚寢隆，上下一體，相得益章。如幾密之商，夜分乃退，則成祖之於七臣也；協心之戒，誥詞親增，則仁廟之於五臣也。或推心置腹，而從容咨訪於燕見之時；或禁苑賜遊，而商議可否於裁决之際，則宣廟、英廟之遇臣，猶可想見也。如楊士奇、李賢諸臣之所紀錄，傳播海宇，歷歷若覩。此其道之相成，而治日以興，有由然矣。賡歌、卷阿之風，其再振乎！

肆我皇上，聖神天縱，嗣纂丕圖，宣累葉之重光，冠百王而獨盛。是蓋當世道一新之會，適禮樂百年之期，中興全盛之運，夫固天啓於今日矣。一時弼理之臣，翕然響應。萬幾之暇，或
translation_en:
Successive sage sovereigns inherited the throne; the dynasty’s fortunes gradually flourished, and the unity and mutual accord of ruler and ministers became ever more manifest. When confidential deliberations continued until the ministers withdrew at midnight, this was Chengzu’s relationship with his seven ministers. When words admonishing ministers to act with one heart were personally added to an imperial pronouncement, this was Renzong’s relationship with his five ministers. Sometimes the sovereign opened his heart and consulted them at leisure during informal audiences; sometimes he granted them excursions in the imperial gardens and discussed the merits of proposals when making decisions. Thus we can still envision how Xuanzong and Yingzong treated their ministers. The records made by such ministers as Yang Shiqi and Li Xian circulated throughout the realm, presenting these events as vividly as if they were before our eyes. That ruler and ministers complemented one another in this way, and that good government flourished day by day, surely had its reasons. Had the spirit of the exchanged songs of ruler and ministers and of “Winding Hills” (Juan e) come to life again?

Now our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom and divine intelligence, has succeeded to the great imperial enterprise, displaying the accumulated brilliance of successive generations and surpassing a hundred kings in his unrivaled splendor. This is indeed a moment when the order of the age is renewed, coinciding with a century of rites and music. Heaven has surely inaugurated today an era of resurgent and consummate prosperity. The ministers assisting in government have responded in unison. In moments of leisure amid his myriad affairs of state, sometimes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
召見便殿不厭密勿之咨或
賜遊西苑特陪
翠華之御
親灑宸翰
頒賜諸臣如
穀祗先蠶壇之賦曰農桑爲先曰以示無逸即
豳風七月之意也曰
陽春和暢曰于樂康年即對時育物之仁也
同遊樂府之作曰薰風解慍但願民康即虞
===
舜南風之奏也曰
但得甘霖降欣然慰老農即商湯桑林之思
也撫盈成亨嘉之運猶切忠良夾持之儆
當逸暇遊觀之時不忘敬承
皇天之念
奎章睿藻昭回雲漢
寶軸瑤函輝映典謨非草茅所能盡述豈非我
皇上以相成之道弘
烈祖之猷而追虞廷周室之盛耶漢唐宋之君
punctuated: 召見便殿，不厭密勿之咨；或賜遊西苑，特陪翠華之御。親灑宸翰，頒賜諸臣，如《穀祗先蠶壇之賦》，曰「農桑爲先」，曰「以示無逸」，即《豳風》《七月》之意也；曰「陽春和暢」，曰「于樂康年」，即對時育物之仁也。《同遊樂府》之作，曰「薰風解慍，但願民康」，即虞舜《南風》之奏也；曰「但得甘霖降，欣然慰老農」，即商湯桑林之思也。撫盈成亨嘉之運，猶切忠良夾持之儆；當逸暇遊觀之時，不忘敬承皇天之念。奎章睿藻，昭回雲漢；寶軸瑤函，輝映典謨，非草茅所能盡述。豈非我皇上以相成之道弘烈祖之猷，而追虞廷周室之盛耶？漢唐宋之君
translation_en:
…summons them to audience in a side hall, never tiring of earnest consultation; at other times he grants them excursions in the Western Park, specially admitting them to accompany the imperial procession beneath its kingfisher-feather banners. He personally writes imperial compositions and bestows them upon his ministers. For example, the Rhapsody on the Altars of Grain, Earth, and the First Silkworm Cultivator [?] says, “Farming and sericulture come first,” and “To demonstrate freedom from idleness.” This expresses the meaning of “The Seventh Month” in the “Airs of Bin” in the Book of Odes. It says, “The spring sunshine is mild and genial,” and “Oh, rejoice in a year of well-being”: this is the benevolence that nurtures all things in accordance with the seasons. The Music Bureau poem “An Excursion Together” says, “The balmy wind dispels resentment; I wish only for the people’s well-being.” This is like the performance of “The South Wind” by Shun of Yu. It says, “If only timely rain would fall, gladly would I comfort the old farmers”: this is the concern shown by Tang of Shang at the Mulberry Grove.

Presiding over an age of full achievement and auspicious prosperity, he still takes deeply to heart the admonition to seek the support of loyal and worthy ministers. During leisure and sightseeing, he does not forget reverently to serve August Heaven. His imperial writings and sagely compositions shine across the Milky Way; their precious scrolls and jeweled cases rival in splendor the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents. These are more than a humble scholar outside official service can fully recount. Is this not our Emperor’s way of enlarging the plans of his illustrious ancestors through mutual assistance between ruler and ministers, and of matching the flourishing courts of Yu and Zhou? As for the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
又何足言哉雖然虞之賡歌則曰勅天命
夏之籲俊則曰尊帝商之克卽則曰丕釐
耿命周之灼見則曰敬事上帝我
祖宗敬
天之實信圖政親賢之本創業守成之基也我
皇上敬一有箴五箴有註播告臣民之語無非
躬行心得之餘純心者用賢之要恭默者
交修之幾則夫精神意氣之感雲龍風虎
之從固有不能外焉者經緯化成之績泰
===
和極治之盛夫豈偶然之故哉執事所謂
聖德淵衷
神謨睿思得非有見於是耶若夫益勵謨明弼
諧之忠以為
聖天子奉
天勤民之助以綿億萬年豐亨豫泰之業者則
固
廟堂輔弼者之任也而豈韋布所得與聞哉
第二問
punctuated:
又何足言哉！雖然，虞之賡歌則曰勅天命，夏之籲俊則曰尊帝，商之克卽則曰丕釐耿命，周之灼見則曰敬事上帝。我祖宗敬天之實，信圖政親賢之本、創業守成之基也。我皇上敬一有箴，五箴有註，播告臣民之語，無非躬行心得之餘。純心者，用賢之要；恭默者，交修之幾。則夫精神意氣之感、雲龍風虎之從，固有不能外焉者。經緯化成之績、泰和極治之盛，夫豈偶然之故哉！執事所謂聖德淵衷、神謨睿思，得非有見於是耶？若夫益勵謨明弼諧之忠，以為聖天子奉天勤民之助，以綿億萬年豐亨豫泰之業者，則固廟堂輔弼者之任也，而豈韋布所得與聞哉！

第二問
translation_en:
…what more need be said of them! Nevertheless, the answering song at the court of Shun spoke of “heeding Heaven’s mandate”; Xia’s summons to the worthy spoke of “honoring the Lord on High”; Shang’s ability to attain its position [?] spoke of “greatly administering the illustrious mandate”; and Zhou’s clear discernment spoke of “reverently serving the Lord on High.” Our imperial ancestors’ genuine reverence for Heaven was indeed the root of their efforts to govern and draw close to the worthy, and the foundation for establishing the dynasty and preserving its accomplishments. Our Emperor has composed an Admonition on Reverence for the One and commentaries on the Five Admonitions. The words he proclaims to his subjects all flow from his personal practice and inward understanding. Purifying the mind is essential to employing the worthy; reverent silence is the incipient basis of mutual moral cultivation. Thus the mutual responsiveness of spirit and purpose, and the following of clouds after dragons and winds after tigers, necessarily fall within this principle. Could the achievements of ordering the realm and bringing its moral transformation to completion, or the flourishing of supreme harmony and perfect government, possibly have come about by chance? When you speak of His Majesty’s sagely virtue and profound heart, his divine counsels and sagacious reflections, surely you have perceived this?

As for further strengthening the loyalty expressed in enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance, thereby helping the sagely Son of Heaven serve Heaven and labor for the people, and perpetuating an enterprise of abundance, prosperity, contentment, and peace for countless ages: this is assuredly the responsibility of the ministers who assist him at court. How could a commoner in plain cloth presume to have a part in such deliberations!

Second Question

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
丘行義
同考試官教諭費批形容字畫之精而本諸
皇上之心學忠悃未有涯也敬服敬服
同考試官教諭方批歷代字學子旣詳其由
來而末復以
聖天子之心畫遠出羲皇之上是可以
獻矣
考試官教諭趙批備述我
朝正韻謂得字學之正傳而
===
皇上超出千古之見又不專於形象點畫吾之取子豈獨以其文哉
考試官學正寇批大小篆隸之變子能一
一道之又於
宸翰之妙言之懇至是可以觀子之奇矣
聖人其猶天乎甞誦棫樸之詩而知聖人
之書法所由章誦文王之詩而知聖人之
心法所由立棫樸之詩曰倬彼雲漢爲章
於天語天文也而書法於是乎肇其始文
王之詩曰上天之載無聲無臭語天道也
punctuated:
丘行義

同考試官教諭費批：形容字畫之精，而本諸皇上之心學，忠悃未有涯也。敬服！敬服！

同考試官教諭方批：歷代字學，子旣詳其由來，而末復以聖天子之心畫遠出羲皇之上，是可以獻矣。

考試官教諭趙批：備述我朝正韻，謂得字學之正傳，而皇上超出千古之見，又不專於形象點畫。吾之取子，豈獨以其文哉？

考試官學正寇批：大小篆隸之變，子能一一道之；又於宸翰之妙，言之懇至，是可以觀子之奇矣。

聖人其猶天乎？甞誦《棫樸》之詩，而知聖人之書法所由章；誦《文王》之詩，而知聖人之心法所由立。《棫樸》之詩曰：「倬彼雲漢，爲章於天。」語天文也，而書法於是乎肇其始。《文王》之詩曰：「上天之載，無聲無臭。」語天道也。
translation_en:
Qiu Xingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: You describe the refinement of written characters and their strokes, grounding it in His Majesty’s learning of the mind. Your loyal sincerity knows no bounds. I admire you! I admire you!

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: You have explained in detail the origins and development of the study of writing through successive dynasties. At the end, you further place the sagely Son of Heaven’s “depiction of the mind” far above that of Emperor Xi (Fuxi). This is worthy of presentation to the throne.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: You give a full account of our dynasty’s Correct Rhymes, saying that it embodies the orthodox transmission of the study of writing. His Majesty’s insight, surpassing that of all past ages, moreover extends beyond forms, dots, and strokes. Could my selection of you be based solely on your composition?

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: You can explain, one by one, the transformations of large-seal, small-seal, and clerical scripts. You also speak with utmost sincerity of the marvelous qualities of the imperial calligraphy. Here one can perceive your exceptional talent.

Is the sage perhaps like Heaven? I have recited the ode “The Oak Clumps” (Yupu) and thereby understood how the sage’s art of writing becomes manifest; I have recited the ode “King Wen” (Wen Wang) and thereby understood how the sage’s method of cultivating the mind is established. “The Oak Clumps” says: “Resplendent is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in Heaven.” It speaks of Heaven’s patterns, and here the art of writing has its beginning. “King Wen” says: “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” It speaks of the Way of Heaven …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
而心法於是乎啓其原惟聖人靜與天爲
體而心法之存於中者合天之道故聖人
動與天爲用而書法之形諸外者則天之
文二者體用一原顯微無間此聖人之所
以與天爲一者也知心法則知書法矣知
天則知聖人矣請因明問而敬陳之粤昔
道涵於太始而不能不會於聖人道會於
聖人而不能不闡於卦畫於是伏羲始畫
八卦以通神明之德以類萬物之情故周
===
子曰聖人之精因畫以示然則畫也者固
聖人之所以畫乎其心者也心畫形而字
文立矣自伏羲而神農而黃帝而堯而禹
其心法之傳者本無不同曰龍書曰穗書
曰鳥書曰龜書曰鍾鼎其書法之善者未
嘗或異猶風雨露雷之化不同其爲上天
於穆之運者則一也卽其尤盛者而論之
伏羲之後其惟黃帝矣乎蓋黃帝之有六
書也猶伏羲之有八卦也道本於易簡而
punctuated:
而心法於是乎啓其原。惟聖人靜與天爲體，而心法之存於中者合天之道；故聖人動與天爲用，而書法之形諸外者則天之文。二者體用一原，顯微無間，此聖人之所以與天爲一者也。知心法則知書法矣，知天則知聖人矣。請因明問而敬陳之。
粤昔道涵於太始，而不能不會於聖人；道會於聖人，而不能不闡於卦畫。於是伏羲始畫八卦，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情。故周子曰：「聖人之精，因畫以示。」然則畫也者，固聖人之所以畫乎其心者也。心畫形而字文立矣。自伏羲而神農而黃帝而堯而禹，其心法之傳者本無不同。曰龍書，曰穗書，曰鳥書，曰龜書，曰鍾鼎，其書法之善者未嘗或異。猶風雨露雷之化不同，其爲上天於穆之運者則一也。卽其尤盛者而論之，伏羲之後，其惟黃帝矣乎！蓋黃帝之有六書也，猶伏羲之有八卦也。道本於易簡而
translation_en:
…and here the teaching of the mind finds its source. In stillness, the sage shares Heaven’s substance, and the teaching of the mind preserved within accords with Heaven’s Way. Thus, in activity, the sage shares Heaven’s functioning, and the art of writing manifested outwardly takes Heaven’s patterns as its model. These two—substance and function—have a single source; between the manifest and the subtle there is no separation. This is how the sage is one with Heaven. To understand the teaching of the mind is to understand the art of writing; to understand Heaven is to understand the sage. Allow me respectfully to expound upon this in response to your illuminating question.
In remote antiquity, the Way was contained within the primordial beginning and could not but converge in the sages. Having converged in the sages, it could not but be made manifest in the lines of the trigrams. Thus Fuxi first drew the Eight Trigrams, thereby communicating with the powers of spiritual beings and classifying the dispositions of the myriad things. Hence Master Zhou said: “The sage’s essential understanding is revealed through the drawn lines.” These lines, then, are precisely the means by which the sage depicts his mind. Once these depictions of the mind took shape, written characters were established. From Fuxi through Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Yu, the teaching of the mind they transmitted was fundamentally the same. Whether called dragon script, grain-ear script, bird script, tortoise script, or bell-and-cauldron inscriptions, their excellence in the art of writing never differed. Likewise, although the transforming effects of wind, rain, dew, and thunder differ, they are one as manifestations of august Heaven’s profound workings. To discuss the most outstanding among them: after Fuxi, surely it was the Yellow Emperor! For the Yellow Emperor’s possession of the Six Principles of Writing was like Fuxi’s possession of the Eight Trigrams. The Way is rooted in ease and simplicity, and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
用極乎天地自象形指事會意諧聲轉注
假借之義立而天下之道備矣比其類而
列之許氏發三耦之微順其序而推之鄭
氏闡相承之祕朱子亦曰心性等字理自
流出則六書之義自倉頡撰之非倉頡始
之必其親得於黃帝心法之傳者也故竊
論書法之傳自伏羲而創其始若剖混沌
而開之者也自黃帝而闡其詳若繼開闢
而疆理之者也伏羲其先天矣乎黃帝其
後天矣乎嗣有作者不可尚矣慨六書之
變而爲大篆也史籀所述也文字漸備而
書法之本旨寢微周宣之德其衰矣大篆
之變而爲小篆也李斯實紛更之簡便日
趨而書法之漸滅殆盡嬴秦之罪莫贖矣
漢光武頒十札於方國唐太宗賜飛白於
馬周宋太宗勒孝經於碑陰賜吏治於棘
寺書法非不善也然皆務翰墨之工無裨
身心之實或深刻之成性或閨門之多慚
punctuated:
用極乎天地。自象形、指事、會意、諧聲、轉注、假借之義立，而天下之道備矣。比其類而列之，許氏發三耦之微；順其序而推之，鄭氏闡相承之祕。朱子亦曰：「心性等字，理自流出。」則六書之義，自倉頡撰之，非倉頡始之，必其親得於黃帝心法之傳者也。故竊論書法之傳，自伏羲而創其始，若剖混沌而開之者也；自黃帝而闡其詳，若繼開闢而疆理之者也。伏羲其先天矣乎！黃帝其後天矣乎！嗣有作者，不可尚矣。
慨六書之變而爲大篆也，史籀所述也，文字漸備，而書法之本旨寢微，周宣之德其衰矣。大篆之變而爲小篆也，李斯實紛更之，簡便日趨，而書法之漸滅殆盡，嬴秦之罪莫贖矣。漢光武頒十札於方國，唐太宗賜飛白於馬周，宋太宗勒孝經於碑陰，賜吏治於棘寺。書法非不善也，然皆務翰墨之工，無裨身心之實。或深刻之成性，或閨門之多慚，
translation_en:
…yet its application extends throughout Heaven and Earth. Once the principles of pictographs, indicative graphs, compound ideographs, phonetic compounds, derivative cognates, and phonetic loans were established, the Way of all under Heaven was fully encompassed. By comparing and arranging their categories, Master Xu disclosed the subtleties of the three pairs; by following their sequence and tracing their development, Master Zheng revealed the mysteries of their succession. Master Zhu also said: “In such characters as ‘mind’ and ‘nature,’ principle flows forth of itself.” Thus, although Cangjie systematized the principles of the six categories of writing, he did not originate them. He must have received them personally through the transmission of the Yellow Emperor’s teaching of the mind. I therefore venture to argue that the transmission of the principles of writing began with Fuxi, as though he had cleaved primordial chaos and opened it up. With the Yellow Emperor, their details were elucidated, as though, following the opening of Heaven and Earth, he had demarcated and ordered the world. Was Fuxi not its “Before Heaven” phase, and the Yellow Emperor its “After Heaven” phase? Those who subsequently arose could not surpass them.
Alas, the six categories of writing changed into the large seal script, which was set forth by the Grand Scribe Zhou. Written forms gradually became more complete, but the fundamental purport of the principles of writing gradually faded: the virtue of King Xuan of Zhou was surely declining. As for the transformation of large seal script into small seal script, it was Li Si who subjected it to wholesale alteration. The pursuit of simplicity and convenience increased daily, while the principles of writing gradually vanished almost entirely. The guilt of the Qin house of Ying could not be redeemed. Emperor Guangwu of Han distributed ten sheets of calligraphy to the regional states; Emperor Taizong of Tang bestowed flying-white calligraphy upon Ma Zhou; and Emperor Taizong of Song had the Classic of Filial Piety engraved on the reverse of a stele and bestowed his calligraphy on the administration of officials upon the Court of Judicial Review [?]. Their calligraphy was certainly accomplished, yet all devoted themselves to skill with brush and ink, without contributing to the actual cultivation of person and mind. In some, harsh severity became second nature; others had much to be ashamed of within their households…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
或彝倫之不能無疚則其所謂書法者抑
末也去羲皇之心法益遠矣文固際遇而
興道必得人而盛是非天意有待於
聖祖及我
皇上乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極肇啓洪圖拯華夏於既
淪而天地定位舉綱常於既墜而宇宙改
觀故天假
聖祖以洩數百年圖書之蘊當時
===
奎畫之流播者若親撰
大誥之編增光日月
御製
大祀之祝照耀乾坤其
諭之臣民達之
郊廟猶有不能悉覩者書法之妙真有以同符
前聖矣然
聖心獨得之微猶欲追古文本旨之舊改字韻
踵襲之訛
punctuated: 或彝倫之不能無疚，則其所謂書法者，抑末也，去羲皇之心法益遠矣。文固際遇而興，道必得人而盛，是非天意有待於聖祖及我皇上乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，繼天立極，肇啓洪圖，拯華夏於既淪而天地定位，舉綱常於既墜而宇宙改觀。故天假聖祖以洩數百年圖書之蘊。當時奎畫之流播者，若親撰《大誥》之編，增光日月；御製大祀之祝，照耀乾坤。其諭之臣民，達之郊廟，猶有不能悉覩者。書法之妙，真有以同符前聖矣。然聖心獨得之微，猶欲追古文本旨之舊，改字韻踵襲之訛，
translation_en:
…or could not be free of reproach in the enduring human relationships. Thus, what they called the art of writing was merely a peripheral accomplishment, ever further removed from the method of the mind of the august Fuxi. Writing indeed flourishes when circumstances favor it, and the Way prospers only when it finds the right person. Was this not Heaven’s intention, awaiting our sagely founder and our present emperor?

We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, inaugurating his grand imperial enterprise.
