He rescued the Chinese realm after it had fallen, and Heaven and Earth assumed their proper positions; he restored the cardinal bonds and constant virtues after their collapse, and the universe took on a new aspect. Thus Heaven endowed our sagely founder with the means to reveal the riches of charts and writings accumulated over several hundred years. Among the imperial writings circulated at that time were the Great Pronouncements, which he personally composed, adding brilliance to the sun and moon, and his imperially composed prayers for the great sacrifices, illuminating Heaven and Earth. Of those addressed to his officials and people, and those presented at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, there are still some that we have been unable to see in full. The excellence of his art of writing truly accorded with that of the sages of old. Yet, through the subtle insights uniquely attained by his sagely mind, he still wished to recover the original intent of ancient writing and correct the errors perpetuated in characters and rhymes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
親命儒臣宋濂等勒成洪武正韻一書其損益
因革之宜一取正於毛晃注釋許慎說文
若支攴毋母之分冬東青清之合是也誠
哉萬世不刊之典有非
大聖人不能作者嘗伏讀我
聖祖之訓而有以識其本矣其
諭曾魯者則有曰人君一心治化之本存於中
者無堯舜之心欲施於外者有堯舜之治
不可得也其
===
諭宋濂者則有曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操而
存之爲甚難朕罔敢自暇自逸則我
聖祖之心是即伏羲神農黃帝堯禹之心也豈
惟有同前聖已乎
聖祖書法之妙其本端在於是迨我
皇上嗣統承休丕揚駿烈天明地察當百年禮
樂之期上乂下安應千載
中興之運故天縱
皇上以昭百八十年貞元之秘即今
punctuated:
親命儒臣宋濂等勒成《洪武正韻》一書，其損益因革之宜，一取正於毛晃注釋、許慎《說文》，若支攴毋母之分、冬東青清之合是也。誠哉，萬世不刊之典，有非大聖人不能作者！嘗伏讀我聖祖之訓，而有以識其本矣。其諭曾魯者則有曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，欲施於外者有堯舜之治，不可得也。」其諭宋濂者則有曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲甚難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」則我聖祖之心，是即伏羲、神農、黃帝、堯、禹之心也，豈惟有同前聖已乎？聖祖書法之妙，其本端在於是。

迨我皇上嗣統承休，丕揚駿烈，天明地察，當百年禮樂之期；上乂下安，應千載中興之運。故天縱皇上，以昭百八十年貞元之秘。即今
translation_en:
…He personally commanded the Confucian scholar-official Song Lian and others to compile the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun). In deciding what appropriately to omit or add, retain or change, they took as their standards Mao Huang’s annotations and Xu Shen’s Explanation of Graphs and Analysis of Characters (Shuowen). Examples include distinguishing 支 from 攴 and 毋 from 母, and combining the rhyme categories 冬 with 東 and 青 with 清. Truly, this is a canon unalterable for ten thousand generations, a work that none but a great sage could have produced!

I have reverently read the instructions of our Sagely Progenitor and thereby come to understand their foundation. In his admonition to Zeng Lu, he said: “The ruler’s single heart is the foundation of government and moral transformation. If what he holds within is not the heart of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes his outward actions to achieve the government of Yao and Shun, it cannot be done.” In his admonition to Song Lian, he said: “The human heart is empty and numinous; it moves out and in with the workings of vital energy. To grasp and preserve it is exceedingly difficult. I dare not indulge in leisure or ease.” Thus the heart of our Sagely Progenitor was precisely the heart of Fuxi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Yu. How could this amount merely to resemblance to the earlier sages? The excellence of the Sagely Progenitor’s calligraphy had its very foundation here.

When our present Emperor succeeded to the imperial line and inherited its blessings, he greatly exalted its magnificent achievements. His illumination was like Heaven’s, his discernment like Earth’s, at the appointed time when rites and music flourish after a hundred years. With order above and peace below, he answered the destiny of a restoration that comes once in a thousand years. Heaven therefore endowed our Emperor with exceptional gifts, through which to reveal the mystery of the cycle’s completion and renewal after a hundred and eighty years. Even now…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
宸翰之宣布者若
明堂或問之解奎璧昭文承天父老之
諭江漢生色其勒之
陵寢播之訓告形之咏歌猶有不能盡覩者書
法之妙眞有以匹休
聖祖矣然一曰
萬幾之暇校書畫之原考因仍之陋嘗示輔
弼諸臣研正字義其妙道精蘊之微皆本
淵衷獨契
===
神授默成若書宬爲突更丸爲圓是也信哉炳
燭丹書糠秕倉史有非
大聖人不能述者嘗伏讀我
皇上敬一之箴而有以測其原矣其言敬有曰
郊則恭誠
廟嚴孝趨肅于
明廷慎於閒居其言一有曰弗參以三弗貳
以二行顧其言終如其始則我
皇上之心是卽
punctuated: 宸翰之宣布者，若《明堂或問》之解，奎璧昭文；承天父老之諭，江漢生色。其勒之陵寢，播之訓告，形之咏歌，猶有不能盡覩者。書法之妙，眞有以匹休聖祖矣。然一曰，萬幾之暇，校書畫之原，考因仍之陋，嘗示輔弼諸臣研正字義。其妙道精蘊之微，皆本淵衷獨契，神授默成。若書宬爲突，更丸爲圓，是也。信哉！炳燭丹書，糠秕倉史，有非大聖人不能述者。嘗伏讀我皇上《敬一》之箴，而有以測其原矣。其言敬有曰：「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝趨，肅于明廷，慎於閒居。」其言一有曰：「弗參以三，弗貳以二，行顧其言，終如其始。」則我皇上之心，是卽
translation_en:
…Among the imperial writings publicly promulgated are the exposition of Questions on the Hall of Light (Mingtang huowen), whose literary brilliance shines like the Kui and Bi constellations, and the admonition to the elders of Chengtian, which lends lustre to the Jiang and Han rivers. Those engraved at the imperial mausoleums, disseminated through instructions and proclamations, or expressed in songs of praise still cannot all be seen. The excellence of his calligraphy truly rivals the glory of the Sagely Founder.
Yet, on one occasion [?], amid respite from the myriad affairs of state, he examined the origins of written forms and investigated the defects of inherited usage. He once instructed his assisting ministers to study and rectify the meanings of characters. The subtleties of this wondrous art and its profound essentials all derive from his deep inward understanding, divinely bestowed and silently perfected. Examples include writing 宬 as 突 [?] and replacing 丸 with 圓. Truly, he illuminates the Cinnabar Writings and treats the work of the scribe Cang as mere chaff: there are things here that none but a great sage could transmit.
I once reverently read Our Sovereign’s Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi), and thereby gained some understanding of its source. On reverence it says: “At the suburban sacrifices, be respectful and sincere; in the ancestral temple, be solemn and proceed with filial devotion; be reverent in the illustrious court and circumspect in private.” On oneness it says: “Do not mix it with three; do not divide it with two. Let your conduct accord with your words; end as you began.” Thus the heart of Our Sovereign is precisely…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之心也豈惟遠紹羲皇矣乎
皇上書法之妙其原蓋出於此是則
聖祖作之於前先天而天弗違伏羲之畫卦者
也
皇上述之於後後天而奉天時黃帝之作書者
也心法之傳曠百世而相感書法之盛越
千古而獨隆天地亨嘉之會治敎休明之
期夫豈偶然者哉愚也涵濡同文之化久
矣竊猶有說焉蓋書法之惡繁而就簡猶
===
水之就下愈趨愈卑吾不知其所終也然
必使盡變而爲古猶決江河而之山也勢
不可得矣然則如之何而後可意者取小
篆而正之古文參之大篆可者存之不可
者釐正之於今文之中而不失古文之義
祛官府之委細斥詭僻之叛經離道者復
歸民於樸則古道或可還也豈惟書法云
乎哉若必多頡而少斯則又以罪揜功者
非大中之論也狂瞽之見如此若通變宜
punctuated:
聖祖之心也，豈惟遠紹羲皇矣乎？皇上書法之妙，其原蓋出於此。是則聖祖作之於前，先天而天弗違，伏羲之畫卦者也；皇上述之於後，後天而奉天時，黃帝之作書者也。心法之傳，曠百世而相感；書法之盛，越千古而獨隆。天地亨嘉之會，治敎休明之期，夫豈偶然者哉？
愚也涵濡同文之化久矣，竊猶有說焉。蓋書法之惡繁而就簡，猶水之就下，愈趨愈卑，吾不知其所終也。然必使盡變而爲古，猶決江河而之山也，勢不可得矣。然則如之何而後可？意者取小篆而正之，古文參之，大篆可者存之，不可者釐正之，於今文之中而不失古文之義。祛官府之委細，斥詭僻之叛經離道者，復歸民於樸，則古道或可還也，豈惟書法云乎哉？若必多頡而少斯，則又以罪揜功者，非大中之論也。狂瞽之見如此，若通變宜
translation_en:
…is the heart of the Sagely Ancestor. How could this be merely a distant continuation of Sovereign Fuxi? The excellence of His Majesty’s art of writing surely has its source here. Thus the Sagely Ancestor created it first: preceding Heaven, yet meeting no opposition from Heaven, he was like Fuxi drawing the trigrams. His Majesty transmitted it afterward: following Heaven and observing Heaven’s seasons, he was like the Yellow Emperor creating writing. The transmission of the method of the mind brings sympathetic resonance across a hundred generations; the flourishing of the art of writing surpasses all antiquity in its singular magnificence. This felicitous conjunction of Heaven and Earth, this age of splendid government and moral instruction—could these possibly be accidental?
I, in my ignorance, have long been steeped in the civilizing influence of a common script. Yet I venture to offer a further observation. The tendency in writing to shun complexity and seek simplicity resembles water flowing downward: the farther it proceeds, the lower it sinks. I do not know where it will end. Yet insisting that everything be changed back to ancient forms would be like opening channels for the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers to flow toward the mountains: circumstances make this impossible. What, then, would be practicable? Perhaps we should take small-seal script and correct it, consulting ancient script alongside it; preserve acceptable forms of large-seal script and rectify unacceptable ones, so that present-day script does not lose the meaning of ancient script. If we eliminate bureaucratic minutiae, reject eccentric forms that depart from the Classics and stray from the Way, and lead the people back to simplicity, then perhaps the ancient Way can be restored. Would this concern only the art of writing? If one insists on praising Cang Jie and disparaging Li Si, this would again let faults obscure achievements; it is not a judgment of perfect impartiality. Such are my rash and benighted views. As for the authority to adapt to change and bring benefit…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
民之權則有議禮制度考文之
聖天子在
第三問
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批仁智可以爲二亦可以
爲一子於是對旣能析其緒而不遺又能合其大
而無外其深造於學而有得者耶
同考試官學正龔批知仁智有二名而非二
道可與言性矣
===
考試官教諭趙批剖析理道亹亹千萬言
不倦其仁智之士歟
考試官學正寇批仁智是如此論
天下之理其協于一矣乎而以爲二焉者
不明道者晦之也聖賢之言其統於同矣
乎而以爲異焉者不知言者岐之也故自
理之散見也名斯殊焉名之殊者歸則一
也故卽用明體者析之斯有以極其精自
理之統會也致斯一焉致之一者殊之本
punctuated:
民之權，則有議禮制度考文之聖天子在。

第三問
黃士觀

同考試官教諭馮批：仁智可以爲二，亦可以爲一。子於是對，旣能析其緒而不遺，又能合其大而無外，其深造於學而有得者耶？

同考試官學正龔批：知仁智有二名而非二道，可與言性矣。

考試官教諭趙批：剖析理道，亹亹千萬言不倦，其仁智之士歟？

考試官學正寇批：仁智是如此論。

天下之理，其協于一矣乎！而以爲二焉者，不明道者晦之也。聖賢之言，其統於同矣乎！而以爲異焉者，不知言者岐之也。故自理之散見也，名斯殊焉；名之殊者，歸則一也。故卽用明體者，析之斯有以極其精。自理之統會也，致斯一焉；致之一者，殊之本
translation_en:
…as for the authority to benefit the people through adaptive change, there is the sagely Son of Heaven, who deliberates on rites, establishes institutions and standards, and examines written forms.

Third Question
Huang Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: Benevolence and wisdom may be regarded as two, but they may also be regarded as one. In this response, you have both distinguished their strands without omission and brought together their entirety without leaving anything outside. Are you someone who has pursued learning deeply and attained understanding for yourself?

Comment by Associate Examiner Gong, Director of Studies: You understand that benevolence and wisdom have two names but are not two Ways. With you one may discuss human nature.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: You analyze principle and the Way, diligently expounding thousands upon thousands of words without tiring. Are you not a man of benevolence and wisdom?

Comment by Examiner Kou, Director of Studies: This is how benevolence and wisdom should be discussed.

Surely the principles of all under Heaven accord in unity! Those who regard them as two obscure them because they do not understand the Way. Surely the words of sages and worthies converge upon the same truth! Those who regard them as divergent split them apart because they do not understand those words. Thus, viewed in its dispersed manifestations, principle bears distinct names; yet what bears distinct names returns to unity. Hence, those who illuminate substance through function can, by analysis, reach the utmost subtlety. Viewed in its unified convergence, principle has a single purport; this unity of purport is the root of differentiation…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也故會偏求全者合之自有以盡其大是
何也天下之理原於性也天下之性具於
心也心一則性無不一矣性一則理無不
一矣故理之通於古今也本無二也而時
或二焉雖二而不害其爲一也言之出於
聖賢也本無異也而時或異焉雖異而不
失其爲同也故必究其所以二而會其所
以一考其所以殊而本其所以同則理融
諸性性融諸心而天下之道已洞然而無
===
遺矣此致知窮理之學極深研幾之要而
爲吾人之所當從事者不然衆言之淆無
以知其至定之的羣說之紛無以考其是
非之辨而吾亦何能有得於向往也哉執
事以仁智之理下詢承學愚也固擿埴而
迷其往者也而何以知之雖然亦嘗反本
窮源稽經質傳而有以知其略矣太極之
流行也奠而爲兩儀布而爲四德其生人
也氣以成形而理亦賦焉在天之元人得
punctuated:
也。故會偏求全者，合之自有以盡其大。是何也？天下之理原於性也，天下之性具於心也。心一則性無不一矣，性一則理無不一矣。故理之通於古今也，本無二也，而時或二焉，雖二而不害其爲一也；言之出於聖賢也，本無異也，而時或異焉，雖異而不失其爲同也。故必究其所以二而會其所以一，考其所以殊而本其所以同，則理融諸性，性融諸心，而天下之道已洞然而無遺矣。此致知窮理之學、極深研幾之要，而爲吾人之所當從事者。不然，衆言之淆，無以知其至定之的；羣說之紛，無以考其是非之辨，而吾亦何能有得於向往也哉？
執事以仁智之理下詢承學，愚也固擿埴而迷其往者也，而何以知之？雖然，亦嘗反本窮源，稽經質傳，而有以知其略矣。太極之流行也，奠而爲兩儀，布而爲四德。其生人也，氣以成形，而理亦賦焉。在天之元，人得
translation_en:
… Thus, those who bring together partial aspects to seek the whole can, by uniting them, fully comprehend its greatness. Why is this? The principles of all under Heaven originate in human nature, and human nature is embodied in the mind. If the mind is one, human nature is in every respect one; if human nature is one, principle is in every respect one. Thus principle, which runs through past and present, is fundamentally without duality. At times it may appear twofold, yet this does not impair its unity. The words issuing from sages and worthies are fundamentally without divergence. At times they may differ, yet these differences do not destroy their underlying agreement. We must therefore investigate what makes principle appear twofold and comprehend what makes it one, examine what makes these words differ and trace them to the basis of their agreement. Then principle is integrated in human nature, and human nature in the mind, so that the Way of all under Heaven becomes thoroughly clear, with nothing left out. This is the essential work of extending knowledge and investigating principle, of probing the utmost depths and examining the first subtle stirrings; it is what we ought to devote ourselves to. Otherwise, amid the confusion of many utterances, we would have no means of knowing the utterly certain standard; amid the profusion of doctrines, we would have no means of judging the distinction between right and wrong. How, then, could we attain any understanding of that toward which we aspire?
You, sir, have condescended to question us students about the principles of benevolence and wisdom. I, in my ignorance, am indeed like a blind man tapping the ground and losing his way: how could I understand them? Nevertheless, I have tried to return to the root and probe the source, consulting the Classics and testing my understanding against their commentaries, and have thereby come to know their broad outlines. In its flowing activity, the Supreme Ultimate establishes itself as the Two Modes, yin and yang, and unfolds as the Four Virtues. When it brings human beings into existence, material force gives them form, and principle is also endowed upon them. What in Heaven is origination, human beings receive …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之而爲仁在天之貞人得之以爲智是仁
智也皆性之德也具于人心而原于天命
者也故相爲體用互爲寂感迭爲終始旋
爲動靜初非判然爲二者也而聖賢之言
仁智也或舉此以該彼或因言以互見而
仁智之說於是不同矣不知不同者正所
以爲同而非仁智之果爲二道也是故智
動仁靜孔子所以論仁智之言也而至於
易傳之釋則又以仁爲動智爲靜何哉蓋
===
自仁智之成性而言則智者達於事理而
周流無滯動而不括者也故以動屬之智
也仁者安於義理而厚重不遷靜而有常
者也故以靜屬之仁也而易以生稟言之
自仁之合德於元則爲陽自智之合德於
貞則爲陰故若見其動靜之互言耳合而
觀之智者達於事理而實有沉幾密察之
道動而未甞不靜也仁者安於義理而實
有生生不息之機靜而未甞不動也此其
punctuated: 之而爲仁，在天之貞，人得之以爲智。是仁智也，皆性之德也，具于人心而原于天命者也。故相爲體用，互爲寂感，迭爲終始，旋爲動靜，初非判然爲二者也。而聖賢之言仁智也，或舉此以該彼，或因言以互見，而仁智之說於是不同矣。不知不同者正所以爲同，而非仁智之果爲二道也。是故「智動仁靜」，孔子所以論仁智之言也；而至於《易傳》之釋，則又以仁爲動、智爲靜，何哉？蓋自仁智之成性而言，則智者達於事理而周流無滯，動而不括者也，故以動屬之智也。仁者安於義理而厚重不遷，靜而有常者也，故以靜屬之仁也。而《易》以生稟言之，自仁之合德於元則爲陽，自智之合德於貞則爲陰，故若見其動靜之互言耳。合而觀之，智者達於事理，而實有沉幾密察之道，動而未甞不靜也；仁者安於義理，而實有生生不息之機，靜而未甞不動也。此其
translation_en:
…and thereby becomes benevolence; what in Heaven is steadfastness (zhen), human beings receive as wisdom. Benevolence and wisdom are both virtues of human nature, inherent in the human heart and originating in Heaven’s mandate. Thus each serves as substance and function for the other; they alternate as stillness and response, ending and beginning, activity and tranquility. From the outset, they are not two sharply divided things. Yet when sages and worthies speak of benevolence and wisdom, sometimes they mention one to encompass the other, and sometimes their statements illuminate the two reciprocally. Hence their accounts of benevolence and wisdom differ. People fail to understand that these differences are precisely what makes for their unity, rather than implying that benevolence and wisdom really constitute two distinct Ways.

Thus, “The wise are active; the benevolent are tranquil” is how Kongzi speaks of benevolence and wisdom. Yet the explanation in the Commentary on the Changes associates benevolence with activity and wisdom with tranquility. Why is this? Considered in terms of benevolence and wisdom as established dispositions, the wise comprehend the principles of affairs and circulate freely without obstruction: they are active and unrestricted. Hence activity is assigned to wisdom. The benevolent rest securely in moral principle, remaining steadfast and substantial without wavering: they are tranquil and constant. Hence tranquility is assigned to benevolence. The Changes, however, speaks in terms of the endowment received at birth. Insofar as benevolence accords in virtue with origination (yuan), it is yang; insofar as wisdom accords in virtue with steadfastness (zhen), it is yin. Thus it merely appears that the associations with activity and tranquility have been reversed.

Viewed together, the wise comprehend the principles of affairs, yet truly possess a way of deeply pondering subtle incipient developments and examining them closely: in their activity they are never without tranquility. The benevolent rest securely in moral principle, yet truly possess the impulse of ceaseless generation: in their tranquility they are never without activity. This, in their…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
動靜之互有所屬是豈爲言之相背乎成
已爲仁成物爲智子思所以論仁智之德
也而至於子貢之賛孔子則又以成已爲
智成物爲仁者何哉蓋自夫誠立天下之
有以誠而成已則天理流行人欲淨盡夫
是之謂仁也以誠而成物則知無不明處
無不當夫是之謂智也而子貢以進學先
之乃以學不厭爲智之所以自明教不倦
爲仁之所以及物□始見其仁智之異說
===
矣合而觀之則正心之盡者斯妙應物之
感而成已固成物之本也達順之妙者由
於體信之極而物成固已成之驗也此其
人已之互有所指又豈爲言之相判乎程
子曰專言仁則包四德是智固在仁之中
也殊不知所謂包四德者蓋自成德而統
其大者言之也觀諸孟子之論仁或以惻
隱羞惡辭讓是非而並列於四者之間或
謂天之尊爵人之安宅而統貫於四德之
punctuated: 動靜之互有所屬，是豈爲言之相背乎？成已爲仁，成物爲智，子思所以論仁智之德也。而至於子貢之賛孔子，則又以成已爲智，成物爲仁者，何哉？蓋自夫誠立天下之有，以誠而成已，則天理流行，人欲淨盡，夫是之謂仁也；以誠而成物，則知無不明，處無不當，夫是之謂智也。而子貢以進學先之，乃以學不厭爲智之所以自明，教不倦爲仁之所以及物，□始見其仁智之異說矣。合而觀之，則正心之盡者，斯妙應物之感，而成已固成物之本也；達順之妙者，由於體信之極，而物成固已成之驗也。此其人已之互有所指，又豈爲言之相判乎？程子曰：「專言仁則包四德。」是智固在仁之中也。殊不知所謂包四德者，蓋自成德而統其大者言之也。觀諸孟子之論仁，或以惻隱、羞惡、辭讓、是非而並列於四者之間，或謂天之尊爵、人之安宅而統貫於四德之
translation_en:
…Thus activity and stillness each have their respective associations in these alternating accounts. How could the statements contradict one another? Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom: this is how Zisi discusses the virtues of benevolence and wisdom. Yet when Zigong praises Confucius, he takes perfecting oneself to be wisdom and perfecting things to be benevolence. Why is this? Sincerity establishes all that exists under Heaven. Through sincerity, one perfects oneself: heavenly principle flows freely, and selfish human desires are utterly purged. This is what is called benevolence. Through sincerity, one perfects things: nothing remains unclear to one’s understanding, and nothing is handled inappropriately. This is what is called wisdom. Zigong, however, gives priority to advancement in learning. He therefore regards learning without weariness as the means by which wisdom brings enlightenment to oneself, and teaching without fatigue as the means by which benevolence extends to other things. [?] Only then do the differing accounts of benevolence and wisdom become apparent.

Considered together, one who fully rectifies the mind responds with subtle mastery to the prompting of things; perfecting oneself is indeed the foundation for perfecting things. Subtle mastery in extending harmonious accord arises from the fullest embodiment of trustworthiness; the perfection of things is indeed evidence that one has perfected oneself. Here, references to others and oneself each have their respective points. How could the statements be at odds?

Master Cheng says: “When benevolence is spoken of exclusively, it encompasses all four virtues.” Wisdom is thus certainly contained within benevolence. Yet one must understand that “encompassing all four virtues” is said from the standpoint of perfected virtue, comprehending its overarching scope. Consider Mencius’s discussions of benevolence: sometimes, through compassion, shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and the sense of right and wrong, he places it alongside the other virtues among the four; sometimes he calls it Heaven’s honored rank and humanity’s secure dwelling, thereby comprehensively uniting the four virtues …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
首則程子之言信矣然又何害於仁智之
偏言者乎朱子曰四德之智如四時之冬
萬物成始而成終是仁又在智之中也殊
不知所謂成始終者蓋自進學而功之切
者言之也觀諸大學之至善而能得由於
知止中庸之服膺而能守由於能擇則朱
子之言信矣然又何害於專言之兼智者
乎孔子以智屬乎天仁屬乎地蓋觀於仁
智之深故為是擬議也王通本之而有智
===
圓仁方之說是有得於天圓地方之粗迹
者也雖其所造未能望於聖人而一言之
幾乎道也夫豈可以盡遺哉孔子以智仁
勇為三達德蓋厚望於其君故陳之以君
德之備也司馬光祖之而有仁明武之言
是有見於智仁勇之發用者也雖其所陳
未能究竟其理而出言之不背於聖也夫
豈可以或少哉要之天下之理其雜物撰
德泛然示人廣者雖不可以一端求而吾
punctuated: 首，則程子之言信矣。然又何害於仁智之偏言者乎？朱子曰：「四德之智，如四時之冬，萬物成始而成終。」是仁又在智之中也。殊不知所謂成始終者，蓋自進學而功之切者言之也。觀諸《大學》之至善而能得，由於知止；《中庸》之服膺而能守，由於能擇，則朱子之言信矣。然又何害於專言之兼智者乎？孔子以智屬乎天，仁屬乎地，蓋觀於仁智之深，故為是擬議也。王通本之而有智圓仁方之說，是有得於天圓地方之粗迹者也。雖其所造未能望於聖人，而一言之幾乎道也，夫豈可以盡遺哉？孔子以智仁勇為三達德，蓋厚望於其君，故陳之以君德之備也。司馬光祖之而有仁明武之言，是有見於智仁勇之發用者也。雖其所陳未能究竟其理，而出言之不背於聖也，夫豈可以或少哉？要之，天下之理，其雜物撰德，泛然示人廣者，雖不可以一端求，而吾
translation_en:
…at their head, Master Cheng’s words are indeed true. Yet how does this conflict with speaking of benevolence and wisdom separately? Master Zhu said: “Wisdom among the four virtues is like winter among the four seasons: the myriad things complete their beginning and their end.” Thus benevolence, in turn, is contained within wisdom. But this overlooks the fact that “completing the beginning and the end” is spoken of in terms of advancing in learning and the crucial work this requires. Consider how, in the Great Learning, attaining the highest good depends on knowing where to rest, and how, in the Doctrine of the Mean, holding fast to the good and preserving it depends on being able to choose it. Master Zhu’s words are indeed true. Yet how does this conflict with speaking of benevolence comprehensively, so that it includes wisdom?

Confucius associated wisdom with Heaven and benevolence with Earth. Having perceived the depths of benevolence and wisdom, he made these comparisons. Wang Tong drew upon this to formulate the saying that wisdom is round and benevolence square. He thus grasped something of the outward configuration of round Heaven and square Earth. Although his attainment could not approach that of the sage, this one saying came close to the Way. How, then, could it be discarded altogether?

Confucius took wisdom, benevolence, and courage as the three universally applicable virtues. Having high expectations of his ruler, he presented them as the full complement of a ruler’s virtues. Sima Guang followed this precedent in speaking of benevolence, discernment, and martial prowess. He thus perceived something of how wisdom, benevolence, and courage manifest themselves in practice. Although his exposition did not fully fathom their underlying principles, his words did not run counter to the sage. How, then, could they be disparaged in any way?

In sum, the principles of all under Heaven, intermingling things and setting forth their virtues, reveal their breadth to people everywhere and cannot be sought through a single aspect; yet our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
性之德廣大咸備燦然示人顯者則唯仁
智而已矣是仁智也道固未嘗相離而功
不容於或缺也有覺以言仁斯合仁於智
乎而後仁可全否則吾懼其病於博愛流
於姑息也已擇術以爲智是合智於仁乎
而後仁可得否則吾懼其失於泛濫害於
穿鑿也已故曰仁智合一存乎聖仁智合
而能事畢矣是故義也者由此而宜之也
禮也者由此而履之也信也者由此而成
===
之也勇也者由此而達之也而又何待於
他求也哉要之天下之理一而已矣舉體
可以該用即用可以窺體聖賢固不必屑
屑於比而言之也聖賢之言同而已矣舉
全足以該偏指偏未始遺全聖賢固不必
拘拘於强而同之也或先後之互有所發
而觀會者不失於爲通或彼此之互有所
指而得意者自足以忘言庶於至當協一
之論洞然無遺而終身之指歸或不能有
punctuated:
性之德，廣大咸備，燦然示人顯者，則唯仁智而已矣。是仁智也，道固未嘗相離，而功不容於或缺也。有覺以言仁，斯合仁於智乎，而後仁可全；否則吾懼其病於博愛，流於姑息也已。擇術以爲智，是合智於仁乎，而後仁可得；否則吾懼其失於泛濫，害於穿鑿也已。故曰：「仁智合一存乎聖。」仁智合，而能事畢矣。是故義也者，由此而宜之也；禮也者，由此而履之也；信也者，由此而成之也；勇也者，由此而達之也。而又何待於他求也哉？

要之，天下之理，一而已矣。舉體可以該用，即用可以窺體，聖賢固不必屑屑於比而言之也。聖賢之言，同而已矣。舉全足以該偏，指偏未始遺全，聖賢固不必拘拘於强而同之也。或先後之互有所發，而觀會者不失於爲通；或彼此之互有所指，而得意者自足以忘言。庶於至當協一之論，洞然無遺，而終身之指歸，或不能有
translation_en:
…the virtues of our nature, vast and fully endowed, which reveal themselves brilliantly and plainly to us, are simply benevolence and wisdom. As for benevolence and wisdom, their ways have never been separate, and neither may be absent in their operation. To speak of benevolence in terms of awareness is surely to unite benevolence with wisdom; only then can benevolence be complete. Otherwise, I fear that it will suffer from indiscriminate love and lapse into indulgence. To regard the choice of methods as wisdom is surely to unite wisdom with benevolence; only then can benevolence be attained. Otherwise, I fear that wisdom will err through unrestrained wandering and suffer from forced interpretations. Thus it is said: “The unity of benevolence and wisdom rests in sagehood.” When benevolence and wisdom are united, all that can be accomplished is accomplished. Thus righteousness means acting appropriately on this basis; ritual propriety means putting it into practice; trustworthiness means bringing it to completion; and courage means carrying it through. What need, then, is there to seek elsewhere?

In essence, the principle of all under Heaven is but one. By setting forth its substance, one can encompass its functioning; through its functioning, one can glimpse its substance. Sages and worthies certainly need not labor over speaking of the two side by side. The words of sages and worthies are at one. To set forth the whole suffices to encompass the partial; to point to the partial does not mean leaving out the whole. There is certainly no need to insist on forcing their words into uniformity. Sometimes earlier and later statements illuminate one another, and those who perceive their convergence will not fail to understand them comprehensively. Sometimes statements here and there point to one another, and those who grasp their meaning can dispense with the words. In this way, one may hope to understand fully, leaving nothing obscure, a discourse that is perfectly fitting and harmonious in its unity; and the guiding aim of one’s entire life may perhaps have nothing …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
出於是也雖然求仁智於方策則辨之雖
詳亦不過爲口耳之學求仁智於吾心則
操之有要斯可爲自得之真學者於仁智
抑將何以爲求端用力之方哉必也好學
以開其始力行以踐其實則庶乎明通公
溥仁智合德矣動靜不偏體用兼該矣成
己成物功效廣大矣配乎天地德行光明
矣方圓不滯變通無方矣仁智之道豈不
會歸於我而亦奚有於異同之論也哉此
===
固道之足以訂證千古而功之可以詔示
方來者也執事以爲何如
第四問
游日章
同考試官教諭方　批　親民之至計久任之要
法盡於篇中見之得士如此可以藉手矣
同考試官教諭黎　批　歷評守令之善而折衷
古今求才考課久任之法其論正其氣昌其爲吏
可誌其必循矣
punctuated:
出於是也。雖然，求仁智於方策，則辨之雖詳，亦不過爲口耳之學；求仁智於吾心，則操之有要，斯可爲自得之真。學者於仁智，抑將何以爲求端用力之方哉？必也好學以開其始，力行以踐其實，則庶乎明通公溥，仁智合德矣；動靜不偏，體用兼該矣；成己成物，功效廣大矣；配乎天地，德行光明矣；方圓不滯，變通無方矣。仁智之道，豈不會歸於我，而亦奚有於異同之論也哉？此固道之足以訂證千古，而功之可以詔示方來者也。執事以爲何如？

第四問
游日章

同考試官教諭方批：親民之至計，久任之要法，盡於篇中見之。得士如此，可以藉手矣。

同考試官教諭黎批：歷評守令之善，而折衷古今求才、考課、久任之法。其論正，其氣昌，其爲吏，可誌其必循矣。
translation_en:
…go beyond this. Nevertheless, if one seeks benevolence and wisdom in written texts, however detailed one’s distinctions, this remains merely learning passed from ear to mouth. If one seeks benevolence and wisdom within one’s own mind, grasping what is essential, this can constitute genuine understanding attained for oneself. In pursuing benevolence and wisdom, then, how should the student find a starting point and a means of applying effort? Surely one must begin with a love of learning and put its substance into practice through strenuous action. Then one may attain penetrating understanding and impartial breadth, uniting benevolence and wisdom in virtue; avoid partiality toward either activity or stillness, encompassing both substance and function; perfect oneself and other beings, achieving broad and great results; match Heaven and Earth, making one’s virtuous conduct radiant; and remain unimpeded by either square or round forms, adapting to change without fixed limits. Would not the Way of benevolence and wisdom thus converge within oneself? What further need would there be to debate their differences and similarities? This is indeed a Way sufficient to verify and clarify the teachings of all ages, an achievement capable of instructing generations to come. What is your judgment, honored examiner?

Fourth Policy Question
You Rizhang

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: The finest plans for caring for the people and the essential methods for keeping officials long in office are all displayed in this essay. Having selected a scholar like this, we have something worthy to present.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He reviews in turn the merits of prefects and county magistrates, weighing ancient and modern methods of seeking talent, evaluating performance, and retaining officials in their posts. His arguments are sound, and his spirit is vigorous. Of his future service as an official, one may confidently predict that he will be conscientious.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙批文辭典雅雖議處守令
而駸駸有古作者矩度可以見
聖世氣化之隆矣
考試官學正寇批古今循吏無如西漢子
能言之而末復致望於
今日之考課者子其有希文先憂之志哉
人君體上天之意以惠天下之民其責將
誰委哉亦曰守令而已矣夫天生民而不
能自養於是乎託之君以養之故曰亶聰
===
明作元后元后作民父母然以君而視民
其勢則甚懸也迺自近而宰輔奉其德以
分布六卿而達之諸司以下及於郡縣故
曰聖人養賢以及萬民然則郡縣之職亦
微且遠矣而識治者重之何也其治小其
任專其於民也近蓋若家人父子之親痌
瘝皆切於其身者也是故言出而民易從
事舉而效隨應任之得人則百姓受其福
不得其人則德澤壅而君人體天之意孤
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批：文辭典雅，雖議處守令，而駸駸有古作者矩度，可以見聖世氣化之隆矣。
考試官學正寇批：古今循吏，無如西漢。子能言之，而末復致望於今日之考課者，子其有希文先憂之志哉！
人君體上天之意，以惠天下之民，其責將誰委哉？亦曰守令而已矣。夫天生民而不能自養，於是乎託之君以養之，故曰：「亶聰明，作元后；元后作民父母。」然以君而視民，其勢則甚懸也。迺自近而宰輔奉其德，以分布六卿，而達之諸司，以下及於郡縣，故曰：「聖人養賢以及萬民。」然則郡縣之職亦微且遠矣，而識治者重之，何也？其治小，其任專，其於民也近，蓋若家人父子之親，痌瘝皆切於其身者也。是故言出而民易從，事舉而效隨應。任之得人，則百姓受其福；不得其人，則德澤壅，而君人體天之意孤
translation_en:
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: The language is refined and elegant. Although the essay discusses arrangements for prefects and magistrates, it steadily approaches the standards of ancient writers. In this one can see the flourishing moral influence of this sagely age.
Examiner Kou, School Director, comments: Among the conscientious officials of past and present, none compare with those of the Western Han. You have discussed them well, and at the end you further express hopes for those responsible for evaluating officials today. Surely you share Xiwen’s aspiration to be the first to take on the world’s cares!
The ruler embodies the intention of Heaven above in bringing benefits to the people of the realm. To whom should he entrust this responsibility? Surely to prefects and magistrates, and no others. Heaven gives birth to the people, but they cannot sustain themselves; it therefore entrusts them to a ruler to sustain them. Thus it is said: “One truly perceptive and discerning becomes the sovereign; the sovereign becomes the father and mother of the people.” Yet the ruler stands at a great distance from the people. Thus, beginning with those closest to him, the chief councilors uphold his virtue and distribute its influence among the six ministers, transmitting it to the various offices and thence down to the prefectures and counties. Hence the saying: “The sage nourishes worthy men, thereby reaching all the people.”
The offices of prefect and magistrate are thus lowly and remote; why, then, do those who understand government attach such importance to them? Their jurisdictions are small, their responsibility is concentrated, and they are close to the people. Their intimacy resembles that of father and son within a household: the people’s suffering and distress touch them as though afflicting their own bodies. Thus, when they speak, the people readily follow; when they undertake an affair, results follow in response. If suitable men are appointed, the common people receive the benefits. If unsuitable men are appointed, the flow of beneficence is obstructed, and the ruler’s intention to embody Heaven’s will is frustrated…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣此爲守令者貴知自愛而在上者亦當
知所勸之也故曰天下政平訟理惟良二
千石又曰宰天下不如縣令之爲樂樂者
樂乎澤之易流也求之於古若治蒲而得
三善之稱則有子路焉治單父而擅鳴琴
之治則有子賤焉子夏治莒父而謹欲速
之戒子游治武城而興禮樂之敎凡以得
聖人爲之依歸而卓然有成者也春秋而
下秦治焚矣漢興去古未遠其循良之治
===
有足稱者是故於蜀郡文翁見其文學之
敷也於潁川黃霸見其敎化安全之政也
於渤海龔遂見其農桑之勸牛犢之化也
於南陽召信臣見其水利之興召父之稱
也然治行第一如吳公而史失其名偽增
戶口如王成而特蒙顯賞則當時循吏之
未能盡信可知矣要之史失其名者漢文
玄默之化循吏不勝其書故也偽增蒙賞
則宣帝綜覈之實何如耶尚何足擬聖門
punctuated:
矣。此爲守令者貴知自愛，而在上者亦當知所勸之也。故曰：「天下政平訟理，惟良二千石。」又曰：「宰天下不如縣令之爲樂。」樂者，樂乎澤之易流也。求之於古，若治蒲而得三善之稱，則有子路焉；治單父而擅鳴琴之治，則有子賤焉；子夏治莒父而謹欲速之戒，子游治武城而興禮樂之敎，凡以得聖人爲之依歸而卓然有成者也。
春秋而下，秦治焚矣。漢興，去古未遠，其循良之治有足稱者。是故於蜀郡文翁，見其文學之敷也；於潁川黃霸，見其敎化安全之政也；於渤海龔遂，見其農桑之勸、牛犢之化也；於南陽召信臣，見其水利之興、召父之稱也。然治行第一如吳公，而史失其名；偽增戶口如王成，而特蒙顯賞，則當時循吏之未能盡信可知矣。要之，史失其名者，漢文玄默之化，循吏不勝其書故也。偽增蒙賞，則宣帝綜覈之實何如耶？尚何足擬聖門
translation_en:
… This is why prefects and magistrates must value their own integrity, while those above them should also understand how to encourage them. Thus it is said: “For orderly government and the proper settlement of lawsuits throughout the realm, all depends on good officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank.” It is also said: “Governing the realm does not bring as much joy as serving as a district magistrate.” This joy lies in the ease with which one’s beneficence can spread. Looking to antiquity, there was Zilu, whose government of Pu won praise for three good achievements; Zijian, whose government of Shanfu was renowned for his governing while playing the zither; Zixia, who governed Jufu and carefully observed the warning against seeking quick results; and Ziyou, who governed Wucheng and promoted instruction in rites and music. All achieved outstanding results because they had the Sage as their guide and support.
After the Spring and Autumn period, government under Qin was consumed by fire [?]. When the Han arose, antiquity was not yet far distant, and its conscientious and benevolent administration had much worthy of praise. Thus, in Wen Weng of Shu Commandery we see the spread of literary learning; in Huang Ba of Yingchuan, government that transformed the people through instruction and kept them secure; in Gong Sui of Bohai, encouragement of farming and sericulture, and transformation through the acquisition of cattle and calves; and in Shao Xinchen of Nanyang, the development of irrigation and the acclaim expressed in the name “Father Shao.” Yet someone such as Lord Wu, whose administrative performance ranked first, had his personal name omitted from the histories, while someone such as Wang Cheng, who falsely inflated household and population figures, received conspicuous rewards. We can therefore see that accounts of the conscientious officials of that time cannot all be trusted. Ultimately, the omission of a personal name from the histories occurred because, under Emperor Wen of Han’s quiet and unobtrusive transforming rule, conscientious officials were too numerous to record fully. But if falsified increases received rewards, what substance was there to Emperor Xuan’s comprehensive scrutiny? How could such men possibly compare with those of the Sage’s school…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之賢也哉我
國朝官人之法取諸成周親民之選重於西
漢洪武中嘗擢知府趙瑁爲左諭德矣又
嘗擢典史馮堅爲僉都御史矣作循良之
風以新庶官之習是以百八十年來克稱
其職民安其業今即其卓異者言之如廉
察貪暴嚴禁豪猾積米賑農活者無算任
久遷秩留者萬眾則况鍾之守姑蘇也不
爲利回不爲勢怵愛養所部霽
===
天威於一語懷柔遠人蠲商稅以萬計則劉實
之治南雄也始宰莊浪誕著賢聲歷守應
天益彰政譽剛正不撓而吏民懾服廉公
有威而豪貴斂手此顧佐齊名孝肅而致
碩輔之交薦者也始守鎮江綽有偉績比
改蘇郡尤愜輿情舉偏補弊飭夙政之廢
弛築壩浚河濟歲漕之壅滯此林鶚獨持
大體而蒙
英廟之眷遇者也若用法平恕疑獄多所平反
punctuated: 之賢也哉！我國朝官人之法取諸成周，親民之選重於西漢。洪武中，嘗擢知府趙瑁爲左諭德矣，又嘗擢典史馮堅爲僉都御史矣。作循良之風，以新庶官之習，是以百八十年來，克稱其職，民安其業。今即其卓異者言之，如廉察貪暴，嚴禁豪猾，積米賑農，活者無算；任久遷秩，留者萬眾，則况鍾之守姑蘇也。不爲利回，不爲勢怵，愛養所部，霽天威於一語；懷柔遠人，蠲商稅以萬計，則劉實之治南雄也。始宰莊浪，誕著賢聲；歷守應天，益彰政譽。剛正不撓，而吏民懾服；廉公有威，而豪貴斂手。此顧佐齊名孝肅，而致碩輔之交薦者也。始守鎮江，綽有偉績；比改蘇郡，尤愜輿情。舉偏補弊，飭夙政之廢弛；築壩浚河，濟歲漕之壅滯。此林鶚獨持大體，而蒙英廟之眷遇者也。若用法平恕，疑獄多所平反
translation_en:
…compare with the worthies of the sage’s school!

Our dynasty’s methods of appointing officials take their model from the Zhou, and its selection of officials who govern the people directly receives greater emphasis than under the Western Han. During the Hongwu reign, Prefect Zhao Mao was promoted to Left Admonisher, and County Clerk Feng Jian was promoted to Assistant Censor-in-chief. By fostering a tradition of conscientious and benevolent administration, the dynasty renewed the habits of its officials. Thus, for 180 years, officials have fulfilled their duties and the people have pursued their livelihoods in peace.

To speak now of those whose achievements were outstanding: investigating corrupt and oppressive officials, strictly restraining powerful local bullies and rogues, stockpiling rice to relieve farmers and saving countless lives, serving so long that his rank was advanced while tens of thousands sought to retain him—such was Kuang Zhong’s administration of Gusu. Neither swayed by profit nor intimidated by power, nurturing those under his jurisdiction, dispelling imperial wrath with a single utterance, winning over people from afar, and remitting commercial taxes amounting to tens of thousands—such was Liu Shi’s administration of Nanxiong.

Beginning as magistrate of Zhuanglang, Gu Zuo won a distinguished reputation for worthiness; later, as prefect of Yingtian, his administrative reputation grew still greater. Firm, upright, and unyielding, he commanded the awed submission of officials and commoners; incorruptible, impartial, and authoritative, he made the powerful and noble restrain themselves. This was Gu Zuo, who ranked alongside Xiaosu in renown and received recommendations from eminent senior ministers.

When Lin E first served as prefect of Zhenjiang, he achieved notable successes; upon his transfer to Suzhou Prefecture, he satisfied public expectations still more fully. He rectified imbalances and remedied abuses, restoring discipline where earlier administration had fallen into neglect. He built dams and dredged waterways, relieving obstructions to the annual grain transport. This was Lin E, who independently upheld the larger interests of government and received Emperor Yingzong’s favor.

As for applying the law impartially and with forbearance, and reviewing and overturning many doubtful convictions…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
敷政慈惠歲饑賴以全活創書院以敎民
致科目之特盛則王恕之治維揚也期月
令行風裁已可想見思患豫防城濠務先
濬築屹保障於一方擒劇賊於崇朝則許
逵之治樂陵也之數子者遺風善政至今
爲烈庶幾聖門諸賢視漢所稱循吏則旣
無愧矣求其最著而可法者其況之治蘇
王之治維揚乎一則起自掾辟而勳庸茂
著楊士奇贈之有曰十年不愧趙清獻七
===
邑重迎張益州也一則歷事三朝而典刑
不墜王雲鳳記之有曰憂天下之志如范
仲淹濟天下之才如司馬光也是二人名
重當時而風動海內者亦已多矣執事所
謂追跡循良固有不必遠慕而得者非斯
人其誰與歸耶
國家養賢圖治人才輩出至我
今日之盛視昔猶或過之豈謂今之守令盡無
若人乎夫何習尚日趨而常情易玩故操
punctuated:
敷政慈惠，歲饑賴以全活，創書院以敎民，致科目之特盛，則王恕之治維揚也。期月令行，風裁已可想見；思患豫防，城濠務先濬築，屹保障於一方，擒劇賊於崇朝，則許逵之治樂陵也。之數子者，遺風善政，至今爲烈，庶幾聖門諸賢，視漢所稱循吏，則旣無愧矣。求其最著而可法者，其況之治蘇、王之治維揚乎？一則起自掾辟，而勳庸茂著，楊士奇贈之有曰：「十年不愧趙清獻，七邑重迎張益州也。」一則歷事三朝，而典刑不墜，王雲鳳記之有曰：「憂天下之志如范仲淹，濟天下之才如司馬光也。」是二人名重當時，而風動海內者亦已多矣。執事所謂追跡循良，固有不必遠慕而得者，非斯人，其誰與歸耶？
國家養賢圖治，人才輩出。至我今日之盛，視昔猶或過之，豈謂今之守令盡無若人乎？夫何習尚日趨，而常情易玩，故操
translation_en:
…he administered government with compassion and kindness, preserving lives during famine; he founded an academy to educate the people, bringing exceptional flourishing in examination success. Such was Wang Shu’s administration of Weiyang. Within a full year his commands were being carried out, and his firmness and judgment could already be discerned. Anticipating trouble and preparing against it, he gave priority to dredging moats and building walls, standing firm as the region’s bulwark and capturing formidable bandits in a single morning. Such was Xu Kui’s administration of Leling.
These men [?] left exemplary traditions and good government whose influence remains potent today. They approached the worthies of the Sage’s school and need feel no shame when compared with those praised as exemplary officials under the Han. If we seek the most outstanding and worthy of emulation, would these not be Kuang’s administration of Suzhou and Wang’s administration of Weiyang? The former rose from appointment as a clerk and achieved distinguished service. Yang Shiqi wrote in a verse presented to him: “For ten years, worthy of Zhao Qingxian; the seven counties welcome another Zhang Yizhou.” The latter served through three reigns without letting exemplary standards lapse. Wang Yunfeng wrote of him: “In his resolve to care for all under Heaven, he resembled Fan Zhongyan; in his talent for bringing relief to all under Heaven, he resembled Sima Guang.” These two men enjoyed great renown in their day, and many throughout the realm were moved by their example. As for what you call following in the footsteps of exemplary officials, one surely need not look far into antiquity to find models. If not these men, whom should one follow?
Our state nurtures worthy men and seeks good government, and talented men emerge generation after generation. In our present flourishing age, we may even surpass the past. How could one say that among today’s prefects and magistrates there are none like these men? Yet why do prevailing habits daily drift downward, while ordinary human dispositions readily lapse into complacency? Thus, in disciplining…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
勵廉潔者有矣而苞苴之弊不能無分甘
恬澹者有矣而夤緣之私未盡去志在愛
民矣或實惠之未流名為持法矣或執守
之易撓此蠹政戕民不能不為君子之議
而追古傷今固宜厪執事之慨也此其故
何哉蓋自夫久任之法不行而人懷苟且
之志內外之勢偏重而士有顧望之私此
牧民者所以多忽其職而不知所自修也
或依阿淟涊巧為容悅之圖或和光逐物
===
苟為自全之計日覬虛聲坐俟速化其視
官舍如傳郵而視斯民不啻秦越也若此
者亦何取於民之父母哉是惟守令不知
所以自愛而上之愛之者日已薄上不能
重視其下而守令之所以自視者益以輕
如是而欲循良之盛媲美於昔也必不可
得矣然則為守令而不思付託之重靦其
心焉墮其職而以自抵於弗類者是自誣
也為上而罔恤守令之艱不思所以振勵
punctuated:
勵廉潔者有矣，而苞苴之弊不能無；分甘恬澹者有矣，而夤緣之私未盡去；志在愛民矣，或實惠之未流；名為持法矣，或執守之易撓。此蠹政戕民，不能不為君子之議，而追古傷今，固宜厪執事之慨也。此其故何哉？蓋自夫久任之法不行，而人懷苟且之志；內外之勢偏重，而士有顧望之私。此牧民者所以多忽其職，而不知所自修也。或依阿淟涊，巧為容悅之圖；或和光逐物，苟為自全之計。日覬虛聲，坐俟速化，其視官舍如傳郵，而視斯民不啻秦越也。若此者，亦何取於民之父母哉？
是惟守令不知所以自愛，而上之愛之者日已薄；上不能重視其下，而守令之所以自視者益以輕。如是而欲循良之盛媲美於昔也，必不可得矣。然則，為守令而不思付託之重，靦其心焉，墮其職而以自抵於弗類者，是自誣也；為上而罔恤守令之艱，不思所以振勵
translation_en:
…there are those who cultivate integrity and purity, yet the abuse of accepting bribes is not absent; there are those content with a quiet, simple lot, yet private advancement through connections has not entirely ceased. Some aspire to care for the people, yet tangible benefits may fail to reach them; some have a reputation for upholding the law, yet their resolve may easily bend. Such conduct corrupts government and harms the people, and cannot escape the criticism of gentlemen. In recalling antiquity and lamenting the present, you are therefore quite justified in expressing your dismay. What causes this? Since the practice of keeping officials long in their posts has fallen into disuse, men have harbored intentions of merely muddling through; since the balance of influence between metropolitan and local posts has become unequal, officials have privately watched which way advantage lies. This is why those charged with shepherding the people so often neglect their duties and fail to understand how to cultivate themselves. Some comply obsequiously and endure disgrace, cleverly contriving to ingratiate themselves; others mute their own distinction and follow worldly currents, seeking only to preserve their positions. Daily they covet hollow reputations and sit awaiting rapid advancement. They regard their official residences as relay stations, and treat these people as though they were as remote from them as Qin from Yue. What claim can such men have to be the people's father and mother?
It is precisely because prefects and magistrates do not know how to respect themselves that their superiors' regard for them grows daily thinner; because superiors fail to attach importance to their subordinates, prefects and magistrates hold themselves ever more lightly. Under these circumstances, to hope that the flourishing of conscientious and benevolent administration might rival that of former times is surely impossible. Thus, for prefects and magistrates to disregard the gravity of the trust placed in them, to be shameless at heart, and to neglect their duties, thereby reducing themselves to unworthy men, is to deceive themselves. For their superiors to disregard the difficulties faced by prefects and magistrates, and to give no thought to how they might encourage them…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
成全之者是誣人者也二者將焉咎哉亦
惟上下各盡其道焉耳誠使爲之下者知
守令身父母之責念稼穡爲小民之依罔
咈民以從欲罔違道以干譽毋嬰情於內
外之殊毋改節於終始之異毋急於近功
毋阻於小挫吾知盡吾職焉已矣爲之上
者念其勞也而勞之憫其情也而優之程
其勤惰而勸戒之覈其邪正而黜陟之不
專事乎文法之繩而必開誠以布公不取
===
快於儇便之私而必循名以責實吾知盡
吾御下之道焉已矣則秉正孤立者將有
恃而無恐勤公奉職者皆矢心而益勵上
下之間其道各盡而其事交相成矣如是
而何守令之不安何恩澤之不究何古循
吏之不可及何況王諸臣之不多見哉謹
對
第五問
楊嶷
punctuated:
成全之者，是誣人者也。二者將焉咎哉？亦惟上下各盡其道焉耳。誠使爲之下者知守令身父母之責，念稼穡爲小民之依，罔咈民以從欲，罔違道以干譽，毋嬰情於內外之殊，毋改節於終始之異，毋急於近功，毋阻於小挫，吾知盡吾職焉已矣。爲之上者念其勞也而勞之，憫其情也而優之，程其勤惰而勸戒之，覈其邪正而黜陟之，不專事乎文法之繩，而必開誠以布公，不取快於儇便之私，而必循名以責實，吾知盡吾御下之道焉已矣。則秉正孤立者將有恃而無恐，勤公奉職者皆矢心而益勵，上下之間，其道各盡，而其事交相成矣。如是而何守令之不安？何恩澤之不究？何古循吏之不可及？何況王諸臣之不多見哉？謹對。

第五問

楊嶷
translation_en:
…bring them to full accomplishment—such a person wrongs others. Where, then, should blame fall between these two? It is simply a matter of superiors and subordinates each fully fulfilling their proper duties. If those serving below truly understood that prefects and county magistrates bear the responsibilities of parents, and remembered that farming sustains the common people, they would neither defy the people to indulge their own desires nor depart from the Way to seek praise. They would not let differences between service at court and in the provinces entangle their feelings, nor alter their integrity as circumstances changed from beginning to end. They would neither rush after immediate achievements nor be deterred by minor setbacks. Their sole concern would be: “I know only that I must discharge my duties fully.” Those serving above should recognize their subordinates’ toil and acknowledge their service, sympathize with their circumstances and treat them generously, assess their diligence or indolence and encourage or admonish them, and investigate their misconduct or uprightness and demote or promote them accordingly. Rather than devote themselves exclusively to restraining them through written regulations, they must act with openness, sincerity, and impartiality. They must not indulge private gratification in clever expediency, but require actual performance commensurate with official responsibilities. Their sole concern would be: “I know only that I must fully discharge my duty of directing those below me.” Then those who uphold rectitude while standing alone would have support and nothing to fear; all who diligently serve the public and perform their duties would pledge themselves wholeheartedly and strive still harder. Superiors and subordinates would each fully fulfill their proper duties and help one another accomplish their work. If this were so, what prefect or county magistrate would lack security in office? What benevolent benefits would fail to reach the people fully? Why could the exemplary officials of antiquity not be equaled? Why would officials such as Kuang and Wang not appear in greater numbers? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question

Yang Yi

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭胡批閩中鹽法雖少然亦可
以足
國子能言其利而又詳知其弊考鹽政者觀之此足矣子其通達
政體者耶
同考試官教諭費批言鹽法利弊粲然如指
諸掌且斟酌時宜有濟實用真一時俊傑哉
考試官教諭趙批籌邊足用必有資於鹽
政子能深思遠計鑿鑿可行蓋亦素負經濟之略
者歟
===
考試官學正寇批事在目前而憂深謀遠
有志於天下者
聖王以天下之利利天下而不以便其私
故經制畫法而非以為苛也與民守之而
已矣通變趨時而非以為縱也與民宜之
而已矣夫法者一定不易而時宜所在則
又不可重拂焉者使欲執法以齊衆則上
積重而澤不究其勢必至於病民是之謂
苛使欲徇情以廢法則下詭利而事無紀
punctuated:
同考試官教諭胡批：「閩中鹽法雖少，然亦可以足國。子能言其利，而又詳知其弊，考鹽政者觀之，此足矣。子其通達政體者耶？」

同考試官教諭費批：「言鹽法利弊，粲然如指諸掌，且斟酌時宜，有濟實用，真一時俊傑哉！」

考試官教諭趙批：「籌邊足用，必有資於鹽政。子能深思遠計，鑿鑿可行，蓋亦素負經濟之略者歟？」

考試官學正寇批：「事在目前，而憂深謀遠，有志於天下者。」

聖王以天下之利利天下，而不以便其私，故經制畫法，而非以為苛也，與民守之而已矣；通變趨時，而非以為縱也，與民宜之而已矣。夫法者，一定不易，而時宜所在，則又不可重拂焉者。使欲執法以齊衆，則上積重而澤不究，其勢必至於病民，是之謂苛；使欲徇情以廢法，則下詭利而事無紀，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “Although the salt administration in Fujian is limited in scope [?], it can nevertheless provide sufficient resources for the state. You can explain its advantages and also know its abuses in detail. Anyone investigating salt administration need only read this. Are you perhaps one who thoroughly understands the principles of government?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: “Your account of the advantages and abuses of the salt system is brilliantly clear, as though pointing to something in the palm of your hand. Moreover, you weigh what suits present circumstances and offer proposals of practical benefit. Truly an outstanding talent of our time!”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Planning frontier defense and ensuring adequate funds must draw upon salt administration. Your reflections are deep and your calculations far-reaching; your proposals are demonstrably practicable. Surely you have long possessed a capacity for ordering the state and serving the people?”

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: “Though the matter lies immediately before us, his concerns are profound and his plans far-reaching: a man whose aspirations embrace all under Heaven.”

The sage kings used the resources of all under Heaven to benefit all under Heaven, rather than to serve their private interests. Thus, when they established institutions and framed laws, their purpose was not to impose harsh restrictions, but simply to uphold them together with the people. When they adapted to change and kept pace with the times, their purpose was not to permit laxity, but simply to make their measures suitable for the people. Laws, once established, are not to be changed; yet neither may the requirements of the times be gravely disregarded. If one seeks to enforce the law to bring uniformity to the multitude, burdens accumulate above [?] and beneficence fails to reach the people; this will inevitably harm the people. This is what is called harshness. If one seeks to indulge personal considerations and abandon the law, those below pursue illicit gain and affairs lose all order …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其勢必至於病國是之謂縱縱與苛而欲
理天下之事不可得也况於鹽法乎執事
以閩中鹽法下詢固公天下之心也愚閩
產也敢不屛其私圖以對昔自禹貢青州
貢鹽而鹽法之制興自周禮掌鹽之政令
而鹽法之制立則帝王之世鹽法亦所不
免豈不欲與天下相忘於利哉蓋鹽者天
地自然之利而下民有欲無紀則亂法者
禁亂之所由生者也猶坊止水之所自來
===
者也故帝王必有法以齊天下而後鹽可
以利天下不然則猗頓之富將不利於魯
吳王之强且恣虐於漢也可不慎哉洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇稽古立法貽
國家千萬載無疆之休者莫善於飛輓之策
百八十年內安外攘皆賴於此柰何狃於
承平忽於邊計而遂置閩中鹽法於不講
也考之
punctuated:
其勢必至於病國，是之謂縱。縱與苛而欲理天下之事，不可得也，况於鹽法乎？執事以閩中鹽法下詢，固公天下之心也。愚閩產也，敢不屛其私圖以對？昔自《禹貢》青州貢鹽，而鹽法之制興；自《周禮》掌鹽之政令，而鹽法之制立。則帝王之世，鹽法亦所不免，豈不欲與天下相忘於利哉？蓋鹽者，天地自然之利，而下民有欲，無紀則亂。法者，禁亂之所由生者也，猶坊止水之所自來者也。故帝王必有法以齊天下，而後鹽可以利天下。不然，則猗頓之富將不利於魯，吳王之强且恣虐於漢也，可不慎哉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，稽古立法，貽國家千萬載無疆之休者，莫善於飛輓之策。百八十年，內安外攘，皆賴於此。柰何狃於承平，忽於邊計，而遂置閩中鹽法於不講也？考之
translation_en:
…the inevitable consequence will be harm to the state: this is what is called laxity. To seek to order the affairs of the realm through laxity and harshness is impossible; how much more so in administering the salt regulations! Your inquiry concerning the salt regulations in Fujian surely reflects a concern for the common good of the realm. I am a native of Fujian: how could I dare reply without setting aside my private interests? In former times, the system of salt regulation arose with Qingzhou’s tribute of salt recorded in the Tribute of Yu; it became established with the ordinances governing salt recorded in the Rites of Zhou. Thus, even in the age of the sage emperors and kings, salt regulations could not be dispensed with. Was it that they did not wish to live together with all under Heaven without giving thought to profit? Salt is a benefit naturally supplied by Heaven and Earth, but the common people have desires, and without regulation there will be disorder. Laws prevent disorder at its source, just as a dike checks water where it comes from. Thus emperors and kings must have laws to bring order to the realm before salt can benefit the realm. Otherwise, wealth such as Yi Dun’s would bring no benefit to Lu, and power such as the king of Wu’s would permit unrestrained violence against the Han. Can we afford to be incautious?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, in founding the realm, examined antiquity and established laws. Among the measures by which he bequeathed boundless blessings to the state for ten thousand generations, none surpassed the policy of transporting provisions swiftly. For one hundred and eighty years, peace within and resistance to enemies without have depended upon this. How could we become so accustomed to prolonged peace, and so heedless of frontier planning, that we have consequently left Fujian’s salt regulations unexamined? On examining…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
國初建官轉運並峙淮浙責任維鈞也今閩
中所輸每歲僅及二萬而淮運歲輸百萬
浙運亦不下數十萬其鹽法之詳略迥異
者何哉是果產鹽之難歟日晒風花無事
煎煮不可謂不易也是果行鹽之地有未
廣歟八閩際山環海延袤數千里不可謂
不廣也是果食鹽之戶有未蕃歟八閩生
齒日眾戶口不下數百萬不可謂不蕃也
然則其故可知矣此無他淮浙之鹽有法
===
閩中無法故耳所謂無法者其弊有二曰
經畫無方也曰禁令不壹也蓋政久則敝
勢所必致也所貴乎經畫之得其宜耳夫
何襲因仍之舊憚紛改之煩惕利害之故
而斟酌損益之方莫為之所則上無道揆
而商鹽之行者日益滯是謂經畫之無方
嗜利無厭民之恒情也所貴乎禁令之壹
其趨耳夫何別於民竈之殊途格於府衛
之異致阻於豪右之難懲而統御約束之
punctuated: 國初建官，轉運並峙淮浙，責任維鈞也。今閩中所輸，每歲僅及二萬，而淮運歲輸百萬，浙運亦不下數十萬，其鹽法之詳略迥異者何哉？是果產鹽之難歟？日晒風花，無事煎煮，不可謂不易也。是果行鹽之地有未廣歟？八閩際山環海，延袤數千里，不可謂不廣也。是果食鹽之戶有未蕃歟？八閩生齒日眾，戶口不下數百萬，不可謂不蕃也。然則其故可知矣。此無他，淮浙之鹽有法，閩中無法故耳。所謂無法者，其弊有二：曰經畫無方也，曰禁令不壹也。蓋政久則敝，勢所必致也，所貴乎經畫之得其宜耳。夫何襲因仍之舊，憚紛改之煩，惕利害之故，而斟酌損益之方莫為之所，則上無道揆，而商鹽之行者日益滯，是謂經畫之無方。嗜利無厭，民之恒情也，所貴乎禁令之壹其趨耳。夫何別於民竈之殊途，格於府衛之異致，阻於豪右之難懲，而統御約束之
translation_en:
…At the beginning of the dynasty, when offices were established, Fujian’s Salt Distribution Commission stood alongside those of Huai and Zhe, with equal responsibilities. Today, however, Fujian remits barely twenty thousand each year, whereas the Huai commission remits a million annually, and the Zhe commission no less than several hundred thousand. Why is there such a vast difference in the thoroughness of their salt administration? Is salt really difficult to produce here? Sun-drying and crystallization by the wind dispense with boiling; production cannot be called difficult. Is the territory in which salt is distributed insufficiently extensive? The eight prefectures of Fujian reach to the mountains and are encircled by the sea, extending several thousand li; the territory cannot be called small. Are the households consuming salt insufficiently numerous? Fujian’s population grows daily, and its registered population numbers no fewer than several million; it cannot be called sparse. The reason, then, is evident. It is simply that salt in Huai and Zhe is governed by effective regulations, whereas salt in Fujian is not.

This absence of effective regulation has two failings: planning lacks method, and prohibitions lack uniformity. That longstanding administration develops defects is an inevitable tendency; what matters is that planning should address them appropriately. Why, then, cling to inherited practices, shrink from the trouble of making numerous changes, and fear the consequences for vested interests, while making no provision for judicious adjustments [?]? Thus those above lack guiding principles, and the circulation of merchants’ salt becomes increasingly obstructed. This is what is meant by planning without method.

An insatiable appetite for profit is a constant of human nature; what matters is that prohibitions should direct people uniformly. Why, then, should administration be divided between the different arrangements for ordinary households and salt-producing households, impeded by the divergent procedures of prefectures and military guards, and obstructed by the difficulty of punishing powerful local families, so that the orders governing and restraining them…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
令有所不行則下無法守而私販之興者
日益熾是謂禁令之不壹夫私販旣興則
商鹽自困商鹽旣困則報中必寡其事正
相反而其害常相須者也如是而欲
國課之充嵗輸之盈必不可得矣然則淮浙
之鹽難而課多八閩之鹽易而課少者豈
非職此之故哉姑卽鹽法之鉅者論之均
一場司也而徵納有本折之異是固以便
竈也然從宜納價或啓姦竈私鬻之端可
===
不曲防其敝乎同一引鹽也而分析有大
小引之殊是固以便商也然增減無稽或
滋姦詭冒帶之弊可不嚴覈其實乎竈以
辦鹽也而潯浯昞三場之民皆得以米折
價則其日辦之鹽何所為耶課以餉邊也
而潯浯昞三場之課皆盡給泉州軍餉則
其額設之糧何所用耶赴邊中引者不易
之規而姦商土著獨專報中之利則嬴縮
得以自由矣可不繩之以法乎寬免竈丁
punctuated: 令有所不行，則下無法守，而私販之興者日益熾，是謂禁令之不壹。夫私販旣興，則商鹽自困；商鹽旣困，則報中必寡。其事正相反，而其害常相須者也。如是而欲國課之充、嵗輸之盈，必不可得矣。然則淮浙之鹽難而課多，八閩之鹽易而課少者，豈非職此之故哉？姑卽鹽法之鉅者論之：均一場司也，而徵納有本折之異，是固以便竈也。然從宜納價，或啓姦竈私鬻之端，可不曲防其敝乎？同一引鹽也，而分析有大小引之殊，是固以便商也。然增減無稽，或滋姦詭冒帶之弊，可不嚴覈其實乎？竈以辦鹽也，而潯浯昞三場之民皆得以米折價，則其日辦之鹽何所為耶？課以餉邊也，而潯浯昞三場之課皆盡給泉州軍餉，則其額設之糧何所用耶？赴邊中引者，不易之規，而姦商土著獨專報中之利，則嬴縮得以自由矣，可不繩之以法乎？寬免竈丁
translation_en:
…when these regulations fail to be enforced, those below have no laws to observe, and illicit salt trading grows ever more rampant. This is what is meant by a lack of uniformity in prohibitions. Once illicit trading flourishes, the licensed salt trade naturally falls into difficulty; once the licensed trade is in difficulty, applications for salt certificates inevitably become few. These activities stand directly opposed, yet their harmful effects continually reinforce one another. Under such circumstances, adequate state salt revenues and full annual remittances are impossible to obtain. Is this not precisely why salt production in Huai and Zhe is difficult yet yields substantial revenue, while production in the Eight Min regions of Fujian is easy yet yields little?
Let us discuss just the major features of the salt regulations. All are alike saltworks offices, yet their levies differ between payment in kind and commuted payment. This is certainly intended to accommodate salt-producing households. But allowing payment of an equivalent value as convenient may open the way for unscrupulous producers to sell privately. Can we fail to take every precaution against this abuse? Likewise, all are salt certificates, yet they are divided into large and small certificates. This is certainly intended to accommodate merchants. But unchecked increases and reductions may foster fraudulent carriage of extra salt under false claims. Can we fail to scrutinize the actual quantities strictly?
Salt-producing households exist to supply salt. Yet the people of the three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and Bing [?] are all permitted to pay rice in commutation of its value. What, then, becomes of the salt they produce each day? Salt revenues exist to provision the frontier. Yet the revenues of these three saltworks are all devoted entirely to military provisions at Quanzhou. What, then, is the grain allocated under the established quota used for? Going to the frontier to obtain salt certificates by supplying provisions is an unalterable rule. Yet unscrupulous merchants and local residents monopolize the profits of applying for certificates, leaving them free to manipulate surpluses and shortfalls. Can we fail to restrain them by law? Granting reductions and exemptions to salt-production workers…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
者優恤之典而刁竈滑胥遂成詭寄之習
則影射無所不至矣可不糾之以刑乎有
欲别立抽分於潯浯沺三場者正以懲納
價私鬻之姦耳殊不知塲以辦課而肇立
抽分非制也孰若減價召中則商皆樂趨
而姦竈私鬻者自無以專其利矣有欲添
委掣摯於福寧福安地方者不過圖目前
軍門之利耳殊不知商已納價而又額外
加稅非法也孰若嚴捕私販則無事加稅
===
而巡緝所獲者自足以供其用矣一正一
餘淮浙之運鹽則然也而一母二子則夾
帶之漸恐不免矣是或可變而通之者也
懸衡秤較淮浙之榷鹽則然也而圍量抽
掣則欺隱之弊所必至矣是或可倣而正
之者也東路細鹽之規雖似競利矣然邊
海之民利玆貿易實默爲安輯之計也而
或者議之此之謂不知務者矣南路官鹽
之立雖若多事矣然私販之徒樂於趨市
punctuated:
者，優恤之典，而刁竈滑胥遂成詭寄之習，則影射無所不至矣，可不糾之以刑乎？

有欲别立抽分於潯浯沺三場者，正以懲納價私鬻之姦耳。殊不知塲以辦課，而肇立抽分，非制也。孰若減價召中，則商皆樂趨，而姦竈私鬻者自無以專其利矣。有欲添委掣摯於福寧、福安地方者，不過圖目前軍門之利耳。殊不知商已納價，而又額外加稅，非法也。孰若嚴捕私販，則無事加稅，而巡緝所獲者自足以供其用矣。

一正一餘，淮浙之運鹽則然也，而一母二子，則夾帶之漸恐不免矣，是或可變而通之者也。懸衡秤較，淮浙之榷鹽則然也，而圍量抽掣，則欺隱之弊所必至矣，是或可倣而正之者也。

東路細鹽之規，雖似競利矣，然邊海之民利玆貿易，實默爲安輯之計也，而或者議之，此之謂不知務者矣。南路官鹽之立，雖若多事矣，然私販之徒樂於趨市
translation_en:
…is a provision for generous relief. Yet crafty salt producers and unscrupulous clerks have made fraudulent registration under others’ names habitual, so that every conceivable form of evasion under another’s cover occurs. Can this go uncorrected by penal sanctions?

Some wish to establish a separate levy in kind at the three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and Tian, precisely to punish the fraud of paying the assessed price and then selling salt privately. They fail to understand that saltworks exist to meet the salt revenue quota: introducing a levy in kind is outside the established system. How much better to reduce the price and invite merchants to subscribe for salt certificates! Merchants would then gladly come forward, and fraudulent producers selling privately would naturally cease to monopolize the profits. Some wish to appoint additional officials to inspect salt consignments [?] in Funing and Fu’an, merely to secure an immediate benefit for the military headquarters. They fail to understand that merchants have already paid the price; imposing additional taxes beyond the quota is unlawful. How much better to apprehend illicit dealers rigorously! There would then be no need for additional taxation, and the proceeds of patrols and seizures would themselves suffice to meet the expenditure.

One regular allotment and one supplementary allotment: this is the practice for transporting salt in Huai and Zhe. But with one “mother” and two “children” [?], the gradual growth of illicit extra cargo will, I fear, be unavoidable. This is perhaps something that could be modified to make the system work effectively. Suspending balances and checking weights: this is the practice of the salt monopoly in Huai and Zhe. But measuring by circumference and making deductions upon inspection [?] inevitably leads to fraud and concealment. This is perhaps something that could be corrected by following their example.

Although the regulations for fine salt on the eastern route may appear to compete for profit, coastal residents benefit from this trade, which in fact quietly serves to keep them settled and at peace. Yet some criticize it: these are what one calls people who do not understand practical affairs. Although establishing government salt sales on the southern route may seem to create unnecessary business, illicit dealers gladly come to the market…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
實潜消姦宄之習也而或者病之是必不
便其私者矣此閩中鹽法之大都也執事
明問猶欲使法復
祖宗之舊而不拂乎時宜課歸軍國之資而無
病小民之利甚盛心也然亦豈待於他求
哉亦曰經畫有方曰禁令克壹耳愚也嘗
竊爲之繹其說其目有六一曰還額鹽之
舊夫潯浯昞三場隸於運司課以萬計此
太祖定制也泉州暫借以爲軍餉之資不過後
===
人一時權宜之計耳遂襲以爲常久假者
固不知歸暫假之者亦視以爲舊殊不知
閩惟七場而名存實亡已去其半矣是可
不亟反之哉二曰通食鹽之宜竊稽我
太祖之制計口分鹽則興泉等府食鹽皆有定
數戶部額數可稽也今槩食私鹽習以爲
故正以潯浯昞三場之鹽籍口納米恣意
賤鬻故耳懲之則拂民情縱之則干法紀
或者倣兩浙題
punctuated:
實潜消姦宄之習也，而或者病之，是必不便其私者矣。此閩中鹽法之大都也。執事明問，猶欲使法復祖宗之舊而不拂乎時宜，課歸軍國之資而無病小民之利，甚盛心也。然亦豈待於他求哉？亦曰經畫有方，曰禁令克壹耳。愚也嘗竊爲之繹其說，其目有六。
一曰還額鹽之舊。夫潯、浯、昞三場隸於運司，課以萬計，此太祖定制也。泉州暫借以爲軍餉之資，不過後人一時權宜之計耳，遂襲以爲常。久假者固不知歸，暫假之者亦視以爲舊。殊不知閩惟七場，而名存實亡，已去其半矣。是可不亟反之哉？
二曰通食鹽之宜。竊稽我太祖之制，計口分鹽，則興、泉等府食鹽皆有定數，戶部額數可稽也。今槩食私鹽，習以爲故，正以潯、浯、昞三場之鹽，籍口納米，恣意賤鬻故耳。懲之則拂民情，縱之則干法紀。或者倣兩浙題
translation_en:
…in fact quietly dissipates the habit of illicit activity. Yet some find fault with it; these must be people whose private interests it inconveniences. Such is the broad outline of the salt administration in Fujian. Your discerning question seeks further to restore the laws of our imperial ancestors without contravening present needs, and to direct the revenue toward military and state expenses without harming the livelihoods of ordinary people. This is a most generous intention. Yet why should its fulfillment require looking elsewhere? It requires only sound planning and uniform enforcement of prohibitions. I have ventured to work through the matter, and my proposals fall under six headings.
First, restore the former arrangements for quota salt. The three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and Bing [?] belong under the Salt Distribution Commission, and their tax assessments are reckoned in tens of thousands. This was the system established by Emperor Taizu. Quanzhou temporarily borrowed their revenues to fund military provisions; this was merely a temporary expedient adopted by later officials. Yet it was subsequently followed as a standing practice. Those who have borrowed for so long naturally no longer think of returning what they borrowed, while those making a temporary loan likewise regard it as established practice. They fail to realize that Fujian has only seven saltworks: with these remaining under its jurisdiction in name but lost in substance, nearly half are already gone. How can they not be restored urgently?
Second, make suitable arrangements for salt consumption. On examining the system of our Emperor Taizu, I find that salt was apportioned according to population. Thus the prefectures of Xinghua, Quanzhou, and the others all had fixed quantities of salt for consumption, and the quotas can be checked in the records of the Ministry of Revenue. Now everyone consumes illicit salt and has come to regard this as customary. This is precisely because salt from the three works of Xun, Wu, and Bing [?] is sold cheaply at will under the pretext of making grain payments. Punishing this practice goes against popular sentiment; allowing it violates the law. One possible course would be to follow the example of Liangzhe and petition…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
准鹽票而行之令民買票買鹽分之定地嚴之
定期則興泉之鹽法旣行而民心亦無不
順矣三曰正行鹽之地夫汀漳二府本閩
鹽額地後以兩廣軍門暫借吉贛行鹽因
而廣鹽盡布江右乃復遷延浸蔓廣鹽直
達於汀漳遂委二府爲廣鹽之地不亦謬
乎是不可以不正也四曰嚴捕鹽之禁竊
觀今捕鹽之法軍則自衞而達之於所有
司則自府而縣而達之於巡司固通於天
===
下者也八閩獨置而不講何歟况興泉爲
山海淵藪之地汀漳爲韶廣咽喉之所而
私鹽無捕無惑乎鹽法之不行於四府也
夫鹽法旣不行於四府則株守者惟延建
邵耳所輸能幾何哉是不可以不深慮也
五曰專督鹽之責夫轉運之設專掌財賦
本無統轄之權也而欲以列郡之鹽法盡
責之雖欲有志於經畫其如弗率何哉故
必專董之以憲臣而仍統之於監使則責
punctuated:
准鹽票而行之，令民買票買鹽，分之定地，嚴之定期，則興泉之鹽法旣行，而民心亦無不順矣。
三曰正行鹽之地。夫汀漳二府，本閩鹽額地，後以兩廣軍門暫借吉贛行鹽，因而廣鹽盡布江右，乃復遷延浸蔓，廣鹽直達於汀漳，遂委二府爲廣鹽之地，不亦謬乎？是不可以不正也。
四曰嚴捕鹽之禁。竊觀今捕鹽之法，軍則自衞而達之於所，有司則自府而縣而達之於巡司，固通於天下者也。八閩獨置而不講，何歟？况興泉爲山海淵藪之地，汀漳爲韶廣咽喉之所，而私鹽無捕，無惑乎鹽法之不行於四府也。夫鹽法旣不行於四府，則株守者惟延建邵耳，所輸能幾何哉？是不可以不深慮也。
五曰專督鹽之責。夫轉運之設，專掌財賦，本無統轄之權也，而欲以列郡之鹽法盡責之，雖欲有志於經畫，其如弗率何哉？故必專董之以憲臣，而仍統之於監使，則責
translation_en:
…implement the approved salt-ticket system, requiring the people to buy tickets to purchase salt, assigning fixed territories and strictly enforcing fixed time limits. Then the salt regulations in Xinghua and Quanzhou would be implemented, and the people would all willingly comply.
Third, rectify the territories in which salt may be sold. The two prefectures of Tingzhou and Zhangzhou were originally territories assigned to Fujian’s salt quota. Later, the supreme commander of Guangdong and Guangxi temporarily obtained permission to use Ji’an and Ganzhou for salt sales. Consequently, Guangdong salt spread throughout Jiangxi. This arrangement was then prolonged, and its reach gradually expanded until Guangdong salt reached Tingzhou and Zhangzhou directly. The two prefectures were thus relinquished as territories for Guangdong salt. Is this not mistaken? This must be rectified.
Fourth, strictly enforce the prohibitions against illicit salt through its seizure. I humbly observe that under the present system for apprehending salt smugglers, military enforcement proceeds from the guards to the battalions, while civil enforcement proceeds from the prefectures through the counties to the police offices. This is the system throughout the empire. Why does Fujian alone set it aside and neglect it? Moreover, Xinghua and Quanzhou offer mountain and coastal refuges for smugglers, while Tingzhou and Zhangzhou occupy the strategic passage to Shaozhou and Guangzhou. Yet no action is taken against illicit salt. No wonder the salt regulations are not implemented in these four prefectures. If the salt regulations are not implemented there, only Yanping, Jianning, and Shaowu remain bound by them. How much revenue can they remit? This requires profound consideration.
Fifth, assign clear responsibility for supervising salt administration. The Salt Distribution Commission was established specifically to manage fiscal revenues; it originally possessed no authority of general jurisdiction. Yet it is expected to bear full responsibility for salt administration in all the prefectures. Even if its officials are intent on planning and management, what can they do when others will not obey? A censorial official must therefore be given specific responsibility for overseeing it, while it remains under the overall authority of the supervising commissioner [?]. Then the responsibility…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
任攸隆必宏經理之策政令易達自無廢
弛之患矣六曰復中鹽之規夫沿邊召商
報中而內地據引支鹽此建立轉運之初
意也閩鹽不行而邊引不至也久矣有志
於天下者能不深長思也夫既區畫得宜
鹽法無滯然後以漸行之非沿邊報中者
不得支鹽則報中之規既復商鹽之行益
廣如是而閩中鹽法何不及於淮浙也哉
夫如是而後為經畫之有方夫如是而後
===
為禁令之克壹夫如是而後謂之鹽法草
茆藿食之見如斯而已若秉之以公而無
畏乎疆禦持之以久而不惑於流俗則神
而明之存乎其人
punctuated: 任攸隆，必宏經理之策，政令易達，自無廢弛之患矣。六曰：復中鹽之規。夫沿邊召商報中，而內地據引支鹽，此建立轉運之初意也。閩鹽不行，而邊引不至也久矣。有志於天下者，能不深長思也？夫既區畫得宜，鹽法無滯，然後以漸行之，非沿邊報中者不得支鹽，則報中之規既復，商鹽之行益廣。如是而閩中鹽法何不及於淮浙也哉？夫如是而後為經畫之有方，夫如是而後為禁令之克壹，夫如是而後謂之鹽法。草茆藿食之見，如斯而已。若秉之以公而無畏乎疆禦，持之以久而不惑於流俗，則神而明之，存乎其人。
translation_en:
…with responsibility thus enhanced, plans for administration will surely be broadened, government orders will readily reach their destinations, and there will naturally be no danger of neglect or laxity.

Sixth: restore the rules for obtaining salt through the grain-delivery system. Merchants were recruited along the frontier to register deliveries of grain in exchange for salt certificates, and then collected salt in the interior upon presentation of those certificates. This was the original intent behind establishing the Salt Distribution Commission. Salt from Fujian has failed to circulate, and frontier salt certificates have failed to arrive, for a long time now. Can those concerned for the realm fail to reflect deeply and at length upon this? Once arrangements have been properly made and the salt administration operates without obstruction, the rule should gradually be implemented that no one may collect salt without having registered a grain delivery along the frontier. Once this system is restored, the circulation of merchants’ salt will become still more extensive. Under these circumstances, why should Fujian’s salt administration not equal that of the Huai region and Zhejiang? Only then will planning be properly directed; only then will prohibitions be uniformly enforced; only then will it deserve to be called a system of salt administration. These are merely the views of one who dwells in a thatched hut and eats coarse vegetable fare. As for administering it impartially, without fearing the powerful, and maintaining it steadfastly, without being misled by prevailing opinion—its inspired and discerning application rests with the person entrusted with it.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
嘉靖己酉秋八月學正冦韋
敎諭趙文翰各膺聘濫竽福
建試事旣取士錄成文翰當
序諸末簡乃執筆而歎曰猗
歟盛哉道化人文之美由陶
唐以來而復有
===
今日之爲盛也文翰蓋以閩粤之
士觀之昔聖人南面而聽天
下嚮明以爲治光被昭格當
其所面之方照燭休爽尤爲
焜顯而欲考其德之明者亦
於其方之最遠而著者以爲
徴故書頌放勳之大至於海
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

嘉靖己酉秋八月，學正冦韋、敎諭趙文翰各膺聘，濫竽福建試事。旣取士，錄成，文翰當序諸末簡，乃執筆而歎曰：「猗歟，盛哉！道化人文之美，由陶唐以來，而復有今日之爲盛也！」文翰蓋以閩粤之士觀之。昔聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明以爲治，光被昭格。當其所面之方，照燭休爽，尤爲焜顯。而欲考其德之明者，亦於其方之最遠而著者以爲徴。故書頌放勳之大，至於海
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549], School Instructor Kou Wei and County School Instructor Zhao Wenhan each accepted an invitation to serve, unworthily, in conducting the Fujian examination. Once the candidates had been selected and the record completed, I, Wenhan, was to supply a postface on its final leaves. Taking up my brush, I exclaimed: “Ah, how splendid! The beauty of moral transformation and human culture, flourishing under Taotang [Yao], has again attained such splendor today!” I, Wenhan, judge this from the scholars of Min and Yue.

In antiquity, the sage faced south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern. His radiance spread and his luminous influence reached afar. In the direction he faced, its illumination was especially brilliant and clear. Those wishing to examine the luminosity of his virtue likewise sought evidence where its manifestation was most distant in that direction. Thus, in praising the greatness of Fangxun [Yao], the Book of Documents speaks of its reaching as far as the sea…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
隅日出罔不率俾而所謂如
天之蕩蕩者於是乎彷彿而
可名由堯以降莫如文王之
純然其顯於四方者獨著於
南故汝墳江沱之風爲周之
盛然則歷古帝王之德其盛
也必究於南而其極盛也必
===
===
際於最遠詩書所稱可睹已
閩粵在南之方最遠大海之
隅日所從出處也意其荒陋
幽側無以望中國之昭回今
其文之可見者宣躍炳朗發
揮乎詩書禮樂之精宣鬯乎
仁義道德之輝而蔚然治世
punctuated:
隅日出，罔不率俾，而所謂如天之蕩蕩者，於是乎彷彿而可名。由堯以降，莫如文王之純，然其顯於四方者，獨著於南，故汝墳、江沱之風爲周之盛。然則歷古帝王之德，其盛也必究於南，而其極盛也必際於最遠，《詩》《書》所稱可睹已。
閩粵在南之方最遠，大海之隅，日所從出處也。意其荒陋幽側，無以望中國之昭回，今其文之可見者，宣躍炳朗，發揮乎詩書禮樂之精，宣鬯乎仁義道德之輝，而蔚然治世
translation_en:
…at the shores where the sun rises, none failed to follow and obey. Thus what is called his vastness, like that of Heaven, may be dimly apprehended and put into words. From Yao onward, none equaled King Wen in purity of virtue. Yet, though his virtue shone in all four quarters, it was especially manifest in the south. Thus the airs of the banks of the Ru River and the Jiang and Tuo rivers exemplified the flourishing of Zhou. Accordingly, the virtue of ancient emperors and kings, when flourishing, invariably reached the south; at its fullest flourishing, it invariably extended to the remotest places. This can be seen in what the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents recount.
Min and Yue lie in the farthest reaches of the south, at the shores of the great sea, where the sun rises. One might suppose that their wildness, rusticity, obscurity, and remoteness left them unable to aspire to the radiance of the Central Realm. Yet the writings now available for inspection are animated and brilliantly clear. They bring forth the essence of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music, and fully express the splendor of benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue, luxuriantly flourishing in an age of good government…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之能言由其言以論其志皆
有用於世者也堯之光于海
隅也黎獻共惟帝臣文王之
風被于南國田間椓杙之夫
且與公侯匹體人才之生可
爲世用而莫不志於用世是
其所以爲盛之實也故文翰
===
直以此方之士之文而知
今日之盛爲由陶唐氏以來而一
再有也豈不信哉我
皇上一德執中建維皇之極陶成
羣品覆育萬彙蓋秉周文之
純而嗣唐堯之統其德之及
于四表如日月之照臨而其
punctuated: 之能言。由其言以論其志，皆有用於世者也。堯之光于海隅也，黎獻共惟帝臣；文王之風被于南國，田間椓杙之夫，且與公侯匹體。人才之生，可爲世用，而莫不志於用世，是其所以爲盛之實也。故文翰直以此方之士之文，而知今日之盛，爲由陶唐氏以來而一再有也，豈不信哉？我皇上一德執中，建維皇之極，陶成羣品，覆育萬彙，蓋秉周文之純，而嗣唐堯之統。其德之及于四表，如日月之照臨，而其
translation_en: …eloquent voices of a well-governed age. Judging their aspirations from their words, they are all men who can be of service to the world. When Yao’s radiance reached the seacoasts, the worthy among the common people were all the emperor’s servants. When King Wen’s transforming influence spread over the southern lands, even men driving stakes in the fields could stand as peers of dukes and lords. Talented men emerge who can serve their age, and all aspire to put their abilities to public use: this is the substance of that flourishing. Thus I, Wenhan, can tell simply from the writings of this region’s scholars that today’s flourishing is something seen only once or twice since the time of Taotang—that is, Yao. Is this not indeed true? Our emperor, with undivided virtue, holds fast to the Mean and establishes the imperial standard. He shapes all beings and shelters and nurtures the myriad kinds. He possesses the purity of King Wen of Zhou and continues the succession of Yao of Tang. His virtue reaches the four outermost regions like the illuminating presence of the sun and moon, and its…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
所面之方獨切於光華閩粤
之士宜其莫不爲材也昔周
之季淮徐吳越之間猶爲春
秋所外雖當孔孟之時而以
文學名者於吳惟一言偃學
於中國者於楚惟一陳良况
於峻嶺限隔之表大海之隅
===
日所從出處耶彼閩粤於其
時宜荒陋幽側而無所聞於
策也今玆之美若此然則此
方之士豈能自爲材耶凡士
之生雖不繋於地而亦以邇
爲貴豪傑之興固無所待於
上尤願於得所事而快利見
punctuated: 所面之方，獨切於光華。閩粤之士，宜其莫不爲材也。昔周之季，淮徐吳越之間，猶爲《春秋》所外。雖當孔孟之時，而以文學名者，於吳惟一言偃；學於中國者，於楚惟一陳良。况於峻嶺限隔之表、大海之隅、日所從出處耶？彼閩粤於其時，宜荒陋幽側，而無所聞於策也。今玆之美若此，然則此方之士，豈能自爲材耶？凡士之生，雖不繋於地，而亦以邇爲貴。豪傑之興，固無所待於上，尤願於得所事而快利見
translation_en: …the region toward which he faces receives his radiance with particular immediacy. It is fitting that the scholars of Min and Yue should all become men of talent. In the final age of the Zhou, the lands of Huai, Xu, Wu, and Yue were still treated as outside the civilized sphere by the Spring and Autumn Annals. Even in the time of Confucius and Mencius, among those renowned for literary learning, Wu had only Yan Yan; among those who studied in the Central States, Chu had only Chen Liang. How much more was this true beyond the barrier of lofty mountains, at the edge of the great sea, where the sun rises! Min and Yue in those days must have been uncultivated, obscure, and remote, with nothing of them recorded in the annals. Yet their present excellence is such as this! Could the scholars of this region, then, have become men of talent entirely by themselves? Although the emergence of scholars is not bound to any particular place, proximity to the ruler is nevertheless prized. The rise of outstanding men certainly does not depend upon those above them; yet they especially desire to find a ruler worthy of their service and to enjoy the auspicious opportunity of an audience…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
以彼偃良之賢得及江漢汝
墳之風其爲公侯好仇心腹
豈直兎罝野人之比乎以其
不遇徒爲季世下土之賢而
已諸士雖生於最遠猶當
聖人所面之方復能以材自顯使
欲求
===
昭代德化之盛者於此乎徴蓋
已幸矣其尤幸者以
今上之爲君而士之顯於其世者
預其見知之傳刑乎譽髦之
化則藹藹濟濟皆媚于之吉
人以寧之多士也豈如言偃
陳良獨爲季世下土之賢而
punctuated: 以彼偃良之賢，得及江漢汝墳之風，其爲公侯好仇心腹，豈直兎罝野人之比乎？以其不遇，徒爲季世下土之賢而已。諸士雖生於最遠，猶當聖人所面之方，復能以材自顯，使欲求昭代德化之盛者於此乎徴，蓋已幸矣。其尤幸者，以今上之爲君，而士之顯於其世者，預其見知之傳，刑乎譽髦之化，則藹藹濟濟，皆媚于之吉人、以寧之多士也。豈如言偃陳良，獨爲季世下土之賢而
translation_en: …Had men as worthy as Yan Yan and Chen Liang come within the civilizing influence celebrated in “The Jiang and Han Rivers” and “The Banks of the Ru,” would they, as worthy companions and trusted confidants of dukes and lords, have been merely comparable to the rustic rabbit-netters of the Odes? Because they did not encounter such an opportunity, they remained merely worthy men of a declining age and a remote region. Although you scholars were born in the most distant reaches, you nevertheless inhabit the quarter toward which the sage faces. Moreover, you have been able to distinguish yourselves through your talents, allowing those who seek evidence of the flourishing moral influence of this illustrious dynasty to find it here. This is already fortunate indeed. Still more fortunate is that, with His Present Majesty as ruler, scholars who distinguish themselves in his age partake in the transmission of the Way through direct acquaintance with the sage [?] and are shaped by a civilizing influence that nurtures outstanding talent. Thus, abundant and dignified, they are all the good men whom the ruler cherishes, the many scholars through whom he secures peace. How could they resemble Yan Yan and Chen Liang, who remained merely worthy men of a declining age and a remote region …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
已哉諸士其能以無願乎否
則直凡民之不如耳有帝堯
以爲
君而士者不知自異於凡民其能
以無媿乎故文翰序是錄也
而爲諸士告焉
山東濟南府武定州陽信縣
===
儒學教諭趙文翰謹序
punctuated:
已哉？諸士其能以無願乎？否則，直凡民之不如耳。有帝堯以爲君，而士者不知自異於凡民，其能以無媿乎？故文翰序是錄也，而爲諸士告焉。
山東濟南府武定州陽信縣儒學教諭趙文翰謹序。
translation_en:
…and nothing more? Can you gentlemen have no aspirations? Otherwise, you would simply be inferior even to ordinary people. With an Emperor Yao as ruler, if scholars do not know to distinguish themselves from ordinary people, can they be without shame? Thus I, Wenhan, have written this preface to the record to offer these words to you gentlemen.
Preface respectfully composed by Zhao Wenhan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
嘉靖己酉天下士屬當大比
仰惟
皇上致理作人于玆三紀而登進
者凡十科矣猗與盛哉福建
試事届期巡按御史陳宗夔
始被
===
命司監臨祗奉
德意兼程而南旣至則益嚴前御
史楊九澤所聘文學與諸遴
簡執事者以學正寇韋敎諭
趙文翰主試以敎諭黎天啟
蔣仲哲學正龍旆敎諭馮璠
方輅費增胡然分試提調則
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

嘉靖己酉，天下士屬當大比。仰惟皇上致理作人，于玆三紀，而登進者凡十科矣。猗與盛哉！福建試事届期，巡按御史陳宗夔始被命司監臨，祗奉德意，兼程而南。旣至，則益嚴前御史楊九澤所聘文學與諸遴簡執事者。以學正寇韋、敎諭趙文翰主試，以敎諭黎天啟、蔣仲哲、學正龍旆、敎諭馮璠、方輅、費增、胡然分試。提調則
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549], scholars throughout the realm were due to participate in the triennial examination. Reverently considering how His Majesty has brought about good government and cultivated men of talent for three twelve-year cycles, we find that ten examination cohorts in all have been advanced. Ah, how flourishing!

When the time arrived for the Fujian examination, Regional Inspector Chen Zongkui received his appointment to serve as Supervising Official. Reverently carrying out the imperial benevolent intent, he traveled south at an accelerated pace. Upon arriving, he further tightened supervision over the men of learning engaged by the previous Regional Inspector, Yang Jiuze, and the various personnel selected to conduct the examination [?]. School Instructor Kou Wei and Instructor Zhao Wenhan served as Examiners. Instructors Li Tianqi and Jiang Zhongzhe, School Instructor Long Pei, and Instructors Feng Fan, Fang Lu, Fei Zeng, and Hu Ran served as Associate Examiners. As for the Proctors, they were…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
左布政使屠大山右布政使
張鏊監試則按察副使柯喬
僉事鄭炯旣鑰院御史矢言
曰惟玆求賢鉅典仰厪
淵衷形之
詔令屢矣肆吾二三謭劣執事者
其何以對揚之其惟勤惟愼
===
===
惟公無私惟進端純而黜浮
靡衆唯唯籲於
天神乃合士之選於提學副使周
琉者三千有奇三試之拔其
尤得九十人乃鍥其名氏弁
文之優者二十一篇爲錄以
獻韋首序之曰昔閩東南荒服
punctuated:
左布政使屠大山、右布政使張鏊，監試則按察副使柯喬、僉事鄭炯。旣鑰院，御史矢言曰：「惟玆求賢鉅典，仰厪淵衷，形之詔令屢矣。肆吾二三謭劣執事者，其何以對揚之？其惟勤惟愼，惟公無私，惟進端純而黜浮靡。」衆唯唯，籲於天神。乃合士之選於提學副使周琉者三千有奇，三試之，拔其尤，得九十人。乃鍥其名氏，弁文之優者二十一篇，爲錄以獻。
韋首序之曰：「昔閩，東南荒服
translation_en:
…the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, Tu Dashan, and the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, Zhang Ao; examination oversight fell to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ke Qiao and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zheng Jiong. Once the examination compound had been locked, the Censor solemnly declared: “This great undertaking of seeking worthy men has repeatedly engaged His Majesty’s profound concern, expressed in imperial edicts. How, then, shall we few humble and inadequate officials entrusted with this duty acknowledge and carry forward his intentions? Only by diligence and care, by impartiality without selfishness, and by advancing the upright and pure while rejecting the shallow and ornate.” All voiced their assent and invoked the celestial spirits.
They then assembled the more than three thousand scholars selected by Zhou Liu, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant. They examined them in three sessions and chose the most outstanding, obtaining ninety men. They then had their names engraved for printing and placed twenty-one of the finest essays at the beginning, compiling a record for presentation.
Wei supplied the opening preface, saying: “Formerly, Min was a remote outer region in the southeast…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也在宋稱人文其俗爲鄒魯
其出者多名碩有行業聞望
皆儒先倡明理學之餘也然
理學在天地猶元氣也其盛
衰一繫乎時諸儒先雖倡明
之然未甞嚮用尤未能彰顯
如我
===
國家如
今日也蓋帝王心傳之失也久矣
自我
聖祖崇儒肇學
文皇帝建極乃裒經傳而頒示之
於是理學明備暨我
皇上統壹聖眞又以帝王躬行之
punctuated:
