也。在宋稱人文，其俗爲鄒魯，其出者多名碩，有行業聞望，皆儒先倡明理學之餘也。然理學在天地，猶元氣也，其盛衰一繫乎時。諸儒先雖倡明之，然未甞嚮用，尤未能彰顯如我國家、如今日也。
蓋帝王心傳之失也久矣。自我聖祖崇儒肇學，文皇帝建極，乃裒經傳而頒示之，於是理學明備。暨我皇上統壹聖眞，又以帝王躬行之
translation_en:
… During the Song, Fujian became renowned for its cultural accomplishments, and its customs resembled those of Zou and Lu, the homelands of Mencius and Confucius. Many eminent scholars emerged there, distinguished by their conduct, achievements, and reputations. All this was the enduring legacy of earlier Confucian scholars who had promoted and elucidated the Learning of Principle. Yet the Learning of Principle exists within Heaven and Earth like primordial vital energy: its flourishing and decline depend entirely upon the times. Although earlier Confucian scholars promoted and elucidated it, it had never been embraced and put into practice, still less made manifest as under our dynasty and in our own day.
Indeed, the transmission of the Way from mind to mind among emperors and kings had long been lost. Our Sagely Progenitor honored Confucian learning and established schools; the Wen Emperor established the supreme standard of rulership, then assembled the classics and their commentaries and promulgated them. Thus the Learning of Principle became fully elucidated. When our present emperor unified the true teachings of the sages, he further took what emperors and kings personally put into practice …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
理揭之
訓詞
振德之功垂于萬世豈惟一鄉
已哉然則士之盛於閩與主
司之望士皆於是乎在蓋嘗
論之儒之功用大矣而有所
遇以行所學則儒先大願之
===
而不能獲也然必屬諸後人
後之人居其鄉蒙其教澤而
生
聖人之世乃寓於文也舉千百年
之大願而欲售之感慨乎殊
昔奮庸於
清朝其可以厚望也明矣顧主
punctuated: 理，揭之訓詞，振德之功垂于萬世，豈惟一鄉已哉？然則士之盛於閩，與主司之望士，皆於是乎在。蓋嘗論之：儒之功用大矣，而有所遇以行所學，則儒先大願之而不能獲也，然必屬諸後人。後之人居其鄉，蒙其教澤，而生聖人之世，乃寓於文也。舉千百年之大願而欲售之，感慨乎殊昔，奮庸於清朝，其可以厚望也明矣。顧主
translation_en:
…principles, setting them forth in His admonitory pronouncements. The achievement of fostering virtue will endure for ten thousand generations; how could it benefit only a single locality? Thus, both the flourishing of scholars in Fujian and the hopes that the examination officials place in them rest upon this.
I have reflected on this: great indeed is the practical contribution of Confucian scholars. Yet to encounter an opportunity to put their learning into practice was something the earlier Confucian masters deeply desired but could not attain. They therefore necessarily entrusted this aspiration to later generations. Those who came after them dwell in their native region, receive the blessings of their teachings, and are born into the age of a sage ruler; they now give expression to these things in their writing. They seek to realize the great aspiration cherished for hundreds and thousands of years, moved by the distant past [?], and to exert themselves in meritorious service to our illustrious dynasty. Clearly, high hopes may be placed in them. Yet the presiding…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
司惴惴然猶且曰知人難以
言知人尤難言之以一日之
長而庸弗違則尤難之至如
是而曰得士則不明之咎誰
其逭之是以懼抑
國家之待士也重矣待之重則
責之不容不重士何以自責
===
乎矧惟儒先之繼免於暴棄
恥為鄉人焉是可懼尤大也
雖然士先志夫志孰大於道
之行哉然以一物為心則累
於一物累斯怠怠斯畫而求
不負於所學得乎士惟責志
焉耳矣乃若主司之需乎士
punctuated:
司惴惴然，猶且曰：「知人難，以言知人尤難；言之以一日之長，而庸弗違，則尤難之至。如是而曰得士，則不明之咎，誰其逭之？」是以懼。抑國家之待士也重矣，待之重，則責之不容不重。士何以自責乎？矧惟儒先之繼，免於暴棄，恥為鄉人焉，是可懼尤大也。
雖然，士先志。夫志孰大於道之行哉？然以一物為心，則累於一物；累斯怠，怠斯畫，而求不負於所學，得乎？士惟責志焉耳矣。乃若主司之需乎士
translation_en:
…the presiding examiner, anxious and apprehensive, still says: “To know people is difficult; to know them through their words is harder still. To judge their words by the excellence displayed on a single day, and then employ them without their falling short of that judgment [?], is the hardest thing of all. If, under these circumstances, I claim to have found worthy scholars, who could escape blame for a lack of discernment?” This is why I am afraid. Moreover, the state accords scholars great consideration. Since it treats them so highly, its demands upon them must necessarily be correspondingly great. What, then, should scholars demand of themselves? Furthermore, as successors to the earlier Confucian masters, they must avoid casting themselves away and regard it as shameful to be merely ordinary villagers. Here is still greater cause for apprehension.
Nevertheless, for scholars, resolve comes first. What aspiration could be greater than putting the Way into practice? Yet if one sets one’s heart on a single thing, one becomes encumbered by it. Encumbrance leads to indolence, and indolence to setting limits upon oneself. Can one then hope not to betray what one has learned? Scholars need only hold themselves accountable for their resolve. As for what the presiding examiner requires of scholars…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也以世道也不以空言也夫
士不務空言而爲世道所賴
必能脫去恆習粹然於吾儒
之學明體而達用以答
聖功以明
文治無忝先正之鄕而主司亦
附於事
===
君以人者所以交懼而相成也然
非志焉曷爲之孔子曰大道
之行三代之英丘未之逮也
而有志焉夫孔子之志何遠
哉蓋所不能必慰者時也爾
諸士以時自慶矣其尚責志
於終焉是舉也提督軍務右
punctuated:
也，以世道也，不以空言也。夫士不務空言，而爲世道所賴，必能脫去恆習，粹然於吾儒之學，明體而達用，以答聖功，以明文治，無忝先正之鄕，而主司亦附於事君以人者，所以交懼而相成也。然非志焉，曷爲之？孔子曰：「大道之行，三代之英，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」夫孔子之志何遠哉！蓋所不能必慰者，時也。爾諸士以時自慶矣，其尚責志於終焉！
是舉也，提督軍務右
translation_en:
…is for the sake of the moral order of the age, not for empty words. If scholars are to eschew empty words and become those upon whom that moral order depends, they must cast off habitual practices, attain purity in our Confucian learning, comprehend its substance and master its application. Thus they may answer the sage emperor’s achievements, make manifest his civil governance, and bring no dishonor upon the native land of earlier worthies. The presiding examiners, too, may thereby be counted among those who serve their ruler by providing him with worthy men. In this way, both sides share a sense of apprehension and help each other fulfill their responsibilities. Yet without setting their resolve upon this, how could they accomplish it? Confucius said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, have not lived to see them, yet I set my resolve upon them.” How far-reaching was Confucius’s resolve! What cannot be assured of bringing satisfaction [?] is the age in which one lives. You scholars congratulate yourselves upon your age; may you continue to hold yourselves accountable for your resolve to the very end!
For this examination, the superintendent of military affairs and Right …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
副都御史喻智遹觀人文右
叅政朱憲章左叅議吳源按
察副使秦鰲僉事余爌桂榮
張恕顧翀都指揮僉事盧鎧
路正均範理於外左叅政汪
大受僉事楊大章都指揮僉
事田耕顧邦重皆預□□□
===
賀按察使周采以遷秩副使張
謙以上績皆先行蓋嘗與勞
書之
直隸真定府趙州儒學學正
寇韋謹序
punctuated:
副都御史喻智遹觀人文，右叅政朱憲章、左叅議吳源、按察副使秦鰲、僉事余爌、桂榮、張恕、顧翀、都指揮僉事盧鎧、路正均範理於外。左叅政汪大受、僉事楊大章、都指揮僉事田耕、顧邦重皆預□□□賀。按察使周采以遷秩，副使張謙以上績，皆先行，蓋嘗與勞，書之。
直隸真定府趙州儒學學正寇韋謹序。
translation_en:
… Deputy Censor-in-Chief Yu Zhiyu observed the flourishing of literary culture. Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Xianzhang, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Wu Yuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qin Ao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yu Kuang, Gui Rong, Zhang Shu, and Gu Chong, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Lu Kai and Lu Zheng all supervised arrangements outside [the examination compound] [?]. Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Dashou, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Yang Dazhang, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Tian Geng and Gu Bangzhong all participated in [three illegible characters] congratulations [?]. Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Cai had departed earlier because of a promotion, as had Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Qian to report his administrative performance. Since they had shared in the work, their names are recorded here.
Preface respectfully written by Kou Wei, Instructor of the Confucian School of Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

Fujian Provincial Examination, the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing (1549).

Supervising Official:
Chen Zongkui, Regional Inspector of Fujian and Investigating Censor. His courtesy name was Weiyi; he was from Tongshan County, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuxu year.

Proctors:
Tu Dashan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner in the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Guowang; he was from Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Associate Examiners:
Li Tianqi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yudu County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Yunzhong; he was from Shunde County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student of the guimao year.
Jiang Zhongzhe, Instructor in the Confucian School of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Rujian; he was from Quan Subprefecture, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Long Pei, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jingzhou Subprefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Shiyang; he was from Rong County, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Feng Fan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yizhen County, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Meizhong; he was registered in Yongning Guard, Guizhou, and was originally from Qiantang County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student of the jiawu year.

Four Books

“The rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil are the means of serving the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple are the means of sacrificing to one’s ancestors. If one understands the rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altar of soil, and the meaning of the di and chang ancestral sacrifices, would governing a state not be like looking at something displayed on one’s palm?”

“There has never been a righteous person who put his ruler last.”

Book of Changes

“The great man is one whose virtue accords with Heaven and Earth.”

“All ways of increase proceed in step with the times.”

“Thus, closing the door is called kun; opening the door is called qian. Alternately closing and opening is called change; coming and going without end is called free passage. What becomes visible is called an image; what takes shape is called an implement. Fashioning things and putting them to use is called a method; making their use beneficial in coming and going, so that all the people employ them, is called the numinous. Thus, in the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate, which generates the two primary forms. The two primary forms generate the four images; the four images generate the eight trigrams.”

“By this the hundred officials govern, and the myriad people are kept under scrutiny.”

translation_en:
Third Session

Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: The Book of Changes speaks of harmonious intercourse, and the Book of Documents records an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers. Thus, a meeting of ruler and ministers suited to one another occurs perhaps only once in a thousand years. The practice of exchanging songs at the court of Shun is remote indeed. Since the Han and Tang dynasties, instances of mutual accord between rulers and ministers have been fully recorded in the histories. Were there also any that approached the resonance of those answering songs?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao placed the phrase “ruler and ministers taking an excursion together” at the beginning of the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements. How great are these royal words! Truly, Yu [the age of Shun?] shines through the ages [?]. Reading now the Record of the River-Viewing Tower and the Song of the Drunken Academician, one can still imagine the flourishing accord between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers in those days. Yet the imperial intent was profound and far-reaching: can those living ten thousand generations later fathom even a fraction of it?

The successive sage emperors carried on this tradition, with those above and below united as one. Can you give an account of the imperial summonses, banquets, and excursions recorded in the Record of Imperial Instructions and in the writings of Confucian officials?

Coming down to our present emperor, whose reign coincides with an auspicious age and who rides the timely course of peace and prosperity, he once, during …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
萬幾之暇
召見輔臣及
賜同遊西苑真媲美唐虞同符
聖祖矣
宸翰天章皆昭播寰宇諸士子能仰窺其萬一
歟其鋪張揚厲之以鳴
國家之盛
問甞聞聖人之精因畫以示故書也者所
以畫聖人之心法者也自伏羲始畫八
===
卦而書契聿興嗣後群聖授受心法相
因故帝王之書代有作者其詳可歷指
而言歟黃帝命倉頡作六書而字文肇
立至周宣變爲大篆而文字寢備矣於
群聖心法之微抑有所傳歟秦弗師古
書法漸滅自漢而降十札之書頒及方
國飛白之字賚及近臣勒孝經於碑陰
賜吏治於棘寺書非不善也不知果有
得於聖人之心法否乎洪惟我
punctuated:
萬幾之暇，召見輔臣及賜同遊西苑，真媲美唐虞，同符聖祖矣。宸翰天章，皆昭播寰宇，諸士子能仰窺其萬一歟？其鋪張揚厲之，以鳴國家之盛。

問：甞聞聖人之精，因畫以示。故書也者，所以畫聖人之心法者也。自伏羲始畫八卦，而書契聿興，嗣後群聖授受心法相因，故帝王之書，代有作者，其詳可歷指而言歟？黃帝命倉頡作六書，而字文肇立；至周宣，變爲大篆，而文字寢備矣。於群聖心法之微，抑有所傳歟？秦弗師古，書法漸滅。自漢而降，十札之書頒及方國，飛白之字賚及近臣，勒《孝經》於碑陰，賜吏治於棘寺。書非不善也，不知果有得於聖人之心法否乎？洪惟我
translation_en:
…in moments of leisure amid the myriad affairs of government, summoned his grand secretaries to an audience and graciously permitted them to accompany him on an excursion through the Western Park. This truly rivaled the splendor of the ages of Yao and Shun and accorded with the example of the sage founder. His imperial calligraphy and illustrious compositions have been splendidly disseminated throughout the realm. Can you candidates discern even a ten-thousandth part of their significance? Expound and extol them, proclaiming the flourishing state of our dynasty.

Question: We have heard that the essential spirit of the sages is made manifest through drawn strokes. Thus, writing is the means by which the sages’ teachings of the mind are depicted. From the time when Fuxi first drew the eight trigrams, written records arose. Thereafter, successive sages transmitted and received the teachings of the mind in an unbroken succession. Hence, in every age there were emperors and kings who produced works of writing. Can you enumerate and discuss these in detail? The Yellow Emperor commanded Cangjie to devise the six categories of writing, and written characters were first established. By the time of King Xuan of Zhou, these had developed into the large-seal script, and writing gradually became complete. Did this also transmit something of the subtleties of the sages’ teachings of the mind? Qin did not take antiquity as its model, and the methods of writing gradually disappeared. From the Han onward, writings on ten tablets [?] were distributed to the regional states, and examples of “flying-white” calligraphy were bestowed upon close attendants. The Classic of Filial Piety was engraved on the reverse of a stele, and a text on the administration of officials was bestowed upon the Court of Judicial Review. These writings were certainly fine, but did they truly attain anything of the sages’ teachings of the mind? Reverently considering our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝
聖神天縱凡
誥諭臣民對越
郊廟者皆親灑
宸翰又甞
特命儒臣勒成洪武正韻一書盡合古文之本
旨頓洗千古之陋習誠萬世不刊之典
也然書法之或因或革當時儒臣果何
所取正歟迨我
===
皇上聖思神授
睿藻天成甞以一夜註釋五箴或揮灑千言
頃刻立就勒之
陵寢播之訓告形之咏歌者多出自
奎畫今固已炳燭丹書而粃稃倉史矣然我
皇上心法之傳遠紹羲皇媲休
聖祖者則固不在點畫翰墨之間也多士涵濡
同文之化久矣請敬陳之
問仁智性之德也合內外者也而說者不
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝，聖神天縱，凡誥諭臣民、對越郊廟者，皆親灑宸翰。又甞特命儒臣勒成《洪武正韻》一書，盡合古文之本旨，頓洗千古之陋習，誠萬世不刊之典也。然書法之或因或革，當時儒臣果何所取正歟？迨我皇上，聖思神授，睿藻天成，甞以一夜註釋《五箴》，或揮灑千言，頃刻立就。勒之陵寢，播之訓告，形之咏歌者，多出自奎畫。今固已炳燭丹書，而粃稃倉史矣。然我皇上心法之傳，遠紹羲皇，媲休聖祖者，則固不在點畫翰墨之間也。多士涵濡同文之化久矣，請敬陳之。
問：仁智，性之德也，合內外者也，而說者不
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizu Gao, whose sagacity and spiritual insight were Heaven-bestowed, personally wielded the imperial brush for all proclamations instructing his officials and people and all writings addressing the powers worshipped at the suburban altars and ancestral temples. He also specially commanded Confucian officials to compile the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun). Entirely consonant with the fundamental intent of ancient writing, this work swept away the defective practices of ages at a stroke. Truly, it is an authoritative work that shall remain unaltered for ten thousand generations. Yet, in retaining some conventions of writing and changing others, what standards did the Confucian officials of that time actually follow?
Coming to our present Emperor, his sagacious thoughts are divinely inspired, and his discerning compositions are naturally perfected. He once annotated the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen) in a single night; on other occasions he has dashed off a thousand words, completing them in a moment. Writings engraved at the imperial mausoleums, promulgated as instructions and announcements, or expressed in songs of praise have often issued from his imperial brush. Indeed, he has already illuminated the Cinnabar Writings and reduced the achievements of Cang Jie and Shi Zhou to chaff [?]. Yet the transmission of the learning of the mind by our Emperor, which reaches back to Fu Xi and equals the glorious achievement of the sagely imperial ancestor, assuredly does not reside merely in brushstrokes and ink. You assembled scholars have long been steeped in the civilizing influence of a shared written culture. Please respectfully set forth your views.
Question: Benevolence and wisdom are virtues of human nature, uniting the inner and the outer. Yet those who explain them do not…

而朱子釋之曰仁陽智陰則又以仁爲
動而智爲靜何也子思子曰成己仁也
成物智也固矣及子貢稱夫子之聖則
以學言智以教言仁而朱子釋之曰智
所以自明仁所以彶物則又以成己爲
智成物爲仁何也程子云仁包四德是
智在仁之中也朱子謂四德之智如四
===
時之冬萬物成始而成終則仁又在智
之中矣抑又何耶孔子以智屬乎天仁
屬乎地而後人有智圓仁方之說孔子
以智仁勇爲三達德而後人有仁明武
之言果能皆得其旨否乎玆欲卽用明
體而析之有以極其精會偏求全而合
之有以體其大果何如而後爲至當協
一之論也學者因聖賢之立言而求端
用力指歸果安在哉訂證千古詔示方
punctuated: 同，何歟？孔子曰：「智者動，仁者靜。」固矣。至傳易論陰陽之道，别言仁智所見之異，而朱子釋之曰：「仁陽智陰。」則又以仁爲動而智爲靜，何也？子思子曰：「成己，仁也；成物，智也。」固矣。及子貢稱夫子之聖，則以學言智，以教言仁，而朱子釋之曰：「智所以自明，仁所以彶物。」則又以成己爲智，成物爲仁，何也？程子云：「仁包四德。」是智在仁之中也。朱子謂四德之智如四時之冬，萬物成始而成終，則仁又在智之中矣，抑又何耶？孔子以智屬乎天，仁屬乎地，而後人有智圓仁方之說；孔子以智仁勇爲三達德，而後人有仁明武之言，果能皆得其旨否乎？玆欲卽用明體而析之，有以極其精；會偏求全而合之，有以體其大。果何如而後爲至當協一之論也？學者因聖賢之立言而求端用力，指歸果安在哉？訂證千古，詔示方
translation_en:
…differ—why is this? Confucius said, “The wise are active; the benevolent are still.” This is well established. Yet when, in his commentary on the Book of Changes, he discusses the Way of yin and yang, he speaks separately of the different perceptions of the benevolent and the wise. Zhu Xi explains this by saying, “Benevolence is yang; wisdom is yin.” This, however, makes benevolence active and wisdom still. Why is this? Master Zisi said, “Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom.” This too is well established. Yet when Zigong praises the sagehood of Confucius, he speaks of wisdom in terms of learning and benevolence in terms of teaching. Zhu Xi explains this by saying, “Wisdom is that by which one enlightens oneself; benevolence is that by which one reaches out to things [?].” This, however, makes perfecting oneself wisdom and perfecting things benevolence. Why is this?

Master Cheng says, “Benevolence encompasses the four virtues.” Thus wisdom is contained within benevolence. Zhu Xi says that wisdom among the four virtues resembles winter among the four seasons, in which the myriad things achieve their beginning and their completion. Thus benevolence, in turn, is contained within wisdom. How, then, is this to be explained? Confucius associates wisdom with Heaven and benevolence with Earth, and later thinkers speak of wisdom as round and benevolence as square. Confucius takes wisdom, benevolence, and courage as the three universally applicable virtues, and later thinkers speak of benevolence, discernment, and martial prowess. Have all these formulations truly grasped his meaning?

We now wish to elucidate substance through function, distinguishing these concepts so as to attain their utmost subtlety; and to bring together partial insights in pursuit of completeness, uniting them so as to comprehend their full scope. What, then, would constitute an entirely fitting and coherent account? As students seek a starting point for their efforts through the pronouncements of the sages and worthies, where, indeed, should those efforts lead? Critically examine and verify the teachings of the ages, and provide instruction for those yet to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
來不徒泛然口耳而已試以心得者陳
之
問昔人言天下政平訟理惟良二千石又
曰宰天下不如爲縣令之樂以其親民
也故守令賢否係生民休戚而天下之
治因之漢之循吏史冊所載盛矣或文
學化俗或教化安全或勸民農桑樹畜
或疏鑿灌溉而防禁奢靡似矣然坿之
治蒲宰莒諸賢亦可以並駕歟然有稱
===
治行第一而政績罔聞且弁其名而失
之又或僞增戶數而蒙旌賞豈當時所
謂循吏者亦未可盡信歟我
國朝遴選守令屢厪
詔旨特加優重百八十年來民安物阜厥有由
然其人亦可以殫述歟其最著者如况
之治蘇劉之治雄王之治維揚林之治
潤顧之治莊浪許之治樂陵皆守令之
卓異者也其遺風善政孰可以爲法歟
punctuated:
來，不徒泛然口耳而已，試以心得者陳之。

問：昔人言，天下政平訟理，惟良二千石。又曰，宰天下不如爲縣令之樂，以其親民也。故守令賢否，係生民休戚，而天下之治因之。漢之循吏，史冊所載盛矣：或文學化俗，或教化安全，或勸民農桑樹畜，或疏鑿灌溉而防禁奢靡，似矣。然坿之治蒲、宰莒諸賢，亦可以並駕歟？然有稱治行第一而政績罔聞，且弁其名而失之；又或僞增戶數而蒙旌賞，豈當時所謂循吏者亦未可盡信歟？我國朝遴選守令，屢厪詔旨，特加優重。百八十年來，民安物阜，厥有由然，其人亦可以殫述歟？其最著者，如况之治蘇、劉之治雄、王之治維揚、林之治潤、顧之治莊浪、許之治樂陵，皆守令之卓異者也。其遺風善政，孰可以爲法歟？
translation_en:
…future generations, rather than merely engaging in vague learning passed from ear to mouth. Set forth what you have personally grasped.

Question: A man of old said, “For equitable government and the proper settlement of lawsuits throughout the realm, we depend upon good officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank.” Another said, “Governing the realm does not equal the pleasure of serving as a district magistrate,” because the latter is close to the people. Thus, whether prefects and district magistrates are worthy determines the people's well-being or suffering, and the good government of the realm depends upon it. The exemplary officials of the Han are abundantly recorded in the histories. Some transformed customs through literary learning; some brought peace and security through moral instruction; some encouraged farming, sericulture, planting, and livestock raising; and some dredged waterways and dug irrigation channels while curbing extravagance. These appear to fit the ideal. Yet if placed alongside the worthy men who governed Pu and administered Ju, could they indeed stand as their equals? There were, however, men acclaimed as foremost in administrative performance whose achievements in government went unrecorded, and whose names were placed first, mistakenly [?]. Others fraudulently inflated household counts and received commendations and rewards. Could it be that even the reputations of those then called exemplary officials cannot all be trusted?

Our dynasty's selection of prefects and district magistrates has repeatedly occupied the attention of imperial edicts, which accord them particular favor and esteem. For a hundred and eighty years, the people have enjoyed peace and material abundance, and there have been reasons for this. Can all the men responsible be fully enumerated? Among the most celebrated are Kuang, who governed Su; Liu, who governed Xiong; Wang, who governed Weiyang; Lin, who governed Run; Gu, who governed Zhuanglang; and Xu, who governed Leling. All were outstanding prefects or district magistrates. Which of the traditions they left behind and their beneficial administrative practices can serve as models?

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫吏治得失古今炳然司民牧者追跡
循良固有不必遠慕而得者然願治君
子往往有遺慨焉豈所持未得其要歟
抑致此别有道歟諸士子行將有民物
之寄幸以槩於中者言之以為時政之
一助
問
國家經世利用莫善於飛輓之制則鹽法固
今日之大猷也試以閩中鹽法商之夫建官轉
===
運竝峙淮浙其責維鈞而鹽法之詳略
迥異其究可得聞歟淮浙之產鹽也恒
難而課獨有餘八閩之產鹽也恒易而
課每不足果行鹽之地有未廣食鹽之
戶有未蕃歟抑經畫之無方禁令之未
壹歟均一場司也而徵納有本折之異
同為引鹽也而析引有大小之殊辦鹽
為竈丁之業乃又得以米折價額課為
邊餽之需復分給內地軍餉報中則姦
punctuated:
夫吏治得失，古今炳然。司民牧者追跡循良，固有不必遠慕而得者。然願治君子往往有遺慨焉，豈所持未得其要歟？抑致此别有道歟？諸士子行將有民物之寄，幸以槩於中者言之，以為時政之一助。
問：國家經世利用，莫善於飛輓之制，則鹽法固今日之大猷也。試以閩中鹽法商之。夫建官轉運，竝峙淮浙，其責維鈞，而鹽法之詳略迥異，其究可得聞歟？淮浙之產鹽也恒難，而課獨有餘；八閩之產鹽也恒易，而課每不足。果行鹽之地有未廣、食鹽之戶有未蕃歟？抑經畫之無方、禁令之未壹歟？均一場司也，而徵納有本折之異；同為引鹽也，而析引有大小之殊。辦鹽為竈丁之業，乃又得以米折價；額課為邊餽之需，復分給內地軍餉。報中則姦
translation_en:
The successes and failures of official administration are manifest throughout past and present. Those charged with governing the people can follow the example of upright and benevolent officials without necessarily seeking models in the distant past. Yet gentlemen who aspire to good government often still have cause for regret. Is this because their approach has failed to grasp what is essential? Or is there some other reason for this? You candidates will soon be entrusted with the people and their affairs. Please express what moves you in your hearts, thereby contributing to the government of our time.
Question: For ordering the realm and making resources useful, nothing serves the state better than the system of rapid provisioning and transport; the salt regulations are therefore a major policy of the present day. Let us examine the salt regulations of Fujian. Its salt distribution administration stands alongside those of the Huai and Zhe regions, with equal responsibilities, yet their salt regulations differ greatly in detail and comprehensiveness. May we hear a full explanation? Producing salt in Huai and Zhe is generally difficult, yet their tax receipts alone show a surplus; producing salt in the eight prefectures of Fujian is generally easy, yet their receipts repeatedly fall short. Is it really that the territory in which salt may be marketed is insufficiently extensive, or that the households consuming salt are insufficiently numerous? Or is planning ineffectual and enforcement of prohibitions inconsistent? All are saltworks offices, yet some collect payments in kind and others in commuted form. All handle salt covered by certificates, yet the certificates are subdivided into different sizes. Producing salt is the occupation of the salt-making households, yet they are also permitted to substitute rice at a commuted valuation [?]. The assessed salt revenue is intended to supply the frontier, yet portions are also allotted to military provisions in the interior. In registering bids for salt certificates, the dishonest …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
商土著自操贏縮之權賦役則刁竈滑
胥巧爲影射之計是豈立法之舊歟近
於潯浯沋三場有欲別立抽分以助海
防之用者有欲輕價召中以免轉輸之
艱者議孰爲優於福寧福安地方有欲
添委掣摯以增額外之稅者有欲嚴捕
私販以資軍門之需者說孰爲當其運
鹽也一母二子之名似與額定正餘者
不侔其榷鹽也圍量抽掣之法擬之懸
===
衡秤較者有間東路細鹽之規當矣或
有議其競利南路官鹽之立似矣或有
病其多事將何所折衷歟茲皆鹺政之
大都也今欲使其法盡復
祖宗之舊而又丕拂乎時宜使其課盡歸軍國
之資而又不爲小民之病果何施而後
可請備言之以觀用世之學
punctuated: 商土著自操贏縮之權，賦役則刁竈滑胥巧爲影射之計，是豈立法之舊歟？近於潯、浯、沋三場，有欲別立抽分以助海防之用者，有欲輕價召中以免轉輸之艱者，議孰爲優？於福寧、福安地方，有欲添委掣摯以增額外之稅者，有欲嚴捕私販以資軍門之需者，說孰爲當？其運鹽也，一母二子之名，似與額定正餘者不侔；其榷鹽也，圍量抽掣之法，擬之懸衡秤較者有間。東路細鹽之規當矣，或有議其競利；南路官鹽之立似矣，或有病其多事。將何所折衷歟？茲皆鹺政之大都也。今欲使其法盡復祖宗之舊，而又丕拂乎時宜，使其課盡歸軍國之資，而又不爲小民之病，果何施而後可？請備言之，以觀用世之學。
translation_en:
…merchants and local residents themselves control increases and decreases; in taxation and labor service, crafty salt producers and unscrupulous clerks ingeniously devise schemes of evasion through false registration. Can this be what the original legislation prescribed? Recently, at the three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and You, some have proposed instituting a separate levy in kind to help meet coastal-defense expenses; others have proposed lowering the price to attract merchants to subscribe for salt allotments, thereby avoiding the difficulties of transport. Which proposal is preferable? In Funing and Fu’an, some have proposed appointing additional officers to inspect salt consignments [?], thereby increasing tax receipts beyond the quota; others have proposed rigorously apprehending illicit salt dealers to provide for the military command’s needs. Which view is appropriate?

In transporting salt, the designation “one mother and two children” seems inconsistent with the prescribed quotas for regular and surplus salt. In administering the salt monopoly, the methods of measuring by bulk and making deductions at inspection differ from weighing and checking with suspended balances. The regulations for fine salt on the eastern route seem appropriate, yet some criticize them for competing for profit. Establishing government salt on the southern route seems reasonable, yet some complain that it creates excessive administrative business. How should these alternatives be reconciled?

These are all major matters of salt administration. If we now wish to restore its regulations entirely to the precedents of the imperial ancestors while also avoiding conflict with present circumstances [?], and to ensure that its revenues all go toward military and state expenses without becoming a burden upon the common people, what measures would make this possible? Please explain fully, so that we may assess your learning for practical service to the world.
