title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾與回言終日不違如愚退而省其
私亦足以發回也不愚
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批此章語本照應而作者
多欠體貼是篇辭簡意完迥異衆作錄之不獨以文也
同考試官學正龍批孔顏授受之蘊而以舉
業排比之文發之難矣哉錄此以示作論語義者
===
考試官教諭趙批此亦似足以發者
考試官學正寇批善發聖人之蘊
聖人與大賢之悟教而有得於其獨焉夫學以
心悟而不以言求顏子之自得者深矣聖人驗
於其獨而樂與之有以哉昔吾夫子之意蓋謂
君子之學以致道也而君子之教以言傳也故
吾與回言終日要之無非教也而亦無非以明
乎道也夫言以終日則其言已多而其時亦久
矣吾見回也言斯聽之未甞因言而有疑聽斯
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「吾與回言終日，不違如愚。退而省其私，亦足以發。回也不愚。」
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批：「此章語本照應，而作者多欠體貼。是篇辭簡意完，迥異衆作。錄之不獨以文也。」
同考試官學正龍批：「孔顏授受之蘊，而以舉業排比之文發之，難矣哉！錄此以示作論語義者。」
考試官教諭趙批：「此亦似足以發者。」
考試官學正寇批：「善發聖人之蘊。」
聖人與大賢之悟教，而有得於其獨焉。夫學以心悟，而不以言求，顏子之自得者深矣。聖人驗於其獨，而樂與之，有以哉！昔吾夫子之意，蓋謂君子之學以致道也，而君子之教以言傳也。故吾與回言終日，要之無非教也，而亦無非以明乎道也。夫言以終日，則其言已多，而其時亦久矣。吾見回也，言斯聽之，未甞因言而有疑；聽斯
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “I have spoken with Hui all day, and he has raised no objection, as though he were foolish. Yet when he withdraws and I examine his conduct in private, it too suffices to elucidate what I have taught. Hui is not foolish.”

Huang Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, an Instructor: “The wording of this chapter is inherently interconnected, yet most writers fail to appreciate its meaning closely. This essay is concise in expression and complete in meaning, standing far apart from the other compositions. It is included for more than its literary merits alone.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, a Director of Studies: “How difficult it is to bring out the profound meaning of what Confucius transmitted and Yan Hui received through the parallel prose of examination writing! This is included as an example for those composing expositions on the meaning of the Analects.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, an Instructor: “This too seems sufficient to elucidate the teaching.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, a Director of Studies: “It brings out the sage’s profound meaning well.”

The sage approved the great worthy’s understanding of his teaching, finding evidence of it in his conduct when alone. Learning consists in understanding with the mind, rather than seeking through words: Master Yan’s personal attainment was profound indeed. The sage verified it through his conduct when alone and delighted in approving him—with good reason!

The intention of our Master in former times was, presumably, as follows: the gentleman studies in order to attain the Way, and the gentleman teaches by transmitting it in words. Thus, when I spoke with Hui all day, everything I said was instruction, and everything served to illuminate the Way. Now, speaking throughout the day means that much has been said and considerable time has elapsed. I observed that whenever I spoke, Hui listened, never finding cause for doubt in my words; upon hearing them, he…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
受之未嘗因疑而有問是吾言以終日而其不
違亦終日也斯不亦無所於可無所於否而呐
然如愚者耶使其退也而無以發也則亦何取
於回也及因其宴居之暇而考其體驗之真則
又見其非有師友之臨也而坦然見乎日用其
於吾所言者無一而不體會焉非有啓沃之資
也而沛然措諸躬行其與終日語者無一而不
發明焉是其時之靜也見其涵道之體也其感
而通也見其順應之妙也相悅以解而無所於
===
疑相悟以心而無俟於問玆回之所以爲明也
而可以愚目之乎是知不違如愚者乃其迹之
似而亦足以發者固其學之幾於化也夫子豈
真不知回者哉樂與之意深是故反覆其詞以
表見之爾雖然夫子亦以回之愚而警諸子之
才辯也孔門之能悟者回之下其次莫如子貢
然子貢之多識其失也以達回之得也以愚至
論其傳則又在參之魯焉嗟乎有子貢之達而
不足於愚魯尚未之有得而况無子貢之達者
punctuated: 受之，未嘗因疑而有問。是吾言以終日，而其不違亦終日也。斯不亦無所於可、無所於否，而呐然如愚者耶？使其退也而無以發也，則亦何取於回也？及因其宴居之暇，而考其體驗之真，則又見其非有師友之臨也，而坦然見乎日用，其於吾所言者，無一而不體會焉；非有啓沃之資也，而沛然措諸躬行，其與終日語者，無一而不發明焉。是其時之靜也，見其涵道之體也；其感而通也，見其順應之妙也。相悅以解，而無所於疑；相悟以心，而無俟於問。玆回之所以爲明也，而可以愚目之乎？是知不違如愚者，乃其迹之似，而亦足以發者，固其學之幾於化也。夫子豈真不知回者哉？樂與之意深，是故反覆其詞，以表見之爾。雖然，夫子亦以回之愚，而警諸子之才辯也。孔門之能悟者，回之下，其次莫如子貢。然子貢之多識，其失也以達；回之得也以愚。至論其傳，則又在參之魯焉。嗟乎！有子貢之達，而不足於愚魯，尚未之有得，而况無子貢之達者
translation_en:
…he accepts it, never asking questions prompted by doubt. Thus, while I speak all day, he likewise goes all day without contradicting me. Does he not seem to assent to nothing and reject nothing, remaining silent as though a fool? If, upon withdrawing, he had no ability to develop what he had heard, what would there be to commend in Hui? Yet when I examine the genuineness of his understanding and practice in the leisure of his private life, I see that, even without teachers or friends present, it manifests itself naturally in his daily conduct: of all I have said, there is nothing he has not grasped and made his own. Even without the aid of enlightening instruction, he puts it abundantly into personal practice: of all we have discussed throughout the day, there is nothing he does not elucidate. In his moments of stillness, one sees the substance of his inward cultivation of the Way; when moved by things and responding to them, one sees the subtlety of his fitting responses. Through a shared delight in understanding, he has no doubts; through an understanding shared in the heart, he has no need to ask questions. This is what makes Hui discerning. Can he then be regarded as foolish?
From this we know that his failure to contradict, as though foolish, is merely the appearance of his outward conduct; his being fully able to develop what he has heard shows that his learning has indeed approached complete transformation. Could the Master really have failed to understand Hui? His delight in approving him was profound, and so he turned his words over repeatedly to make this evident. Nevertheless, the Master also used Hui’s apparent foolishness to admonish the other disciples for their cleverness and eloquence. Among those in Confucius’s school capable of understanding, none ranked higher after Hui than Zigong. Yet for all Zigong’s extensive knowledge, his failing lay in his intellectual facility; Hui’s attainment lay in his apparent foolishness. As for the transmission of the Way, it rested instead with Shen and his apparent dullness. Alas! Even someone with Zigong’s intellectual facility, but lacking such foolishness and dullness, has yet to attain it; how much more so someone without Zigong’s intellectual facility…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎求聖人之道者於此可以辨其幾矣
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也明乎郊社之禮禘甞之義
治國其如示諸掌乎
丘行義
同考試官教諭方批講治國示掌處異乎諸
生之作似甞於禮制而有得者
同考試官教諭費批作者多勦說浮詞獨是
篇據理敷衍略不作一時俗語是可與言禮矣
===
考試官教諭趙批文有理致
考試官學正寇批發揮精到
中庸推祀禮之大者而君道無不備焉蓋君道
莫大於事神治人也禮之大者有以該之其盡
制何如哉中庸舉武王周公制禮以明道而終
言之如此蓋曰聖人制禮非徒備王制之隆寔
以寓王道之大誠以王者為上帝所寵綏其事
之不可不重也于是乎郊社之禮制焉語精誠
則致其通也語功德則大其報也參一人於兩
punctuated:
乎？求聖人之道者，於此可以辨其幾矣。

郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。明乎郊社之禮、禘甞之義，治國其如示諸掌乎？

丘行義

同考試官教諭方批：講治國示掌處，異乎諸生之作，似甞於禮制而有得者。

同考試官教諭費批：作者多勦說浮詞，獨是篇據理敷衍，略不作一時俗語，是可與言禮矣。

考試官教諭趙批：文有理致。

考試官學正寇批：發揮精到。

中庸推祀禮之大者，而君道無不備焉。蓋君道莫大於事神治人也，禮之大者有以該之，其盡制何如哉？中庸舉武王周公制禮以明道，而終言之如此。蓋曰：聖人制禮，非徒備王制之隆，寔以寓王道之大。誠以王者為上帝所寵綏，其事之不可不重也。于是乎郊社之禮制焉。語精誠，則致其通也；語功德，則大其報也。參一人於兩
translation_en:
…? Those who seek the Way of the sages can discern its subtle workings here.

“The rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altars of soil are how one serves the Supreme Lord; the rites of the ancestral temple are how one sacrifices to one’s forebears. If one understands the rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altars of soil, and the meaning of the di and chang sacrifices, would governing a state not be like displaying something on one’s palm?”

Qiu Xingyi 丘行義

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “The discussion of governing a state as though displaying something on one’s palm differs from the other candidates’ compositions. The author seems to have savored the ritual institutions and gained an understanding of them.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: “Most writers rely on borrowed explanations and empty phrases. This essay alone develops its argument on the basis of principle, without resorting at all to the fashionable commonplaces of the day. Here is someone with whom one may discuss ritual.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The composition has coherence and depth of principle.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: “The exposition is precise and thorough.”

The Doctrine of the Mean expounds the greatest sacrificial rites, in which the Way of the ruler is fully embodied. For nothing in the ruler’s Way is greater than serving the spirits and governing the people. The greatest rites encompass these functions: how complete their institutions are! [?] The Doctrine of the Mean cites King Wu and the Duke of Zhou’s establishment of rites to illuminate the Way, and concludes with these words. Its meaning is this: when the sages established rites, they did not merely furnish the grandeur of royal institutions; they embodied within them the greatness of the kingly Way. Indeed, because the king receives the Supreme Lord’s favor and protection, he must attach the utmost importance to serving him. Thus the rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altars of soil were established. In terms of pure sincerity, they bring communion to its fullest extent; in terms of meritorious beneficence, they magnify the recompense offered for it. They place the One Man—the sovereign—as a third alongside the two …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
間夫固有以憑藉而奉承之矣率仁以饗帝禮
之制不其大乎王者為祖宗所付託其祀之不
可不隆也于是乎宗廟之禮行焉以尊崇則人
情之極也以薦享則天道之經也由一世以萬
世夫固可以率循而對越之矣致孝以饗親禮
之義不其精乎夫斯禮也斯義也制之而仁孝
全擴之而治化備焉者也誠使有聖者作於郊
社而測其微焉於禘甞而研其蘊焉則其於治
國也何有乎蓋神人雖異用而感通之者惟一
===
心禮政雖殊途而推行之者惟一理由其仁以
仁天下而化吾見其易孚也由其孝以教天下
而恩吾見其易洽也𠦑天地吾奠位于上下
祖宗吾昭假於宗祊者也謂之曰其如示諸掌
信乎王制之明而王道特易易矣是則禮制極
乎天親而經制達乎天下此武王周公所以為
盡道而其達孝亦足徵焉矣抑有虞氏禘黃帝
而郊嚳則郊禘之禮自夏殷以上皆行之而尊
尊親親仁至義盡則至武周而後大備也是故
punctuated: 間，夫固有以憑藉而奉承之矣。率仁以饗帝，禮之制不其大乎？王者為祖宗所付託，其祀之不可不隆也。于是乎宗廟之禮行焉：以尊崇，則人情之極也；以薦享，則天道之經也。由一世以萬世，夫固可以率循而對越之矣。致孝以饗親，禮之義不其精乎？夫斯禮也，斯義也，制之而仁孝全，擴之而治化備焉者也。誠使有聖者作，於郊社而測其微焉，於禘甞而研其蘊焉，則其於治國也何有乎？蓋神人雖異用，而感通之者惟一心；禮政雖殊途，而推行之者惟一理。由其仁以仁天下，而化吾見其易孚也；由其孝以教天下，而恩吾見其易洽也。𠦑天地，吾奠位于上下；祖宗，吾昭假於宗祊者也。謂之曰「其如示諸掌」，信乎王制之明而王道特易易矣！是則禮制極乎天親，而經制達乎天下。此武王周公所以為盡道，而其達孝亦足徵焉矣。抑有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，則郊禘之禮自夏殷以上皆行之，而尊尊親親、仁至義盡，則至武周而後大備也。是故
translation_en: …between Heaven and Earth, the ruler surely has that upon which to rely in reverently serving them. Following benevolence in presenting offerings to the Lord on High—is not the institution of these rites grand? The ruler is entrusted with his charge by his ancestors, and sacrifices to them must therefore be exalted. Thus the rites of the ancestral temple are performed: in their reverence and exaltation, they bring human feeling to its utmost expression; in their presentation of offerings, they embody the constant order of Heaven’s Way. From one generation through ten thousand generations, there is assuredly a pattern to follow in reverently responding to the ancestors. Fulfilling filial devotion by offering to one’s forebears—is not the meaning of these rites profound? These rites and their meaning, when established, make benevolence and filial devotion complete; when extended, they bring government and moral transformation to fulfillment. If a sage should indeed arise, fathom the subtleties of the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and the sacrifices to the soil, and investigate the depths of the di ancestral sacrifice and the autumn offering, what difficulty would he have in governing a state? Although spirits and human beings differ in their workings, what moves and communicates with them is a single heart; although ritual and government follow different paths, what carries them into practice is a single principle. Extending his benevolence to treat all under Heaven benevolently, he would, I believe, readily win their trust through moral transformation; extending his filial devotion to instruct all under Heaven, he would, I believe, readily spread his beneficence everywhere. As for Heaven and Earth [?], I establish their positions above and below; as for the ancestors, I reverently approach them in the ancestral temple. To say of this, “It is as though displaying it upon one’s palm”—truly, once royal institutions are understood, the kingly Way is exceedingly easy to practice! Thus ritual institutions reach their culmination in service to Heaven and one’s forebears, while the ordering institutions extend throughout all under Heaven. This is why King Wu and the Duke of Zhou fulfilled the Way completely, and it also sufficiently attests to their universally exemplary filial devotion. Yet the ruler of Youyu offered the di sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor and the suburban sacrifice to Ku. Thus the suburban and di sacrifices were already practiced in the Xia and Yin dynasties and earlier; but honoring the honored and cherishing one’s kin, with benevolence at its utmost and righteousness fully realized, attained their full completeness only with King Wu and the Duke of Zhou. For this reason…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
孔子亟稱之而又推極其道正以見繼述之孝
有在耳先儒曰舜爲人道之極萬世仰之不可
加周爲王制之備萬世由之不能易噫其亦深
知聖人者乎
未有義而後其君者也
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批義必急君是就性分上
說出不可已處此作盡之矣
同考試官教諭黎批詞嚴義正孟子義之絶
===
佳者宜錄以式
考試官教諭趙批發揮忠與義無二道文
字見筆力佳士也
考試官學正寇批親切有味
大賢决言懷義者必能忠乎其君也夫義以行
忠則忠根諸性矣曾謂懷義而有不忠其君者
哉於此見義之爲利而君人者當審所尚也孟
子開導惠王之意如此蓋曰志莫同於上下之
交治莫先於義利之辨吾謂王亦有仁義者豈
punctuated:
孔子亟稱之，而又推極其道，正以見繼述之孝有在耳。先儒曰：「舜爲人道之極，萬世仰之不可加；周爲王制之備，萬世由之不能易。」噫！其亦深知聖人者乎！
未有義而後其君者也。
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批：「義必急君，是就性分上說出不可已處，此作盡之矣。」
同考試官教諭黎批：「詞嚴義正，孟子義之絶佳者，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭趙批：「發揮忠與義無二道，文字見筆力，佳士也。」
考試官學正寇批：「親切有味。」
大賢决言懷義者必能忠乎其君也。夫義以行忠，則忠根諸性矣。曾謂懷義而有不忠其君者哉？於此見義之爲利，而君人者當審所尚也。孟子開導惠王之意如此，蓋曰：「志莫同於上下之交，治莫先於義利之辨。吾謂王亦有仁義者，豈
translation_en:
…Confucius repeatedly praised them and further traced their Way to its fullest extent, precisely to show wherein lay their filial devotion in carrying on their predecessors’ purposes and undertakings. An earlier Confucian scholar said: “Shun represents the pinnacle of the human Way: ten thousand generations look up to him and can add nothing. The Zhou represents the completeness of royal institutions: ten thousand generations follow them and cannot alter them.” Ah! Surely he understood the sages profoundly!
“Never has there been a righteous man who put his ruler last.”
Zheng Yuanshao
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Righteousness necessarily makes service to the ruler urgent. This explains, in terms of one’s innate moral nature, what one cannot cease doing. This composition expresses it fully.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The language is rigorous and the meaning correct. This is an outstanding essay on the meaning of the Mengzi and should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It develops the point that loyalty and righteousness are not two separate Ways. The writing displays literary force. A fine scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: “Directly pertinent and rich in meaning.”
The great worthy declares decisively that one who cherishes righteousness will assuredly be loyal to his ruler. When righteousness guides the practice of loyalty, loyalty is rooted in one’s nature. Could it possibly be said that someone cherishes righteousness yet is disloyal to his ruler? Here we see that righteousness constitutes benefit, and that a ruler of men must carefully consider what he esteems. Such was Mencius’s intent in enlightening King Hui. In effect, he said: “Nothing better unites purposes than mutual engagement between those above and those below; nothing takes precedence in governing over distinguishing righteousness from profit. When I tell Your Majesty that there are benevolence and righteousness, could it be that …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
誠無利於上而言乎彼仁不遺親仁之利也而
於義亦有焉蓋義也者本諸心則爲敬敬君敬
之大者也裁之事則爲宜事君事之急者也人
惟大義之不明是故不知大者之爲急容有之
矣苟使忠愛之誠根於天性而以之效職也必
知尊主之爲恭篤棐之念切於由衷而以之從
上也必知體國之爲急責之所在身先殉之爲
任不同而同於精白以承德者固其情之不能
自已者也事之所在身先任之爲分不同而同
===
於夙夜以在公者固其職之不容自懈者也蓋
未有君臣之義無所逃於天地者旣洞然决擇
於我矣而於公私之際所當辨其上下者乃漠
然不加之意焉忘國家之急以自便其私圖計
利害之私而罔先乎國是是後君矣是不知制
命之義矣則不忠莫大乎是而謂義者有之乎
是知義以爲忠未有忠而不激於義者忠由乎
義未有義而不永其忠者此性之所不已而亦
事之所以相成也人患不明乎義耳而患不忠
punctuated: 誠無利於上而言乎？彼仁不遺親，仁之利也，而於義亦有焉。蓋義也者，本諸心則爲敬，敬君，敬之大者也；裁之事則爲宜，事君，事之急者也。人惟大義之不明，是故不知大者之爲急，容有之矣。苟使忠愛之誠根於天性，而以之效職也，必知尊主之爲恭；篤棐之念切於由衷，而以之從上也，必知體國之爲急。責之所在，身先殉之，爲任不同，而同於精白以承德者，固其情之不能自已者也。事之所在，身先任之，爲分不同，而同於夙夜以在公者，固其職之不容自懈者也。蓋未有君臣之義無所逃於天地者，旣洞然决擇於我矣，而於公私之際所當辨其上下者，乃漠然不加之意焉。忘國家之急，以自便其私；圖計利害之私，而罔先乎國是，是後君矣，是不知制命之義矣。則不忠莫大乎是，而謂義者有之乎？是知義以爲忠，未有忠而不激於義者；忠由乎義，未有義而不永其忠者。此性之所不已，而亦事之所以相成也。人患不明乎義耳，而患不忠
translation_en:
…could this truly have been said because it brings no benefit to those above? That the benevolent do not neglect their parents is the benefit of benevolence; righteousness, too, has its benefits. Rooted in the heart, righteousness becomes reverence, and revering the ruler is the greatest expression of reverence. Applied to the judgment of affairs, it becomes proper conduct, and serving the ruler is the most urgent of duties. It is only because people fail to understand this great righteousness that they may fail to recognize that what is greatest is also most urgent.

If sincere loyalty and love are rooted in one's heaven-given nature and brought to the discharge of one's office, one will surely recognize that honoring the sovereign constitutes reverent service. If the resolve to give devoted assistance springs earnestly from the heart and guides one's service to superiors, one will surely recognize the urgency of taking the state's concerns as one's own. Wherever responsibility lies, one takes the lead in devoting oneself to it. Though assignments differ, all alike serve the ruler's virtue with purity of purpose: their feelings themselves will not allow them to stop. Wherever business requires attention, one takes the lead in undertaking it. Though allotted duties differ, all alike attend to public service from morning to night: their offices themselves permit no slackening.

Surely no one, having clearly discerned and chosen for himself the righteousness binding ruler and minister—a bond from which there is no escape anywhere between Heaven and Earth—could then remain indifferent to the distinction between public and private interests, giving no thought to which should take precedence. To forget the state's urgent needs for one's own private convenience, and to calculate personal advantages and disadvantages without putting the proper course of state affairs first, is to put the ruler last. It is to fail to understand the righteousness governing obedience to commands. No disloyalty could be greater: could one say that a righteous person would act thus?

Thus we know that righteousness gives rise to loyalty: no loyalty is uninspired by righteousness. Loyalty proceeds from righteousness: no righteousness fails to make one's loyalty enduring. This is the ceaseless working of human nature, and also the means by which the two fulfill each other in practice. People need worry only that they do not understand righteousness; need they worry about failing to be loyal…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉噫於此可以見義之爲利矣於此可以見君
當躬行乎義以爲之倡矣抑義利之辨王伯之
分也孟子之在戰國急於明道術以正人心者
而於仁義亦以利言何耶蓋時方功利入人不
有以正之則其機溺而不返不因而誘之則其
志沮而未信利在君親救時之微意也要之行
之以誠抑孰非王道哉故曰仁義固所以利之
又曰王道本於誠意噫合而觀之則得矣
易
===
夫大人者與天地合其德
鄭元韶
同考試官敎諭蔣 批 發揮天地合德之旨殆
無餘蘊蓋深於易者
同考試官敎諭黎 批 雄深雅健讀其文不覺
蹶然起敬
考試官敎諭趙 批 說合德處最盡
考試官學正寇 批 爾雅可愛
文言賛聖德之至協諸天地者也夫天地至大
punctuated:
哉！噫！於此可以見義之爲利矣，於此可以見君當躬行乎義以爲之倡矣。抑義利之辨，王伯之分也。孟子之在戰國，急於明道術以正人心者，而於仁義亦以利言，何耶？蓋時方功利入人，不有以正之，則其機溺而不返；不因而誘之，則其志沮而未信。利在君親，救時之微意也。要之，行之以誠，抑孰非王道哉？故曰：「仁義固所以利之。」又曰：「王道本於誠意。」噫！合而觀之，則得矣。

易

夫大人者，與天地合其德。

鄭元韶

同考試官敎諭蔣批：發揮天地合德之旨，殆無餘蘊，蓋深於易者。

同考試官敎諭黎批：雄深雅健，讀其文，不覺蹶然起敬。

考試官敎諭趙批：說合德處最盡。

考試官學正寇批：爾雅可愛。

文言賛聖德之至，協諸天地者也。夫天地至大
translation_en:
…indeed! Ah! Here we can see how righteousness brings benefit; here we can see that the ruler must personally practice righteousness to set an example. Yet the distinction between righteousness and profit is what separates true kingship from hegemony. During the Warring States period, Mencius urgently sought to clarify the Way and its methods so as to rectify people’s hearts. Why, then, did he also speak of benevolence and righteousness in terms of benefit? At that time, the pursuit of achievement and profit was entering people’s hearts. Without something to correct them, their impulses would sink into it beyond recovery; without drawing on those concerns to guide them, their resolve would falter and they would remain unconvinced. Locating benefit in service to ruler and parents was his subtle intention in rescuing his age. Ultimately, when practiced with sincerity, how could any of this fail to be the Kingly Way? Thus it is said, “Benevolence and righteousness are indeed the means of benefiting them.” It is also said, “The Kingly Way is rooted in sincerity of intention.” Ah! Consider these together, and the meaning becomes clear.

Book of Changes

“As for the great man, his virtue accords with that of Heaven and Earth.”

Zheng Yuanshao

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “He elucidates the meaning of virtue according with Heaven and Earth, leaving scarcely anything unexplored. He clearly has a profound understanding of the Changes.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Powerful, profound, elegant, and vigorous. Reading his composition, one involuntarily rises in sudden respect.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “His explanation of the accordance of virtue is exceptionally thorough.”

Examiner Kou, Director of Studies, comments: “Refined and pleasing.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text praises the perfection of the sage’s virtue, which accords with Heaven and Earth. Now Heaven and Earth are supremely vast…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也而聖德同之德斯至矣其爲物所利見也宜
哉文言申乾九五爻義如此今夫道必體而後
可與語天德之純德必至而後可以建天下之
極然則其惟九五之大人乎剛健中正其心純
矣而太極之全體不虧基命宥密其敬至矣而
天命之本眞不鑿存神以立本則廓然而大公
者无非天地之心也知化以達用則物來而順
應者无非天地之事也是天地生人之理其在
大人也旣兼體而不遺則大人造德之純其於
===
天地也自配合而无間大生廣生德固至矣而
无私者其本也大人无私則帝德之廣運有以
協上下以同流誠通誠復德云大矣而无私者
其運也大人无私則至德之淵微有以參兩儀
而竝運以其在天地者而視之乎聖人焉則命
之所以不已者卽誠之所以不息也蓋不可以
形器觀矣以其在聖人者而配之乎天地焉則
情順萬事而无情者卽心普萬物而无心者也
又可以彼此論耶是何也道之一也衆人狃於
punctuated: 也，而聖德同之，德斯至矣。其爲物所利見也，宜哉！文言申乾九五爻義如此。今夫道必體而後可與語天德之純，德必至而後可以建天下之極。然則其惟九五之大人乎？剛健中正，其心純矣，而太極之全體不虧；基命宥密，其敬至矣，而天命之本眞不鑿。存神以立本，則廓然而大公者，无非天地之心也；知化以達用，則物來而順應者，无非天地之事也。是天地生人之理，其在大人也，旣兼體而不遺，則大人造德之純，其於天地也，自配合而无間。大生廣生，德固至矣，而无私者其本也。大人无私，則帝德之廣運，有以協上下以同流。誠通誠復，德云大矣，而无私者其運也。大人无私，則至德之淵微，有以參兩儀而竝運。以其在天地者而視之乎聖人焉，則命之所以不已者，卽誠之所以不息也，蓋不可以形器觀矣。以其在聖人者而配之乎天地焉，則情順萬事而无情者，卽心普萬物而无心者也，又可以彼此論耶？是何也？道之一也。衆人狃於
translation_en:
…yet the sage’s virtue equals them: his virtue is thus consummate. It is fitting indeed that all beings should benefit from seeing him! Such is the way the Commentary on the Words elucidates the meaning of the fifth, yang line of Qian. Now, only after one embodies the Way can one speak of the purity of Heaven’s virtue; only after one’s virtue reaches perfection can one establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. Must this not, then, be the great man of the fifth, yang line? Firm and vigorous, centered and correct, his mind is pure, and the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate remains unimpaired. Establishing Heaven’s mandate in profound stillness, his reverence is consummate, and the original authenticity of Heaven’s mandate remains unspoiled by contrivance. By preserving the spirit to establish the foundation, his openness and complete impartiality are none other than the mind of Heaven and Earth. By understanding transformation to give full scope to practical functioning, his fitting responses to things as they come are none other than the workings of Heaven and Earth. Since the principle by which Heaven and Earth generate human beings is embodied fully and without omission in the great man, the purity of the virtue he attains naturally accords with Heaven and Earth without any separation.

In their great and expansive generation of life, their virtue is indeed consummate, and selflessness is its foundation. Through the great man’s selflessness, the broad reach of his imperial virtue enables him to harmonize with what is above and below and flow together with them. In sincerity’s unfolding and return, their virtue may be called great, and selflessness characterizes its operation. Through the great man’s selflessness, the depth and subtlety of his consummate virtue enable him to form a triad with the Two Powers, Heaven and Earth, and operate alongside them. If we consider in the sage what is present in Heaven and Earth, that by which the mandate never ceases is precisely that by which sincerity never rests. This surely cannot be viewed in terms of physical forms and vessels. If we match what is present in the sage with Heaven and Earth, his feelings, which respond fittingly to every affair yet are free of personal feeling, are precisely their mind, which encompasses all things yet has no deliberate intention. Can these, then, be discussed as separate from one another? Why is this so? Because the Way is one. Ordinary people are habituated to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
有我而不能相通是以見其異聖人體之至公
而无所間隔是以見其同要之豈誠出於斯道
之外而強合也哉是則德之純也旣參天地而
不違則聖之作也宜乎其繼天地以立極矣物
所利見夫豈无自也哉雖然聖人豈惟合德天
地而已其彌綸參賛之妙實則範圍之以成其
能是天地之位萬物之育皆不能无待於聖人
者然則聖人之功之德其可易易言耶是故觀
合德而可以得聖德之純觀位育而可以得聖
===
功之極
百官以治萬民以察
楊珂
同考試官教諭蔣 批 說出聖人書契之利且
文意詳整易義之優者未能先於子矣
同考試官教諭黎 批 其㫖遠其辭文非有得
於同文之妙者不能到此
考試官教諭趙 批 精潔渾成
考試官學正寇 批 治察是如此說
punctuated:
有我而不能相通，是以見其異；聖人體之至公，而无所間隔，是以見其同。要之，豈誠出於斯道之外而強合也哉？是則德之純也。旣參天地而不違，則聖之作也，宜乎其繼天地以立極矣。物所利見，夫豈无自也哉？雖然，聖人豈惟合德天地而已？其彌綸參賛之妙，實則範圍之以成其能。是天地之位、萬物之育，皆不能无待於聖人者。然則聖人之功之德，其可易易言耶？是故觀合德而可以得聖德之純，觀位育而可以得聖功之極。

百官以治，萬民以察。

楊珂

同考試官教諭蔣批：「說出聖人書契之利，且文意詳整，易義之優者未能先於子矣。」

同考試官教諭黎批：「其㫖遠，其辭文，非有得於同文之妙者不能到此。」

考試官教諭趙批：「精潔渾成。」

考試官學正寇批：「治察是如此說。」
translation_en:
…having a self and being unable to communicate with one another, and thus they perceive differences. The sage embodies the utmost impartiality, with no intervening barriers, and thus perceives unity. Ultimately, could sincerity lie outside this Way and be forcibly joined to it? This, then, is purity of virtue. Since the sage stands alongside Heaven and Earth without contravening them, it is fitting that, in his actions, he should carry on their work and establish the supreme standard. That all beings benefit from beholding him surely has its grounds! Yet does the sage merely unite his virtue with that of Heaven and Earth? The subtlety of his all-encompassing activity and his participation in and assistance to their transforming work lies in giving these order and bounds, thereby bringing their capacities to fulfillment. Thus, Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and the myriad beings attaining their full growth alike depend upon the sage. Can the sage’s achievements and virtue, then, be spoken of lightly? Accordingly, by contemplating his union in virtue with Heaven and Earth, one may apprehend the purity of his sagely virtue; by contemplating their proper placement and the nurturing of beings, one may apprehend the ultimate reach of his sagely achievements.

“The hundred officials thereby maintained order, and the myriad people thereby gained clarity.”

Yang Ke

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “You bring out the benefits of the sage’s introduction of writing and written tallies. Moreover, the ideas in your essay are fully developed and well ordered. Even the finest writers of essays on the Book of Changes could not surpass you.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Its purport is far-reaching, its language refined. No one who had not grasped the subtle workings of a shared written culture could attain this level.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Refined and clean, forming a seamless whole.”

Examiner Kou, Director of Studies, comments: “This is how ‘maintaining order’ and ‘gaining clarity’ should be explained.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖人同文之化而有以徵諸臣民焉夫臣職脩
而民志定是固合同而化矣自非聖人通變而
考之以文其孰能與於此今夫聖人不先天以
開人每因時而立政其以書契易結繩者豈不
欲與天下相安於无事而爲是更變哉時之所
會有不能違耳是故布列庶位而佐王以出治
者有百官焉罔不欲其各脩其職也但風教日
移相沿而飾治者亦多矣復可以上古之簡例
之乎惟書契有作則紀法定而旌别之義昭功
===
罪明而勸懲之典著庶寮之肅遵王度也有位
之儆守官箴也君執要以馭臣而臣明徵以脩
職朝無倖位揖讓之風行矣百官有弗治乎百
官治是上焉者誠於書契焉有賴矣至於生聚
萬方而遵王以會極者有萬民焉罔不欲其各
得其情也但風會日流相率而爲僞者亦衆矣
復可以上古之淳待之乎惟書契有作則綜覈
詳於約劑之明簡稽得於品式之具以登民數
則多寡有程也以察民故則是非有辨也君脩
punctuated: 聖人同文之化，而有以徵諸臣民焉。夫臣職脩而民志定，是固合同而化矣。自非聖人通變而考之以文，其孰能與於此？今夫聖人不先天以開人，每因時而立政。其以書契易結繩者，豈不欲與天下相安於无事而爲是更變哉？時之所會，有不能違耳。是故布列庶位而佐王以出治者，有百官焉，罔不欲其各脩其職也。但風教日移，相沿而飾治者亦多矣，復可以上古之簡例之乎？惟書契有作，則紀法定而旌别之義昭，功罪明而勸懲之典著。庶寮之肅遵王度也，有位之儆守官箴也，君執要以馭臣，而臣明徵以脩職，朝無倖位，揖讓之風行矣。百官有弗治乎？百官治，是上焉者誠於書契焉有賴矣。至於生聚萬方而遵王以會極者，有萬民焉，罔不欲其各得其情也。但風會日流，相率而爲僞者亦衆矣，復可以上古之淳待之乎？惟書契有作，則綜覈詳於約劑之明，簡稽得於品式之具。以登民數，則多寡有程也；以察民故，則是非有辨也。君脩
translation_en:
The sage’s transforming influence through a shared written culture finds verification among his ministers and people. When ministers discharge their duties and the people’s aspirations are settled, unity and transformation have indeed been achieved. Without the sage adapting to change and examining affairs through written records, who could have brought this about? The sage does not anticipate Heaven in enlightening the people, but always establishes government in accordance with the times. In replacing knotted cords with written documents, was he not making this change because he wished to enjoy undisturbed peace together with all under Heaven? Yet the circumstances of the times imposed demands that could not be resisted.

Thus, there are the hundred officials, arrayed in their various positions to assist the king in governing; he wishes every one of them to discharge his duties. But as customs and moral instruction change daily, many follow established practices while presenting only an appearance of good government. Could they still be judged by the simplicity of high antiquity? Once written documents were instituted, regulations and laws became fixed, and the principles for recognizing and distinguishing officials became clear; merits and offenses became evident, and the rules for encouragement and punishment became manifest. The various officials reverently observe royal standards, and those holding office vigilantly heed official admonitions. The ruler grasps the essentials in directing his ministers, while the ministers make the evidence clear in discharging their duties. No one holds a position at court through undeserved good fortune, and a spirit of courtesy and deference prevails. Could any of the hundred officials fail to be properly governed? That the hundred officials are properly governed shows that those above indeed depend upon written documents.

As for those who live and multiply throughout the myriad regions, following the king and converging upon the supreme standard, these are the myriad people; he wishes the true circumstances of each to be ascertained. But as prevailing customs shift daily, many lead one another into deceit. Could they still be treated as possessing the sincerity of high antiquity? Once written documents were instituted, comprehensive scrutiny became detailed through the clarity of contracts, and inspection and verification became effective through the provision of classifications and prescribed forms. When these are used to register the population, its greater or smaller numbers have a definite measure; when used to investigate the people’s affairs, right and wrong can be distinguished. The ruler cultivates…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
文以立極而民遵道以作乂比屋可封於變之
化成矣萬民有弗察乎萬民察是下焉者亦於
書契焉有賴矣是則書契一易而百官萬民罔
不賴之以順治聖人通變考文之功何其大哉
抑邃古之風遠矣後世疑心志而信耳目疑耳
目而信簡書法愈煩民愈詐而書契適足以滋
僞而聖人之心至是亦戚矣然則若之何而可
曰捄詐存乎朴御物存乎誠然則通變宜民之
術又當得諸書契之外而後可
===
書
凡厥庶民有猷有爲有守汝則念之不協
于極不罹于咎皇則受之而康而色曰
予攸好德汝則錫之福時人斯其惟皇
之極
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批 箕子演極之意模寫殆
盡當是作手
同考試官學正龍批 造詞精切且正大典則
punctuated:
文以立極，而民遵道以作乂，比屋可封，於變之化成矣。萬民有弗察乎？萬民察，是下焉者亦於書契焉有賴矣。是則書契一易，而百官萬民罔不賴之以順治，聖人通變考文之功何其大哉！抑邃古之風遠矣，後世疑心志而信耳目，疑耳目而信簡書，法愈煩，民愈詐，而書契適足以滋僞，而聖人之心至是亦戚矣。然則若之何而可？曰：「捄詐存乎朴，御物存乎誠。」然則通變宜民之術，又當得諸書契之外而後可。

書

凡厥庶民，有猷、有爲、有守，汝則念之；不協于極，不罹于咎，皇則受之，而康而色，曰：「予攸好德。」汝則錫之福，時人斯其惟皇之極。

黃士觀

同考試官教諭馮批：「箕子演極之意，模寫殆盡，當是作手。」

同考試官學正龍批：「造詞精切，且正大典則
translation_en:
…cultivation to establish the supreme standard, while the people follow the Way and bring about good order. Every household becomes worthy of enfeoffment, and the transforming influence that makes the people good is accomplished. Could any of the myriad people remain beyond scrutiny? When the myriad people are scrutinized, those below likewise have written records and contracts to rely upon. Thus, once the change to written records and contracts was made, the hundred officials and the myriad people all relied upon them to achieve orderly government. How great was the sages’ achievement in adapting to change and examining written forms!

Yet the ways of remote antiquity are far distant. Later generations distrusted intentions and trusted their ears and eyes; then they distrusted their ears and eyes and trusted written documents. The more cumbersome the laws, the more deceitful the people became, so that written records and contracts served only to multiply falsehood. At this, even the sages would have felt sorrow. What, then, should be done? The answer is: “The remedy for deceit lies in simplicity; the ordering of affairs lies in sincerity.” Thus, the art of adapting to change for the people’s benefit must also be sought beyond written records and contracts.

Book of Documents

“Of all the common people, those who have plans, accomplishments, or steadfast principles—you should keep them in mind. Those who do not accord with the supreme standard but have incurred no blame—the sovereign should accept them. Make your expression gracious and say, ‘What I love is virtue.’ You should then bestow blessings upon them, and these people will follow the sovereign’s supreme standard.”

Huang Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “He has conveyed almost completely Jizi’s meaning in expounding the supreme standard. Surely an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor: “The wording is refined and precise, and moreover upright, dignified, and in accordance with canonical standards …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
可以爲式矣
考試官教諭趙批平實之文
考試官學正寇批整潔可誦
王者務成人以善則天下之善成矣蓋天下之
才不皆善而所賴以成之者君也苟能成之而
不已焉民其有不協於極哉箕子演皇極之疇
以告武王及此若曰王旣建極以端天下之本
矣而納民於極當何如哉誠以天之生才難矣
庶民之中不可以語成德也然亦有精於方物
===
者焉有優於幹理者焉有秉執不撓者焉此則
質之可以語上者也王其存而念之咸造之以
錫類之仁又有弗協於休復之吉亦不淪於迷
復之凶者焉此則行之可導而上下者也王其
矜而受之亦成之以容保之度苟斯人也果能
感慕以圖成進修以無倦觀其色粹乎其安和
也聽其言確乎其好德也此其志專矣然未協
於克一也王豈惟念受而已哉必也福以勸之
或旌其賢也有匪頒之典或馭其幸也有賚予
punctuated:
可以爲式矣。
考試官教諭趙批：平實之文。
考試官學正寇批：整潔可誦。
王者務成人以善，則天下之善成矣。蓋天下之才不皆善，而所賴以成之者君也。苟能成之而不已焉，民其有不協於極哉？箕子演皇極之疇以告武王，及此，若曰：王旣建極以端天下之本矣，而納民於極當何如哉？誠以天之生才難矣，庶民之中，不可以語成德也。然亦有精於方物者焉，有優於幹理者焉，有秉執不撓者焉，此則質之可以語上者也。王其存而念之，咸造之以錫類之仁。又有弗協於休復之吉，亦不淪於迷復之凶者焉，此則行之可導而上下者也。王其矜而受之，亦成之以容保之度。苟斯人也，果能感慕以圖成，進修以無倦，觀其色，粹乎其安和也；聽其言，確乎其好德也。此其志專矣，然未協於克一也。王豈惟念受而已哉？必也福以勸之。或旌其賢也，有匪頒之典；或馭其幸也，有賚予
translation_en:
…may serve as a model.
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “An unadorned and substantial composition.”
Examiner Kou, School Instructor, comments: “Orderly and polished, worthy of recitation.”
When a king strives to bring people to fulfillment through goodness, the goodness of all under Heaven reaches fulfillment. For the talents of those under Heaven are not all good; it is upon their ruler that they depend to bring them to fulfillment. If he can accomplish this without ceasing, could any of the people fail to accord with the supreme standard? When Jizi expounded the section on the August Ultimate to King Wu and reached this point, it was as though he said: You, O King, have already established the supreme standard, thereby setting right the foundation of all under Heaven. But how should you bring the people into accord with that standard?
Indeed, Heaven does not readily produce talent. Among the common people, one cannot speak of fully realized virtue. Yet there are those skilled in discerning things, those proficient in managing affairs, and those who hold steadfastly to their principles without yielding. Such people possess native qualities that make them capable of higher attainment. You should keep them in mind and attend to them, bringing them all to fulfillment through benevolence that extends blessings to others of their kind. There are also those who do not attain the auspiciousness of a gracious return to goodness, yet do not sink into the misfortune of a deluded return. These are people whose conduct can be guided upward or downward. You should show them compassion and receive them, bringing them too to fulfillment through your capacity to embrace and protect them.
If such people truly can be moved to admiration and strive toward fulfillment, advancing in self-cultivation without weariness, then, when you observe their countenances, their serenity and harmony are pure; when you hear their words, their love of virtue is firm. Their resolve is now single-minded, yet they have not attained steadfast unity. Could you merely keep them in mind and receive them, and stop there? You must bestow blessings to encourage them. Perhaps, to honor their worthiness, there is the prescribed distribution of gifts; or, to guide those whom you favor [?], there are bestowals of…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之施夫然則進善之機旣發於其始而爲善之
力又輕於其終吾見承王之錫者皆曰大君養
人以善也吾何爲不善莫不益勵於王道之歸
焉泳王之化者皆曰王者域民以中吾何爲不
中莫不益安於帝則之順焉夫以王者成人如
是其難用心如是其至此其爲建極而代天也
王可不知所務哉抑箕子旣以錫福告王矣下
文又曰凡厥正人旣富方穀夫待敎而善必賞
而後勸者中才也聖人之意豈不以豪傑待天
===
下歟蓋帝王之道必本於人情養而後善固理
之不可易者臣民之馭庸非所當先哉若夫自
修以協極者則固有本末耳夫知本則義義則
協極矣是故知協極之爲義而後知錫福之爲
仁
以敬事上帝立民長伯
陳道基
同考試官敎諭馮 批 文武用三宅三俊而責
任之重於是作見之
punctuated:
之施。夫然，則進善之機旣發於其始，而爲善之力又輕於其終。吾見承王之錫者皆曰：「大君養人以善也，吾何爲不善？」莫不益勵於王道之歸焉。泳王之化者皆曰：「王者域民以中，吾何爲不中？」莫不益安於帝則之順焉。夫以王者成人，如是其難；用心，如是其至。此其爲建極而代天也，王可不知所務哉？抑箕子旣以錫福告王矣，下文又曰：「凡厥正人，旣富方穀。」夫待敎而善，必賞而後勸者，中才也。聖人之意，豈不以豪傑待天下歟？蓋帝王之道，必本於人情；養而後善，固理之不可易者。臣民之馭，庸非所當先哉？若夫自修以協極者，則固有本末耳。夫知本則義，義則協極矣。是故知協極之爲義，而後知錫福之爲仁。

以敬事上帝，立民長伯。
陳道基

同考試官敎諭馮批：「文武用三宅三俊，而責任之重，於是作見之。」
translation_en:
…the bestowal of gifts. Thus, once the impulse to advance in goodness has been awakened at the outset, the effort required to practise goodness becomes lighter in the end. I see that all who receive the king’s gifts say: “The great ruler nurtures people through goodness. Why should I fail to be good?” None fails to strive still harder to return to the kingly Way. All who bathe in the king’s transforming influence say: “The king guides his people within the bounds of the mean. Why should I fail to accord with the mean?” None fails to find greater ease in following Heaven’s standard. For a king to bring people to fulfilment is so difficult, and his care is so thoroughgoing. This is how he establishes the supreme standard and acts on Heaven’s behalf. Can the king fail to recognize what he must devote himself to?

Moreover, Jizi has already instructed the king about bestowing blessings, yet the passage below also says: “As for all those upright men, once enriched, they will become good.” Those who await instruction before becoming good, and must be rewarded before being encouraged, are people of middling ability. Could the sage’s intention be anything other than to treat the people of the realm as persons of outstanding ability? Yet the Way of emperors and kings must be rooted in human feelings. That people become good after being nurtured is indeed an unalterable principle. In governing subjects and common people, should this not take precedence? As for those who cultivate themselves to accord with the supreme standard, there is certainly a distinction between root and branch. Knowing the root leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to accord with the supreme standard. Thus, only after understanding that according with the supreme standard constitutes righteousness can one understand that bestowing blessings constitutes benevolence.

“To serve the Lord on High reverently, and to establish leaders and chiefs for the people.”
Chen Daoji

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “Kings Wen and Wu employed the occupants of the three offices and the three groups of outstanding men; the weight of the responsibilities entrusted to them is here made manifest [?].”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正龍批叙敬事立民有許多雋
永意思
考試官教諭趙批詞理詳盡可取
考試官學正寇批意足詞暢
二聖於宅俊之賢而以天人之任責之焉夫人
君事天治民任莫有重焉者也而皆於宅俊兼
之文武任人之專為何如哉昔周公以知恤之
道啓成王及此意謂天下之治天下之賢為之
也知之既真固可以語推心之誠而任之不重
===
又豈足以盡其用哉文武之於宅俊也蓋盡任
使之道者矣何也人君為天之宗子仰有事天
之道然而一日萬幾豈能獨事也惟以宅俊之
賢與天合德者也于是用以敬事上帝焉或因
其道而裁成也夙夜惟寅以盡夫彌綸參贊之
務或因其宜而輔相也朝夕有恪式竭夫左右
宣力之勞承天以理事而敬以凝庶績也承天
以守法而敬以清刑獄也承天以子民而敬以
助康和也天道不言而成化臣道無成以代終
punctuated:
同考試官學正龍批：叙敬事、立民，有許多雋永意思。
考試官教諭趙批：詞理詳盡，可取。
考試官學正寇批：意足詞暢。
二聖於宅俊之賢，而以天人之任責之焉。夫人君事天治民，任莫有重焉者也，而皆於宅俊兼之，文、武任人之專為何如哉？昔周公以知恤之道啓成王及此，意謂天下之治，天下之賢為之也。知之既真，固可以語推心之誠；而任之不重，又豈足以盡其用哉？文、武之於宅俊也，蓋盡任使之道者矣。何也？人君為天之宗子，仰有事天之道，然而一日萬幾，豈能獨事也？惟以宅俊之賢，與天合德者也，于是用以敬事上帝焉。或因其道而裁成也，夙夜惟寅，以盡夫彌綸參贊之務；或因其宜而輔相也，朝夕有恪，式竭夫左右宣力之勞。承天以理事，而敬以凝庶績也；承天以守法，而敬以清刑獄也；承天以子民，而敬以助康和也。天道不言而成化，臣道無成以代終，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Long 龍 comments: In recounting reverently serving [the Lord on High] and establishing [elders and chiefs for] the people, there are many deeply meaningful and evocative ideas.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: The diction and reasoning are thorough and detailed; worthy of selection.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Kou 寇 comments: The meaning is full and the phrasing fluent.
With regard to the worthies who held office and those of outstanding talent, the two sages charged them with responsibilities toward both Heaven and humanity. Now, in a ruler's serving Heaven and governing the people, no responsibility is heavier than these; yet both were combined in the men of office and talent. How singular was the dedication with which Kings Wen and Wu entrusted men! Of old, the Duke of Zhou, in enlightening King Cheng on the way of knowing and showing solicitude [for worthies], touched upon this. His meaning was that the governance of the world is accomplished by the worthies of the world. Once one knows them truly, one may indeed speak of the sincerity of reposing one's heart in them; yet if one does not entrust them with heavy responsibility, how could that suffice to exhaust their usefulness? In their treatment of the men of office and talent, Kings Wen and Wu truly exhausted the way of employing men. Why is this? The ruler is the eldest son of Heaven; looking up, he has the way of serving Heaven, and yet with a myriad affairs in a single day, how can he perform this service alone? Only because the worthies of office and talent are men whose virtue matches that of Heaven did they employ them to reverently serve the Lord on High. At times, following Heaven's way, they regulate and complete it, remaining reverent day and night to fulfill the task of comprehensively ordering and assisting [in cosmic transformation]; at times, following what is fitting to Heaven, they aid and support it, remaining respectful morning and evening to exhaust their toil in rendering service on the left and right. Receiving [the mandate of] Heaven to manage affairs, through reverence they consolidate the multitudinous achievements; receiving [the mandate of] Heaven to uphold the laws, through reverence they purify punishments and litigation; receiving [the mandate of] Heaven to treat the people as children, through reverence they assist in bringing about peace and harmony. The Way of Heaven does not speak, yet brings transformations to completion; the way of the minister claims no achievement of its own, yet brings things to completion on [the ruler's] behalf; …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
天工亮而帝載熈文武代天理物之責始可以
無愧矣人君爲民之父母俯有治人之道然而
惟惠之懷不能以獨治也惟以宅俊之賢宜于
人民者也于是用以立民長伯焉位乎民極也
提綱挈領以成天下之務處乎具瞻也統宗會
元以安天下之民理事以先天下而期無叢脞
也守法以先天下而期無冤民也子民以先天
下而期無弊俗也宅俊妙倡率之機天下被咸
和之澤下民協而萬邦休文武宅中圖治之責
===
始可以無歉矣夫以一宅俊之任而道極於天
人功光於上下此文武所以開我周有道之長
也王其知所法哉抑論知人則哲惟帝其難此
周公告成王知恤之道大旣以夏商告之矣而
復懇懇以文武爲言無非欲其遠稽近述以盡
道也厥後成王果得之周官之訓精微蘊奥著
於言辭禮樂文章形於訓誥然則成王果知恤
乎先儒有言純心要矣用賢急焉抑以是而知
成王之能純心
punctuated: 天工亮而帝載熈，文武代天理物之責始可以無愧矣。人君爲民之父母，俯有治人之道，然而惟惠之懷，不能以獨治也。惟以宅俊之賢宜于人民者也，于是用以立民長伯焉。位乎民極也，提綱挈領以成天下之務；處乎具瞻也，統宗會元以安天下之民。理事以先天下而期無叢脞也，守法以先天下而期無冤民也，子民以先天下而期無弊俗也。宅俊妙倡率之機，天下被咸和之澤，下民協而萬邦休，文武宅中圖治之責始可以無歉矣。夫以一宅俊之任，而道極於天人，功光於上下，此文武所以開我周有道之長也。王其知所法哉！抑論知人則哲，惟帝其難，此周公告成王知恤之道，大旣以夏商告之矣，而復懇懇以文武爲言，無非欲其遠稽近述以盡道也。厥後成王果得之，《周官》之訓，精微蘊奥著於言辭，禮樂文章形於訓誥。然則成王果知恤乎？先儒有言：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」抑以是而知成王之能純心。
translation_en:
…Heaven’s work is accomplished and the Supreme Lord’s undertakings flourish. Only then could Kings Wen and Wu discharge without shame their responsibility to order all things on Heaven’s behalf. The ruler is the father and mother of the people, charged with governing those below him. Yet, though he cherishes benevolence, he cannot govern alone. It is precisely because the worthy men he appoints are suited to serve the people that he establishes them as their leaders. Standing as the people’s highest standard, they grasp the guiding principles and essential matters to accomplish the affairs of the realm; occupying positions to which all look, they bring together fundamental principles to secure peace for the people of the realm. In managing affairs, they lead the realm, seeking to prevent confused attention to petty details; in upholding the laws, they lead the realm, seeking to ensure that no one suffers injustice; in nurturing the people, they lead the realm, seeking to eliminate corrupt customs. Appointing outstanding men brings the workings of leadership to perfection, and the realm receives the blessings of universal harmony. The common people are united and the myriad states prosper. Only then could Kings Wen and Wu discharge without regret their responsibility to occupy the center and seek good government.

Through the single responsibility of appointing outstanding men, their Way reached its fullest extent in Heaven and among humankind, and their achievements shone above and below. This is how Wen and Wu inaugurated the enduring rule of the Way in our Zhou. May the king know whom to emulate! Yet discerning men is wisdom, and even the sage emperor found it difficult. In explaining to King Cheng the way to understand what should concern him, the Duke of Zhou had already spoken broadly [?] of Xia and Shang; he then spoke earnestly again of Wen and Wu. His sole desire was that the king should investigate distant precedents and follow recent ones, thereby fulfilling the Way.

Afterward, King Cheng indeed grasped this. In the instructions of “The Officers of Zhou” (Zhouguan), subtle meanings and profound implications were made manifest in words, while ritual, music, and cultured forms found expression in admonitions and proclamations. Did King Cheng, then, truly understand what should concern him? Earlier Confucian scholars said: “Purifying the heart is essential; employing the worthy is urgent.” From this, indeed, we know that King Cheng was able to purify his heart.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
詩
參差荇菜左右采之窈窕淑女琴瑟友之
參差荇菜左右芼之窈窕淑女鍾鼓樂
之
丘行義
同考試官教諭費批簡而文典而雅詩人好
德之意正如此
同考試官教諭方批其意切其辭莊蓋一唱
三歎而有餘音焉
===
考試官教諭趙批得風人之旨
考試官學正寇批就性情上說來良是
詩人兩興既得聖配而深致夫好德之情焉蓋
莫難於聖配之得也宮人好之而無不用其情
焉有以哉關雎詩人於文王既得太姒而興言
之蓋曰參差乎荇菜也苟為吾筐筥之盛者必
左右以取之而一莖一葉咸為明信之需矣况
我淑女窈窕之德幸而見焉匪致吾之慇懃不
可也蓋必以琴瑟之在御者而是搏是拊於以
punctuated:
詩

「參差荇菜，左右采之。窈窕淑女，琴瑟友之。參差荇菜，左右芼之。窈窕淑女，鍾鼓樂之。」

丘行義

同考試官教諭費批：「簡而文，典而雅，詩人好德之意正如此。」

同考試官教諭方批：「其意切，其辭莊，蓋一唱三歎而有餘音焉。」

考試官教諭趙批：「得風人之旨。」

考試官學正寇批：「就性情上說來，良是。」

詩人兩興既得聖配，而深致夫好德之情焉。蓋莫難於聖配之得也，宮人好之而無不用其情焉，有以哉！《關雎》詩人於文王既得太姒而興言之，蓋曰：參差乎荇菜也，苟為吾筐筥之盛者，必左右以取之，而一莖一葉咸為明信之需矣。况我淑女窈窕之德，幸而見焉，匪致吾之慇懃不可也。蓋必以琴瑟之在御者，而是搏是拊，於以
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Water plants of uneven lengths: to left and right we gather them. The lovely, virtuous maiden: with zithers we befriend her. Water plants of uneven lengths: to left and right we select them. The lovely, virtuous maiden: with bells and drums we gladden her.”

Qiu Xingyi

Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor, comments: “Concise yet polished, classically grounded yet elegant: precisely such is the poet’s intention in loving virtue.”

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “Its meaning is heartfelt; its language dignified. It is like a single song answered by three sighs, with a resonance that lingers.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “It captures the intent of the poet of the Airs.”

Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: “It approaches the subject through human nature and feeling—very sound indeed.”

Through two evocative images, the poet celebrates the obtaining of a sage consort and gives profound expression to the feeling of loving virtue. Nothing, indeed, is harder than obtaining a sage consort. There is good reason why the palace attendants cherish her and give full expression to their feelings! Once King Wen had obtained Tai Si as his consort, the poet of ‘Guan ju’ (‘The Ospreys’) spoke through evocative images, saying in effect: The water plants are of uneven lengths. If they are to fill our square and round baskets, we must gather them to left and right, so that every stem and leaf may serve the needs of purity and sincerity in ritual offerings. How much more, then, when we are fortunate enough to behold the lovely virtue of our good lady, must we express our earnest devotion! Surely we must take the zithers set before us and strike and pluck them, thereby to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
依炙而戀慕之庶同牢合卺之辰而聞此優柔
平中之奏亦爲之一慶焉豈以綢繆而爲瀆耶
參差乎荇菜也苟爲吾錡釡之湘者必無方以
薦之而或菹或茹咸爲馨香之助矣况我淑女
德之窈窕幸而見焉匪將吾之誠篤不可也又
必以鍾鼓之在懸者而載考載擊於以歡洽而
悅懌之庶洽陽渭涘之顧而聞此諧和雝肅之
音尤爲之一慰焉豈以繾綣而爲煩耶是何也
有不世之德如淑女以配聖人以成內治蓋願
===
於昔而酬於今鬱於前而舒於後者也一時喜
樂尊奉之極奚容已哉吁詩人可謂得於性情
之正矣大抵天下之化始於閨門而感人尤莫
速於德太姒之聖德能使宮人形於憂樂者如
此蓋已協天人之心備諸福之本矣由是而樛
木而螽斯而麟趾莫非德之徵應而王化昭焉
豈偶然哉及觀之易之坤則以代終爲訓噫此
其爲文王脩齊之明效而孔子取以冠乎詩也
歟
punctuated: 依炙而戀慕之，庶同牢合卺之辰，而聞此優柔平中之奏，亦爲之一慶焉，豈以綢繆而爲瀆耶？參差乎荇菜也，苟爲吾錡釡之湘者，必無方以薦之，而或菹或茹，咸爲馨香之助矣。况我淑女，德之窈窕，幸而見焉，匪將吾之誠篤不可也。又必以鍾鼓之在懸者，而載考載擊，於以歡洽而悅懌之，庶洽陽渭涘之顧，而聞此諧和雝肅之音，尤爲之一慰焉，豈以繾綣而爲煩耶？是何也？有不世之德如淑女，以配聖人，以成內治，蓋願於昔而酬於今，鬱於前而舒於後者也。一時喜樂尊奉之極，奚容已哉！吁！詩人可謂得於性情之正矣。大抵天下之化始於閨門，而感人尤莫速於德。太姒之聖德，能使宮人形於憂樂者如此，蓋已協天人之心，備諸福之本矣。由是而《樛木》，而《螽斯》，而《麟趾》，莫非德之徵應，而王化昭焉，豈偶然哉？及觀之《易》之《坤》，則以代終爲訓。噫！此其爲文王脩齊之明效，而孔子取以冠乎《詩》也歟？
translation_en:
…to draw close to her [?] and express loving admiration, hoping that on the day when they share the marriage meal and drink the nuptial cups, hearing these gentle, balanced melodies may give her further cause for rejoicing. Could such affectionate devotion be considered disrespectful? Uneven in length is the floating heart: if it is to be cooked in our cauldrons and pots, we must use every means to present it, whether pickled or cooked as vegetables, all contributing to the fragrant offering. How much more, then, when we are fortunate enough to behold our virtuous lady and the secluded grace of her virtue, must we express our heartfelt sincerity! We must also strike and sound the suspended bells and drums, delighting her with joyful harmony. We hope that, when she comes from the sunny bank of the Qia to the banks of the Wei [?], hearing these harmonious, solemn sounds may give her still greater comfort. Could such tender attachment be considered vexatious?

Why is this so? A virtuous lady possessed of virtue rarely seen in an age has become the sage’s consort and brought order to the inner household. What was wished for in the past is fulfilled today; feelings once pent up now find release. How could the utmost joy and reverent service of that moment possibly be restrained? Ah! The poet may truly be said to have attained correctness in human nature and feeling.

In general, the moral transformation of the world begins within the household, and nothing moves people more swiftly than virtue. Tai Si’s sagely virtue could cause the palace women to express themselves in anxiety and joy in this way. It had already brought the hearts of Heaven and humanity into accord and established the foundation of every blessing. Hence the poems Trees with Down-Curving Branches (Jiu mu), Locusts (Zhong si), and The Qilin’s Hooves (Lin zhi) are all signs and responses to virtue, through which kingly transformation becomes manifest. Could this be accidental? When we turn to the Kun hexagram in the Book of Changes, its teaching is to carry another’s undertaking through to completion. Ah! Is this not the manifest result of King Wen’s cultivation of himself and ordering of his household, and the reason Confucius chose this poem to stand at the head of the Book of Odes?

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
如松柏之茂無不爾或承
林應揚
同考試官教諭費批觀此猶可想見有周臣
子忠愛氣象
同考試官教諭方批文從字順敷陳祝君之
意宛然
考試官教諭趙批舂容典雅
考試官學正寇批寫得人臣祝君的意思出
詩人頌君之福取諸物之常盛者焉夫福以盛
===
===
爲難也福之不已而常盛斯其福之至乎天保
臣子之答君如此其意蓋曰吾君之福以進盛
則日月矣以悠久則南山矣而其常盛也何如
哉彼天下之物二儀煦而榮悴生焉有時而或
悴者非所貴也四時變而盛衰異焉有時而或
衰者不足取也惟松柏之茂造化之栽培獨至
氣機之生育特隆而吾君之福如之其必洪休
之踵至而循環不已多福之駢集而日新罔渝
舊者固已邁矣而其新者又於是乎來焉何其
punctuated:
「如松柏之茂，無不爾或承。」
林應揚
同考試官教諭費批：「觀此，猶可想見有周臣子忠愛氣象。」
同考試官教諭方批：「文從字順，敷陳祝君之意宛然。」
考試官教諭趙批：「舂容典雅。」
考試官學正寇批：「寫得人臣祝君的意思出。」
詩人頌君之福，取諸物之常盛者焉。夫福以盛爲難也，福之不已而常盛，斯其福之至乎！《天保》，臣子之答君如此。其意蓋曰：吾君之福，以進盛則日月矣，以悠久則南山矣，而其常盛也何如哉？彼天下之物，二儀煦而榮悴生焉，有時而或悴者，非所貴也；四時變而盛衰異焉，有時而或衰者，不足取也。惟松柏之茂，造化之栽培獨至，氣機之生育特隆，而吾君之福如之。其必洪休之踵至而循環不已，多福之駢集而日新罔渝。舊者固已邁矣，而其新者又於是乎來焉，何其
translation_en:
“Like the luxuriance of pine and cypress, may nothing fail to sustain you.”
Lin Yingyang
Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor, comments: “Reading this, one can still envision the loyal and loving spirit of the subjects of the Zhou.”
Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “The prose flows and the wording is smooth; the wish to bless the ruler is vividly expressed.”
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Ample and poised [?], refined and elegant.”
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: “It brings out what a subject means when invoking blessings upon his ruler.”
In praising his ruler’s blessings, the poet draws upon things that flourish perpetually. For blessings to flourish is difficult; if they continue without end and flourish perpetually, is this not the utmost fullness of blessing? Such is the subjects’ response to their ruler in “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao). Its meaning is roughly this: In their increasing fullness, our ruler’s blessings resemble the sun and moon; in their enduring longevity, they resemble the Southern Mountain. But what is their perpetual flourishing like? Among the things of this world, the warming influence of Heaven and Earth produces both flourishing and withering. Whatever sometimes withers is not what we prize. As the four seasons change, flourishing and decline alternate. Whatever sometimes declines is not worthy of selection. Only in the luxuriance of pine and cypress does the nurturing care of creation reach a singular perfection, and the generative workings of vital force attain exceptional abundance. Our ruler’s blessings are like these. Great blessings must surely arrive one after another, recurring without end; manifold blessings gather together, renewed daily and never failing. The old have already passed, and the new then come again. How …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
相續而不絶已乎新者未之往矣而其後者又
於是乎至焉何其相繼而無息已乎斂其福於
一身則緝熈純嘏衍而爲眉壽萬年之休布其
福於天下則德化昭明流而爲宗社無疆之慶
保太和以培其根萃百順以達其枝時有推移
而福無隆替其與松柏之舊葉將落而新葉巳
生者其理不亦同哉必如是而後臣子之心乃
能答君恩於萬一也抑書稱幾康弼直繼以昭
受上帝申命用休若以福爲德應而詩人盡託
===
之天何也蓋君臣之體分懸絶言不可以直遂
況事之戩穀神之孝享民之徧德皆古帝王之
要道而祈天永命之本有周臣子雖頌禱君福
託名於天而陳善之敬亦於是乎寓矣故曰美
不忘規天保有焉
春秋
夏齊人伐我北鄙〔僖公二十六年〕晉欒書
帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕公會晉侯宋公衛
侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世子光滕子薛伯
punctuated:
相續而不絶已乎？新者未之往矣，而其後者又於是乎至焉，何其相繼而無息已乎？斂其福於一身，則緝熈純嘏，衍而爲眉壽萬年之休；布其福於天下，則德化昭明，流而爲宗社無疆之慶。保太和以培其根，萃百順以達其枝，時有推移，而福無隆替，其與松柏之舊葉將落而新葉巳生者，其理不亦同哉？必如是，而後臣子之心乃能答君恩於萬一也。抑《書》稱「幾康弼直」，繼以「昭受上帝，申命用休」，若以福爲德應，而詩人盡託之天，何也？蓋君臣之體分懸絶，言不可以直遂。況事之戩穀、神之孝享、民之徧德，皆古帝王之要道，而祈天永命之本。有周臣子雖頌禱君福，託名於天，而陳善之敬亦於是乎寓矣。故曰：「美不忘規，《天保》有焉。」

《春秋》
夏，齊人伐我北鄙。〔僖公二十六年〕晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯
translation_en:
…succeed one another without end! The new blessings have not yet departed when those following them arrive: how ceaselessly they follow one another! Gathered in the ruler’s own person, these blessings shine continually in their fullness, expanding into the felicity of venerable longevity lasting ten thousand years. Spread throughout the realm, they make his transforming virtue radiantly manifest, flowing forth as boundless good fortune for the ancestral temple and the altars of state. He preserves supreme harmony to nourish their roots and gathers every favorable influence to extend their branches. Times change, but his blessings neither wax nor wane. Is this not the same principle as that of pines and cypresses, whose new leaves have already grown when the old ones are about to fall? Only thus can his servants and subjects fulfill their heartfelt wish to repay even a ten-thousandth part of their ruler’s grace.

Yet the Book of Documents speaks of “affairs well ordered and assistants upright” [?], followed by “illustriously receiving Heaven above, and receiving renewed commands bringing favor.” This seems to treat blessings as a response to virtue; why, then, does the poet attribute them entirely to Heaven? The respective standing of ruler and minister is separated by an immense distance, so words cannot proceed with complete directness. Moreover, prosperity in affairs, the spirits’ acceptance of filial offerings, and the people’s universal practice of virtue are all essential principles of the ancient sovereigns and the foundation for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. Although the servants and subjects of Zhou praised their ruler’s blessings and prayed for them in Heaven’s name, their reverence in setting forth what is good was also embodied therein. Thus it is said: “Praise that does not forget admonition—Heaven Protects You exemplifies this.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “He integrates the Classic and its commentaries, leaving nothing unaddressed in his judgments. Reading it leaves one refreshed.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Accords with the meaning of the commentary.”

Comment by Examiner Kou, Director of Studies: “Achieves a careful and rigorous style.”

Observe the differences between how our own state and other states dealt with enemies, and the guilt of those skilled in warfare becomes clear. In dealing with enemies, nothing surpasses relying on righteousness; sheer strength has no part in it. Thus, when we examine how Lu and Jin confronted their enemies, is not the disparity between their successes and failures considerable? I have heard that maintaining one's military might and making one's virtue manifest are sound principles of warfare, while relying on strength to bully the weak is its great prohibition. This is why the gentleman prizes the ending of conflict and dares not bring harm upon the multitude: it is entirely because the people's lives must be valued. Few grandees of the Spring and Autumn period understood virtue. Hence, those skilled in governing a state do not resort to arms. In Lu, I find one such man: Liuxia Hui. title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
好勝者孰不快於一逞惠也展喜之遣文告脩
焉申之以王命魯有所恃而不恐數之以廢職
齊有所怍而弗爲卒之師旅不勤甲兵不頓而
民命賴焉謂非聖之和者哉下此者其惟善師
乎是故欒書之救鄭也一聞申息之起遂下旋
旆之令其於不陣似矣然繞角之役桑隧之遇
溱洧之往來寧不念悄悄之征夫耶擬之善爲
國者事固不逮矣下此者其惟善陣乎是故知
罃之駕楚也運謀還師以敝之三分四軍以逆
===
之其於不戰似矣然牛首之師北林之會東門
之觀兵寧弗勞驍驍之大衆耶較之善師者其
德愈衰矣乃若荀吳之善戰猶有異焉夫狄人
之侵至于大原攘之可也而乃聽魏舒之詐謀
廢司馬之成法五乘爲三伍也多方以誘其狎
五陳以相離也未列而薄其師喜功生事變制
多殺非惟下惠之罪人抑亦書罃之罪人矣是
則善戰者服上刑善陣者次之善師者又次之
而皆不若不師之爲尤愈也春秋備書其望天
punctuated: 好勝者，孰不快於一逞？惠也，展喜之遣，文告脩焉。申之以王命，魯有所恃而不恐；數之以廢職，齊有所怍而弗爲。卒之師旅不勤，甲兵不頓，而民命賴焉。謂非聖之和者哉？下此者，其惟善師乎？是故欒書之救鄭也，一聞申息之起，遂下旋旆之令，其於不陣似矣。然繞角之役、桑隧之遇、溱洧之往來，寧不念悄悄之征夫耶？擬之善爲國者，事固不逮矣。下此者，其惟善陣乎？是故知罃之駕楚也，運謀還師以敝之，三分四軍以逆之，其於不戰似矣。然牛首之師、北林之會、東門之觀兵，寧弗勞驍驍之大衆耶？較之善師者，其德愈衰矣。乃若荀吳之善戰，猶有異焉。夫狄人之侵，至于大原，攘之可也，而乃聽魏舒之詐謀，廢司馬之成法。五乘爲三伍也，多方以誘其狎；五陳以相離也，未列而薄其師。喜功生事，變制多殺，非惟下惠之罪人，抑亦書罃之罪人矣。是則善戰者服上刑，善陣者次之，善師者又次之，而皆不若不師之爲尤愈也。春秋備書，其望天
translation_en: …among those bent on winning, who would not have delighted in a chance to vent his anger? As for Liu Xiahui, when Zhan Xi was dispatched, the diplomatic address was carefully prepared. By invoking the king’s command, he gave Lu something to rely upon, dispelling its fear; by reproaching Qi for neglecting its duties, he made it ashamed and caused it to desist. In the end, the troops were not wearied, arms were not blunted, and the people’s lives were preserved. Could he be called anything other than the harmonious one among sages? Below him, would there not be those skilled in conducting campaigns? Thus, when Luan Shu came to Zheng’s rescue, as soon as he heard that the forces of Shen and Xi had mobilized, he ordered his banners turned homeward. In this he came close to avoiding the deployment of battle formations. Yet in the campaign at Raojiao, the encounter at Sangsui, and the movements to and fro along the Zhen and Wei rivers, did he never consider the anxious soldiers on campaign? Compared with one skilled in governing a state, his conduct certainly fell short. Below this, would there not be those skilled in deploying battle formations? Thus, when Zhi Ying sought to overpower Chu, he employed stratagems, withdrawing his forces to exhaust the enemy and dividing his four armies into three groups to confront it. In this he came close to avoiding battle. Yet in the expedition to Niushou, the meeting at Beilin, and the display of troops at the eastern gate, did he not wear out his valiant host? Compared with one skilled in conducting campaigns, his virtue was still more diminished. As for Xun Wu’s skill in battle, it was something different again. When the Di invaded as far as Taiyuan, repelling them would have been acceptable. Instead, he listened to Wei Shu’s deceitful plan and discarded the established military regulations of the Minister of War. He reorganized five chariot units into three infantry squads and used various means to entice the enemy into overconfidence; he separated his five formations and pressed upon the enemy’s troops before they could form ranks. Delighting in achievements and provoking trouble, altering established arrangements and killing many, he was culpable not only by Xiahui’s standard but also by those of Luan Shu and Zhi Ying. Thus, those skilled in battle should suffer the highest punishment; those skilled in deploying battle formations, the next; and those skilled in conducting campaigns, the next again. All fall short of the still better course of not employing an army at all. The Spring and Autumn Annals records these matters fully, in the hope that all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
下以王者之事也而用兵禦敵之略不具見哉
抑古之以車戰也謂以正相加不幸而失捷猶
無以重衂戕乎民也至春秋則以詐覆敵後世
沿習不已如孫吳之爲將秦隋之爲君則失之
愈遠而生民之禍極矣豈惟毒乎一世而已哉
噫此下惠所以師於百世而君子尚論夫王道
也
公孫歸父會齊人伐莒　秋晉侯會狄于
欑函〔宣公十一年〕
===
楊嶷

愈讀愈有滋味
考試官教諭趙　批　曲盡聖人書法之妙
考試官學正寇　批　詞義嚴正
春秋紀內外之兵好有所以謹大防者有所以
明大義者攷莒之伐欑函之會外狄而貶魯晉
聖人於夷夏君臣之際其嚴矣乎且魯之會齊
伐莒以其不恭也晉之會狄于欑函以其求成
punctuated:
下以王者之事也，而用兵禦敵之略不具見哉？抑古之以車戰也，謂以正相加，不幸而失捷，猶無以重衂戕乎民也。至春秋，則以詐覆敵，後世沿習不已。如孫吳之爲將、秦隋之爲君，則失之愈遠，而生民之禍極矣，豈惟毒乎一世而已哉？噫！此下惠所以師於百世，而君子尚論夫王道也。
公孫歸父會齊人伐莒。秋，晉侯會狄于欑函。〔宣公十一年〕
