translation_en:
…all under heaven to undertake the work of a true king. And are not the strategies for employing troops and resisting enemies fully revealed therein? Moreover, in ancient times, warfare with chariots meant confronting one another through regular methods. Even if victory unfortunately eluded them, they would still not inflict grievous losses and suffering upon the people. By the Spring and Autumn period, however, deception was used to overthrow the enemy, and later ages continued this practice without end. With commanders such as Sun Wu and Wu Qi, and rulers such as those of Qin and Sui, the departure grew ever greater, and calamity for the people reached its extreme. How could its poison have been confined to a single age? Alas! This is why Liuxia Hui serves as a teacher for a hundred generations, and why the gentleman holds discourse on the Kingly Way in such esteem.
Gongsun Guifu joined men of Qi in attacking Ju. In autumn, the Marquis of Jin met with the Di at Cuanhan. 〔The eleventh year of Duke Xuan〕
Yang Yi
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: His narration is precise and disciplined, and his writing vigorous and forceful. The more one reads it, the more rewarding it becomes.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: He brings out in full the subtlety of the Sage’s method of recording events.
Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: The wording and meaning are rigorous and upright.
In recording warfare and friendly relations within and beyond the state, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes safeguards the fundamental distinctions and sometimes makes clear the great principles of right conduct. Examining the attack on Ju and the meeting at Cuanhan, we find that it treats the Di as outsiders and censures Lu and Jin. How exacting the Sage is concerning the distinctions between the non-Chinese peoples and the Xia, and between ruler and minister! Now, Lu joined Qi in attacking Ju because Ju had been disrespectful; Jin met with the Di at Cuanhan because they sought peace…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也夫伐則小國以懲會則夷狄以懷矣曷言乎
外狄而責魯晉耶蓋內夏外夷天下之大防也
蠻夷戎狄族類之異明矣邈然要荒止其所焉
可也惟玆以求成之故而竝登乎壇壝之上假
服屬之名而混列於會同之間尚謂有別也乎
吾聞先王之御夷也正朔之不加禮教之不及
朝聘之不通凡以懲淫慝一內外也匪是之由
而遂倖倖於禮文之接玉帛之好焉向使挾詐
以逞伺隙而動斯則盛世之所憂者能無懼乎
===
聖人以謂寧無眾狄之會而不可無族類之分
是故略詞以外之其以謹華夷之辨與若禁亂
誅暴天下之大義也廐矢竊發徵舒之惡著矣
魯晉協力請而戮之可也乃者懲細過於小弱
而廢天討之所當加求外比於遠夷而遺王法
之所不貸尚謂知類也乎吾聞先王之敕法也
有甲兵之威有軍旅之伐有鈇鉞之誅凡以治
姦惡正典刑也匪是之圖而顧汲汲於一莒之
伐眾狄之會焉致使三綱以淪九法以斁斯則
punctuated: 也。夫伐則小國以懲，會則夷狄以懷矣，曷言乎外狄而責魯晉耶？蓋內夏外夷，天下之大防也。蠻夷戎狄，族類之異明矣，邈然要荒，止其所焉可也。惟玆以求成之故，而竝登乎壇壝之上；假服屬之名，而混列於會同之間，尚謂有別也乎？吾聞先王之御夷也，正朔之不加，禮教之不及，朝聘之不通，凡以懲淫慝，一內外也。匪是之由，而遂倖倖於禮文之接、玉帛之好焉。向使挾詐以逞，伺隙而動，斯則盛世之所憂者，能無懼乎？聖人以謂寧無眾狄之會，而不可無族類之分。是故略詞以外之，其以謹華夷之辨與？若禁亂誅暴，天下之大義也。廐矢竊發，徵舒之惡著矣，魯晉協力，請而戮之可也。乃者懲細過於小弱，而廢天討之所當加；求外比於遠夷，而遺王法之所不貸，尚謂知類也乎？吾聞先王之敕法也，有甲兵之威，有軍旅之伐，有鈇鉞之誅，凡以治姦惡，正典刑也。匪是之圖，而顧汲汲於一莒之伐、眾狄之會焉，致使三綱以淪，九法以斁，斯則
translation_en:
…was the reason. Now, through the campaign the small state was chastised, and through the meeting the alien peoples were conciliated. Why, then, speak of treating the Di as outsiders and censuring Lu and Jin? To place the Xia within and the alien peoples outside is the great boundary under Heaven. The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are plainly distinct peoples; it is fitting that they remain in their own places, far away in the outermost domains. Yet now, on the grounds of seeking peace, they ascend together onto the covenant altar and its enclosure; under the pretext of their submission, they mingle among those assembled at interstate meetings. Can this still be called maintaining distinctions? I have heard that when the former kings governed relations with alien peoples, they did not extend their calendar to them, did not bring them within ritual instruction, and did not exchange court audiences and diplomatic visits with them. All this served to restrain depravity and establish a consistent distinction between inside and outside. Instead of following this course, they eagerly [?] pursue ceremonial intercourse and friendly exchanges of jade and silk. Should the others employ deceit to achieve their purposes, watching for an opening to act, this would be a cause for concern even in a flourishing age. Could one be without fear? The Sage held that it was preferable to forgo a meeting with the various Di peoples than to abandon distinctions between peoples. Thus he used abbreviated wording to mark them as outsiders. Was this not to safeguard the distinction between Hua and Yi?

As for suppressing disorder and punishing violence, this is the great moral obligation under Heaven. Arrows were treacherously loosed at the stables, and Zhengshu’s wickedness was manifest. Lu and Jin could properly have joined forces, requested authorization, and put him to death. Instead, they punished minor faults in a small and weak state while neglecting the one upon whom Heaven’s punishment should have fallen; they sought alliances abroad with distant alien peoples while overlooking the one whom royal law could not pardon. Could this still be called understanding the proper distinctions? I have heard that when the former kings enforced the laws, they employed the might of arms, the campaigns of armies, and execution by the axe. All this served to punish the treacherous and wicked and uphold the established penal laws. Instead of attending to this, they busied themselves with a campaign against the single state of Ju and a meeting with the various Di peoples. They thereby caused the Three Bonds to collapse and the Nine Laws to fall into ruin. This, then, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
人心之當正者可無譏乎聖人以謂寧無莒狄
之謀而不可無徵舒之討是故直書以貶之其
以治亂賊之黨與此義行則華夷辨而貴賤殊
君臣嚴而天地泰矣謂春秋之成爲世道一治
不其然與雖然宣也奪嫡頃也忘親是固宜其
無意於陳也獨惜晉景主伯林父新將而舉動
若此是亦可謂無制中夏之略矣卒之栗門轘
而京觀建致使王室懿親奔走於蛇豕之國又
將誰咎也哉君子是以嗟桓文之早而悼悼之
===
晚也
禮記
天垂象□人則之郊所以明天道也
鄧原玉
同考試官教諭馮批郊以明天道與社以
神地道同意作者類不知此獨子能發明美報
之義是用錄出
考試官教諭趙批渾厚爾雅得聖人明天
道之意
punctuated:
人心之當正者，可無譏乎？聖人以謂寧無莒狄之謀，而不可無徵舒之討。是故直書以貶之，其以治亂賊之黨與？此義行，則華夷辨而貴賤殊，君臣嚴而天地泰矣。謂《春秋》之成爲世道一治，不其然與？雖然，宣也奪嫡，頃也忘親，是固宜其無意於陳也。獨惜晉景主伯，林父新將，而舉動若此，是亦可謂無制中夏之略矣。卒之栗門轘而京觀建，致使王室懿親奔走於蛇豕之國，又將誰咎也哉？君子是以嗟桓文之早而悼悼之晚也。

《禮記》
天垂象，□人則之。郊所以明天道也。
鄧原玉

同考試官教諭馮批：「郊以明天道，與社以神地道同意。作者類不知此，獨子能發明美報之義，是用錄出。」

考試官教諭趙批：「渾厚爾雅，得聖人明天道之意。」
translation_en:
…Where people’s hearts require correction, could there be no censure? The sage considered that plans concerning Ju and the Di could be dispensed with, but a punitive expedition against Zhengshu could not. He therefore recorded the events directly to condemn them: was this not to punish the accomplices of rebels and regicides? If this principle prevails, the distinction between the Chinese and the non-Chinese will be clear, the noble and the lowly differentiated, the relationship between ruler and subject strictly maintained, and Heaven and Earth at peace. Is it not true, then, that the completion of the Spring and Autumn Annals brought an ordering of the world?

Nevertheless, Duke Xuan usurped the rightful heir’s position, and Duke Qing forgot his kin; it was only to be expected that they should have no concern for Chen. What is especially regrettable is that Duke Jing of Jin, as leader of the hegemonic alliance, and Linfu, newly appointed commander, should have acted in this way. They too may be said to have lacked a strategy for governing the central states. In the end came dismemberment at the Li Gate [?] and the erection of a mound of enemy corpses, causing close kinsmen of the royal house to flee about in a land of snakes and boars. Whom else could they blame? Thus the gentleman laments that Dukes Huan and Wen departed so early, and grieves that Duke Dao came so late.

Record of Rites
“Heaven displays its signs, and the □ person takes them as a model [one character illegible]. The suburban sacrifice serves to make manifest the Way of Heaven.”
Deng Yuanyu

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “The suburban sacrifice’s making manifest the Way of Heaven has the same meaning as the sacrifice to the soil altar’s honoring the Way of Earth as divine. Writers generally do not understand this. You alone have been able to elucidate the meaning of praising Heaven’s beneficence and requiting it; for this reason, your essay has been selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Substantial, dignified, and classically elegant: it grasps the sage’s intention in making manifest the Way of Heaven.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正寇批不鑿不浮發揮聖人則
天處明盡
觀郊祭法天以備物而聖人崇祀之義著矣蓋
天以生物爲功者也聖人備物以崇祀則其明
天之道者義獨至矣特牲詳論郊祀之禮而結
言其意也蓋謂盡物以致飾者聖王祀天之文
因物以致義者聖王祀天之實循文以究其實
郊之所觀者深矣彼法象莫大乎天雖化工之
默運也而懸象著明者已昭垂於冲穆之表禮
===
制莫善於聖人固經制之悉具也而備物致用
者皆效法乎制作之原日月相推而明生焉十
二月相推而歲成焉袞冕於是乎倣其文也天
道無爲而質具焉乾道變化而龍生焉車旂於
是乎尚其象也郊祀之法天備物者如此豈徒
極觀美之具哉亦以明天道焉耳蓋乾元資始
品物流形天地間無非法象無非道也聖人備
物以崇祀則太和保合之體假物采以闡其微
而含萬物以化光者皆昭晰於明禋之際化育
punctuated:
考試官學正寇批：不鑿不浮，發揮聖人則天處明盡。

觀郊祭法天以備物，而聖人崇祀之義著矣。蓋天以生物爲功者也，聖人備物以崇祀，則其明天之道者，義獨至矣。特牲詳論郊祀之禮，而結言其意也。蓋謂盡物以致飾者，聖王祀天之文；因物以致義者，聖王祀天之實。循文以究其實，郊之所觀者深矣。彼法象莫大乎天，雖化工之默運也，而懸象著明者，已昭垂於冲穆之表；禮制莫善於聖人，固經制之悉具也，而備物致用者，皆效法乎制作之原。日月相推而明生焉，十二月相推而歲成焉，袞冕於是乎倣其文也；天道無爲而質具焉，乾道變化而龍生焉，車旂於是乎尚其象也。郊祀之法天備物者如此，豈徒極觀美之具哉？亦以明天道焉耳。蓋乾元資始，品物流形，天地間無非法象，無非道也。聖人備物以崇祀，則太和保合之體，假物采以闡其微，而含萬物以化光者，皆昭晰於明禋之際。化育
translation_en:
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: “Neither forced nor superficial, it expounds clearly and fully how the sage takes Heaven as his model.”

When we observe how the suburban sacrifice models itself upon Heaven in providing its ritual objects, the meaning of the sage’s reverent worship becomes manifest. Heaven’s achievement lies in bringing things into being. When the sage provides the full array of objects for reverent worship, the significance of his making Heaven’s Way manifest is therefore supremely profound. The chapter The Single Victim (Te sheng) [?] discusses the rites of the suburban sacrifice in detail and concludes by explaining their meaning. Its point is that employing the full range of objects to achieve ornamentation constitutes the outward form of the sage king’s sacrifice to Heaven; drawing upon those objects to convey meaning constitutes its substance. By following the outward form to investigate its substance, one finds profound things to contemplate in the suburban sacrifice.

Among models and images, none is greater than Heaven. Although the work of transformation proceeds silently, the luminous images suspended above already shine forth beyond its deep stillness. Among ritual institutions, none surpasses those of the sage. Although their established arrangements are complete in every detail, the provision of objects and their employment all take as their model the source from which these institutions were fashioned. The sun and moon succeed one another, producing light; the twelve months succeed one another, completing the year. Thus the ceremonial robe and cap imitate their patterns. Heaven’s Way acts without deliberate action, yet substance is fully present; the Way of Qian transforms, and dragons come into being. Thus the carriage and its banners give prominence to these images. Such is the way the suburban sacrifice models itself upon Heaven in providing its objects. Could these merely be implements for achieving the utmost visual splendor? They also serve to make Heaven’s Way manifest.

For all beginnings depend upon the primal power of Qian, and the myriad kinds of things flow into their forms. Between Heaven and Earth, nothing is without a model or image; nothing is apart from the Way. When the sage provides the ritual objects for reverent worship, the subtlety of the reality through which supreme harmony is preserved and united is disclosed through their colors and ornamentation. That which embraces the myriad things and makes transformation glorious is thus clearly revealed at the time of the luminous, pure sacrifice. The transforming and nurturing…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
流行之機因效法以章其蘊而幹歲功於不忒
者悉顯示於昭假之餘夫如是而後見上天生
物之功爲不可掩聖人美報之禮爲不可巳也
否則衮冕車旂之設者皆文焉而巳豈聖人崇
祀之意哉是其始也法天以制禮其終也用禮
以顯天至敎至德之相須爲用也如此抑聞之
易曰乾始能以美利利天下而不言所利大
矣哉則無心成化者天道之自然而有心無爲
聖人之所以合德於天者惟聖人合德於天而
===
後能以明乎天之道此又郊祀之微義也嗚呼
非天下之至仁孰能與於此
樂由中出故靜禮自外作故文大樂必易
大禮必簡
張孔脩
同考試官敎諭馮批言醇而和蓋知學禮樂
而有得者足以占所蘊矣
考試官敎諭趙批只順題講去而於先王
制禮樂之意提掇明甚是之取爾
punctuated:
流行之機，因效法以章其蘊，而幹歲功於不忒者，悉顯示於昭假之餘。夫如是，而後見上天生物之功爲不可掩，聖人美報之禮爲不可巳也。否則，衮冕車旂之設者，皆文焉而巳，豈聖人崇祀之意哉？是其始也，法天以制禮；其終也，用禮以顯天。至敎至德之相須爲用也如此。抑聞之，《易》曰：「乾始能以美利利天下，而不言所利，大矣哉！」則無心成化者，天道之自然；而有心無爲，聖人之所以合德於天者。惟聖人合德於天，而後能以明乎天之道。此又郊祀之微義也。嗚呼！非天下之至仁，孰能與於此？

樂由中出，故靜；禮自外作，故文。大樂必易，大禮必簡。
張孔脩

同考試官敎諭馮批：言醇而和，蓋知學禮樂而有得者，足以占所蘊矣。

考試官敎諭趙批：只順題講去，而於先王制禮樂之意，提掇明甚，是之取爾。
translation_en:
…the workings of its ceaseless flow: through imitation, their underlying significance is made manifest; that which accomplishes the work of the seasons without error is fully revealed through the luminous rite’s reaching the spirits. Only then can one see that High Heaven’s achievement in bringing forth living things cannot be concealed, and that the sages’ rites of splendid recompense cannot cease. Otherwise, the provision of ceremonial robes and caps, carriages and banners would be mere ornament. Could this be the sages’ intention in exalting sacrifice? Thus, at the outset they model rites on Heaven; in the end they use rites to reveal Heaven. Such is the mutual dependence of consummate teaching and consummate virtue in their operation. Moreover, I have heard it said in the Book of Changes: “Qian, in initiating things, can benefit all under Heaven with its excellent benefits, yet does not speak of what it benefits. Great indeed!” To accomplish transformation without conscious intent is the spontaneous operation of Heaven’s Way; to possess conscious intent yet act without contrivance is how the sages unite their virtue with Heaven. Only when the sages unite their virtue with Heaven can they illuminate Heaven’s Way. This, too, is a subtle meaning of the suburban sacrifice. Alas! Who but those of the utmost benevolence under Heaven could participate in this?

“Music issues from within and is therefore still; ritual arises from without and is therefore patterned. Great music must be easy; great ritual must be simple.”
By Zhang Kongxiu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: His language is pure and harmonious. He evidently understands how to study ritual and music and has gained insight into them; this is sufficient to discern what he holds within.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: He simply follows the topic in his exposition, yet brings out very clearly the intention of the former kings in establishing ritual and music. This is why I selected it.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正寇批發揮大樂必易二句最
爲得㫖敬羡敬羡
記者推禮樂之妙而賛其體天地之撰焉蓋天
地之撰易簡而已也禮樂爲能體之則其靜文
之妙可識矣想昔記者之意若謂禮樂之道和
序焉盡之矣始之發於身心極之合乎天地夫
豈有二乎哉彼樂者聲容具陳若難乎其爲靜
矣惟樂由中出則心也者樂之本也審一定和
者既有以涵主靜之源則順成和動者自有以
===
安至靜之體以五聲則成文也以八音則從律
也以百度則得數也蓋不必外和以求靜而靜
卽妙於和之中矣何靜如之禮者經曲異宜若
難乎其爲文矣惟禮自外作則身也者禮之原
也比類成行者既有以端人文之本則嘉會合
禮者自有以煥人道之羣以容貌則得莊也以行
列則得正也以進退則得齊也蓋不必舎序以
求文而文不出於序之外矣何文如之夫天下
之道靜者或隱而難惟大樂與天地同和則其
punctuated:
考試官學正寇批：發揮「大樂必易」二句，最爲得㫖。敬羡！敬羡！

記者推禮樂之妙，而賛其體天地之撰焉。蓋天地之撰，易簡而已也。禮樂爲能體之，則其靜文之妙可識矣。想昔記者之意，若謂禮樂之道，和序焉盡之矣。始之發於身心，極之合乎天地，夫豈有二乎哉？彼樂者，聲容具陳，若難乎其爲靜矣。惟樂由中出，則心也者，樂之本也。審一定和者，既有以涵主靜之源，則順成和動者，自有以安至靜之體。以五聲則成文也，以八音則從律也，以百度則得數也。蓋不必外和以求靜，而靜卽妙於和之中矣。何靜如之！禮者，經曲異宜，若難乎其爲文矣。惟禮自外作，則身也者，禮之原也。比類成行者，既有以端人文之本，則嘉會合禮者，自有以煥人道之羣。以容貌則得莊也，以行列則得正也，以進退則得齊也。蓋不必舎序以求文，而文不出於序之外矣。何文如之！夫天下之道，靜者或隱而難，惟大樂與天地同和，則其
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Kou, an Instructor: The exposition of the two clauses beginning “Great music must be easy” captures their purport especially well. Admirable! Admirable!

The author of the Record explores the subtle excellence of rites and music and praises their embodiment of the workings of Heaven and Earth. For the workings of Heaven and Earth are simply ease and simplicity. Since rites and music can embody these, the subtle excellence of their stillness and patterned expression can be understood. I imagine that the author's original meaning was this: harmony and order exhaust the Way of rites and music. Beginning with their emergence from the body and mind, and reaching their culmination in accord with Heaven and Earth, how could they constitute two different principles?

In music, sounds and bodily movements are displayed together, seemingly making stillness difficult to attain. Yet music issues from within, and thus the mind is its foundation. Through examining unity and establishing harmony, one nurtures the source from which stillness is made central; through orderly completion and harmonious movement, one naturally settles into the substance of utmost stillness. The five notes form patterns; the eight classes of instruments follow the pitch standards; the hundred measures attain their proper numerical proportions. There is therefore no need to seek stillness outside harmony: stillness finds its subtle realization within harmony itself. What stillness could equal this!

In rites, the general rules and detailed observances have different requirements, seemingly making patterned expression difficult to attain. Yet rites arise from without, and thus the body is their source. By grouping like with like and forming ranks, one sets right the foundation of human cultural forms; through fine gatherings that accord with ritual, one naturally brings lustre to the communities of human life. In appearance and bearing, dignity is attained; in the arrangement of ranks, correctness; in advancing and withdrawing, uniformity. There is therefore no need to abandon order to seek patterned expression: patterned expression does not lie outside order. What patterned expression could equal this!

Now, among the ways of the world, those characterized by stillness may be obscure and difficult. Only great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth, and thus its …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
靜者非有事於强也自吾心之至和者充之聲
得之而爲聲焉音得之而爲音焉度得之而爲
度焉各順其自然而已矣擬諸乾知大始而確
然示人易者何異哉天下之道文者或彙而煩
惟大禮與天地同節則其文者非徒事於末也
舉吾身之至序者推之時乎莊而莊焉時乎正
而正焉時乎齊而齊焉皆行所無事而已矣擬
諸坤作成物而隤然示人簡者何異哉是惟易
而靜也而後見其靜者爲和之至惟簡而文也
===
而後見其文者爲序之極禮樂之道斯其至矣
抑論天地設位聖人成能則禮樂易簡之妙豈
惟合諸天地而已哉要之易簡之道在我則禮
樂參贊之化皆不外此故曰易簡而天下之理
得天下之理得而成位乎其中矣學者能合而
觀之則天地也禮樂也身心也其一貫矣乎
第貳塲
論
聖人先得我心之同然
punctuated:
靜者非有事於强也。自吾心之至和者充之，聲得之而爲聲焉，音得之而爲音焉，度得之而爲度焉，各順其自然而已矣。擬諸乾知大始而確然示人易者，何異哉？天下之道，文者或彙而煩。惟大禮與天地同節，則其文者非徒事於末也。舉吾身之至序者推之，時乎莊而莊焉，時乎正而正焉，時乎齊而齊焉，皆行所無事而已矣。擬諸坤作成物而隤然示人簡者，何異哉？是惟易而靜也，而後見其靜者爲和之至；惟簡而文也，而後見其文者爲序之極。禮樂之道，斯其至矣。抑論天地設位，聖人成能，則禮樂易簡之妙，豈惟合諸天地而已哉？要之，易簡之道在我，則禮樂參贊之化皆不外此。故曰：「易簡而天下之理得，天下之理得而成位乎其中矣。」學者能合而觀之，則天地也，禮樂也，身心也，其一貫矣乎！

第貳塲

論

聖人先得我心之同然
translation_en:
…its stillness does not depend upon forcing anything. Extend the utmost harmony of my own heart: individual sounds receive it and become sounds; musical tones receive it and become tones; measures receive it and become measures. Each simply follows its own natural course. How does this differ from Qian, which presides over the great beginning and, in its firmness, shows people ease? Among the ways of the world, patterned forms may become tangled and cumbersome. Yet great ritual shares the measured order of Heaven and Earth, so its patterned forms are not merely concerned with superficial details. Extend the utmost order embodied in my own person: when solemnity is called for, be solemn; when rectitude is called for, be correct; when uniformity is called for, be orderly. All this is simply acting without contrivance. How does this differ from Kun, which brings things to completion and, in its yielding compliance, shows people simplicity? Only through ease and stillness do we see that this stillness is harmony at its utmost; only through simplicity and patterned form do we see that this patterned form is order at its fullest. Here the Way of ritual and music reaches its consummation.

Moreover, consider how Heaven and Earth establish their positions and the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment. Can the subtle workings of ease and simplicity in ritual and music consist merely in accord with Heaven and Earth? In essence, when the Way of ease and simplicity resides in oneself, the transforming work of ritual and music—joining with and assisting Heaven and Earth—never extends beyond it. Thus it is said: “Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are apprehended. Once those principles are apprehended, one establishes one’s position in their midst.” If students can view these things together, will they not see that Heaven and Earth, ritual and music, and body and heart are pervaded by a single principle?

Second Session

Discourse

“The Sage Has Already Apprehended What Our Hearts Recognize in Common”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批場中作此題者說理則
枯騁詞則泛是作只就本旨發揮而議論層出氣
若有不可禦者子豈一國之士也哉
同考試官學正龍批據題立說而文勢闔闢
曲盡其妙錄之固以其理勝與
考試官教諭趙批但道正義不雜浮辭讀
之不覺終篇
考試官學正寇批義本精切詞亦古雅其
===
深造而有得者
能盡其心者盡天下之道者也盡天下之道者
超天下者也夫聖人以道而超天下道非自聖
人而始有也以其養心而得也道非至夫人而
始無也以其無所養而失也是天之與人者何
嘗不一而不一者人之學也聖人亦人焉者而
豈異於天下雖無所異而於道獨先得焉是眾
人不能有而聖人獨有之也聖人先得我心之
同然吾於是見人性之善而盡心之學所以為
punctuated:
黃士觀

同考試官教諭馮批：場中作此題者，說理則枯，騁詞則泛。是作只就本旨發揮，而議論層出，氣若有不可禦者。子豈一國之士也哉！

同考試官學正龍批：據題立說，而文勢闔闢，曲盡其妙。錄之，固以其理勝與！

考試官教諭趙批：但道正義，不雜浮辭，讀之不覺終篇。

考試官學正寇批：義本精切，詞亦古雅，其深造而有得者！

能盡其心者，盡天下之道者也；盡天下之道者，超天下者也。夫聖人以道而超天下，道非自聖人而始有也，以其養心而得也；道非至夫人而始無也，以其無所養而失也。是天之與人者，何嘗不一？而不一者，人之學也。聖人亦人焉者，而豈異於天下？雖無所異，而於道獨先得焉，是眾人不能有而聖人獨有之也。聖人先得我心之同然，吾於是見人性之善，而盡心之學所以為
translation_en:
Huang Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: Among those in the examination who addressed this topic, those who expounded principles were dry, while those who indulged in rhetoric were diffuse. This composition develops only the essential meaning of the topic, yet its arguments emerge one after another, with a force that seems irresistible. Are you merely a scholar of a single state!

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: He grounds his argument in the topic, and the movement of his prose, contracting and expanding, fully realizes its subtle possibilities. Surely it is the strength of its reasoning that warrants selecting it!

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: He expounds only the correct meaning, without mixing in empty rhetoric. One reads to the end without realizing it.

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: Its meaning is precise and apt, and its language antique and elegant. Here is someone who has pursued learning deeply and attained understanding for himself!

One who fully realizes his own heart fully realizes the Way of all under Heaven; one who fully realizes the Way of all under Heaven surpasses all others under Heaven. The sage surpasses all others through the Way. The Way did not first come into existence with the sage: he attained it by nourishing his heart. Nor does the Way cease to exist in ordinary people: they lose it because they fail to nourish their hearts. When has what Heaven bestows upon people ever been unequal? What differs is their learning. The sage, too, is a human being: how could he be different from everyone else under Heaven? Although he is no different, he alone attains the Way first. Thus, what ordinary people fail to possess, the sage alone possesses. The sage first attains that which our hearts alike affirm. In this I see the goodness of human nature and the reason why the learning that fully realizes the heart is…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
大也蓋嘗觀之天地間之至貴者謂之人人之
至靈者謂之心心之生生者謂之性性之括萬
善而不遺者謂之理義故理義之在人也發之
親而孝長而敬事君而忠臨民而仁親疎貴賤
厚薄而別聲色臭味嗜慾而節五常百行千變
萬化皆明覺而有倫理是皆不學而知不慮而
能者也非以堯存非以桀亡非以賢知而通非
以愚不肖而塞何也所謂性之善而心之同然
者本如此其妙也而聖人獨先得之豈天之獨
===
厚聖人耶嘗求其故矣試語於眾曰人之有心
異於耳目口鼻乎曰無以異也心之同然異於
耳目之同聽目之同美口之同嗜鼻之同臭乎曰
無以異也夫於耳目口鼻吾皆通之而於心則
蔽焉豈非得之天者同而所以事其心者未至
與夫人生而靜天之性也感於物而動性之欲
也聖人知動之為害而心以制之去其所本無
而復其所固有故曰盡心之學所以為大也盡
之也者存之也孳孳於善存而不失慎獨以研
punctuated:
大也。蓋嘗觀之：天地間之至貴者謂之人，人之至靈者謂之心，心之生生者謂之性，性之括萬善而不遺者謂之理義。故理義之在人也，發之親而孝，長而敬，事君而忠，臨民而仁，親疎貴賤厚薄而別，聲色臭味嗜慾而節，五常百行，千變萬化，皆明覺而有倫理。是皆不學而知，不慮而能者也。非以堯存，非以桀亡，非以賢知而通，非以愚不肖而塞。何也？所謂性之善而心之同然者，本如此其妙也。而聖人獨先得之，豈天之獨厚聖人耶？

嘗求其故矣。試語於眾曰：「人之有心，異於耳目口鼻乎？」曰：「無以異也。」「心之同然，異於耳目之同聽、目之同美、口之同嗜、鼻之同臭乎？」曰：「無以異也。」夫於耳目口鼻，吾皆通之，而於心則蔽焉，豈非得之天者同，而所以事其心者未至與？夫人生而靜，天之性也；感於物而動，性之欲也。聖人知動之為害，而心以制之，去其所本無，而復其所固有。故曰：「盡心之學所以為大也。」盡之也者，存之也。孳孳於善，存而不失，慎獨以研
translation_en:
…is great. I have considered this: the most precious being between Heaven and Earth is called the human being; the most spiritually perceptive part of a human being is called the heart-mind; the ceaseless generative activity of the heart-mind is called human nature; and that in human nature which encompasses every goodness without omission is called moral principle and rightness. Thus, moral principle and rightness within people manifest themselves as filial devotion toward parents, respect toward elders, loyalty in serving the ruler, and benevolence in governing the people. They distinguish degrees of closeness and distance, high and low status, and greater and lesser regard; they regulate appetites and desires for sounds, sights, smells, and tastes. Through the five constant virtues and the hundred forms of conduct, amid a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes, all is guided by clear awareness and ordered human relationships. These are all things people know without learning and can do without deliberation. They do not exist because of Yao, nor perish because of Jie; they are not opened up by worthiness and wisdom, nor blocked by foolishness and unworthiness. Why? What we call the goodness of human nature and the common assent of all heart-minds is inherently wondrous in precisely this way. Yet sages alone apprehend it first. Can it be that Heaven favors sages alone?

I have sought the reason. Suppose one asks people: “Is possessing a heart-mind different from possessing ears, eyes, a mouth, and a nose?” They reply: “There is no difference.” “Does the common assent of heart-minds differ from the shared hearing of ears and eyes [?], the shared appreciation of beauty by eyes, the shared preferences of mouths, or the shared perception of smells by noses?” They reply: “There is no difference.” In the case of ears, eyes, mouth, and nose, we all exercise these capacities freely, yet in the heart-mind we are obstructed. Is this not because what we receive from Heaven is the same, while our efforts to tend the heart-mind have yet to reach their full extent? When people are born and are still, this is their Heaven-given nature; when they are affected by things and stirred into activity, this is the desire of that nature. Sages recognize the harm that such stirrings can cause and use the heart-mind to control them, removing what it originally lacked and restoring what it inherently possessed. Thus it is said: “This is why the learning that fully realizes the heart-mind is great.” Fully realizing it means preserving it. Striving diligently toward goodness, preserving it without losing it, and being watchful over oneself when alone in order to investigate…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其幾親師友以致其助識前言往行以畜其德
而吾之學始精一矣窮理盡性而天下之道始
備矣此聖人所以得我心之同然而衆人不能
也夫衆人之不能何也蓋以純駁雜擾之資加
之以或輟或作之學於其心之蔽着未能祛而
復之是故不迷於意見則惑於聲利不騖於亢
激則溺於卑污紛紛籍籍不爲異物者亦希矣
至是而人心之同然安得不爲聖人之獨有哉
聖人從事於心旣有以致其精而物之紛然者
===
又不能爲吾動是以同寂而異感同體而異發
同蘊而異用親也而先得我心之孝焉兄也而
先得我心之敬焉君也而先得我心之忠焉民
也而先得我心之仁焉親疎貴賤厚薄也而先
得我心之别焉食色臭味也而先得我心之節
焉五常百行千變萬化而先得我心之明覺條
理焉有天下以爲是而吾矯以爲非得我心之
公非焉有天下以爲非而吾矯以爲是得我心
之公是焉其存主曰德吐詞曰經用世曰業無
punctuated: 其幾，親師友以致其助，識前言往行以畜其德，而吾之學始精一矣。窮理盡性，而天下之道始備矣。此聖人所以得我心之同然，而衆人不能也。夫衆人之不能，何也？蓋以純駁雜擾之資，加之以或輟或作之學，於其心之蔽着，未能祛而復之。是故不迷於意見，則惑於聲利；不騖於亢激，則溺於卑污。紛紛籍籍，不爲異物者亦希矣。至是，而人心之同然，安得不爲聖人之獨有哉？聖人從事於心，旣有以致其精，而物之紛然者又不能爲吾動，是以同寂而異感，同體而異發，同蘊而異用。親也，而先得我心之孝焉；兄也，而先得我心之敬焉；君也，而先得我心之忠焉；民也，而先得我心之仁焉；親疎貴賤厚薄也，而先得我心之别焉；食色臭味也，而先得我心之節焉；五常百行，千變萬化，而先得我心之明覺條理焉。有天下以爲是，而吾矯以爲非，得我心之公非焉；有天下以爲非，而吾矯以爲是，得我心之公是焉。其存主曰德，吐詞曰經，用世曰業，無
translation_en:
…its incipient stirrings; draw close to teachers and friends to obtain their help; and acquaint oneself with the words and deeds of the past to cultivate one’s virtue. Only then does my learning become refined and single-minded. By thoroughly investigating principle and fully realizing one’s nature, one comes to comprehend the Way of all under Heaven in its entirety. This is how sages grasp what our hearts all recognize alike, whereas ordinary people cannot. Why can ordinary people not do so? Their endowments mingle purity and impurity in confused disorder, and their learning is pursued by fits and starts. They cannot remove the obscurations that cling to their hearts and restore them. Thus, if they are not misled by their own opinions, they are beguiled by fame and profit; if they do not pursue arrogant excess, they sink into baseness and corruption. Amid all this confusion, few avoid becoming alien to their human nature. At this point, how could what all human hearts recognize alike fail to become the exclusive possession of sages?

Sages devote themselves to the heart. Having brought its refinement to completion, they cannot be moved by the bewildering multiplicity of external things. Thus, though alike in stillness, they differ in their responses; though alike in substance, they differ in its expression; though alike in what they contain, they differ in its application. Toward parents, the sage is first to grasp the filial devotion in my heart; toward elder brothers, the respect in my heart; toward the ruler, the loyalty in my heart; toward the people, the benevolence in my heart. In degrees of closeness and distance, high and low status, and greater and lesser consideration, he is first to grasp the distinctions in my heart. In food, sexual desire, smells, and tastes, he is first to grasp the restraints in my heart. Throughout the five constant virtues and the hundred forms of conduct, amid a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations, he is first to grasp the lucid awareness and ordered principles in my heart. When all under Heaven deem something right, yet I stand against them and deem it wrong, he grasps the impartial judgment of wrong in my heart. When all under Heaven deem something wrong, yet I stand against them and deem it right, he grasps the impartial judgment of right in my heart. What he preserves within and takes as his guiding principle is called virtue; what he expresses in words is called the classics; what he puts into practice in the world is called achievement; being without…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
過不及曰中約而言之曰天下古今同然之理
義嗟乎至矣吾嘗求之古昔而嘆先得我心之
難也得之而繼天者堯舜禹湯文武之爲君也
得之而佐命者臯夔伊周之爲臣也得之而明
道者孔孟之爲師也戰國之季人之陷溺其心
如碩果不食者亦至矣而孟子惓惓性善而取
證於人心之同然將何從而得之耶延平李子
有言曰人理義之心未嘗無惟持守之卽在爾
夫不失之謂得不亡之謂存持守也者存之也
===
存則大大則廣廣則塞是故至大配天至廣配
地至塞配萬化學而至是其孰爲得耶孰爲先
得耶孰爲我耶孰爲聖人耶善學者求之心性
焉盡矣請以是足孟子之意
同前
鄧原玉
同考試官教諭胡批
詞反堆積可厭惟此作明淨可誦錄之
題本明白往往掇拾他
同考試官學正龍批說聖人盡心之學令人
punctuated:
過不及曰中，約而言之，曰天下古今同然之理義。嗟乎，至矣！吾嘗求之古昔，而嘆先得我心之難也。得之而繼天者，堯舜禹湯文武之爲君也；得之而佐命者，臯夔伊周之爲臣也；得之而明道者，孔孟之爲師也。戰國之季，人之陷溺其心，如碩果不食者亦至矣，而孟子惓惓性善，而取證於人心之同然，將何從而得之耶？延平李子有言曰：「人理義之心未嘗無，惟持守之卽在爾。」夫不失之謂得，不亡之謂存。持守也者，存之也。存則大，大則廣，廣則塞。是故至大配天，至廣配地，至塞配萬化。學而至是，其孰爲得耶？孰爲先得耶？孰爲我耶？孰爲聖人耶？善學者求之心性焉，盡矣。請以是足孟子之意。
同前。
鄧原玉。
同考試官教諭胡批：詞反堆積可厭，惟此作明淨可誦，錄之。題本明白，往往掇拾他。
同考試官學正龍批：說聖人盡心之學，令人
translation_en:
…neither exceeding nor falling short is called the Mean. To put it briefly, these are the principles and righteousness universally acknowledged throughout the world, past and present. Ah, how consummate! I have sought this in antiquity and sighed at the difficulty of apprehending before others what is in my own heart. Those who apprehended it and succeeded Heaven were the rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Those who apprehended it and assisted in establishing the heavenly mandate were the ministers Gao, Kui, Yi, and Zhou. Those who apprehended it and elucidated the Way were the teachers Confucius and Mencius. At the end of the Warring States period, people had sunk into the corruption of their hearts; those who remained were like the great fruit left uneaten [?]. Yet Mencius tirelessly upheld the goodness of human nature and sought evidence in what human hearts universally acknowledge. By what means could this be apprehended? Master Li of Yanping said: “People have never lacked the heart of principle and righteousness. Simply hold fast to it, and it is there.” Not losing it is what is meant by apprehending it; not letting it perish is what is meant by preserving it. Holding fast to it means preserving it. Preserved, it becomes great; great, it becomes broad; broad, it fills all things. Thus, in its utmost greatness it matches Heaven; in its utmost breadth it matches Earth; in its utmost fullness it matches the myriad transformations. When learning reaches this point, who apprehends it? Who apprehends it first? Who is the self? Who is the sage? Those who learn well seek it in the heart and human nature: that is all. Let me offer this to complete Mencius’s meaning.
Same as above.
Deng Yuanyu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “The wording instead piles up tediously; this composition alone is clear, pure, and worthy of recitation, so I have included it. The topic itself is clear, yet writers frequently gather up other…” [The transcription appears disordered here; this last fragment apparently belongs before “wording.”]
Comment by Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor: “Its account of the sages’ learning through fully realizing the heart makes one…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
有遐思焉是不可以風多士乎
考試官敎諭趙批是善言聖人者
考試官學正寇批義理之文
心統天下之道者也聖人所以立人極者亦惟
盡其心而已天以太極之理畀諸人蘊之爲性
廓之爲理義而心統之者也外心以言理義非
以語性也外心以立人極非以合天也百姓日
用而不知盡心之道鮮矣夫聖人者豈異人哉
不過卽夫人心之同以成能耳蓋降衷之恆厥
===
賦鈞焉天無心也盡心之極同然者取足焉聖
人無異也以人合天而心極盡心極盡而人極
立矣此盡心之學所以爲大歟今夫天地之大
德曰生是故陰陽寒暑之動盪也四時日月之
推移也根荄蝡息蠕動之竝育竝行也其生不
息其化不窮其理謂之道其用謂之神其主宰
謂之帝其實則一元始之也元者何天地之心
是已故曰復其見天地之心乎天地匪心無以
幹萬化聖人匪心無以裁天地別之爲聖狂賢
punctuated:
有遐思焉，是不可以風多士乎？
考試官敎諭趙批：是善言聖人者。
考試官學正寇批：義理之文。
心統天下之道者也。聖人所以立人極者，亦惟盡其心而已。天以太極之理畀諸人，蘊之爲性，廓之爲理義，而心統之者也。外心以言理義，非以語性也；外心以立人極，非以合天也。百姓日用而不知，盡心之道鮮矣。夫聖人者，豈異人哉？不過卽夫人心之同以成能耳。蓋降衷之恆，厥賦鈞焉。天無心也，盡心之極，同然者取足焉。聖人無異也，以人合天而心極盡，心極盡而人極立矣。此盡心之學所以爲大歟！今夫天地之大德曰生。是故陰陽寒暑之動盪也，四時日月之推移也，根荄蝡息蠕動之竝育竝行也，其生不息，其化不窮。其理謂之道，其用謂之神，其主宰謂之帝，其實則一元始之也。元者何？天地之心是已。故曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」天地匪心無以幹萬化，聖人匪心無以裁天地。別之爲聖狂賢
translation_en:
…evokes far-reaching reflections. Could this not inspire the many scholars?
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: This is someone who speaks well of the sage.
Examiner Kou, Instructor, comments: An essay on moral principle.
The mind unifies the Way of all under Heaven. The means by which the sage establishes the supreme standard for humanity consists simply in fully realizing his mind. Heaven bestows upon people the principle of the Supreme Ultimate: contained within, it constitutes human nature; expanded outward, it constitutes principle and righteousness. The mind unifies them. To speak of principle and righteousness apart from the mind is no way to discuss human nature; to establish the supreme standard for humanity apart from the mind is no way to accord with Heaven. The common people use it daily without knowing it; rare indeed is the practice of fully realizing the mind. Is the sage, then, different from other people? He merely takes what human minds share and brings his capacities to fulfillment. For the constant moral nature bestowed by Heaven is imparted equally to all. Heaven has no deliberate intention; at the utmost realization of the mind, what all share is sufficient. The sage is no different: by bringing the human into accord with Heaven, he realizes the mind to its utmost; when the mind is fully realized, the supreme standard for humanity is established. Is this not why the learning devoted to fully realizing the mind is great?
Now, the great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation. Thus, through the alternating movements of yin and yang, cold and heat; through the succession of the four seasons, sun and moon; and through the concurrent growth and activity of rooted plants and breathing, crawling creatures, generation never ceases and transformation is inexhaustible. Its principle is called the Way; its operation is called the numinous; its governing power is called the Sovereign. In substance, a single primal source initiates it all. What is this primal source? It is precisely the mind of Heaven and Earth. Hence the saying: “In Return, do we not see the mind of Heaven and Earth!” Without mind, Heaven and Earth could not direct the myriad transformations; without mind, the sage could not regulate Heaven and Earth. Distinguished, people become sages, the wayward, the worthy…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
愚形也而統之者心秩之爲仁義禮智性也而
統之者心敘之爲君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友倫
也而統之者心以人物則表裏焉以古今則進
退焉以造化則出入焉而心管之矣口於味目
於色耳於聲其形同也獨心異乎哉夫太極生
人之初一而已粹然其性渾然其理燦然其義
皆人心之所同有也而聖人何以先得之蓋天
以統元氣也地以統元形也人以統元識也吾
以一身中天地固將會天地之心以立心相似
===
而不違者也而形生神發之後始有役於形昏
於氣溺於慾鑿於情與聖人大相遠者天之所
降安所繆盭若是哉不能盡其心而已聖人所
以與天地參者其諸盡心乎聖人之心何心也
天地之心也藏於密而不溷之以形會於精而
不雜之以氣誠於幾而不敛之以慾通於靈而
不滑之以情夫藏於密則靜深而心之淵源者
無不盡矣會於精則昭曠而心之廣大者無不
盡矣誠於幾而通於靈則大公順應而吾心之
punctuated: 愚，形也，而統之者心；秩之爲仁義禮智，性也，而統之者心；敘之爲君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友，倫也，而統之者心。以人物則表裏焉，以古今則進退焉，以造化則出入焉，而心管之矣。口於味，目於色，耳於聲，其形同也，獨心異乎哉？夫太極生人之初，一而已。粹然其性，渾然其理，燦然其義，皆人心之所同有也，而聖人何以先得之？蓋天以統元氣也，地以統元形也，人以統元識也。吾以一身中天地，固將會天地之心以立心，相似而不違者也。而形生神發之後，始有役於形、昏於氣、溺於慾、鑿於情，與聖人大相遠者。天之所降，安所繆盭若是哉？不能盡其心而已。聖人所以與天地參者，其諸盡心乎？聖人之心，何心也？天地之心也。藏於密而不溷之以形，會於精而不雜之以氣，誠於幾而不敛之以慾，通於靈而不滑之以情。夫藏於密，則靜深而心之淵源者無不盡矣；會於精，則昭曠而心之廣大者無不盡矣；誠於幾而通於靈，則大公順應而吾心之
translation_en:
…and foolish: these are distinctions of embodied form, yet what unifies them is the mind. Ordered as benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, they constitute human nature, yet what unifies them is the mind. Arranged as ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend, they constitute human relationships, yet what unifies them is the mind. In relation to people and things, there are outward and inward aspects; in relation to past and present, advance and retreat; in relation to creation and transformation, emergence and withdrawal. The mind governs them all. Mouths respond to flavors, eyes to colors, and ears to sounds: their bodily constitution is alike. Could minds alone differ?

When the Supreme Ultimate first brings human beings into existence, there is only unity. Their nature in its purity, their principle in its integral wholeness, and their moral rightness in its brilliance are all things that human minds possess in common. How, then, does the sage apprehend them first? Heaven unifies primordial vital energy; earth unifies primordial form; human beings unify primordial awareness. With my single person standing between Heaven and Earth, I must bring together their mind to establish my own, resembling them without departing from them. Only after bodily form arises and spiritual awareness unfolds do some become enslaved to form, clouded by vital energy, submerged in desires, and distorted by feelings, thus becoming greatly removed from the sage. How could what Heaven bestows be so perverse? It is simply that they fail to realize their minds fully.

Is it not through fully realizing his mind that the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth? What mind is the sage’s mind? It is the mind of Heaven and Earth. He keeps it in hidden depths without muddying it with bodily form, gathers it in its essential purity without adulterating it with vital energy, makes it sincere at the incipient stirrings without constraining it through desire, and opens it to spiritual efficacy without confusing it through feelings. Kept in hidden depths, it is still and profound, and the mind’s deepest sources are fully realized. Gathered in its essential purity, it is luminous and expansive, and the mind’s breadth and greatness are fully realized. Sincere at the incipient stirrings and open to spiritual efficacy, it responds with utter impartiality and accord, and my mind’s…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
體用又一以貫之矣由是而踐形由是而盡性
由是而惇倫由是而經天綱奠地維陳藝極著
話言以知覺天下後世而彌綸參贊舉之矣孰
非盡心之功哉故曰心之精爽是謂聖人此付
形受質之始聖人衆人無以異也而踐形盡性
聖人雖欲不異于人不可也夫其所以爲人者
非外心以成身不能不與人同所以先得者非
外盡心以成聖不能不與人異同異之間人自
爲之低昂之機天曷故焉若要其始則桀可使
===
語命也跖可使語道也塗人可使爲堯舜也容
聖愚豐嗇哉然則心之所在聖人以能盡而成
聖衆人以不能盡之而爲衆人使夫人而皆知
盡心也則夫人而聖賢矣性善之說此其章章
著者也故曰聖人所以立人極者盡心而已是
故舉其類則位之所在堯舜以其盡心者垂而
爲時雍風動之休矣道之所在夫子以其盡心
者寄而爲刪述垂憲之功矣故曰得中數者立
於上焉得窮數者立於下焉道化無紀極聖人
punctuated: 體用又一以貫之矣。由是而踐形，由是而盡性，由是而惇倫，由是而經天綱、奠地維、陳藝極、著話言，以知覺天下後世，而彌綸參贊舉之矣。孰非盡心之功哉？故曰：「心之精爽，是謂聖人。」此付形受質之始，聖人衆人無以異也；而踐形盡性，聖人雖欲不異于人，不可也。夫其所以爲人者，非外心以成身，不能不與人同；所以先得者，非外盡心以成聖，不能不與人異。同異之間，人自爲之；低昂之機，天曷故焉？若要其始，則桀可使語命也，跖可使語道也，塗人可使爲堯舜也，容聖愚豐嗇哉？然則心之所在，聖人以能盡而成聖，衆人以不能盡之而爲衆人。使夫人而皆知盡心也，則夫人而聖賢矣。性善之說，此其章章著者也。故曰：「聖人所以立人極者，盡心而已。」是故舉其類，則位之所在，堯舜以其盡心者垂而爲時雍風動之休矣；道之所在，夫子以其盡心者寄而爲刪述垂憲之功矣。故曰：「得中數者立於上焉，得窮數者立於下焉。」道化無紀極，聖人
translation_en: …the substance and functioning of my heart-mind are likewise united by a single thread. Through this one fulfills one’s bodily form; through this one fully realizes one’s nature; through this one strengthens human relationships; and through this one orders Heaven’s guiding cords, establishes Earth’s supporting bonds, sets forth the standards of the arts, and makes exemplary teachings manifest, thereby awakening understanding throughout the world and in later generations. The work of comprehensively ordering all things and assisting Heaven and Earth in their transforming and nourishing activity is thus accomplished. Which of these is not an achievement of fully realizing the heart-mind? Thus it is said: “The refined intelligence of the heart-mind is what makes a sage.” At the outset, when bodily form is conferred and material constitution received, sages and ordinary people do not differ. Yet in fulfilling bodily form and fully realizing human nature, sages could not remain indistinguishable from others even if they wished to. What makes them human is that they do not establish themselves apart from the heart-mind: in this they cannot but be the same as others. What they apprehend before others is that they do not become sages apart from fully realizing the heart-mind: in this they cannot but differ from others. Whether people remain alike or become different is their own doing. What part does Heaven play in the workings by which they sink or rise? If we examine their beginnings, then even Jie could be brought to discourse on Heaven’s mandate, Zhi could be brought to discourse on the Way, and a person on the road could be brought to become a Yao or a Shun. Could Heaven have bestowed abundantly on sages and sparingly on fools? Thus, where the heart-mind is concerned, sages become sages because they can realize it fully, while ordinary people remain ordinary because they cannot. If everyone knew how to realize the heart-mind fully, everyone would become a sage or worthy. Here the doctrine that human nature is good is conspicuously manifest. Thus it is said: “The means by which sages establish the highest standard for humanity is simply to realize the heart-mind fully.” Accordingly, to cite examples of this kind: where political position was theirs, Yao and Shun transmitted their full realization of the heart-mind in the blessings of universal harmony and influence that moved the people like the wind; where the Way was his, the Master, Confucius, embodied his full realization of the heart-mind in the achievement of editing and transmitting the classics and bequeathing enduring models. Thus it is said: “Those who obtain a favorable allotment of fate [?] stand above; those who obtain an adverse allotment stand below.” The transforming influence of the Way knows no bounds; the sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
不虛生大造生成之功用其賴此以成能乎天
地生人之心至是亦甚慊矣雖然心者天之理
也無心則天矣聖人之心與天合一其次未至
於聖者亦求盡心而已本其靜而養之之謂豫
研其幾而察之之謂精持其心而守之之謂一
而又集義以存之知言養氣以培植之勿忘勿
助以默成之則聖人先得我心之同而吾又先
得聖心之同矣奈何性晦道裂曲學淫詞籍籍
然起贅疣天地幻妄吾心防决瀾倒害如洪水
===
非孟子公言排斥不遺餘力則聖人之聖取諸
人心之同然者又孰得而知之哉說者以為孟
軻功不在禹下蓋謂此也
表
擬宋賜直講孫復五品服謝表〔慶曆四年〕
陳道基
同考試官教諭馮批用事造語俱精練不凡
殆工於四六者
同考試官學正龍批表語渾厚且有警策與
punctuated:
不虛生，大造生成之功用，其賴此以成能乎？天地生人之心，至是亦甚慊矣。雖然，心者天之理也，無心則天矣。聖人之心與天合一，其次未至於聖者，亦求盡心而已。本其靜而養之之謂豫，研其幾而察之之謂精，持其心而守之之謂一。而又集義以存之，知言養氣以培植之，勿忘勿助以默成之，則聖人先得我心之同，而吾又先得聖心之同矣。奈何性晦道裂，曲學淫詞籍籍然起，贅疣天地，幻妄吾心，防决瀾倒，害如洪水。非孟子公言排斥、不遺餘力，則聖人之聖，取諸人心之同然者，又孰得而知之哉？說者以為孟軻功不在禹下，蓋謂此也。

表
擬宋賜直講孫復五品服謝表〔慶曆四年〕
陳道基

translation_en:
… do not come into being in vain. Does not the generative and nurturing operation of the great creative power depend on this to fulfill its capacity? The intention of Heaven and Earth in giving birth to human beings is, at this point, amply satisfied. Nevertheless, the heart is Heaven’s principle; to be without a deliberate mind is to be Heaven itself. The sage’s heart is united with Heaven. Those below this level, who have not yet attained sagehood, likewise need only seek to realize their hearts fully. To nourish the heart on the basis of its stillness is called preparedness; to examine its incipient movements closely is called refinement; to hold fast to the heart and preserve it is called singleness. Further, one preserves it by accumulating righteousness, cultivates it by understanding words and nourishing vital energy, and brings it silently to fulfillment by neither forgetting it nor trying to force its growth. Then the sage has apprehended before me what our hearts share, and I in turn apprehend in advance what I share with the sage’s heart. Yet how has human nature become obscured and the Way fragmented? Distorted learning and excessive rhetoric arise in noisy profusion, becoming excrescences upon Heaven and Earth and deluding our hearts. The embankments burst and the waves pour forth, causing harm like a great flood. Had Mencius not openly denounced and rejected these things, sparing no effort, who could have known that what makes a sage a sage is drawn from what human hearts alike affirm? Those who say that Meng Ke’s achievement was no less than Yu’s presumably mean this.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
場中只具謝體者不同矣
考試官敎諭趙批寓忠悃於陳謝之中得
宋表體
考試官學正寇批駢麗中寫出忠愛之意
可嘉
慶曆四年某月某日國子監直講臣孫復
伏蒙
聖恩賜以五品服者
帝德中虛式廣論心之益
===
皇恩下賚爰推同體之仁仰承衣被之自
天俯愧服庥之無地光榮罕儷踴躍奚勝臣誠
惶誠恐稽首頓首竊以君臣道合若股肱
心膂以相資上下志同如黼黻玄黃而共
濟煥天章以成帝服備物彩以肅臣工司
服詔於司勳儀禮謹有功之報玄袞昭乎
玄德周王隆丕享之誠蓋天命所存而等
威之攸辨寔王章是正而頒賚之有經苟
以加于無良疇足稱乎作勸自羔羊之委
punctuated:
場中只具謝體者不同矣。
考試官敎諭趙批：寓忠悃於陳謝之中，得宋表體。
考試官學正寇批：駢麗中寫出忠愛之意，可嘉。
慶曆四年某月某日，國子監直講臣孫復，伏蒙聖恩賜以五品服者。
帝德中虛，式廣論心之益；皇恩下賚，爰推同體之仁。仰承衣被之自天，俯愧服庥之無地。光榮罕儷，踴躍奚勝！臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以君臣道合，若股肱心膂以相資；上下志同，如黼黻玄黃而共濟。煥天章以成帝服，備物彩以肅臣工。司服詔於司勳，儀禮謹有功之報；玄袞昭乎玄德，周王隆丕享之誠。蓋天命所存，而等威之攸辨；寔王章是正，而頒賚之有經。苟以加于無良，疇足稱乎作勸？自羔羊之委

…differs from those in the examination hall that merely observe the form of a thanksgiving memorial.

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: Within his expression of thanks he conveys heartfelt loyalty, capturing the style of Song memorials.

Examiner Kou, School Director, comments: Amid the elegance of the parallel prose, he expresses loyalty and devotion. This is commendable.

On a certain day of a certain month in the fourth year of Qingli [1044], your servant Sun Fu, Lecturer in the Directorate of Education, humbly received the imperial favor of robes of the fifth rank.

Your imperial virtue is receptive, thereby extending the benefits of heartfelt discussion; your imperial grace bestows gifts upon those below, thus spreading the benevolence that regards ruler and ministers as one body. Looking upward, I receive clothing bestowed from Heaven; looking downward, I am ashamed to find no ground on which I deserve such favor. This glory has few equals; how could I contain my elation! Your servant, in utmost awe and fear, bows his head to the ground and kowtows.

I humbly consider that when ruler and ministers are united in the Way, they sustain one another like limbs, heart, and backbone; when superiors and subordinates share one purpose, they work together like the axe patterns, paired angular patterns, and black and yellow colors of ceremonial robes. Resplendent celestial patterns complete the emperor’s robes; the full array of colors and emblems lends solemnity to his ministers. The Master of the Wardrobe gives instructions to the Director of Merit: ritual observances carefully provide recompense for achievement. The dark dragon robe makes manifest profound virtue: the king of Zhou displays his sincerity through lavish bestowal. These are where Heaven’s mandate resides and distinctions of rank and dignity are made clear. Truly, royal regulations are thereby set right, and the distribution of gifts follows established rules. If such gifts were bestowed upon the unworthy, how could they serve to encourage merit? Since the composed bearing celebrated in “The Lamb’s Fur”…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
蛇旣邈而梁鵜之濡翼斯張漢高衣解淮
陰武功粗定孝宣寵加黃覇吏治用登賜
三公而去檐帷猶寓禮賢之餼歷四時而
稱仕宦莫逃曠位之譏奪錦龍門燕豫終
乖於雅道賜衣虎觀誇恩何補於人文是
非彰德於身豈曰祇承于帝玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
恭己守文
凝神體道
===
經天緯地淵微肇尚絅之
聖修
玉色金聲英美發黃中之峻德服靡厭乎三
澣儉以永圖武不試於五兵治綿保大匪
頒有式禮嚴在笥之將職授非宜法信終
朝之褫篤緇衣之好賢雋彙征嘉赤舄之
忠疑丞協輔謂仲尼乃斯道宗祖而太學
寔王化所關爰修釋菜之上儀迺幸辟雍
之重地橋門觀聽信三王四代之維師爼
punctuated:
蛇旣邈，而梁鵜之濡翼斯張。漢高衣解淮陰，武功粗定；孝宣寵加黃覇，吏治用登。賜三公而去檐帷，猶寓禮賢之餼；歷四時而稱仕宦，莫逃曠位之譏。奪錦龍門，燕豫終乖於雅道；賜衣虎觀，誇恩何補於人文？是非彰德於身，豈曰祇承于帝？
玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，恭己守文，凝神體道。經天緯地，淵微肇尚絅之聖修；玉色金聲，英美發黃中之峻德。服靡厭乎三澣，儉以永圖；武不試於五兵，治綿保大。匪頒有式，禮嚴在笥之將；職授非宜，法信終朝之褫。篤緇衣之好，賢雋彙征；嘉赤舄之忠，疑丞協輔。謂仲尼乃斯道宗祖，而太學寔王化所關。爰修釋菜之上儀，迺幸辟雍之重地。橋門觀聽，信三王四代之維師；爼
translation_en:
…the unhurried dignity of old has long receded, while the spectacle of the pelican wetting its wings upon the fish-weir has become prevalent. Emperor Gao of Han took off his own robe to clothe the Marquis of Huaiyin, and military success was largely secured; Emperor Xiaoxuan bestowed favor upon Huang Ba, and civil administration thereby improved. When robes were bestowed upon the Three Dukes and their carriage curtains removed, the gifts still expressed respect for worthy men. Yet those who called themselves officeholders through all four seasons could not escape criticism for neglecting their duties. Winning the brocade at Longmen was festive amusement that ultimately departed from the proper Way; bestowing robes at the Tiger Observatory merely flaunted favor—what did it contribute to cultural refinement? Such acts did not display virtue in the person: how could they be called reverent service to the Lord on High?
Now, however, we have humbly encountered Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇], who reverently orders his own conduct and preserves established institutions, concentrating his spirit upon embodying the Way. Ordering Heaven and Earth, your profound and subtle sagely cultivation begins with concealing brilliance beneath a plain outer garment. With a countenance like jade and a voice like bronze, your radiant excellence expresses the lofty virtue of inner centrality, symbolized by yellow. You do not disdain garments washed three times, but plan for the enduring future through frugality. Your martial power is not put to the test with the five weapons; your governance perpetuates the preservation of greatness. Distributions of gifts follow prescribed forms [?], and ritual strictly governs the conferral of robes kept in their chests. When an office is improperly bestowed, the law ensures that its insignia may be stripped away before the morning is over. Deepening the love of worthy men expressed in “The Black Robe,” you draw talented men forward together; honoring the loyalty symbolized by the red ceremonial shoes, you receive the united assistance of your vice preceptors and vice assistants.
You hold that Zhongni is the ancestral master of this Way and that the Imperial University is indeed central to kingly moral transformation. Thus you performed the exalted rite of presenting vegetable offerings and visited the august precincts of the Biyong. Those gathered at its encircling gates to see and hear truly beheld a teacher worthy of the Three Kings and the Four Dynasties. The sacrificial stands…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
豆輝煌昭千聖萬賢之一道似此斯文之
幸慶洽儒流豈意衰陋之軀特承
寵賚竊念臣復學未通方志惟信古以聖人
之心不可復見著春秋尊王發微以君子
之節在有不爲居泰山安貧俟命自分
明時之求逸不圖
休命之荐臨石介颺言本出門牆師友之義
輔臣聯薦深慚道德經術之褒濫竽講筵
厠員胄學豈有康侯之望特紆晉錫之蕃
===
使後大夫載叨緋服今趨
禁闥乃佩銀魚敢云儒者之榮竊忝縉紳之
盛臣敢不益堅晚節自勵初心服美而思
曝就
日望雲之悃佩華而玩達潜淵在渚之機啓
乃心以沃心闡一德以輔德奉謀謨而補
衮用輸襪線之能陳仁義以彌縫上徹
宸旒之聽伏願
滋休純嘏
punctuated: 豆輝煌，昭千聖萬賢之一道。似此斯文之幸，慶洽儒流。豈意衰陋之軀，特承寵賚！竊念臣復，學未通方，志惟信古。以聖人之心不可復見，著春秋尊王發微；以君子之節在有不爲，居泰山安貧俟命。自分明時之求逸，不圖休命之荐臨。石介颺言，本出門牆師友之義；輔臣聯薦，深慚道德經術之褒。濫竽講筵，厠員胄學，豈有康侯之望，特紆晉錫之蕃。使後大夫，載叨緋服；今趨禁闥，乃佩銀魚。敢云儒者之榮，竊忝縉紳之盛。臣敢不益堅晚節，自勵初心！服美而思曝，就日望雲之悃；佩華而玩達，潜淵在渚之機。啓乃心以沃心，闡一德以輔德。奉謀謨而補衮，用輸襪線之能；陳仁義以彌縫，上徹宸旒之聽。伏願滋休純嘏……
translation_en:
…the sacrificial vessels shine, manifesting the single Way shared by the myriad sages and worthies. Such good fortune for our cultural tradition brings rejoicing throughout the ranks of scholars. Who could have imagined that this aged and unworthy person would receive Your Majesty’s special gifts?

I humbly reflect that I, your servant Fu, have not attained comprehensive learning; my aspiration has been simply to trust in antiquity. Since the sage’s mind could no longer be seen directly, I wrote on the Spring and Autumn Annals, honoring royal authority and bringing subtle meanings to light. Since a gentleman’s integrity lies in refusing certain actions, I dwelt on Mount Tai, content in poverty and awaiting Heaven’s mandate. I considered myself destined to seek retirement in this enlightened age, never expecting your gracious commands to arrive repeatedly. Shi Jie’s outspoken praise arose from the bonds between teacher and friend within my school; the joint recommendations of your chief ministers leave me deeply ashamed of their praise for my moral character and classical learning. Unworthily filling a place at the imperial lectures and serving among the instructors of the imperial students, how could I aspire to the standing of the Marquis of Kang? Yet I have received lavish gifts like those described in the Book of Changes’ hexagram Jin, “Advancement.”

[The phrase concerning service and a grand master is doubtful: ?]; I again received the unmerited favor of a crimson robe. Now, approaching the palace gates, I wear a silver fish insignia. Dare I call this an honor to scholars? I merely occupy, unworthily, a place in the splendid company of officials. How could I fail to strengthen my integrity in my later years and renew my original resolve? Wearing this fine robe, I think of offering the warmth of the sun, with the sincerity of one who draws near the sun and gazes toward the clouds. Wearing this splendid ornament, I ponder advancement [?] and the timely choice between remaining hidden in the depths and appearing by the shoals. I shall open my heart to enrich Your Majesty’s heart and expound undivided virtue to assist Your Majesty’s virtue. Offering plans and counsel to mend the imperial robes—that is, to remedy shortcomings in government—I shall contribute my slender ability, like thread for stockings. Expounding benevolence and righteousness to make good deficiencies, I shall strive to reach Your Majesty’s hearing behind the pendants of the imperial crown. I humbly wish that Your Majesty may increase in felicity and abundant blessings…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
典學緝熈
挈綱領以整齊萬方
美黼冕而懷柔羣祀
恩弘挾纊小民毋曰怨咨
化廣素絲有官皆以安吉斯民樂樂利利均
荷煖衣之歡惟
皇子子孫孫丕振垂裳之治臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第參塲
策
第一問
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批我
皇上君臣同遊上之媲美
punctuated:
典學緝熈，挈綱領以整齊萬方，美黼冕而懷柔羣祀。恩弘挾纊，小民毋曰怨咨；化廣素絲，有官皆以安吉。斯民樂樂利利，均荷煖衣之歡；惟皇子子孫孫，丕振垂裳之治。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第參塲
策
第一問
鄭元韶
同考試官教諭蔣批：「我皇上君臣同遊上之媲美
translation_en:
…may Your Majesty devote yourself to learning and extend its brilliance, grasp the guiding principles to bring order to all regions, and adorn the ceremonial robes and crown to conciliate the spirits receiving sacrifice. May your expansive grace warm the people like padded silk, so that the common people voice no resentment; may your transforming influence spread the purity symbolized by white silk, so that all officials enjoy peace and good fortune. May these people delight in their pleasures and profit from their gains, sharing alike in the joy of warm clothing; and may your imperial sons and grandsons greatly advance the effortless rule symbolized by letting the robes hang down. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the Sage, cannot contain his fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zheng Yuanshao

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖遠之超邁唐虞子能一一敷揚使天下傳而誦之是必涵泳
聖化久矣可以科目士盡子哉
同考試官教諭黎批是篇氣昌詞偉志遠謀恭
聖天子中興之治所以望於臣下者不在是哉
考試官教諭趙批歷叙唐虞賡歌之盛而
聖祖
皇上實遠紹之此作能道其實且厚望焉是堯舜吾
君之志也得士如此良以自慶矣
考試官學正寇批君臣同遊之盛夫人能
===
言之至於治道之所由成則鮮克知者子能及此
可以為天下士矣
世之隆也其運之相乘乎治之興也其道
之相成乎蓋機會之相乘者運也而世之
隆汚繫之矣上下之相成者道也而治之
興替繫之矣夫惟乘間世之運則上下之
道不期而自合夫惟恊相成之道則雍熈
之化不戒而自孚此有虞之風所以獨盛
於前我
punctuated:
聖祖，遠之超邁唐虞。子能一一敷揚，使天下傳而誦之，是必涵泳聖化久矣，可以科目士盡子哉？

同考試官教諭黎批：是篇氣昌詞偉，志遠謀恭。聖天子中興之治，所以望於臣下者，不在是哉？

考試官教諭趙批：歷叙唐虞賡歌之盛，而聖祖、皇上實遠紹之。此作能道其實，且厚望焉，是堯舜吾君之志也。得士如此，良以自慶矣。

考試官學正寇批：君臣同遊之盛，夫人能言之；至於治道之所由成，則鮮克知者。子能及此，可以為天下士矣。

世之隆也，其運之相乘乎？治之興也，其道之相成乎？蓋機會之相乘者，運也，而世之隆汚繫之矣；上下之相成者，道也，而治之興替繫之矣。夫惟乘間世之運，則上下之道不期而自合；夫惟恊相成之道，則雍熈之化不戒而自孚。此有虞之風所以獨盛於前，我
translation_en:
…the sagely founder and, reaching farther back, surpass Tang and Yu. You have expounded each point, enabling all under Heaven to transmit and recite it. Surely you have long steeped yourself in the sage ruler’s transforming influence. Could the designation “examination scholar” encompass all that you are?

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: This essay has abundant vigor and magnificent diction, far-reaching aspirations and reverent counsels. Is this not what the sage Son of Heaven expects of his subjects in his work of restoring flourishing government?

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The essay recounts in sequence the splendor of the responsive songs of ruler and ministers under Tang and Yu; the sagely founder and His Majesty have indeed continued that distant legacy. This composition articulates the reality of this achievement and also expresses lofty expectations. It embodies the aspiration to make our ruler a Yao or Shun. To have found such a scholar is truly cause for self-congratulation.

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: Anyone can speak of the splendor of ruler and ministers sharing their pleasures. Few, however, understand how the Way of government is brought to fulfillment. Since you can reach this understanding, you may be counted a scholar of all under Heaven.

When an age flourishes, is it because its favorable circumstances build upon one another? When good government arises, is it because its guiding principles bring one another to fulfillment? What consists in opportunities building upon one another is the working of fortune; upon it depend the flourishing or decline of an age. What consists in those above and below bringing one another to fulfillment is the Way; upon it depend the rise or fall of good government. Only by taking advantage of a fortune rarely encountered in successive ages do the ways of those above and below come together of themselves, without prior arrangement. Only by harmonizing the Way of mutual fulfillment does the transforming influence of harmony and prosperity win trust of itself, without admonition. This is why the influence of Yu’s rule flourished uniquely in former times, and why our …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
祖宗
聖皇所以嗣響於今而非漢唐以下所得彷彿
其萬一也執事策諸生而欲鋪張揚厲以
鳴
國家之盛顧愚何足以知之蓋嘗讀易而得
君臣相與之道矣上天下澤曰履孔子傳
之曰君子以辨上下定民志而其傳履之
彖則曰履帝位而不疚光明也乾下坤上
曰泰孔子傳之曰后以裁成天地之道輔
===
相天地之宜以左右民而其傳泰之彖則
曰天地交而萬物通也上下交而其志同
也蓋上下之分不定無以示光明不疚之
履而上下之志不交又何以成裁成輔相
之治哉粤昔唐虞二帝中天而興應運以
生廣四聰於畢達孚庶尹於允諧臣鄰弼
直藹都俞吁咈之風明良遭逢慶元首股
肱之盛然勅天時幾之儆不忘於喜起賡
歌之中蓋運之相乘至有虞而特隆故道
punctuated: 祖宗、聖皇所以嗣響於今，而非漢唐以下所得彷彿其萬一也。執事策諸生，而欲鋪張揚厲，以鳴國家之盛，顧愚何足以知之？蓋嘗讀《易》而得君臣相與之道矣。上天下澤曰履，孔子傳之曰：「君子以辨上下，定民志。」而其傳履之彖則曰：「履帝位而不疚，光明也。」乾下坤上曰泰，孔子傳之曰：「后以裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」而其傳泰之彖則曰：「天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。」蓋上下之分不定，無以示光明不疚之履；而上下之志不交，又何以成裁成輔相之治哉？粤昔唐虞二帝，中天而興，應運以生，廣四聰於畢達，孚庶尹於允諧，臣鄰弼直，藹都俞吁咈之風；明良遭逢，慶元首股肱之盛。然勅天時幾之儆，不忘於喜起賡歌之中。蓋運之相乘，至有虞而特隆，故道
translation_en:
…ancestors and sagely emperors have carried on its resonance into the present; those of the Han and Tang and subsequent ages could not approximate even one ten-thousandth of it. You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question to us students, wishing us to expound and extol the flourishing state of the dynasty. Yet how could someone as ignorant as I adequately understand it? I have, however, read the Book of Changes and gained some understanding of the way ruler and ministers should associate with one another.

Heaven above and the lake below constitute Lü, “Treading.” Confucius comments: “The noble man thereby distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people's aspirations.” His Commentary on the Judgment of Lü says: “He treads the imperial seat without fault: this is luminous clarity.” Qian below and Kun above constitute Tai, “Peace.” Confucius comments: “The sovereign thereby regulates and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting to Heaven and Earth, and thus guides and supports the people.” His Commentary on the Judgment of Tai says: “Heaven and Earth interact, and the myriad things communicate freely; those above and those below interact, and their purposes are one.” Unless the distinctions between those above and those below are settled, there is no means of displaying conduct that is luminous and free from fault. Yet unless their purposes communicate, how can they achieve a government that regulates, completes, and assists the work of Heaven and Earth?

Long ago, the two emperors Yao and Shun arose like the sun at the zenith, born in response to their destined age. They extended their hearing in all four directions until everything reached them, and inspired trust among the many officials until genuine harmony prevailed. Ministers close to the throne assisted and corrected them, and an atmosphere of candid assent and dissent flourished. Enlightened rulers and worthy ministers encountered one another, celebrating the flourishing partnership of sovereign and ministers, like a head and its limbs. Yet amid their joyous songs of mutual encouragement, sung in response to one another, they did not forget the admonitions to attend reverently to Heaven and to the first stirrings of affairs. The succession of favorable circumstances reached a particular height under Shun; therefore the Way…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之相成至有虞而特著也嗣是如湯之於
伊尹則一德之咸有也高宗之於傳說則
麴糵鹽梅之交修也周室之盛君歌鹿鳴
以燕其臣臣歌天保以答其君而卷阿之
詩則召公從遊之作也然周行之求遂歌
之矢猶有虞廷時幾之意焉要皆運之會
也道之成也漢唐以還風斯下矣洛陽宴
會讓三傑之不如漢祖所以興炎劉之業
丹霄侍從諒魏徵之疎慢唐宗所以成貞
===
觀之治若夫杯酒猜疑之釋藝祖之優功
臣也賞花釣魚之賦仁宗之宴近僚也要
其君臣之遇亦足以稱一時之盛然宴遊
之儀雖侈飭戒之實或疎蓋其運寢微故
其道寢降仰窺賡歌之風則旣遠矣彼善
於此其惟丹霄之宴猶庶幾存交儆之遺
乎君子未可以停仆一事病之也宋祚旣
移胡元竊僭天運積否而開泰人心厭亂
而思治此其時矣洪惟我
punctuated: 之相成，至有虞而特著也。嗣是，如湯之於伊尹，則一德之咸有也；高宗之於傳說，則麴糵鹽梅之交修也。周室之盛，君歌《鹿鳴》以燕其臣，臣歌《天保》以答其君，而《卷阿》之詩，則召公從遊之作也。然周行之求、遂歌之矢，猶有虞廷時幾之意焉。要皆運之會也，道之成也。漢唐以還，風斯下矣。洛陽宴會，讓三傑之不如，漢祖所以興炎劉之業；丹霄侍從，諒魏徵之疎慢，唐宗所以成貞觀之治。若夫杯酒猜疑之釋，藝祖之優功臣也；賞花釣魚之賦，仁宗之宴近僚也。要其君臣之遇，亦足以稱一時之盛。然宴遊之儀雖侈，飭戒之實或疎，蓋其運寢微，故其道寢降。仰窺賡歌之風，則旣遠矣。彼善於此，其惟丹霄之宴，猶庶幾存交儆之遺乎！君子未可以停仆一事病之也。宋祚旣移，胡元竊僭，天運積否而開泰，人心厭亂而思治，此其時矣。洪惟我
translation_en:
…the mutual completion of the Way became especially manifest under the ruler of Yu, Shun. Thereafter, Tang and Yi Yin both possessed a single virtue; Gaozong and Fu Yue mutually cultivated one another, like yeast and ferment in brewing, or salt and plums in seasoning. In the flourishing days of the Zhou house, the ruler sang “Deer Calling” to feast his ministers, and the ministers sang “Heaven Protects” in response to their ruler. The poem “Winding Hills” was composed by the Duke of Shao while accompanying the king on an excursion. Yet its search for men fit for the ranks of office and its presentation of song [?] still conveyed the spirit of vigilance over the incipient workings of affairs at Shun’s court. All these, in essence, were convergences of favorable destiny and fulfillments of the Way.

From the Han and Tang onward, this ethos declined. At the banquet in Luoyang, the Han founder acknowledged that he fell short of his three outstanding ministers: this was how he established the enterprise of the Liu house, whose dynastic virtue was Fire. At Danxiao, the Tang emperor tolerated Wei Zheng’s casual disregard for ceremony while attending him: this was how he achieved the good government of the Zhenguan reign. As for dispelling suspicion over cups of wine, this was the Song founder’s generous treatment of his meritorious ministers; composing verses while viewing flowers and fishing was Renzong’s way of feasting his close officials. The harmonious encounters of these rulers and ministers were indeed sufficient to be called glories of their respective times. Yet although their banquets and excursions were lavish in ceremony, the substance of admonition and warning was sometimes neglected. As their dynastic fortunes gradually weakened, so their practice of the Way gradually declined. Looking back toward the ethos of exchanging songs at Shun’s court, they were already far removed from it. If one was better than another, was it not the banquet at Danxiao alone that perhaps retained something of the legacy of mutual admonition? A gentleman should not condemn the emperor merely for the single incident of the monument’s demolition [?].

Once the Song’s mandate had passed away, the barbarian Yuan usurped the throne. Heaven’s course, after accumulated obstruction, opened into prosperity; people’s hearts, weary of disorder, longed for good government. This was precisely the moment. Profoundly do we reflect upon our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝挺生淮甸肇創函夏扶綱常於再
造廓宇宙於重新是蓋乘撥亂反正之運
啟旋乾轉坤之業劉基天授之說已識
帝王之有真矣一時明良之盛振古罕儷
大誥三篇首冠以君臣同遊之言其虞廷賡歌
之遺響乎拾失摶過不忘上下交修之念
其勅天時幾之微意乎觀其於儒臣宋濂
也或閱江有樓而
特令為之記以紀其事非但侈登臨之勝蓋欲
===
藉遊覽以動保治之思也或賜飲至醉而
親為之賦又
命侍臣皆為醉學士歌非徒示優老之恩蓋欲
使後世知同遊之樂也寓交儆之意於豫
逸之中篤不忘之懷於晉接之頃他如
召見賜坐之歡下逮不一經史時事之訪聽
納惟虛豈非我
聖祖以相成之道開統天之業以為貽謀燕翼
之圖耶
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝挺生淮甸，肇創函夏，扶綱常於再造，廓宇宙於重新。是蓋乘撥亂反正之運，啟旋乾轉坤之業。劉基天授之說，已識帝王之有真矣。一時明良之盛，振古罕儷。《大誥》三篇，首冠以君臣同遊之言，其虞廷賡歌之遺響乎？拾失摶過，不忘上下交修之念，其勅天時幾之微意乎？

觀其於儒臣宋濂也，或閱江有樓，而特令為之記以紀其事，非但侈登臨之勝，蓋欲藉遊覽以動保治之思也。或賜飲至醉，而親為之賦，又命侍臣皆為《醉學士歌》，非徒示優老之恩，蓋欲使後世知同遊之樂也。寓交儆之意於豫逸之中，篤不忘之懷於晉接之頃。他如召見賜坐之歡，下逮不一；經史時事之訪，聽納惟虛。豈非我聖祖以相成之道，開統天之業，以為貽謀燕翼之圖耶？
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, arose preeminent in the Huai region and founded anew the realm of China, restoring the cardinal relationships and constant moral principles as he rebuilt it, and bringing order to the world as he renewed it. He thus seized the moment for quelling disorder and restoring rightful rule, inaugurating an enterprise that turned Heaven and Earth around. Liu Ji’s words about authority bestowed by Heaven had already recognized that there is a true emperor. The flourishing partnership of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers at that time had few equals since antiquity. The three parts of the Great Pronouncements (Da gao) open with words about ruler and ministers enjoying outings together. Was this not an echo of the songs exchanged at Shun’s court? In remedying omissions and correcting faults [?], they never forgot that superior and subordinate should cultivate one another. Was this not the subtle intent of reverently heeding Heaven and attending to the incipient signs of affairs?

Consider his treatment of the Confucian minister Song Lian. When a tower was built for viewing the river, he specially commanded Song to compose an account recording the occasion. This was not merely to celebrate the splendid prospect from its heights; he wished to use sightseeing to stir reflection on preserving good government. On another occasion, he bestowed drink upon Song until he was drunk and personally composed a rhapsody for him. He also commanded all the attendant ministers to compose a Song of the Drunken Academician. This was not merely a display of gracious favor toward an elder; he wished later generations to know the joy of ruler and ministers taking their pleasure together. Amid leisure and ease, he conveyed the intent of mutual admonition; in granting audiences, he deepened his enduring affection. Other pleasures, such as being summoned to an audience and granted a seat, were extended to his subordinates on many occasions. When consulting them about the classics, histories, and current affairs, he listened and accepted their counsel with an open mind. Was this not our sagely founding emperor’s way of establishing his Heaven-governed enterprise through mutual support between ruler and ministers, thereby laying plans to bequeath security and assistance to his descendants?

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承運祚寢隆上下一體相得益章如幾
密之商夜分乃退則
成祖之於七臣也協心之戒
誥詞親增則
仁廟之於五臣也或推心置腹而從容咨訪於
燕見之時或
禁苑賜遊而商議可否於裁决之際則
宣廟
英廟之遇臣猶可想見也如楊士奇李賢諸臣
===
之所紀錄傳播海宇歷歷若覩此其道之
相成而治日以興有由然矣賡歌卷阿之
風其再振乎肆我
皇上聖神天縱嗣纂丕圖宣
累葉之重光冠百王而獨盛是蓋當世道一新
之會適禮樂百年之期
中興全盛之運夫固天啟於
今日矣一時弼理之臣翕然嚮應
萬幾之暇或
punctuated:
列聖相承，運祚寢隆，上下一體，相得益章。如幾密之商，夜分乃退，則成祖之於七臣也；協心之戒，誥詞親增，則仁廟之於五臣也。或推心置腹，而從容咨訪於燕見之時；或禁苑賜遊，而商議可否於裁决之際，則宣廟、英廟之遇臣，猶可想見也。如楊士奇、李賢諸臣之所紀錄，傳播海宇，歷歷若覩。此其道之相成，而治日以興，有由然矣。賡歌、《卷阿》之風，其再振乎？

肆我皇上，聖神天縱，嗣纂丕圖，宣累葉之重光，冠百王而獨盛。是蓋當世道一新之會，適禮樂百年之期，中興全盛之運，夫固天啟於今日矣。一時弼理之臣，翕然嚮應，萬幾之暇，或
translation_en:
Successive sage emperors inherited the throne; the dynasty’s fortunes grew ever more splendid. Sovereign and ministers formed one body, and their mutual accord became increasingly manifest. When confidential affairs were discussed and the ministers withdrew only at midnight, such was Chengzu’s treatment of his seven ministers. When words of admonition to act with one heart were personally added to an imperial proclamation, such was Renzong’s treatment of his five ministers. Sometimes the emperor opened his heart and consulted them at leisure during informal audiences; sometimes he granted them excursions in the imperial park and discussed the merits of proposed actions when making decisions. Thus we can still picture how Xuanzong and Yingzong treated their ministers. The accounts recorded by such ministers as Yang Shiqi and Li Xian circulated throughout the realm, so vivid that one seems to witness these events. There was indeed a reason why sovereign and ministers thus complemented one another in the Way and good government flourished day by day. Had the spirit of the exchanged songs of ruler and ministers, and of “The Winding Mound” (Juan’e), been revived once more?

Now our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom and spiritual insight, has succeeded to the great imperial enterprise. He extends the accumulated radiance of successive generations, surpassing a hundred kings in his peerless glory. This is an occasion when the order of the age is wholly renewed, coinciding with the completion of a century of rites and music. Heaven has surely inaugurated today an era of resurgent and consummate prosperity. The ministers assisting his governance respond in unanimous accord. In moments of respite from the myriad affairs of state, sometimes …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
召見便殿不厭密勿之咨或
賜遊西苑特陪
翠華之御
親灑宸翰
頒賜諸臣如
穀祗蠶壇之賦曰農桑爲先曰以示無逸卽
豳風七月之意也曰
陽春和暢曰于樂康年卽對時育物之仁也
同遊樂府之作曰薰風解愠但願民康卽虞
===
舜南風之奏也曰
但得甘霖降欣然慰老農卽商湯桑林之思
也撫盈成亨嘉之運猶切忠良夾持之儆
當逸暇遊觀之時不忘敬承
皇天之念
奎章睿藻昭回雲漢
寶軸瑤函輝映典謨非草茅所能盡述豈非我
皇上以相成之道弘
烈祖之猷而追虞廷周室之盛耶漢唐宋之君
punctuated: 召見便殿，不厭密勿之咨；或賜遊西苑，特陪翠華之御。親灑宸翰，頒賜諸臣。如《穀祗蠶壇之賦》，曰「農桑爲先」，曰「以示無逸」，卽《豳風》《七月》之意也；曰「陽春和暢」，曰「于樂康年」，卽對時育物之仁也。《同遊樂府》之作，曰「薰風解愠，但願民康」，卽虞舜《南風》之奏也；曰「但得甘霖降，欣然慰老農」，卽商湯桑林之思也。撫盈成亨嘉之運，猶切忠良夾持之儆；當逸暇遊觀之時，不忘敬承皇天之念。奎章睿藻，昭回雲漢；寶軸瑤函，輝映典謨。非草茅所能盡述。豈非我皇上以相成之道弘烈祖之猷，而追虞廷周室之盛耶？漢唐宋之君
translation_en:
…he summons them to audience in an informal palace hall, never tiring of earnest, confidential consultation; at other times he grants them an excursion to the Western Park, specially admitting them to accompany the imperial carriage beneath its kingfisher-feather standards. With his own hand he writes imperial compositions and bestows them upon his ministers. For example, the “Rhapsody on the Grain Spirit and the Silkworm Altar” [?] says, “Farming and sericulture come first,” and “To demonstrate freedom from idleness.” These express the meaning of “The Seventh Month” in the “Airs of Bin” in the Book of Odes. Its words, “The spring sunshine is mild and pleasant,” and “Oh, rejoice in a year of well-being,” express the benevolence that nurtures all things in accordance with the seasons. The composition “Music Bureau Verse on an Excursion Together” says, “The balmy wind dispels resentment; I wish only for the people’s well-being.” This is the import of Shun of Yu’s performance of “The South Wind.” Its words, “If only sweet rain would fall, gladly would I bring comfort to the aged farmers,” express the concern of Tang of Shang at the Mulberry Grove.

Presiding over an age of plenitude, accomplishment, and flourishing prosperity, he remains keenly mindful of the admonition to have loyal and worthy men supporting him on either side. Amid leisure and sightseeing, he does not forget reverently to serve August Heaven. His imperial writings and sagacious compositions shine through the Milky Way; their precious scrolls and jeweled cases rival in splendor the “Canons” and “Counsels” of the Book of Documents. One dwelling among grass and thatch cannot recount them fully. Is this not our Emperor, through the Way of mutual assistance, extending the plans of his illustrious ancestors and emulating the flourishing court of Yu and royal house of Zhou? As for the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
又何足言哉雖然虞之賡歌則曰勅天命
夏之籲俊則曰尊帝商之克即則曰丕釐
耿命周之灼見則曰敬事上帝我
祖宗敬
天之實信圖政親賢之本創業守成之基也我
皇上敬一有箴五箴有註播告臣民之語無非
躬行心得之餘純心者用賢之要恭黙者
交修之幾則夫精神意氣之感雲龍風虎
之從固有不能外焉者經緯化成之績泰
===
和極治之盛夫豈偶然之故哉執事所謂
至德淵衷
神謨睿思得非有見於是耶若夫益勵謨明弼
諧之忠以為
聖天子奉
天勤民之助以綿億萬年豐亨豫泰之業者則
固
廟堂輔弼者之任也而豈韋布所得與聞哉
第二問
punctuated:
又何足言哉！雖然，虞之賡歌則曰「勅天命」，夏之籲俊則曰「尊帝」，商之克即則曰「丕釐耿命」，周之灼見則曰「敬事上帝」。我祖宗敬天之實，信圖政親賢之本、創業守成之基也。我皇上敬一有箴，五箴有註，播告臣民之語，無非躬行心得之餘。純心者，用賢之要；恭黙者，交修之幾。則夫精神意氣之感、雲龍風虎之從，固有不能外焉者。經緯化成之績、泰和極治之盛，夫豈偶然之故哉！執事所謂「至德淵衷，神謨睿思」，得非有見於是耶？若夫益勵謨明弼諧之忠，以為聖天子奉天勤民之助，以綿億萬年豐亨豫泰之業者，則固廟堂輔弼者之任也，而豈韋布所得與聞哉！

第二問
translation_en:
…how could they merit further mention! Nevertheless, the responsive singing at the court of Yu spoke of “attending reverently to Heaven’s mandate”; Xia’s summoning of outstanding men, of “honoring the Lord on High”; Shang’s attainment of its settled place [?], of “greatly administering the luminous mandate”; and Zhou’s clear discernment, of “reverently serving the Lord on High.” Our imperial ancestors’ actual practice of revering Heaven was indeed the root of their planning government and drawing worthy men close, and the foundation of both founding the dynasty and preserving its achievements. Our Emperor has composed an Admonition on Reverent Unity and supplied commentaries on the Five Admonitions. The words he proclaims to officials and people alike all flow from his personal practice and inward understanding. Purity of heart is essential to employing worthy men; reverent silence is the subtle beginning of mutual cultivation. Thus the sympathetic response of spirit and intention, and the following of clouds after dragons and winds after tigers, necessarily arise within this same principle. Could the achievements of ordering the realm and bringing moral transformation to completion, or the flourishing of supreme harmony and consummate government, possibly be accidental? When you, honored examiner, speak of “supreme virtue and profound inner purpose, divine plans and sagely thought,” is it not because you perceive this?

As for further strengthening the loyal service that offers enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance, thereby helping the sagely Son of Heaven to serve Heaven and labor for the people, and perpetuating for countless millions of years the enterprise of abundance, prosperity, contentment, and peace: this is assuredly the responsibility of the assisting ministers at court. How could a commoner in plain cloth presume to have a part in it!

Second Policy Question

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
丘行義
同考試官教諭費批形容字畫之精而本諸
皇上之心學忠悃未有涯也敬服敬服
同考試官教諭方批歷代字學子旣詳其由
來而末復以
聖天子之心畫遠出羲皇之上是可以
獻矣
考試官教諭趙批備述我
朝正韻謂得字學之正傳而
===
皇上超出千古之見又不專於形象點畫吾之取子豈獨以其文哉
考試官學正寇批大小篆隸之變子能一
一道之又於
宸翰之妙言之懇至是可以觀子之竒矣
聖人其猶天乎甞誦棫樸之詩而知聖人
之書法所由章誦文王之詩而知聖人之
心法所由立棫樸之詩曰倬彼雲漢爲章
於天語天文也而書法於是乎肇其始文
王之詩曰上天之載無聲無臭語天道也
punctuated:
丘行義

同考試官教諭費批：形容字畫之精，而本諸皇上之心學，忠悃未有涯也。敬服！敬服！

同考試官教諭方批：歷代字學，子旣詳其由來，而末復以聖天子之心畫遠出羲皇之上，是可以獻矣。

考試官教諭趙批：備述我朝正韻，謂得字學之正傳，而皇上超出千古之見，又不專於形象點畫。吾之取子，豈獨以其文哉？

考試官學正寇批：大小篆隸之變，子能一一道之；又於宸翰之妙，言之懇至，是可以觀子之竒矣。

聖人其猶天乎？甞誦《棫樸》之詩，而知聖人之書法所由章；誦《文王》之詩，而知聖人之心法所由立。《棫樸》之詩曰：「倬彼雲漢，爲章於天。」語天文也，而書法於是乎肇其始。《文王》之詩曰：「上天之載，無聲無臭。」語天道也，
translation_en:
Qiu Xingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: You describe the refinement of written strokes and ground it in His Majesty’s learning of the mind. Your loyal sincerity knows no bounds. I admire this most respectfully—most respectfully!

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: You have explained in detail the origins and development of the study of writing through successive dynasties. At the end, you further place the sagely Son of Heaven’s writing, the expression of his mind, far above that of Fuxi. This is worthy of presentation to the throne.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: You give a full account of our dynasty’s Correct Rhymes, declaring that it embodies the orthodox transmission of the study of writing. Yet His Majesty’s insight, surpassing that of all past ages, is not confined to forms, dots, and strokes. Would I select you solely for your literary skill?

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: You can explain one by one the transformations of the greater and lesser seal scripts and the clerical script. Moreover, you speak with utmost sincerity of the marvels of the imperial brush. In this one can discern your exceptional gifts.

Is the sage not like Heaven? I have read the ode “The Oak Trees” (Yupu) and thereby understood how the sage’s art of writing becomes manifest; I have read the ode “King Wen” (Wen Wang) and thereby understood how the sage’s method of cultivating the mind is established. The ode “The Oak Trees” says: “Bright is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in Heaven.” This speaks of Heaven’s patterns, and here the art of writing has its beginning. The ode “King Wen” says: “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” This speaks of the Way of Heaven …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
而心法於是乎啓其原惟聖人靜與天爲
體而心法之存於中者合天之道故聖人
動與天爲用而書法之形諸外者則天之
文二者體用一原顯微無間此聖人之所
以與天爲一者也知心法則知書法矣知
天則知聖人矣請因明問而敬陳之粤昔
道涵於太始而不能不會於聖人道會於
聖人而不能不闡於卦畫於是伏羲始畫
八卦以通神明之德以類萬物之情故周
===
子曰聖人之精因畫以示然則畫也者固
聖人之所以畫乎其心者也心畫形而字
文立矣自伏羲而神農而黃帝而堯而禹
其心法之傳者本無不同曰龍書曰穗書
曰鳥書曰龜書曰鍾鼎其書法之善者未
甞或異猶風雨露雷之化不同其爲上天
於穆之運者則一也卽其尤盛者而論之
伏羲之後其惟黃帝矣乎蓋黃帝之有六
書也猶伏羲之有八卦也道本於易簡而
punctuated:
而心法於是乎啓其原。惟聖人靜與天爲體，而心法之存於中者合天之道；故聖人動與天爲用，而書法之形諸外者則天之文。二者體用一原，顯微無間，此聖人之所以與天爲一者也。知心法則知書法矣，知天則知聖人矣。請因明問而敬陳之。
粤昔道涵於太始，而不能不會於聖人；道會於聖人，而不能不闡於卦畫。於是伏羲始畫八卦，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情。故周子曰：「聖人之精，因畫以示。」然則畫也者，固聖人之所以畫乎其心者也。心畫形而字文立矣。自伏羲而神農而黃帝而堯而禹，其心法之傳者本無不同；曰龍書，曰穗書，曰鳥書，曰龜書，曰鍾鼎，其書法之善者未甞或異。猶風雨露雷之化不同，其爲上天於穆之運者則一也。卽其尤盛者而論之，伏羲之後，其惟黃帝矣乎！蓋黃帝之有六書也，猶伏羲之有八卦也。道本於易簡而
translation_en:
…and here the teaching of the mind finds its source. In stillness, the sage shares Heaven’s substance, and the teaching of the mind preserved within him accords with Heaven’s Way. Thus, in activity, the sage shares Heaven’s functioning, and his calligraphy, manifested outwardly, takes Heaven’s patterns as its model. In these two, substance and function have a single source, and the manifest and the subtle admit no separation. This is how the sage is one with Heaven. To understand the teaching of the mind is to understand calligraphy; to understand Heaven is to understand the sage. Allow me respectfully to set this forth in response to your illuminating question.
In remotest antiquity, the Way lay within the primordial beginning and necessarily came together in the sages; having come together in the sages, it necessarily found expression in the lines of the trigrams. Thus Fuxi first drew the Eight Trigrams to communicate the potency of the spirits and to classify the true conditions of the myriad things. Hence Master Zhou said: “The sage’s essential understanding is revealed through the drawn lines.” These lines, then, were precisely the means by which the sage depicted his mind. Once these drawings of the mind took form, written characters came into being. From Fuxi through Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Yu, the teaching of the mind they transmitted was fundamentally the same. Whether called dragon script, grain-ear script, bird script, tortoise script, or bell-and-cauldron inscriptions, their excellence in writing never differed. Similarly, although the transformations wrought by wind, rain, dew, and thunder differ, they are one as the workings of Heaven in its profound majesty. If we discuss the most outstanding instance, who after Fuxi could rival the Yellow Emperor? For the Yellow Emperor’s possession of the Six Principles of Writing was like Fuxi’s possession of the Eight Trigrams. The Way is rooted in ease and simplicity, and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
用極乎天地自象形指事會意諧聲轉注
假借之義立而天下之道備矣比其類而
列之許氏發三耦之微順其序而推之鄭
氏闡相承之秘朱子亦曰心性等字理自
流出則六書之義自倉頡撰之非倉頡始
之必其親得於黃帝心法之傳者也故竊
論書法之傳自伏羲而創其始若剖混沌
而開之者也自黃帝而闡其詳若繼開闢
而疆理之者也伏羲其先天矣乎黃帝其
===
後天矣乎嗣有作者不可尚矣慨六書之
變而爲大篆也史籀所述也文字漸備而
書法之本旨寢微周宣之德其衰矣大篆
之變而爲小篆也李斯實紛更之簡便日
趨而書法之漸滅殆盡嬴秦之罪莫贖矣
漢光武頒十札於方國唐太宗賜飛白於
馬周宋太宗勒孝經於碑陰賜吏治於棘
寺書法非不善也然皆務翰墨之工無裨
身心之實或深刻之成性或閨門之多慚
punctuated:
用極乎天地。自象形、指事、會意、諧聲、轉注、假借之義立，而天下之道備矣。比其類而列之，許氏發三耦之微；順其序而推之，鄭氏闡相承之秘。朱子亦曰：「心性等字，理自流出。」則六書之義，自倉頡撰之，非倉頡始之，必其親得於黃帝心法之傳者也。
故竊論書法之傳，自伏羲而創其始，若剖混沌而開之者也；自黃帝而闡其詳，若繼開闢而疆理之者也。伏羲其先天矣乎！黃帝其後天矣乎！嗣有作者，不可尚矣。慨六書之變而爲大篆也，史籀所述也，文字漸備，而書法之本旨寢微，周宣之德其衰矣。大篆之變而爲小篆也，李斯實紛更之，簡便日趨，而書法之漸滅殆盡，嬴秦之罪莫贖矣。
漢光武頒十札於方國，唐太宗賜飛白於馬周，宋太宗勒《孝經》於碑陰，賜《吏治》於棘寺。書法非不善也，然皆務翰墨之工，無裨身心之實：或深刻之成性，或閨門之多慚
translation_en:
…its application extends throughout Heaven and Earth.
