Once the principles of pictographs, indicative characters, compound ideographs, phonetic compounds, mutually explanatory characters, and phonetic loans were established, the Way of all under Heaven was fully embodied. By grouping and arranging their categories, Master Xu disclosed the subtleties of the three pairs; by following their sequence and developing its implications, Master Zheng elucidated the hidden principles of their succession. Master Zhu also said: “In characters such as ‘mind’ and ‘nature,’ principle flows forth of itself.” Thus, although Cangjie compiled the principles of the Six Methods of Writing, he did not originate them. He must have received them personally through the transmission of the Yellow Emperor’s teaching of the mind.
I therefore venture to discuss the transmission of the art of writing as follows. Fuxi established its beginnings, as though cleaving primordial chaos and opening it up. The Yellow Emperor elucidated its particulars, as though following the opening of the cosmos by marking out and ordering its domains. Might Fuxi be said to have preceded Heaven, and the Yellow Emperor to have followed Heaven? Those who subsequently arose to create could not surpass them. Alas, the transformation of the Six Methods into large-seal script was the work of the Grand Scribe Zhou. Written characters gradually became more complete, yet the fundamental purport of the art of writing gradually faded: the virtue of King Xuan of Zhou was surely declining. As for the transformation of large-seal into small-seal script, Li Si was indeed responsible for its sweeping alterations. The pursuit of simplicity and convenience increased daily, while the art of writing gradually vanished almost entirely. The guilt of the Qin house of Ying could not be redeemed.
Emperor Guangwu of Han distributed ten sheets of writing to the regional states; Emperor Taizong of Tang bestowed flying-white calligraphy upon Ma Zhou; Emperor Taizong of Song had the Classic of Filial Piety engraved on the reverse of a stele and bestowed Administration of Officials [?] upon the Court of Judicial Review. Their calligraphy was certainly accomplished. Yet all pursued skill with brush and ink, without contributing to the substantive cultivation of body and mind: in some, harsh severity became ingrained in their nature; others had much to be ashamed of within their households…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
或彝倫之不能無疚則其所謂書法者抑
末也去羲皇之心法益遠矣文固際遇而
興道必得人而盛是非天意有待於
聖祖及我
皇上乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極肇啓洪圖拯華夏於旣
淪而天地定位舉綱常於旣墜而宇宙改
觀故天假
聖祖以洩數百年圖書之蘊當時
===
奎畫之流播者若親撰
大誥之編增光日月
御製
大祀之祝照耀乾坤其
諭之臣民達之
郊廟猶有不能悉覩者書法之妙眞有以同符
前聖矣然
聖心獨得之微猶欲追古文本旨之舊改字韻
踵襲之訛
punctuated: 或彝倫之不能無疚，則其所謂書法者，抑末也，去羲皇之心法益遠矣。文固際遇而興，道必得人而盛，是非天意有待於聖祖及我皇上乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，繼天立極，肇啓洪圖，拯華夏於旣淪而天地定位，舉綱常於旣墜而宇宙改觀。故天假聖祖以洩數百年圖書之蘊。當時奎畫之流播者，若親撰《大誥》之編，增光日月；御製大祀之祝，照耀乾坤。其諭之臣民、達之郊廟，猶有不能悉覩者。書法之妙，眞有以同符前聖矣。然聖心獨得之微，猶欲追古文本旨之舊，改字韻踵襲之訛，
translation_en:
…or they could not remain free of fault in the enduring human relationships. Thus what they called calligraphy was merely a secondary pursuit, ever further removed from the method of the mind of the sovereign Fuxi. Writing indeed flourishes when favorable circumstances arise, and the Way prospers only when it finds the right person. Was this not Heaven’s intention, awaiting the Sagely Progenitor and our present Emperor?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, inaugurating his grand enterprise. He rescued Huaxia from its fallen state, and Heaven and Earth assumed their proper positions; he restored the cardinal bonds and constant virtues after their collapse, and the universe took on a new aspect. Thus Heaven employed the Sagely Progenitor to disclose the riches of charts and writings accumulated over several hundred years. Among the imperial writings circulated at that time, the Great Pronouncements, which he personally composed, added brilliance to the sun and moon; his imperially composed prayers for the great sacrifices illuminated Heaven and Earth. Of the writings through which he instructed officials and commoners and addressed the suburban altars and ancestral temples, there were still some that could not all be seen. The excellence of his calligraphy truly accorded with that of the earlier sages. Yet, through the subtle understanding uniquely attained by his sagely mind, he still wished to recover the original purport of ancient writing and correct errors in characters and rhymes perpetuated through inherited usage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
親命儒臣宋濂等勒成洪武正韻一書其損益
因革之宜一取正於毛晃注釋許慎說文
若攴支毋母之分冬東青清之合是也誠
哉萬世不刊之典有非
大聖人不能作者甞伏讀我
聖祖之訓而有以識其本矣其
諭曾魯者則有曰人君一心治化之本存於中
者無堯舜之心欲施於外者有堯舜之治
不可得也其
===
===
諭宋濂者則有曰人心虛靈乗氣機出入操而
存之爲甚難朕罔敢自暇自逸則我
聖祖之心是即伏羲神農黄帝堯禹之心也豈
惟有同前聖已乎
聖祖書法之妙其本端在於是我
皇上嗣統承休丕揚駿烈天明地察當百年禮
樂之期上乂下安應千載
中興之運故天縱
皇上以昭百八十年貞元之祕即今
punctuated:
親命儒臣宋濂等勒成《洪武正韻》一書，其損益因革之宜，一取正於毛晃注釋、許慎《說文》，若攴支毋母之分、冬東青清之合是也。誠哉，萬世不刊之典，有非大聖人不能作者！甞伏讀我聖祖之訓，而有以識其本矣。其諭曾魯者則有曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，欲施於外者有堯舜之治，不可得也。」其諭宋濂者則有曰：「人心虛靈，乗氣機出入，操而存之爲甚難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」則我聖祖之心，是即伏羲、神農、黄帝、堯、禹之心也，豈惟有同前聖已乎？聖祖書法之妙，其本端在於是。

我皇上嗣統承休，丕揚駿烈，天明地察，當百年禮樂之期；上乂下安，應千載中興之運。故天縱皇上，以昭百八十年貞元之祕。即今
translation_en:
…He personally commanded the Confucian officials Song Lian and others to compile the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun). In determining appropriate additions and deletions, continuities and changes, they took as their standards Mao Huang’s annotations and Xu Shen’s Explanation of Written Characters (Shuowen). Examples include distinguishing 攴 from 支 and 毋 from 母, and combining the rhyme categories 冬 and 東, and 青 and 清. Truly, this is an authoritative work unalterable for ten thousand generations, such as none but a great sage could produce! I have reverently read the instructions of our Sagely Ancestor and thereby come to understand their foundation. In his instructions to Zeng Lu, he said: “The ruler’s mind alone is the foundation of governance and moral transformation. If what he harbors within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes his outward actions to achieve the government of Yao and Shun, this cannot be attained.” In his instructions to Song Lian, he said: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. To hold fast to it and preserve it is exceedingly difficult. I dare not allow myself leisure or ease.” Thus the mind of our Sagely Ancestor was precisely the mind of Fuxi, Shennong, Huangdi, Yao, and Yu. Was it merely that he resembled the former sages? The foundation of our Sagely Ancestor’s marvelous calligraphy lies precisely here.

Our present Emperor has succeeded to the imperial line and inherited its blessings, magnificently advancing its great achievements. His illumination is like Heaven’s, his discernment like Earth’s. He has reached the time when a century of rule brings rites and music to fruition; with order above and peace below, he answers the destiny of a restoration such as comes once in a thousand years. Thus Heaven has endowed our Emperor to reveal the mystery of the passage from completion to renewal across these hundred and eighty years. At this very time…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
宸翰之宣布者若
明堂或問之解奎璧昭文承天父老之
諭江漢生色其勒之
陵寢播之訓告形之咏歌猶有不能盡觀者書
法之妙眞有以匹休
聖祖矣然一日
萬幾之暇校書畫之原考因仍之陋嘗示輔
弼諸臣研正字義其妙道精蘊之微皆本
淵衷獨契
===
神授默成若書宬爲宬吏丸爲圓是也信哉炳
燭丹書糠粃倉史有非
大聖人不能述者嘗伏讀我
皇上敬一之箴而有以測其原矣其言敬有曰
郊則恭誠
廟嚴孝趨肅于
明廷慎於閒居其言一有曰弗參以三弗貳
以二行顧其言終如其始則我
皇上之心是卽
punctuated:
宸翰之宣布者，若《明堂或問》之解，奎璧昭文；承天父老之諭，江漢生色。其勒之陵寢，播之訓告，形之咏歌，猶有不能盡觀者。書法之妙，眞有以匹休聖祖矣。然一日萬幾之暇，校書畫之原，考因仍之陋，嘗示輔弼諸臣研正字義。其妙道精蘊之微，皆本淵衷獨契，神授默成，若書宬爲宬、吏丸爲圓是也。信哉！炳燭丹書，糠粃倉史，有非大聖人不能述者。
嘗伏讀我皇上《敬一》之箴，而有以測其原矣。其言敬，有曰：「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝趨，肅于明廷，慎於閒居。」其言一，有曰：「弗參以三，弗貳以二，行顧其言，終如其始。」則我皇上之心，是卽
translation_en:
…Among the imperial writings that have been promulgated are the explanation of Questions on the Bright Hall, whose literary brilliance shines like the Kui and Bi constellations, and the instruction to the elders of Chengtian, which lends lustre to the Yangzi and Han rivers. Those engraved at the imperial mausoleums, disseminated in admonitions and proclamations, and expressed in songs of praise still cannot all be surveyed. The excellence of His Majesty’s calligraphy truly rivals the glory of the Sagely Progenitor.
Yet, amid the intervals in each day’s myriad affairs, His Majesty examines the origins of written forms and investigates defects perpetuated through customary usage. He has instructed his assisting ministers to study and rectify the meanings of characters. The subtleties of this wondrous way and its profound essentials all derive from his own deep understanding: uniquely apprehended within his heart, divinely imparted and silently perfected. Examples are writing cheng 宬 as cheng 宬 and “li wan 吏丸” as yuan 圓 [?]. Truly, he illuminates the Vermilion Writing and treats the writings of Cang, the ancient scribe, as mere chaff [?]. There are things here that none but a great sage could transmit.
I have reverently read our Emperor’s Admonition on Reverence and Unity and thereby gained some understanding of its source. Speaking of reverence, it says: “At the suburban sacrifices, be respectful and sincere; in the ancestral temple, solemnly hasten to perform filial service. Be reverent in the illustrious court and circumspect when dwelling in private.” Speaking of unity, it says: “Do not mix it with a third; do not divide it into two. Let conduct accord with words, and finish as you began.” Thus the heart of our Emperor is precisely…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之心也豈惟遠紹羲皇矣乎
皇上書法之妙其原蓋出於此是則
聖祖作之於前先天而天弗違伏羲之畫卦者
也
皇上述之於後後天而奉天時黃帝之作書者
也心法之傳曠百世而相感書法之盛越
千古而獨隆天地亨嘉之會治敎休明之
期夫豈偶然者哉愚也涵濡同文之化久
矣竊猶有說焉蓋書法之惡繁而就簡猶
===
水之就下愈趨愈卑吾不知其所終也然
必使盡變而爲古猶決江河而之山也勢
不可得矣然則如之何而後可意者取小
篆而正之古文參之大篆可者存之不可
者釐正之於今文之中而不失古文之義
祛官府之委細斥詭僻之叛經離道者復
歸民於樸則古道或可還也豈惟書法云
乎哉若必多頡而少斯則又以罪揜功者
非大中之論也狂瞽之見如此若通變宜
punctuated:
聖祖之心也，豈惟遠紹羲皇矣乎？皇上書法之妙，其原蓋出於此。是則聖祖作之於前，先天而天弗違，伏羲之畫卦者也；皇上述之於後，後天而奉天時，黃帝之作書者也。心法之傳，曠百世而相感；書法之盛，越千古而獨隆。天地亨嘉之會，治敎休明之期，夫豈偶然者哉？

愚也涵濡同文之化久矣，竊猶有說焉。蓋書法之惡繁而就簡，猶水之就下，愈趨愈卑，吾不知其所終也。然必使盡變而爲古，猶決江河而之山也，勢不可得矣。然則如之何而後可？意者取小篆而正之古文，參之大篆，可者存之，不可者釐正之，於今文之中而不失古文之義，祛官府之委細，斥詭僻之叛經離道者，復歸民於樸，則古道或可還也。豈惟書法云乎哉？若必多頡而少斯，則又以罪揜功者，非大中之論也。狂瞽之見如此，若通變宜
translation_en:
…is the heart of the Sagely Ancestor. How could it merely continue the distant legacy of Fuxi? The excellence of His Majesty’s art of writing surely originates here. Thus the Sagely Ancestor created it first: acting before Heaven, yet Heaven did not depart from him—like Fuxi drawing the trigrams. His Majesty continued it afterward: acting after Heaven and observing Heaven’s seasons—like the Yellow Emperor creating writing. The transmission of the method of the heart resonates across a hundred generations; the flourishing of the art of writing surpasses all antiquity in its unique splendor. This auspicious convergence of Heaven and Earth, this age of splendid government and instruction—could these possibly have come about by chance?

I, in my ignorance, have long been steeped in the civilizing influence of a shared script. Yet I venture to offer a further observation. The tendency in writing to dislike complexity and seek simplicity resembles water flowing downward: the farther it proceeds, the lower it goes, and I do not know where it will end. Yet to insist on changing everything back to ancient forms would be like opening channels for the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers and directing them toward the mountains: circumstances make this impossible. What, then, would be practicable? Perhaps we might take small-seal script and correct it against ancient script, consulting large-seal script as well. We could preserve what is acceptable and rectify what is not, retaining the meanings of ancient writing within present-day script. If we eliminated the petty complexities of government offices, rejected the strange and aberrant forms that betray the Classics and depart from the Way, and brought the people back to simplicity, perhaps the ancient Way could be restored. Would this concern only the art of writing? If one insists on praising Cangjie and disparaging Li Si, that would again be to let faults obscure achievements, rather than a judgment of true impartiality. Such are my rash and benighted views. As for the authority to respond to change and benefit…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
民之權則有議禮制度考文之
聖天子在
第三問
黃士觀
同考試官教諭馮批仁智可以為二亦可以
為一子於是對既能析其緒而不遺又能合其大
而無外其深造於學而有得者耶
同考試官學正范批知仁智有二名而非二
道可與言性矣
===
考試官教諭趙批剖析理道亹亹千萬言
不倦其仁智之士歟
考試官學正寇批仁智是如此論
天下之理其協于一矣乎而以為二焉者
不明道者晦之也聖賢之言其統於同矣
乎而以為異焉者不知言者岐之也故自
理之散見也名斯殊焉名之殊者歸則一
也故即用明體者析之斯有以極其精自
理之統會也致斯一焉致之一者殊之本
punctuated:
民之權，則有議禮、制度、考文之聖天子在。

第三問
黃士觀

同考試官教諭馮批：仁智可以為二，亦可以為一。子於是對，既能析其緒而不遺，又能合其大而無外，其深造於學而有得者耶！

同考試官學正范批：知仁智有二名而非二道，可與言性矣。

考試官教諭趙批：剖析理道，亹亹千萬言不倦，其仁智之士歟！

考試官學正寇批：仁智是如此論。

天下之理，其協于一矣乎！而以為二焉者，不明道者晦之也。聖賢之言，其統於同矣乎！而以為異焉者，不知言者岐之也。故自理之散見也，名斯殊焉；名之殊者，歸則一也。故即用明體者，析之斯有以極其精。自理之統會也，致斯一焉；致之一者，殊之本
translation_en:
…the authority to benefit the people rests with the sage Son of Heaven, who deliberates on rites, establishes institutions, and examines written forms.

Third Policy Question
Huang Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: Benevolence and wisdom may be treated as two, or as one. In this response, you distinguish their various strands without omission and unite them in their full scope without leaving anything outside. Surely you have pursued learning deeply and attained understanding!

Comment by Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor: You understand that benevolence and wisdom have two names but are not two Ways. With you one may discuss human nature.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: You analyze principle and the Way, tirelessly setting forth thousands upon thousands of words. Are you not a man of benevolence and wisdom!

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: This is how benevolence and wisdom should be discussed.

Do not the principles of all under Heaven accord in unity? Those who regard them as two obscure them through their failure to understand the Way. Do not the words of sages and worthies converge upon the same truth? Those who regard them as divergent split them apart through their failure to understand those words. Thus, insofar as principle appears in its dispersed manifestations, its names differ; yet what bears different names ultimately returns to unity. Hence, those who elucidate substance through function can, by analysis, reach its utmost subtlety. Insofar as principle is comprehensively united, its ultimate purport is one; this unity of purport is the root of its diversity…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
也故會偏求全者合之自有以盡其大是
何也天下之理原於性也天下之性具於
心也心一則性無不一矣性一則理無不
一矣故理之通於古今也本無二也而時
或二焉雖二而不害其爲一也言之出於
聖賢也本無異也而時或異焉雖異而不
失其爲同也故必究其所以二而會其所
以一考其所以殊而本其所以同則理融
諸性性融諸心而天下之道已洞然而無
===
遺矣此致知窮理之學極深研幾之要而
爲吾人之所當從事者不然衆言之淆無
以知其至定之的羣說之紛無以考其是
非之辯而吾亦何能有得於向往也哉執
事以仁智之理下詢承學愚也固擿埴而
迷其往者也而何以知之雖然亦甞反本
窮源稽經質傳而有以知其略矣太極之
流行也奠而爲兩儀布而爲四德其生人
也氣以成形而理亦賦焉在天之元人得
punctuated:
也。故會偏求全者，合之自有以盡其大。是何也？天下之理原於性也，天下之性具於心也。心一則性無不一矣，性一則理無不一矣。故理之通於古今也，本無二也，而時或二焉，雖二而不害其爲一也；言之出於聖賢也，本無異也，而時或異焉，雖異而不失其爲同也。故必究其所以二，而會其所以一；考其所以殊，而本其所以同。則理融諸性，性融諸心，而天下之道已洞然而無遺矣。此致知窮理之學、極深研幾之要，而爲吾人之所當從事者。不然，衆言之淆，無以知其至定之的；羣說之紛，無以考其是非之辯，而吾亦何能有得於向往也哉？
執事以仁智之理下詢承學，愚也固擿埴而迷其往者也，而何以知之？雖然，亦甞反本窮源，稽經質傳，而有以知其略矣。太極之流行也，奠而爲兩儀，布而爲四德。其生人也，氣以成形，而理亦賦焉。在天之元，人得
translation_en:
…Thus, those who gather partial aspects to seek the whole can, by uniting them, fully comprehend its greatness. Why is this? The principles of all under Heaven originate in human nature, and human nature is contained in the mind. If the mind is one, human nature is invariably one; if human nature is one, principle is invariably one. Thus, principle, which runs through past and present, is fundamentally without duality. Though at times it appears twofold, this does not impair its unity. The words issuing from sages and worthies are fundamentally without divergence. Though at times they differ, they do not lose their underlying agreement. We must therefore investigate what makes principle appear twofold and comprehend what makes it one; examine what makes these words differ and trace them back to their common foundation. Then principle is integrated within human nature, and human nature within the mind, so that the Way of all under Heaven becomes perfectly clear, with nothing left out. This is the essential point of the learning that extends knowledge and investigates principle, plumbs the depths and examines the incipient signs of change; it is what we ought to pursue. Otherwise, amid the confusion of many voices, we have no means of knowing the utterly certain standard; amid the tangle of competing explanations, we have no means of examining the distinction between right and wrong. How, then, could we gain any understanding of what we aspire to?
You, honored examiner, have condescended to inquire of us students about the principles of benevolence and wisdom. In my ignorance, I am like a blind man tapping the ground, lost as to where to go: how could I understand them? Nevertheless, I have tried to return to the root and exhaust the source, examining the classics and consulting their commentaries, and have thereby gained some understanding of their broad outlines. In its flowing activity, the Supreme Ultimate establishes itself as the Two Modes, yin and yang, and distributes itself as the Four Virtues: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy. When it brings human beings into existence, material force gives them bodily form, while principle too is bestowed upon them. What in Heaven is origination, human beings receive…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之而爲仁在天之貞人得之以爲智是仁
智也皆性之德也具于人心而原于天命
者也故相爲體用互爲寂感迭爲終始旋
爲動靜初非判然爲二者也而聖賢之言
仁智也或舉此以該彼或因言以互見而
仁智之說於是不同矣不知不同者正所
以爲同而非仁智之果爲二道也是故智
動仁靜孔子所以論仁智之言也而至於
易傳之釋則又以仁爲動智爲靜何哉蓋
===
自仁智之成性而言則智者達於事理而
周流無滯動而不括者也故以動屬之智
也仁者安於義理而厚重不遷靜而有常
者也故以靜屬之仁也而易以生象言之
自仁之合德於元則爲陽自智之合德於
貞則爲陰故若見其動靜之互言耳合而
觀之智者達於事理而實有沉幾密察之
道動而未甞不靜也仁者安於義理而實
有生生不息之機靜而未甞不動也此其
punctuated: 之而爲仁；在天之貞，人得之以爲智。是仁智也，皆性之德也，具于人心而原于天命者也。故相爲體用，互爲寂感，迭爲終始，旋爲動靜，初非判然爲二者也。而聖賢之言仁智也，或舉此以該彼，或因言以互見，而仁智之說於是不同矣。不知不同者，正所以爲同，而非仁智之果爲二道也。是故「智動仁靜」，孔子所以論仁智之言也。而至於易傳之釋，則又以仁爲動、智爲靜，何哉？蓋自仁智之成性而言，則智者達於事理而周流無滯，動而不括者也，故以動屬之智也。仁者安於義理而厚重不遷，靜而有常者也，故以靜屬之仁也。而易以生象言之，自仁之合德於元，則爲陽；自智之合德於貞，則爲陰。故若見其動靜之互言耳。合而觀之，智者達於事理，而實有沉幾密察之道，動而未甞不靜也；仁者安於義理，而實有生生不息之機，靜而未甞不動也。此其
translation_en:
…receives it and it becomes benevolence; what in Heaven is steadfastness (zhen), human beings receive as wisdom. Benevolence and wisdom are both virtues of human nature, present in the human heart and originating in Heaven’s mandate. Thus each serves as the other’s substance and function; they alternate as stillness and response, ending and beginning, activity and tranquility. From the outset, they have never been two sharply separated things. Yet when sages and worthies speak of benevolence and wisdom, they sometimes mention one to encompass the other, and sometimes make their meanings mutually apparent through their statements. Hence their accounts of benevolence and wisdom differ. People fail to understand that these differences are precisely what makes them consistent, and do not mean that benevolence and wisdom really constitute two distinct Ways.

Thus, “The wise are active; the benevolent are tranquil” is Confucius’s statement concerning benevolence and wisdom. Yet the explanation in the Commentary on the Changes instead treats benevolence as active and wisdom as tranquil. Why is this? Speaking of benevolence and wisdom as established dispositions, the wise comprehend the principles of affairs and move freely without obstruction: they are active and unconstrained. Hence activity is assigned to wisdom. The benevolent rest securely in moral principles and are steadfast and unmoved: they are tranquil and constant. Hence tranquility is assigned to benevolence. The Changes, however, speaks in terms of the images of generation. Insofar as benevolence accords in virtue with origination (yuan), it is yang; insofar as wisdom accords in virtue with steadfastness, it is yin. Thus it merely appears that activity and tranquility have exchanged their referents.

Considered together, the wise comprehend the principles of affairs, yet truly possess a way of deeply pondering subtle incipient tendencies and examining things closely: in their activity, they are never without tranquility. The benevolent rest securely in moral principles, yet truly possess the impulse toward ceaseless generation: in their tranquility, they are never without activity. This is how their…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
動靜之互有所屬是豈爲言之相背乎成
已爲仁成物爲智子思所以論仁智之德
也而至於子貢之贊孔子則又以成已爲
智成物爲仁者何哉蓋自夫誠立天下之
有以誠而成已則天理流行人欲淨盡夫
是之謂仁也以誠而成物則知無不明處
無不當夫是之謂智也而子貢以進學先
之乃以學不厭爲智之所以自明敎不倦
爲仁之所以及物此始見其仁智之異說
===
矣合而觀之則正理之盡者斯妙應物之
感而成已固成物之本也達順之妙者由
於體信之極而物成固已成之驗也此其
人已之互有所指又豈爲言之相判乎程
子曰專言仁則包四德是智固在仁之中
也殊不知所謂包四德者蓋自成德而統
其大者言之也觀諸孟子之論仁或以惻
隱羞惡辭讓是非而並列於四者之間或
謂天之尊爵人之安宅而統貫於四德之
punctuated:
動靜之互有所屬，是豈爲言之相背乎？成已爲仁，成物爲智，子思所以論仁智之德也。而至於子貢之贊孔子，則又以成已爲智，成物爲仁者，何哉？蓋自夫誠立天下之有，以誠而成已，則天理流行，人欲淨盡，夫是之謂仁也；以誠而成物，則知無不明，處無不當，夫是之謂智也。而子貢以進學先之，乃以學不厭爲智之所以自明，敎不倦爲仁之所以及物，此始見其仁智之異說矣。合而觀之，則正理之盡者，斯妙應物之感，而成已固成物之本也；達順之妙者，由於體信之極，而物成固已成之驗也。此其人已之互有所指，又豈爲言之相判乎？
程子曰：「專言仁則包四德。」是智固在仁之中也。殊不知所謂包四德者，蓋自成德而統其大者言之也。觀諸孟子之論仁，或以惻隱、羞惡、辭讓、是非，而並列於四者之間；或謂天之尊爵、人之安宅，而統貫於四德之
translation_en:
…Thus activity and stillness each have their respective associations in these alternating formulations. How could the statements contradict one another? Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom: this is how Zisi discusses the virtues of benevolence and wisdom. Yet when Zigong praises Confucius, he instead takes perfecting oneself as wisdom and perfecting things as benevolence. Why is this? Consider how sincerity establishes all that exists under Heaven [?]. When one perfects oneself through sincerity, heavenly principle flows freely and human desires are utterly purged: this is what is called benevolence. When one perfects things through sincerity, nothing in one’s understanding remains unclear, and nothing in one’s handling of affairs is inappropriate: this is what is called wisdom. Zigong, however, gives priority to advancing in learning. He therefore takes learning without satiety as the means by which wisdom brings illumination to oneself, and teaching without weariness as the means by which benevolence extends to others. Only from this perspective do their accounts of benevolence and wisdom appear different. Considered together, however, fully realizing correct principle enables one to respond with subtle mastery to the things that move one; perfecting oneself is indeed the foundation of perfecting things. Subtle mastery in extending harmonious accord arises from the utmost embodiment of trustworthiness; the perfection of things is indeed evidence that oneself has been perfected. Thus these alternating references to others and oneself each have their intended object. How could the statements be at odds?
Master Cheng says: “When benevolence is spoken of on its own, it encompasses the four virtues.” Thus wisdom is certainly contained within benevolence. Yet one must recognize that ‘encompassing the four virtues’ is said from the standpoint of perfected virtue, taking the greatest of them as comprehending the whole. Consider Mencius’s discussions of benevolence. Sometimes, through the feelings of compassion, shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and right and wrong, he places it alongside the other members of the four. Sometimes he calls it Heaven’s honored rank and the secure dwelling of humankind, presenting it as unifying and pervading the four virtues …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
首則程子之言信矣然又何害於仁智之
偏言者乎朱子曰四德之智如四時之冬
萬物成始而成終是仁又在智之中也殊
不知所謂成始終者蓋自進學而功之切
者言之也觀諸大學之至善而能得由於
知止中庸之服膺而能守由於能擇則朱
子之言信矣然又何害於專言之兼智者
乎孔子以智屬乎天仁屬乎地蓋觀於仁
智之深故爲是擬議也王通本之而有智
===
圓仁方之說是有得於天圓地方之粗迹
者也雖其所造未能望於聖人而一言之
幾乎道也夫豈可以盡遺哉孔子以智仁
勇爲三達德蓋厚望於其君故陳之以君
德之備也司馬光祖之而有仁明武之言
是有見於智仁勇之發用者也雖其所陳
未能究竟其理而出言之不背於聖也夫
豈可以或少哉要之天下之理其雜物撰
德泛然示人廣者雖不可以一端求而吾
punctuated: 首，則程子之言信矣。然又何害於仁智之偏言者乎？朱子曰：「四德之智，如四時之冬，萬物成始而成終。」是仁又在智之中也。殊不知所謂成始終者，蓋自進學而功之切者言之也。觀諸《大學》之至善，而能得由於知止；《中庸》之服膺，而能守由於能擇，則朱子之言信矣。然又何害於專言之兼智者乎？孔子以智屬乎天，仁屬乎地，蓋觀於仁智之深，故爲是擬議也。王通本之而有智圓仁方之說，是有得於天圓地方之粗迹者也。雖其所造未能望於聖人，而一言之幾乎道也，夫豈可以盡遺哉？孔子以智仁勇爲三達德，蓋厚望於其君，故陳之以君德之備也。司馬光祖之而有仁明武之言，是有見於智仁勇之發用者也。雖其所陳未能究竟其理，而出言之不背於聖也，夫豈可以或少哉？要之，天下之理，其雜物撰德，泛然示人廣者，雖不可以一端求，而吾
translation_en:
…at their head, then Master Cheng’s words are indeed true. Yet how does this conflict with speaking of benevolence and wisdom separately? Master Zhu said: “Wisdom among the four virtues is like winter among the four seasons: through it the myriad things complete their beginning and their end.” Thus benevolence, in turn, is contained within wisdom. Yet this overlooks the fact that “completing the beginning and end” is said with reference to advancing in learning and the crucial work involved. Consider attaining the highest good in the Great Learning: the ability to attain it proceeds from knowing where to rest. Or consider holding fast to goodness in the Doctrine of the Mean: the ability to preserve it proceeds from being able to choose it. Master Zhu’s words are indeed true. Yet how does this conflict with an overarching use of “benevolence” that includes wisdom?

Confucius associated wisdom with Heaven and benevolence with Earth. He made this comparison because he perceived the depths of benevolence and wisdom. Wang Tong drew upon this to formulate the saying, “Wisdom is round; benevolence is square.” In this he grasped something of the outward traces of Heaven’s roundness and Earth’s squareness. Although his attainment could not approach that of the sage, this single saying came close to the Way. How, then, could it be dismissed entirely?

Confucius took wisdom, benevolence, and courage as the three universally applicable virtues. Because he had high expectations of his ruler, he set them forth as the full complement of a ruler’s virtues. Sima Guang followed this precedent in speaking of benevolence, discernment, and martial prowess. In this he perceived how wisdom, benevolence, and courage manifest themselves in practice. Although his exposition did not fully fathom their underlying principles, his words did not depart from the sage’s teaching. How, then, could they be disparaged at all?

In sum, the principles of all under Heaven, intermingling things and bringing together their qualities, display their breadth everywhere to human beings. Although they cannot be sought through a single aspect, yet our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
性之德廣大咸備燦然示人顯者則唯仁
智而已矣是仁智也道固未嘗相離而功
不容於或缺也有覺以言仁斯合仁於智
乎而後仁可全否則吾懼其病於博愛流
於姑息也已擇術以為智是合智於仁乎
而後仁可得否則吾懼其失於泛濫害於
穿鑿也已故曰仁智合一存乎聖仁智合
而能事畢矣是故義也者由此而宜之也
禮也者由此而履之也信也者由此而成
===
之也勇也者由此而達之也而又何待於
他求也哉要之天下之理一而已矣舉體
可以該用即用可以窺體聖賢固不必屑
屑於比而言之也聖賢之言同而已矣舉
全足以該偏指偏未始遺全聖賢固不必
拘拘於強而同之也或先後之互有所發
而觀會者不失於為通或彼此之互有所
指而得意者自足以忘言庶於至當協一
之論洞然無遺而終身之指歸或不能有
punctuated:
性之德，廣大咸備，燦然示人顯者，則唯仁智而已矣。是仁智也，道固未嘗相離，而功不容於或缺也。有覺以言仁，斯合仁於智乎，而後仁可全；否則吾懼其病於博愛，流於姑息也已。擇術以為智，是合智於仁乎，而後仁可得；否則吾懼其失於泛濫，害於穿鑿也已。故曰：「仁智合一存乎聖。」仁智合而能事畢矣。是故義也者，由此而宜之也；禮也者，由此而履之也；信也者，由此而成之也；勇也者，由此而達之也。而又何待於他求也哉？

要之，天下之理，一而已矣。舉體可以該用，即用可以窺體，聖賢固不必屑屑於比而言之也。聖賢之言，同而已矣。舉全足以該偏，指偏未始遺全，聖賢固不必拘拘於強而同之也。或先後之互有所發，而觀會者不失於為通；或彼此之互有所指，而得意者自足以忘言。庶於至當協一之論，洞然無遺，而終身之指歸，或不能有
translation_en:
…the virtues of our nature are vast and fully comprehensive, yet what shines forth clearly for people to see is simply benevolence and wisdom. In the Way, benevolence and wisdom have never been separate; in their operation, neither can be lacking. To speak of benevolence in terms of awareness—is this not to unite benevolence with wisdom, so that benevolence can then be complete? Otherwise, I fear it will suffer from indiscriminate love and lapse into indulgence. To take the choosing of an occupation as wisdom—is this not to unite wisdom with benevolence, so that benevolence may then be attained? Otherwise, I fear it will go astray through indiscriminate rambling and do harm through strained interpretations. Thus it is said: “The union of benevolence and wisdom rests in the sage.” When benevolence and wisdom unite, all that can be accomplished is accomplished. Thus righteousness is to act appropriately on this basis; ritual propriety is to put it into practice; trustworthiness is to bring it to fulfillment; and courage is to carry it through. What further need is there to seek elsewhere?

In essence, the principle of all under Heaven is one. To set forth its substance can encompass its functioning; through its functioning one can glimpse its substance. The sages and worthies therefore need not labor over discussing the two side by side. The sayings of the sages and worthies are alike in their purport. To set forth the whole is sufficient to encompass the part; to point to the part does not mean abandoning the whole. The sages and worthies therefore need not insist on forcing them into uniformity. Sometimes earlier and later statements illuminate one another, and those who perceive their convergence do not fail to comprehend them; sometimes statements here and there point to one another, and those who grasp their meaning can dispense with the words. One may thus hope to understand fully, without omission, these supremely fitting and harmonious arguments, while the guiding purpose of one’s entire life may perhaps have nothing …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
出於是也雖然求仁智於方策則辯之雖
詳亦不過爲口耳之學求仁智於吾心則
操之有要斯可爲自得之真學者於仁智
抑將何以爲求端用力之方哉必也好學
以開其始力行以踐其實則庶乎明通公
溥仁智合德矣動靜不偏體用兼該矣成
已成物功效廣大矣配乎天地德行光明
矣方圓不滯變通無方矣仁智之道豈不
會歸於我而亦奚有於異同之論也哉此
===
固道之足以訂證千古而功之可以詔示
方來者也執事以爲何如
第四問
游日章
同考試官教諭方批親民之至計久任之要
法盡於篇中見之得士如此可以藉手矣
同考試官教諭黎批歷評守令之善而折衷
古今求才考課久任之法其論正其氣昌其爲吏
可諗其必循矣
punctuated:
出於是也。雖然，求仁智於方策，則辯之雖詳，亦不過爲口耳之學；求仁智於吾心，則操之有要，斯可爲自得之真。學者於仁智，抑將何以爲求端用力之方哉？必也好學以開其始，力行以踐其實，則庶乎明通公溥，仁智合德矣；動靜不偏，體用兼該矣；成已成物，功效廣大矣；配乎天地，德行光明矣；方圓不滯，變通無方矣。仁智之道，豈不會歸於我，而亦奚有於異同之論也哉？此固道之足以訂證千古，而功之可以詔示方來者也。執事以爲何如？

第四問
游日章

同考試官教諭方批：親民之至計，久任之要法，盡於篇中見之。得士如此，可以藉手矣。

同考試官教諭黎批：歷評守令之善，而折衷古今求才、考課、久任之法。其論正，其氣昌，其爲吏，可諗其必循矣。
translation_en:
…go beyond this. Nevertheless, if one seeks benevolence and wisdom in written texts, then, however detailed one’s argument, it remains merely learning that passes from ear to mouth. If one seeks benevolence and wisdom within one’s own heart, grasping their essentials, one can attain the truth of personal understanding. How, then, should students find a starting point and a method for applying their efforts to benevolence and wisdom? Surely they must begin with a love of learning and realize its substance through earnest practice. Then they may attain penetrating understanding and impartial breadth, uniting benevolence and wisdom in their virtue; favor neither activity nor stillness, encompassing both substance and function; perfect themselves and other beings, achieving far-reaching results; match Heaven and Earth, making their virtuous conduct shine; and remain unimpeded by either the square or the round, adapting to change without being bound to any fixed method. Would not the Way of benevolence and wisdom then converge within oneself? What occasion would remain for debating similarities and differences? This is indeed a Way sufficient to judge and verify the understanding of all past ages, and an achievement capable of instructing generations to come. What is your judgment, honored sir?

Fourth Question
You Rizhang

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “The finest plans for caring for the people and the essential methods for keeping officials in office for extended terms are all to be found in this essay. In obtaining a scholar of this caliber, we have an achievement to present.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “He reviews in turn the merits of prefects and magistrates, weighing ancient and modern methods of seeking talent, evaluating officials’ performance, and retaining them in office for extended terms. His arguments are sound, and his spirit is vigorous. Should he serve as an official, we can be confident that he will be a conscientious administrator.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙批文辭典雅雖議處守令
而駸駸有古作者矩度可以見
聖世氣化之隆矣
考試官學正寇批古今循吏無如西漢子
能言之而末復致望於
今日之考課者子其有希文先憂之志哉
人君體上天之意以惠天下之民其責將
誰委哉亦曰守令而已矣夫天生民而不
能自養於是乎託之君以養之故曰亶聰
===
明作元后元后作民父母然以君而視民
其勢則甚懸也迺自近而宰輔奉其德以
分布六卿而達之諸司以下及於郡縣故
曰聖人養賢以及萬民然則郡縣之職亦
微且遠矣而識治者重之何也其治小其
任專其於民也近蓋若家人父子之親痾
瘝皆切於其身者也是故言出而民易從
事舉而效隨應任之得人則百姓受其福
不得其人則德澤壅而君人體天之意孤
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批：文辭典雅，雖議處守令，而駸駸有古作者矩度，可以見聖世氣化之隆矣。

考試官學正寇批：古今循吏無如西漢，子能言之，而末復致望於今日之考課者，子其有希文先憂之志哉！

人君體上天之意以惠天下之民，其責將誰委哉？亦曰守令而已矣。夫天生民而不能自養，於是乎託之君以養之，故曰：「亶聰明作元后，元后作民父母。」然以君而視民，其勢則甚懸也。迺自近而宰輔奉其德，以分布六卿而達之諸司，以下及於郡縣，故曰：「聖人養賢以及萬民。」然則郡縣之職亦微且遠矣，而識治者重之，何也？其治小，其任專，其於民也近，蓋若家人父子之親，痾瘝皆切於其身者也。是故言出而民易從，事舉而效隨應。任之得人，則百姓受其福；不得其人，則德澤壅而君人體天之意孤
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The language is refined and elegant. Although the discussion concerns arrangements for prefects and magistrates, it approaches the standards of ancient authors. Here one can discern the flourishing moral influence of this sage age.

Comment by Examiner Kou, School Instructor: Among the conscientious officials of ancient and modern times, none surpass those of the Western Han. You have been able to discuss them, and at the end you again express your hopes for those responsible for evaluating officials today. Surely you possess Xiwen’s aspiration to be the first to bear the world’s cares!

The ruler embodies Heaven’s intentions in order to benefit the people of the realm. To whom should he entrust this responsibility? The answer is simply prefects and magistrates. Heaven gives birth to the people but cannot itself nourish them; it therefore entrusts them to a ruler to nourish them. Thus it is said: “One who is truly discerning becomes the sovereign; the sovereign becomes father and mother to the people.” Yet the ruler’s position is very distant from that of the people. Thus, beginning with those near him, the chief councilors uphold his virtue and distribute its influence through the six ministers to the various offices, extending downward to the prefectures and counties. Thus it is said: “The sage nourishes the worthy, and thereby reaches all the people.”

The offices of prefecture and county are therefore lowly and remote. Why, then, do those who understand government attach such importance to them? Their jurisdictions are small, their responsibilities concentrated, and they are close to the people. Their intimacy resembles that of fathers and sons within a household: the people’s illnesses and sufferings touch them as though these afflicted their own bodies. Thus, when they speak, the people readily obey; when they undertake an action, results follow in response. If suitable men are appointed, the common people enjoy the benefits. If the appointees are unsuitable, the flow of beneficence is obstructed, and the ruler’s intention to embody Heaven’s purposes is frustrated…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣此為守令者貴知自愛而在上者亦當
知所勸之也故曰天下政平訟理惟良二
千石又曰宰天下不如縣令之為樂樂者
樂乎澤之易流也求之於古若治蒲而得
三善之稱則有子路焉治單父而擅鳴琴
之治則有子賤焉子夏治莒父而謹欲速
之戒子游治武城而興禮樂之教凡以得
聖人為之依歸而卓然有成者也春秋而
下秦治棼矣漢興去古未遠其循良之治
===
有足稱者是故於蜀郡文翁見其文學之
敷也於潁川黃霸見其教化安全之政也
於渤海龔遂見其農桑之勸牛犢之化也
於南陽召信臣見其水利之興召父之稱
也然治行第一如吳公而史失其名偽增
戶口如王成而特蒙顯賞則當時循吏之
未能盡信可知矣要之史失其名者漢文
玄默之化循吏不勝其書故也偽增蒙賞
則宣帝綜覈之實何如耶尚何足擬聖門
punctuated: 矣。此為守令者貴知自愛，而在上者亦當知所勸之也。故曰：「天下政平訟理，惟良二千石。」又曰：「宰天下不如縣令之為樂。」樂者，樂乎澤之易流也。求之於古，若治蒲而得三善之稱，則有子路焉；治單父而擅鳴琴之治，則有子賤焉；子夏治莒父而謹欲速之戒，子游治武城而興禮樂之教，凡以得聖人為之依歸而卓然有成者也。春秋而下，秦治棼矣。漢興，去古未遠，其循良之治有足稱者。是故於蜀郡文翁，見其文學之敷也；於潁川黃霸，見其教化安全之政也；於渤海龔遂，見其農桑之勸、牛犢之化也；於南陽召信臣，見其水利之興、召父之稱也。然治行第一如吳公，而史失其名；偽增戶口如王成，而特蒙顯賞，則當時循吏之未能盡信可知矣。要之，史失其名者，漢文玄默之化，循吏不勝其書故也。偽增蒙賞，則宣帝綜覈之實何如耶？尚何足擬聖門
translation_en:
…Thus, those serving as prefects and county magistrates must know to cherish their own integrity, while those above them should also know how to encourage them. Hence the saying: “Orderly government and properly adjudicated lawsuits throughout the realm depend upon good officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank.” It is also said: “Governing the realm does not afford as much joy as serving as a county magistrate.” This joy lies in the ease with which beneficence can reach the people.

Looking to antiquity, there was Zilu, who governed Pu and earned praise for three virtues; there was Zijian, who governed Shanfu and won renown for governing through playing the zither. Zixia governed Jufu, carefully observing the warning against seeking quick results; Ziyou governed Wucheng and promoted instruction in rites and music. All achieved outstanding success because they had the Sage as their guide and support. After the Spring and Autumn period, government under the Qin fell into disorder. When the Han arose, antiquity was not yet far distant, and its conscientious and benevolent administration offered much worthy of praise.

Thus, in Wen Weng of Shu Commandery we see the spread of literary learning; in Huang Ba of Yingchuan, government that instructed and transformed the people, bringing them security; in Gong Sui of Bohai, encouragement of agriculture and sericulture, and the transformation wrought by inducing people to acquire cattle and calves; and in Shao Xinchen of Nanyang, the development of irrigation and the acclaim that earned him the name “Father Shao.” Yet although Lord Wu ranked first in administrative performance, the histories failed to preserve his personal name; while Wang Cheng, who falsely inflated household and population figures, received conspicuous rewards. We can therefore see that accounts of the conscientious officials of that time cannot be trusted in every particular.

In essence, the failure of the histories to preserve that personal name was because Emperor Wen of Han transformed the people through quiet, unobtrusive rule, producing more conscientious officials than could be recorded. But if falsified increases received rewards, how effective in practice was Emperor Xuan’s comprehensive scrutiny? How could such men possibly compare with those of the Sage’s school…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之賢也哉我
國朝官人之法取諸成周親民之選重於西
漢洪武中嘗擢知府趙瑁爲左諭德矣又
嘗擢典史馮堅爲僉都御史矣作循良之
風以新庶官之習是以百八十年來吏稱
其職民安其業今卽其卓異者言之如廉
察貪暴嚴禁豪猾積米賑農活者無算任
久遷秩留者萬眾則况鍾之守姑蘇也不
爲利回不爲勢怵愛養所部霽
===
天威於一語懷柔遠人蠲商稅以萬計則劉實
之治南雄也始宰莊浪誕著賢聲歷守應
天益彰政譽剛正不撓而吏民懾服廉公
有威而豪貴斂手此顧佐齊名孝肅而致
碩輔之交薦者也始守鎭江綽有偉績比
改蘇郡尤愜輿情舉偏補弊飭夙政之廢
弛築壩浚河濟歲漕之壅滯此林鶚獨持
大體而蒙
英廟之眷遇者也若用法平恕疑獄多所平反
punctuated: 之賢也哉！我國朝官人之法取諸成周，親民之選重於西漢。洪武中嘗擢知府趙瑁爲左諭德矣，又嘗擢典史馮堅爲僉都御史矣。作循良之風，以新庶官之習，是以百八十年來，吏稱其職，民安其業。今卽其卓異者言之，如廉察貪暴，嚴禁豪猾，積米賑農，活者無算；任久遷秩，留者萬眾，則况鍾之守姑蘇也。不爲利回，不爲勢怵，愛養所部，霽天威於一語；懷柔遠人，蠲商稅以萬計，則劉實之治南雄也。始宰莊浪，誕著賢聲；歷守應天，益彰政譽。剛正不撓，而吏民懾服；廉公有威，而豪貴斂手。此顧佐齊名孝肅，而致碩輔之交薦者也。始守鎭江，綽有偉績；比改蘇郡，尤愜輿情。舉偏補弊，飭夙政之廢弛；築壩浚河，濟歲漕之壅滯。此林鶚獨持大體，而蒙英廟之眷遇者也。若用法平恕，疑獄多所平反，
translation_en:
…how could they possibly compare with the worthies of the Sage’s school!

Our dynasty takes its methods of appointing officials from the Zhou and attaches even greater importance than the Western Han to selecting officials who govern the people directly. During the Hongwu reign, the prefect Zhao Mao was promoted to Left Admonitor, and the Chief Clerk Feng Jian was promoted to Assistant Censor-in-chief. By encouraging conscientious and benevolent administration, the dynasty renewed the habits of its officials. Thus, for the past 180 years, officials have fulfilled their duties and the people have pursued their livelihoods in peace.

To speak now of those whose achievements were outstanding: investigating corrupt and oppressive officials, strictly restraining powerful rogues, and storing grain to relieve farmers, thereby saving countless lives; serving so long that his rank was raised, with multitudes seeking to retain him—such was Kuang Zhong’s administration of Gusu. Unswerved by profit and undaunted by power, caring for those under his jurisdiction, and calming imperial wrath with a single utterance; winning over people from afar and remitting commercial taxes amounting to tens of thousands—such was Liu Shi’s administration of Nanxiong.

When first serving as magistrate of Zhuanglang, Gu Zuo established a distinguished reputation for worthiness; later, as prefect of Yingtian, he won still greater renown for his administration. Upright and unyielding, he commanded the awed obedience of officials and commoners; incorruptible, impartial, and authoritative, he made the powerful and noble restrain themselves. This was the Gu Zuo whose fame equaled that of Xiaosu and who received recommendations from eminent ministers one after another.

When first serving as prefect of Zhenjiang, Lin E achieved conspicuous successes; upon his transfer to Suzhou, he satisfied popular expectations still more fully. He corrected imbalances and remedied abuses, restoring discipline where earlier administration had fallen into neglect. He built dams and dredged rivers, relieving obstructions to the annual grain transport. This was the Lin E who showed exceptional command of the essentials of governance and received Emperor Yingzong’s favor.

As for applying the law with fairness and forbearance, and overturning many unjust verdicts in doubtful cases…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
敷政慈惠歲饑賴以全活創書院以教民
致科目之特盛則王恕之治維揚也期月
令行風裁已可想見思患豫防城濠務先
濬築屹保障於一方擒劇賊於崇朝則許
逵之治樂陵也之數子者遺風善政至今
爲烈庶幾聖門諸賢視漢所稱循吏則旣
無愧矣求其最著而可法者其况之治蘇
王之治維揚乎一則起自掾辟而勳庸茂
著楊士奇贈之有曰十年不愧趙清獻七
===
邑重迎張益州也一則歷事三朝而典刑
不墜王雲鳳記之有曰憂天下之志如范
仲淹濟天下之才如司馬光也是二人名
重當時而風動海内者亦已多矣執事所
謂追跡循良固有不必遠慕而得者非斯
人其誰與歸耶
國家養賢圖治人才輩出至我
今日之盛視昔猶或過之豈謂今之守令盡無
若人乎夫何習尚日趨而常情易玩故操
punctuated:
敷政慈惠，歲饑賴以全活，創書院以教民，致科目之特盛，則王恕之治維揚也。期月令行，風裁已可想見；思患豫防，城濠務先濬築，屹保障於一方，擒劇賊於崇朝，則許逵之治樂陵也。之數子者，遺風善政，至今爲烈，庶幾聖門諸賢；視漢所稱循吏，則旣無愧矣。求其最著而可法者，其况之治蘇、王之治維揚乎？一則起自掾辟，而勳庸茂著，楊士奇贈之有曰：「十年不愧趙清獻，七邑重迎張益州也。」一則歷事三朝，而典刑不墜，王雲鳳記之有曰：「憂天下之志如范仲淹，濟天下之才如司馬光也。」是二人名重當時，而風動海内者亦已多矣。執事所謂追跡循良，固有不必遠慕而得者，非斯人，其誰與歸耶？

國家養賢圖治，人才輩出。至我今日之盛，視昔猶或過之，豈謂今之守令盡無若人乎？夫何習尚日趨，而常情易玩，故操
translation_en:
…He administered government with kindness and generosity, preserving lives during famine; he founded an academy to educate the people, bringing exceptional success in the examinations. Such was Wang Shu’s administration of Weiyang. Within a month, orders were being carried out, and his authoritative bearing could already be discerned. Anticipating trouble and taking precautions, he made dredging moats and building walls his first concern, establishing a firm bulwark for the region and capturing formidable bandits in a single morning. Such was Xu Kui’s administration of Leling. These several men [?] left exemplary ways and good government whose influence remains powerful to this day. They approached the worthies of the Sage’s school and could certainly stand without shame beside those praised as exemplary officials under the Han. If we seek the most outstanding and imitable examples, would they not be Kuang’s administration of Suzhou and Wang’s administration of Weiyang?

The former rose from appointment as a subordinate functionary and achieved distinguished service. In a verse presented to him, Yang Shiqi wrote: “For ten years, worthy of Zhao Qingxian; the seven counties welcome Zhang of Yizhou once again.” The latter served through three reigns without allowing the exemplary standards of the past to lapse. Wang Yunfeng wrote of him: “In his determination to concern himself with the realm’s troubles, he resembled Fan Zhongyan; in his ability to bring relief to the realm, he resembled Sima Guang.” These two men enjoyed great renown in their day, and their example stirred many throughout the empire. As for following in the footsteps of exemplary officials, as you have proposed, one can certainly find models without looking to the distant past. If we do not turn to these men, to whom should we turn?

The state nurtures worthy men and seeks good government, and talented men emerge in succession. In the flourishing conditions of our own day, we may even surpass the past. How could one say that among today’s prefects and county magistrates there are none like these men? Yet why do prevailing habits daily deteriorate, while ordinary human dispositions so readily lapse into complacency? Thus, in cultivating…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
勵廉潔者有矣而苞苴之弊不能無分甘
恬澹者有矣而夤緣之私未盡去志在愛
民矣或實惠之未流名為持法矣或執守
之易撓此蠹政戕民不能不為君子之議
而追古傷今固宜厪執事之慨也此其故
何哉蓋自夫久任之法不行而人懷苟且
之志內外之勢偏重而士有顧望之私此
牧民者所以多忽其職而不知所自修也
或依阿淟涊巧為容悅之圖或和光逐物
===
苟為自全之計日覬虛聲坐俟速化其視
官舍如傳郵而視斯民不啻秦越也若此
者亦何取於民之父母哉是惟守令不知
所以自愛而上之愛之者日已薄上不能
重視其下而守令之所以自視者益以輕
如是而欲循良之盛媲美於昔也必不可
得矣然則為守令而不思付託之重顛越
心焉墮其職而以自抵於弗類者是自誣
也為上而罔恤守令之艱不思所以振勵
punctuated:
勵廉潔者有矣，而苞苴之弊不能無；分甘恬澹者有矣，而夤緣之私未盡去；志在愛民矣，或實惠之未流；名為持法矣，或執守之易撓。此蠹政戕民，不能不為君子之議，而追古傷今，固宜厪執事之慨也。此其故何哉？蓋自夫久任之法不行，而人懷苟且之志；內外之勢偏重，而士有顧望之私。此牧民者所以多忽其職，而不知所自修也。或依阿淟涊，巧為容悅之圖；或和光逐物，苟為自全之計。日覬虛聲，坐俟速化，其視官舍如傳郵，而視斯民不啻秦越也。若此者，亦何取於民之父母哉！是惟守令不知所以自愛，而上之愛之者日已薄；上不能重視其下，而守令之所以自視者益以輕。如是而欲循良之盛媲美於昔也，必不可得矣。
然則為守令而不思付託之重，顛越心焉，墮其職而以自抵於弗類者，是自誣也；為上而罔恤守令之艱，不思所以振勵
translation_en:
…there are those who cultivate incorruptibility, yet the abuse of gifts offered as bribes cannot be wholly eliminated; there are those content with quiet simplicity, yet private advancement through connections has not entirely ceased. Some aspire to care for the people, yet tangible benefits may fail to reach them; some are reputed to uphold the law, yet their resolve may readily bend. Such conduct corrupts government and harms the people, and cannot escape the criticism of gentlemen. In recalling antiquity and lamenting the present, you, sir, have ample reason for dismay.
Why is this so? Because the practice of keeping officials long in their posts is no longer observed, men harbor an inclination merely to muddle through; because the balance of influence between service at court and service outside it is unequal, officials privately watch for opportunities before committing themselves. This is why those charged with tending the people so often neglect their duties and do not know how to cultivate themselves. Some acquiesce and wallow in degradation, cleverly scheming to ingratiate themselves; others dim their own light and drift with circumstances, seeking merely to preserve their positions. Daily they covet empty renown and sit awaiting speedy promotion. They regard their official residences as relay stations and these people as no less remote from themselves than Qin from Yue. What claim have such men to be the people's parents? Thus prefects and magistrates fail to value themselves, while their superiors' regard for them grows daily thinner; their superiors fail to accord their subordinates due weight, while prefects and magistrates regard themselves ever more lightly. Under such circumstances, it is surely impossible to expect conscientious and benevolent administration to flourish as splendidly as in the past.
Accordingly, prefects and magistrates who fail to consider the weight of the trust placed in them, go astray in their hearts [?], neglect their duties, and thereby reduce themselves to unworthiness deceive themselves. Those in authority who have no concern for the difficulties of prefects and magistrates and give no thought to how to encourage them…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
成全之者是誣人者也二者將焉咎哉亦
惟上下各盡其道焉耳誠使爲之下者知
守令身父母之責念稼穡爲小民之依罔
咈民以從欲罔違道以干譽毋嬰情於內
外之殊毋改節於終始之異毋急於近功
毋阻於小挫吾知盡吾職焉已矣爲之上
者念其勞也而勞之憫其情也而優之程
其勤惰而勸戒之覈其邪正而黜陟之不
專事乎文法之繩而必開誠以布公不取
===
快於儇便之私而必循名以責實吾知盡
吾御下之道焉已矣則秉正孤立者將有
恃而無恐勤公奉職者皆矢心而益勵上
下之間其道各盡而其事交相成矣如是
而何守令之不安何恩澤之不究何古循
吏之不可及何况王諸臣之不多見哉謹
對
第五問
楊嶷
punctuated:
成全之者，是誣人者也。二者將焉咎哉？亦惟上下各盡其道焉耳。誠使爲之下者，知守令身父母之責，念稼穡爲小民之依，罔咈民以從欲，罔違道以干譽，毋嬰情於內外之殊，毋改節於終始之異，毋急於近功，毋阻於小挫，吾知盡吾職焉已矣。爲之上者，念其勞也而勞之，憫其情也而優之，程其勤惰而勸戒之，覈其邪正而黜陟之，不專事乎文法之繩，而必開誠以布公；不取快於儇便之私，而必循名以責實，吾知盡吾御下之道焉已矣。則秉正孤立者將有恃而無恐，勤公奉職者皆矢心而益勵，上下之間，其道各盡，而其事交相成矣。如是，而何守令之不安？何恩澤之不究？何古循吏之不可及？何况王諸臣之不多見哉？謹對。

第五問

楊嶷
translation_en:
…and bring them to full accomplishment—such superiors wrong others. Where, then, does blame lie between these two parties? It is simply for superiors and subordinates each to fulfill their proper responsibilities. Let those serving below truly understand that prefects and magistrates bear the responsibilities of parents, and remember that farming sustains the common people. Let them neither go against the people to indulge their own desires nor violate the Way to seek praise. Let them not become emotionally entangled in distinctions between service at court and in the provinces, nor alter their integrity as circumstances change from the beginning of their service to its end. Let them neither rush after immediate achievements nor be deterred by minor setbacks, thinking only: “I know that I must fully discharge my duties.”

Let those serving above recognize their exertions and reward them, sympathize with their circumstances and treat them generously, assess their diligence or indolence and accordingly encourage or admonish them, and investigate their uprightness or depravity and accordingly promote or dismiss them. Rather than devote themselves exclusively to restraining them through formal regulations, they must act with sincerity and impartiality. They must not gratify private preferences for the glib and ingratiating, but must demand actual performance commensurate with an official’s appointed role, thinking only: “I know that I must fully discharge my responsibilities in directing my subordinates.” Then those who uphold what is right, even when standing alone, will have support and be without fear; those who diligently serve the public and perform their duties will all pledge themselves to their work and strive still harder. Superiors and subordinates will each fulfill their proper responsibilities and assist one another in accomplishing their tasks. Under such circumstances, how could prefects and magistrates fail to feel secure? How could beneficent favor fail to reach everywhere? How could the exemplary officials of antiquity remain beyond our reach? And how could ministers such as Kuang and Wang fail to appear in greater numbers? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question

Yang Yi

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭胡批閩中鹽法雖少然亦可
以足
國子能言其利而又詳知其弊考鹽政者觀之此足矣子其通達
政體者耶
同考試官敎諭費批言鹽法利弊粲然如指
諸掌且斟酌時宜有濟實用真一時俊傑哉
考試官敎諭趙批籌邊足用必有資於鹽
政子能深思遠計鑿鑿可行蓋亦素負經濟之略
者歟
===
考試官學正寇批事在目前而憂深謀遠
有志於天下者
聖王以天下之利利天下而不以便其私
故經制畫法而非以爲苛也與民守之而
已矣通變趨時而非以爲縱也與民宜之
而已矣夫法者一定不易而時宜所在則
又不可重拂焉者使欲執法以齊衆則上
積重而澤不究其勢必至於病民是之謂
苛使欲狗情以廢法則下詭利而事無紀
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭胡批：閩中鹽法雖少，然亦可以足國。子能言其利，而又詳知其弊，考鹽政者觀之，此足矣。子其通達政體者耶？

同考試官敎諭費批：言鹽法利弊，粲然如指諸掌，且斟酌時宜，有濟實用，真一時俊傑哉！

考試官敎諭趙批：籌邊足用，必有資於鹽政。子能深思遠計，鑿鑿可行，蓋亦素負經濟之略者歟？

考試官學正寇批：事在目前，而憂深謀遠，有志於天下者。

聖王以天下之利利天下，而不以便其私，故經制畫法，而非以爲苛也，與民守之而已矣；通變趨時，而非以爲縱也，與民宜之而已矣。夫法者，一定不易，而時宜所在，則又不可重拂焉者。使欲執法以齊衆，則上積重而澤不究，其勢必至於病民，是之謂苛；使欲狗情以廢法，則下詭利而事無紀。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: Although the salt administration in Fujian yields little [?], it can nevertheless supply the needs of the state. You can explain its benefits and also understand its abuses in detail. For anyone investigating salt administration, reading this is enough. Are you not someone thoroughly conversant with the principles of government?

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: Your explanation of the benefits and abuses of the salt administration is brilliantly clear, as though pointing to something in the palm of your hand. Moreover, you weigh what is appropriate to the times and offer proposals of practical value. Truly an outstanding talent of the age!

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: Planning frontier defense and ensuring adequate resources necessarily depend in part on salt administration. You have thought deeply and planned far ahead; your proposals are sound and practicable. Surely you have long possessed a capacity for statecraft?

Comment by Examiner Kou, Instructor: The matter lies immediately before us, yet your concerns run deep and your plans reach far: you are someone whose aspirations embrace all under Heaven.

The sage kings used the benefits of all under Heaven to benefit all under Heaven, rather than to serve their private interests. Thus, in establishing institutions and devising laws, they did not intend harshness: they merely upheld them together with the people. In adapting to change and keeping pace with the times, they did not intend laxity: they merely sought what was fitting for the people. Laws, once fixed, do not change; yet the requirements of the times must not be gravely contravened either. If one seeks to enforce the law to bring everyone into uniform order, then burdens accumulate above [?], while beneficence fails to reach the people. This will inevitably harm the people: this is what is called harshness. If one seeks to indulge personal feelings [?] and thereby set aside the law, then those below pursue profit deceitfully, and affairs fall into disorder …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
其勢必至於病國是之謂縱縱與苛而欲
理天下之事不可得也况於鹽法乎執事
以閩中鹽法下詢固公天下之心也愚閩
產也敢不屏其私圖以對昔自禹貢青州
貢鹽而鹽法之制興自周禮掌鹽之政令
而鹽法之制立則帝王之世鹽法亦所不
免豈不欲與天下相忘於利哉蓋鹽者天
地自然之利而下民有欲無紀則亂法者
禁亂之所由生者也猶坊止水之所自來
===
者也故帝王必有法以齊天下而後鹽可
以利天下不然則猗頓之富將不利於魯
吳王之強且恣虐於漢也可不慎哉洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇稽古立法貽
國家千萬載無疆之休者莫善於飛輓之策
百八十年內安外攘皆賴於此奈何狃於
承平忽於邊計而遂置閩中鹽法於不講
也考之
punctuated:
其勢必至於病國，是之謂縱。縱與苛而欲理天下之事，不可得也，况於鹽法乎？執事以閩中鹽法下詢，固公天下之心也。愚閩產也，敢不屏其私圖以對？昔自禹貢青州貢鹽，而鹽法之制興；自周禮掌鹽之政令，而鹽法之制立。則帝王之世，鹽法亦所不免，豈不欲與天下相忘於利哉？蓋鹽者，天地自然之利，而下民有欲，無紀則亂。法者，禁亂之所由生者也，猶坊止水之所自來者也。故帝王必有法以齊天下，而後鹽可以利天下。不然，則猗頓之富將不利於魯，吳王之強且恣虐於漢也，可不慎哉？

洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，稽古立法，貽國家千萬載無疆之休者，莫善於飛輓之策。百八十年，內安外攘，皆賴於此。奈何狃於承平，忽於邊計，而遂置閩中鹽法於不講也？考之
translation_en:
…the inevitable result will be harm to the state: this is what is called laxity. To seek to govern the affairs of the realm through laxity and harshness is impossible; how much more so in administering the salt laws! Your inquiry concerning the salt laws in Fujian certainly expresses an impartial concern for the realm. I am a native of Fujian: dare I answer without setting aside my private interests? In antiquity, the institution of salt regulation arose with Qingzhou’s tribute of salt recorded in the Tribute of Yu; it became established with the administrative ordinances governing salt in the Rites of Zhou. Thus even in the age of the sage emperors and kings, salt regulation could not be dispensed with. Did they not wish that they and all under Heaven might together forget considerations of profit? Salt is a bounty naturally produced by Heaven and Earth, but the common people have desires, and without regulation disorder follows. Laws restrain disorder at its source, just as dikes stop water where it comes from. Thus emperors and kings must have laws to bring order to the realm before salt can benefit it. Otherwise, wealth such as Yi Dun’s would prove detrimental to Lu, and power such as the King of Wu’s would allow unchecked tyranny against the Han. Can we fail to exercise caution?

We reverently reflect that when our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm, he examined antiquity and established laws. Among the measures by which he bequeathed boundless blessings to the state for countless ages, none surpassed his policy for the swift transport of provisions. For 180 years, internal peace and the repulsion of external threats have all depended upon this. How, then, have we become so accustomed to peace and so neglectful of frontier provisioning that we have left Fujian’s salt laws unexamined? Upon examining…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
國初建官轉運並峙淮浙責任維鈞也今閩
中所輸每歲僅及二萬而淮運歲輸百萬
浙運亦不下數十萬其鹽法之詳略迥異
者何哉是果產鹽之難歟日晒風花無事
煎煮不可謂不易也是果行鹽之地有未
廣歟八閩際山環海延袤數千里不可謂
不廣也是果食鹽之戶有未蕃歟八閩生
齒日衆戶口不下數百萬不可謂不蕃也
然則其故可知矣此無他淮浙之鹽有法
===
閩中無法故耳所謂無法者其弊有二曰
經畫無方也曰禁令不壹也蓋政久則敝
勢所必致也所貴乎經畫之得其宜耳夫
何襲因仍之舊憚紛改之煩惕利害之故
而斟酌損益之方莫為之所則上無道揆
而商鹽之行者日益滯是謂經畫之無方
嗜利無厭民之恒情也所貴乎禁令之壹
其趨耳夫何别於民竈之殊途格於府衛
之異致阻於豪右之難懲而統御約束之
punctuated:
國初建官轉運，並峙淮浙，責任維鈞也。今閩中所輸，每歲僅及二萬，而淮運歲輸百萬，浙運亦不下數十萬。其鹽法之詳略迥異者，何哉？是果產鹽之難歟？日晒風花，無事煎煮，不可謂不易也。是果行鹽之地有未廣歟？八閩際山環海，延袤數千里，不可謂不廣也。是果食鹽之戶有未蕃歟？八閩生齒日衆，戶口不下數百萬，不可謂不蕃也。然則其故可知矣。此無他，淮浙之鹽有法，閩中無法故耳。
所謂無法者，其弊有二：曰經畫無方也，曰禁令不壹也。蓋政久則敝，勢所必致也，所貴乎經畫之得其宜耳。夫何襲因仍之舊，憚紛改之煩，惕利害之故，而斟酌損益之方莫為之所，則上無道揆，而商鹽之行者日益滯，是謂經畫之無方。嗜利無厭，民之恒情也，所貴乎禁令之壹其趨耳。夫何别於民竈之殊途，格於府衛之異致，阻於豪右之難懲，而統御約束之
translation_en:
…at the founding of the dynasty, officials were appointed to administer salt transport, with Fujian standing alongside Huai and Zhe and bearing equal responsibilities. Yet Fujian now remits barely twenty thousand each year, while the Huai Salt Distribution Commission remits a million annually and the Zhe commission no fewer than several hundred thousand. Why do their systems of salt administration differ so greatly in thoroughness? Is producing salt here really difficult? Sun-drying and wind-induced crystallization require no boiling; this can hardly be called difficult. Is the territory in which salt is sold insufficiently extensive? The eight prefectures of Fujian border mountains and are encircled by the sea, extending several thousand li; this can hardly be called a small territory. Are the households consuming salt insufficiently numerous? Fujian’s population increases daily, and its registered population numbers no fewer than several million; this can hardly be called sparse. The reason is therefore clear. It is simply that salt in Huai and Zhe is administered according to a system, whereas salt in Fujian is not.
This absence of a system has two defects: planning lacks a sound method, and prohibitions are not uniformly enforced. Administrative arrangements inevitably deteriorate over time; what matters is that planning should suit the circumstances. Why, then, cling to inherited practices, shrink from the trouble of extensive changes, and take fright at considerations of advantage and harm, while making no provision for judicious reductions and additions? Those above thus lack the guidance of proper principles, and the circulation of licensed merchants’ salt becomes increasingly obstructed. This is what is meant by planning without a sound method. An insatiable appetite for profit is an enduring human disposition; what matters is that prohibitions should direct people toward a single course. Why, then, is administration divided between the separate arrangements for ordinary households and salt-producing households, impeded by the differing jurisdictions of prefectures and military guards, and obstructed by the difficulty of punishing powerful local families, so that the measures for overall control and restraint…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
令有所不行則下無法守而私販之興者
日益熾是謂禁令之不壹夫私販旣興則
商鹽自困商鹽旣困則報中必寡其事正
相反而其害常相須者也如是而欲
國課之充歲輸之盈必不可得矣然則淮浙
之鹽難而課多八閩之鹽易而課少者豈
非職此之故哉姑卽鹽法之鉅者論之均
一塲司也而徵納有本折之異是固以便
竈也然從宜納價或啟姦竈私鬻之端可
===
不曲防其敝乎同一引鹽也而分析有大
小引之殊是固以便商也然增減無稽或
滋姦詭冒帶之弊可不嚴覈其實乎竈以
辦鹽也而潯浯洅三塲之民皆得以米折
價則其日辦之鹽何所爲耶課以餉邊也
而潯浯洅三塲之課皆盡給泉州軍餉則
其額設之糧何所用耶赴邊中引者不易
之規而姦商土著獨專報中之利則嬴縮
得以自由矣可不繩之以法乎寬免竈丁
punctuated: 令有所不行，則下無法守，而私販之興者日益熾，是謂禁令之不壹。夫私販旣興，則商鹽自困；商鹽旣困，則報中必寡。其事正相反，而其害常相須者也。如是而欲國課之充、歲輸之盈，必不可得矣。然則淮浙之鹽難而課多，八閩之鹽易而課少者，豈非職此之故哉？姑卽鹽法之鉅者論之：均一塲司也，而徵納有本折之異，是固以便竈也。然從宜納價，或啟姦竈私鬻之端，可不曲防其敝乎？同一引鹽也，而分析有大小引之殊，是固以便商也。然增減無稽，或滋姦詭冒帶之弊，可不嚴覈其實乎？竈以辦鹽也，而潯浯洅三塲之民，皆得以米折價，則其日辦之鹽何所爲耶？課以餉邊也，而潯浯洅三塲之課，皆盡給泉州軍餉，則其額設之糧何所用耶？赴邊中引者，不易之規，而姦商土著獨專報中之利，則嬴縮得以自由矣，可不繩之以法乎？寬免竈丁
translation_en:
…when the regulations are not enforced everywhere, those below have no consistent rules to observe, and illicit trading grows ever more rampant. This is what is meant by a lack of uniformity in the prohibitions. Once illicit trading flourishes, the authorized salt trade naturally suffers; once the authorized salt trade suffers, applications for salt certificates inevitably become few. These activities stand in direct opposition, yet the harm they cause is mutually reinforcing. Under such circumstances, it is impossible to secure ample state revenue and full annual remittances. Is this not precisely why salt operations in Huai and Zhe are difficult yet yield substantial revenue, while those in Fujian are easy yet yield little?

Let us consider only the major features of the salt system. The salt-field offices are alike, yet some collect dues in kind and others in commuted payments. This is certainly intended to accommodate salt producers. Yet allowing payment of an assessed price as circumstances warrant may open the way for dishonest producers to sell salt privately. Can we fail to take every precaution against this abuse? Salt covered by certificates is likewise one and the same commodity, yet its allotment distinguishes between large and small certificates. This is certainly intended to accommodate merchants. Yet increases and reductions without verification may foster fraudulent carriage of extra salt. Can we fail to scrutinize the actual quantities strictly?

Salt producers are responsible for supplying salt, yet the people of the three salt fields of Xun, Wu, and Zai [?] are all permitted to pay rice in lieu of the assessed price. What, then, becomes of the salt they produce daily? Salt revenue is intended to provision the frontier, yet the revenue of these three salt fields is used entirely to provision the troops at Quanzhou. What, then, is the grain allocated under the established quota used for? Going to the frontier to obtain salt certificates by supplying provisions is an unalterable rule. Yet dishonest merchants and local residents monopolize the profits of applying for certificates, leaving them free to manipulate surpluses and shortfalls. Can we fail to restrain them by law? The granting of exemptions to salt workers…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
者優恤之典而刁竈滑胥遂成詭寄之習
則影射無所不至矣可不糾之以刑乎有
欲別立抽分於潯浯昞三場者正以懲納
價私鬻之姦耳殊不知場以辦課而肇立
抽分非制也孰若減價召中則商皆樂趨
而姦竈私鬻者自無以專其利矣有欲添
委掣摯於福寧福安地方者不過圖目前
軍門之利耳殊不知商已納價而又額外
加稅非法也孰若嚴捕私販則無事加稅
===
而巡緝所獲者自足以供其用矣一正一
餘淮浙之運鹽則然也而一母二子則夾
帶之漸恐不免矣是或可變而通之者也
懸衡秤較淮浙之榷鹽則然也而圍量抽
掣則欺隱之弊所必至矣是或可倣而正
之者也東路細鹽之規雖似競利矣然邊
海之民利玆貿易實默爲安輯之計也而
或者議之此之謂不知務者矣南路官鹽
之立雖若多事矣然私販之徒樂於趨市
punctuated: 者，優恤之典，而刁竈滑胥遂成詭寄之習，則影射無所不至矣，可不糾之以刑乎？有欲別立抽分於潯浯昞三場者，正以懲納價私鬻之姦耳。殊不知場以辦課，而肇立抽分，非制也。孰若減價召中，則商皆樂趨，而姦竈私鬻者自無以專其利矣。有欲添委掣摯於福寧、福安地方者，不過圖目前軍門之利耳。殊不知商已納價，而又額外加稅，非法也。孰若嚴捕私販，則無事加稅，而巡緝所獲者自足以供其用矣。一正一餘，淮浙之運鹽則然也，而一母二子，則夾帶之漸恐不免矣。是或可變而通之者也。懸衡秤較，淮浙之榷鹽則然也，而圍量抽掣，則欺隱之弊所必至矣。是或可倣而正之者也。東路細鹽之規，雖似競利矣，然邊海之民利玆貿易，實默爲安輯之計也。而或者議之，此之謂不知務者矣。南路官鹽之立，雖若多事矣，然私販之徒樂於趨市
translation_en:
…is a provision for generous relief. Yet crafty salt producers and unscrupulous clerks have made a practice of fraudulent registration under others’ names, extending the abuse of exemptions to every possible case. Can this go uncorrected by penal sanctions? Some wish to establish a separate levy in kind at the three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and Bing [?], precisely to punish the fraud of paying the commuted assessment while selling salt privately. They fail to understand that saltworks were established to meet the salt revenue assessment; instituting a levy in kind is outside the prescribed system. Would it not be better to lower the price and invite merchants to subscribe for salt certificates? Merchants would then gladly come forward, and dishonest producers selling privately would naturally lose their exclusive hold on the profits. Some wish to appoint additional salt-inspection personnel [?] in Funing and Fu’an, merely to secure an immediate gain for the military command. They fail to understand that merchants have already paid the price: imposing a further tax beyond the prescribed amount is unlawful. Would it not be better to apprehend illicit dealers rigorously? There would then be no need for additional taxation, and seizures made during patrols would themselves suffice to meet the command’s expenses.

One regular load and one supplementary load: this is the practice for transporting salt in Huai and Zhe. But with one “mother” load and two “child” loads, the gradual growth of concealed extra cargo is probably unavoidable. This is perhaps a practice that could be modified to make the system work. Suspending a balance and checking the weight: this is the practice under the salt monopoly in Huai and Zhe. But measuring by circumference and inspecting by sampling [?] inevitably gives rise to deception and concealment. Here, perhaps, their example could be followed to rectify the practice.

The regulations for fine salt on the eastern route may seem to compete for profit. Yet the coastal people benefit from this trade, which in fact quietly serves to keep them settled and at peace. Some nevertheless criticize it: these are people who do not understand practical affairs. Establishing the sale of government salt on the southern route may seem to create unnecessary business. Yet illicit dealers gladly come to the market …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
實潛消姦宄之習也而或者病之是必不
便其私者矣此閩中鹽法之大都也執事
明問猶欲使法復
祖宗之舊而不拂乎時宜課歸軍國之資而無
病小民之利甚盛心也然亦豈待於他求
哉亦曰經畫有方曰禁令克壹耳愚也嘗
竊爲之繹其說其目有六一曰還額鹽之
舊夫潯浯洑三場隷於運司課以萬計此
太祖定制也泉州暫借以爲軍餉之資不過後
===
人一時權宜之計耳遂襲以爲常久假者
固不知歸暫假之者亦視以爲舊殊不知
閩惟七場而名存實亡已去其半矣是可
不亟反也哉二曰通食鹽之宜竊稽我
太祖之制計口分鹽則興泉等府食鹽皆有定
數戸部額數可稽也今槩食私鹽習以爲
故正以潯浯洑三場之鹽籍口納米恣意
賤鬻故耳懲之則拂民情縱之則干法紀
或者倣兩浙題
punctuated:
實潛消姦宄之習也，而或者病之，是必不便其私者矣。此閩中鹽法之大都也。執事明問，猶欲使法復祖宗之舊，而不拂乎時宜；課歸軍國之資，而無病小民之利，甚盛心也。然亦豈待於他求哉？亦曰經畫有方，曰禁令克壹耳。愚也嘗竊爲之繹其說，其目有六。
一曰還額鹽之舊。夫潯、浯、洑三場隷於運司，課以萬計，此太祖定制也。泉州暫借以爲軍餉之資，不過後人一時權宜之計耳，遂襲以爲常。久假者固不知歸，暫假之者亦視以爲舊。殊不知閩惟七場，而名存實亡，已去其半矣。是可不亟反也哉？
二曰通食鹽之宜。竊稽我太祖之制，計口分鹽，則興、泉等府食鹽皆有定數，戸部額數可稽也。今槩食私鹽，習以爲故，正以潯、浯、洑三場之鹽，籍口納米，恣意賤鬻故耳。懲之則拂民情，縱之則干法紀。或者倣兩浙題
translation_en:
…in fact quietly erodes the habits of lawlessness. Yet some criticize it; surely these are people whose private interests it inconveniences. Such is the general outline of the salt administration in Fujian. Your discerning question seeks to restore the laws of the imperial ancestors without running counter to present circumstances, and to secure salt revenues for military and state expenses without harming the livelihoods of ordinary people. This is a most admirable intention. But need the means be sought elsewhere? It requires only sound planning and consistent enforcement of prohibitions. I have ventured to consider the matter in detail, under six headings.
First, restore the original arrangements for quota salt. The three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and Fu belong to the Salt Distribution Commission, and their levies are reckoned in tens of thousands. This was the system established by Taizu. Quanzhou’s temporary borrowing of these revenues to fund military provisions was merely an expedient adopted by later officials to meet a passing need. Yet it was perpetuated as a regular arrangement. Those who have borrowed for so long naturally have no thought of returning what they borrowed, while those who temporarily lent it likewise regard the arrangement as established practice. They fail to realize that Fujian has only seven saltworks: with these surviving in name but lost in substance, nearly half are already gone. Can this fail to demand an urgent reversal?
Second, make suitable arrangements for access to salt for consumption. I have examined the system established by our Taizu: salt was apportioned according to population, so the prefectures of Xinghua, Quanzhou, and elsewhere all had fixed quantities for consumption. The quotas can be verified in the records of the Ministry of Revenue. Now everyone consumes illicit salt and has come to regard this as customary. This is precisely because salt from the three saltworks of Xun, Wu, and Fu is obtained by registering consumers and paying rice, then sold cheaply at will. Punishing this would offend popular sentiment; permitting it would violate the law. Some suggest following the practice of the Two Zhe regions and submitting a memorial [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
淮鹽票而行之令民買票買鹽分之定地嚴之
定期則興泉之鹽法旣行而民心亦無不
順矣三曰正行鹽之地夫汀漳二府本閩
鹽額地後以兩廣軍門暫借吉贛行鹽因
而廣鹽盡布江右乃復遷延浸蔓廣鹽直
達於汀漳遂委二府爲廣鹽之地不亦謬
乎是不可以不正也四曰嚴捕鹽之禁竊
觀今捕鹽之法軍則自衞而達之於所有
司則自府而縣而達之於巡司固通於天
===
下者也八閩獨置而不講何歟况興泉爲
山海淵藪之地汀漳爲韶廣咽喉之所而
私鹽無捕無惑乎鹽法之不行於四府也
夫鹽法旣不行於四府則株守者惟延建
邵耳所輸能幾何哉是不可以不深慮也
五曰專督鹽之責夫轉運之設專掌財賦
本無統轄之權也而欲以列郡之鹽法盡
責之雖欲有志於經畫其如弗率何哉故
必專董之以憲臣而仍統之於監使則責
punctuated:
淮鹽票而行之，令民買票買鹽，分之定地，嚴之定期，則興泉之鹽法旣行，而民心亦無不順矣。
三曰：正行鹽之地。夫汀漳二府，本閩鹽額地，後以兩廣軍門暫借吉贛行鹽，因而廣鹽盡布江右，乃復遷延浸蔓，廣鹽直達於汀漳，遂委二府爲廣鹽之地，不亦謬乎？是不可以不正也。
四曰：嚴捕鹽之禁。竊觀今捕鹽之法，軍則自衞而達之於所，有司則自府而縣而達之於巡司，固通於天下者也。八閩獨置而不講，何歟？况興泉爲山海淵藪之地，汀漳爲韶廣咽喉之所，而私鹽無捕，無惑乎鹽法之不行於四府也。夫鹽法旣不行於四府，則株守者惟延建邵耳，所輸能幾何哉？是不可以不深慮也。
五曰：專督鹽之責。夫轉運之設，專掌財賦，本無統轄之權也，而欲以列郡之鹽法盡責之，雖欲有志於經畫，其如弗率何哉？故必專董之以憲臣，而仍統之於監使，則責
translation_en:
…Huai salt permits and put this into practice, requiring the people to buy permits to purchase salt, assigning fixed territories and strictly enforcing fixed time limits. Then the salt regulations in Xinghua and Quanzhou would be implemented, and the people would all willingly comply.
Third: rectify the territories in which salt is marketed. The two prefectures of Tingzhou and Zhangzhou originally belonged to the designated market for Fujian salt. Later, the supreme commander of Liangguang temporarily borrowed Ji’an and Ganzhou as markets for salt, with the result that Guangdong salt spread throughout Jiangxi. This arrangement then persisted and gradually expanded, until Guangdong salt reached Tingzhou and Zhangzhou directly. Thus the two prefectures were surrendered as markets for Guangdong salt. Is this not mistaken? This must be rectified.
Fourth: enforce strictly the prohibitions against illicit salt through apprehension. I observe that, under the present system for apprehending salt smugglers, military enforcement proceeds from the guards down to the battalions, while civil enforcement proceeds from the prefectures through the counties to the police offices. This system applies throughout the empire. Why does Fujian alone set it aside and leave it unattended to? Moreover, Xinghua and Quanzhou have mountain and coastal terrain that affords havens for smugglers, while Tingzhou and Zhangzhou form the strategic passage to Shaozhou and Guangzhou. Yet illicit salt goes unchecked. It is no wonder that the salt regulations fail to operate in these four prefectures. Since they do not operate there, only Yanping, Jianning, and Shaowu remain holding to the system. How much revenue can they remit? This demands deep consideration.
Fifth: assign specific responsibility for supervising salt administration. The Salt Distribution Commission was established expressly to manage revenue; it originally had no authority to exercise general jurisdiction. Yet it is expected to bear full responsibility for salt administration in all the prefectures. Even if its officials are intent on planning and management, what can they do when others will not comply? A censorial official must therefore be given specific responsibility for overseeing it, while it remains under the authority of the supervising commissioner. Then responsibility…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
任攸隆必宏經理之策政令易達自無廢
弛之患矣六曰復中鹽之規夫沿邊召商
報中而內地據引支鹽此建立轉運之初
意也閩鹽不行而邊引不至也久矣有志
於天下者能不深長思也夫旣區畫得宜
鹽法無滯然後以漸行之非沿邊報中者
不得支鹽則報中之規旣復商鹽之行益
廣如是而閩中鹽法何不及於淮浙也哉
夫如是而後爲經畫之有方夫如是而後
===
爲禁令之克壹夫如是而後謂之鹽法草
茆藿食之見如斯而已若秉之以公而無
畏乎疆禦持之以久而不惑於流俗則神
而明之存乎其人
punctuated:
任攸隆，必宏經理之策；政令易達，自無廢弛之患矣。

六曰：復中鹽之規。夫沿邊召商報中，而內地據引支鹽，此建立轉運之初意也。閩鹽不行，而邊引不至也久矣。有志於天下者，能不深長思也？夫旣區畫得宜，鹽法無滯，然後以漸行之：非沿邊報中者，不得支鹽。則報中之規旣復，商鹽之行益廣。如是，而閩中鹽法何不及於淮浙也哉？

夫如是而後爲經畫之有方，夫如是而後爲禁令之克壹，夫如是而後謂之鹽法。草茆藿食之見，如斯而已。若秉之以公，而無畏乎疆禦；持之以久，而不惑於流俗，則神而明之，存乎其人。
translation_en:
…with the responsibility thus given greater weight, plans for administration will assuredly be broadened; government directives will be readily transmitted, and there will naturally be no danger of neglect or laxity.

Sixth: restore the rules for obtaining salt through the frontier provisioning system. Recruiting merchants along the frontier to undertake provisioning contracts, and allowing them to draw salt in the interior upon presentation of salt certificates—this was the original intention behind establishing the Salt Distribution Commission. Salt from Fujian has long failed to circulate, and certificates issued at the frontier have long failed to arrive. Can anyone concerned with the affairs of the realm fail to reflect deeply and at length upon this? Once arrangements have been properly made and the salt administration operates without obstruction, the system should then be introduced gradually: anyone who has not undertaken a provisioning contract along the frontier must not be permitted to draw salt. Once the rules for these contracts are restored, the circulation of salt through merchants will expand further. With this accomplished, why should Fujian’s salt administration not equal that of the Huai and Zhe regions?

Only then can administrative planning be called sound; only then can prohibitions be made uniform; only then can this be called a proper salt system. Such, and no more, are the views of one who lives in a thatched dwelling and subsists on bean leaves. As for administering it impartially, without fearing the powerful and overbearing, and maintaining it steadfastly, without being misled by prevailing opinion—the ability to bring it to its fullest, most discerning realization rests with the person entrusted with it.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
嘉靖已酉秋八月學正寇韋
敎諭趙文翰各膺聘濫竽福
建試事既取士錄成文翰當
序諸末簡乃執筆而歎曰猗
歟盛哉道化人文之美由陶
唐以來而復有
===
今日之爲盛也文翰蓋以閩粵之
士觀之昔聖人南面而聽天
下嚮明以爲治光被昭格當
其所面之方照燭休爽尤爲
焜顯而欲考其德之明者亦
於其方之最遠而著者以爲
徴故書頌放勳之大至於海
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

嘉靖已酉秋八月，學正寇韋、敎諭趙文翰各膺聘，濫竽福建試事。既取士，錄成，文翰當序諸末簡，乃執筆而歎曰：「猗歟盛哉！道化人文之美，由陶唐以來，而復有今日之爲盛也！」文翰蓋以閩粵之士觀之。昔聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明以爲治，光被昭格。當其所面之方，照燭休爽，尤爲焜顯；而欲考其德之明者，亦於其方之最遠而著者以爲徴。故《書》頌放勳之大，至於海
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549; the transcription has 已酉 for 己酉], School Instructor Kou Wei and Instructor Zhao Wenhan each accepted an invitation to serve, unworthily, in conducting the Fujian examination. Once the candidates had been selected and the record completed, it fell to Wenhan to compose a postface for its final leaves. Taking up his brush, he exclaimed: “Ah, how splendid! Since the time of Taotang [Yao], the beauty of moral transformation and cultural accomplishment has once again attained such flourishing as we see today!” Wenhan bases this judgment on his observation of the scholars of Min and Yue.

In antiquity, the sage faced south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern. His radiance spread abroad and reached everywhere with manifest brilliance. In the direction he faced, its illumination was auspicious and bright [?], shining with particular splendor. Those wishing to examine the brilliance of his virtue likewise sought evidence in its manifestations in the most distant reaches of that direction. Thus the Book of Documents, extolling the greatness of Fangxun [Yao], speaks of its reaching as far as the sea …

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
隅日出罔不率俾而所謂如
天之蕩蕩者於是乎彷佛而
可名由堯以降莫如文王之
純然其顯於四方者獨著於
南故汝墳江沱之風爲周之
盛然則歷古帝王之德其盛
也必究於南而其極盛也必
===
際於最遠詩書所稱可睹已
閩粤在南之方最遠大海之
隅日所從出處也意其荒陋
幽側無以望中國之昭回今
其文之可見者宣曜炳朗發
揮乎詩書禮樂之精宣鬯乎
仁義道德之輝而蔚然治世
punctuated: 隅日出，罔不率俾，而所謂如天之蕩蕩者，於是乎彷佛而可名。由堯以降，莫如文王之純，然其顯於四方者，獨著於南，故汝墳江沱之風爲周之盛。然則歷古帝王之德，其盛也必究於南，而其極盛也必際於最遠，《詩》《書》所稱可睹已。閩粤在南之方最遠，大海之隅，日所從出處也。意其荒陋幽側，無以望中國之昭回。今其文之可見者，宣曜炳朗，發揮乎詩書禮樂之精，宣鬯乎仁義道德之輝，而蔚然治世
translation_en: …the coastal reaches where the sun rises, none fail to follow and obey. Thus what is described as being “as boundless as Heaven” can be dimly apprehended and put into words. From Yao onward, none equaled King Wen in purity of virtue. Yet although his virtue shone throughout the four quarters, it was especially manifest in the south. Thus the airs of the banks of the Ru River and of the Jiang and Tuo rivers expressed the flourishing of the Zhou. Accordingly, the virtue of the emperors and kings of antiquity, when flourishing, invariably extended to the south; at its fullest flourishing, it invariably reached the most distant places. This can be seen in the accounts of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Min-Yue lies in the farthest reaches of the south, at the edge of the great sea, where the sun rises. One might suppose that its wildness, rusticity, obscurity, and remoteness left it unable to aspire to the radiance of the central lands. Yet the writings now visible there shine forth brilliantly, expounding the essence of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music, and freely spreading the radiance of benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue—a splendid flowering in an age of good government…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
之能言由其言以論其志皆
有用於世者也堯之光于海
隅也黎獻共惟帝臣文王之
風被于南國田間椓杙之夫
且與公侯匹體人才之生可
爲世用而莫不志於用世是
其所以爲盛之實也故文翰
===
直以此方之士之文而知
今日之盛爲由陶唐氏以來而一
再有也豈不信哉我
皇上一德執中建維皇之極陶成
羣品覆育萬彙蓋秉周文之
純而嗣唐堯之統其德之及
于四表如日月之照臨而其
punctuated:
之能言，由其言以論其志，皆有用於世者也。堯之光于海隅也，黎獻共惟帝臣；文王之風被于南國，田間椓杙之夫且與公侯匹體。人才之生，可爲世用，而莫不志於用世，是其所以爲盛之實也。故文翰直以此方之士之文，而知今日之盛，爲由陶唐氏以來而一再有也，豈不信哉！
我皇上一德執中，建維皇之極，陶成羣品，覆育萬彙，蓋秉周文之純，而嗣唐堯之統。其德之及于四表，如日月之照臨，而其
translation_en:
…eloquent spokesmen for an age of good government. Judging their aspirations by their words, they are all men who can be of service to the world. When Yao’s radiance reached the corners of the seas, the worthy among the common people all became the emperor’s servants. When King Wen’s influence spread over the southern lands, even men driving stakes in the fields stood as peers of dukes and marquises. That talented men arise who can serve their age, and that all aspire to such service: this is the substance of its flourishing. Thus I, Wenhan, can tell simply from the writings of this region’s scholars that the flourishing of our present age is something witnessed only once or twice since the time of Taotang, the sage ruler Yao. Is this not indeed true?
Our August Emperor holds to the Mean with undivided virtue and establishes the sovereign’s supreme standard. He molds and perfects all beings, shelters and nurtures the myriad creatures. He possesses the purity of King Wen of Zhou and continues the succession of Tang Yao. His virtue reaches the four outermost bounds like the illumination of the sun and moon, and his…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
所面之方獨切於光華閩粤
之士宜其莫不爲材也昔周
之季淮徐吳越之間猶爲春
秋所外雖當孔孟之時而以
文學名者於吳惟一言偃學
於中國者於楚惟一陳良况
於峻嶺限隔之表大海之隅
===
日所從出處耶彼閩粤於其
時宜荒陋幽側而無所聞於
策也今玆之美若此然則此
方之士豈能自爲材耶凡士
之生雖不繫於地而亦以邇
爲貴豪傑之興固無所待於
上尤願於得所事而快利見
punctuated: 所面之方，獨切於光華，閩粤之士宜其莫不爲材也。昔周之季，淮徐吳越之間，猶爲《春秋》所外。雖當孔孟之時，而以文學名者，於吳惟一言偃；學於中國者，於楚惟一陳良。况於峻嶺限隔之表、大海之隅、日所從出處耶？彼閩粤於其時，宜荒陋幽側，而無所聞於策也。今玆之美若此，然則此方之士豈能自爲材耶？凡士之生，雖不繫於地，而亦以邇爲貴。豪傑之興，固無所待於上，尤願於得所事而快利見
translation_en: …the region toward which he faces receives his radiance with particular immediacy. It is fitting that the scholars of Min and Yue should all become men of talent. In the closing years of the Zhou, the lands of Huai, Xu, Wu, and Yue were still treated as outside the bounds by the Spring and Autumn Annals. Even in the time of Confucius and Mencius, Wu had only one Yan Yan renowned for literary learning, and Chu only one Chen Liang who studied in the Central States. How much more was this true of places beyond the barrier of lofty mountain ranges, at the edge of the great sea, where the sun rises? Min and Yue in those days would naturally have been uncultivated, remote, and obscure, with nothing of them recorded in the annals. Yet their excellence today is such as this! Could the scholars of this region, then, have become men of talent by themselves? Although the emergence of scholars is not determined by locality, proximity is nevertheless prized. The rise of outstanding men assuredly does not depend upon those above them; yet they especially wish to find a ruler to serve and to enjoy the favorable encounter…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
以彼偃良之賢得及江漢汝
墳之風其爲公侯好仇心腹
豈直兎罝野人之比乎以其
不遇徒爲季世下土之賢而
已諸士雖生於最遠猶當
聖人所面之方復能以材自顯使
欲求
===
昭代德化之盛者於此乎徵蓋
已幸矣其尤幸者以
今上之爲君而士之顯於其世者
預其見知之傳刑乎譽髦之
化則藹藹濟濟皆媚于之吉
人以寧之多士也豈如言偃
陳良獨爲季世下土之賢而
punctuated: 以彼偃、良之賢，得及江漢、汝墳之風，其爲公侯好仇、心腹，豈直兎罝野人之比乎？以其不遇，徒爲季世下土之賢而已。諸士雖生於最遠，猶當聖人所面之方，復能以材自顯，使欲求昭代德化之盛者於此乎徵，蓋已幸矣。其尤幸者，以今上之爲君，而士之顯於其世者，預其見知之傳，刑乎譽髦之化，則藹藹濟濟，皆媚于之吉人、以寧之多士也。豈如言偃、陳良獨爲季世下土之賢而
translation_en:
Had men as worthy as Yan Yan and Chen Liang come within the influence celebrated in the songs of the Jiang and Han rivers and the banks of the Ru, would they, as fine companions and trusted confidants of dukes and lords, have been merely comparable to the rustic rabbit-net setters of the Odes? Because they did not meet with such an opportunity, they remained merely worthy men of a declining age in distant lands. Although you scholars were born in the remotest region, you nevertheless inhabit the quarter toward which the sage faces. Moreover, you have distinguished yourselves through your abilities, allowing those who seek evidence of the flourishing moral influence of our illustrious dynasty to find it here. This is already good fortune indeed.

Your still greater good fortune is to have His present Majesty as your ruler. Scholars who distinguish themselves in his age participate in the transmission of wisdom known through direct encounter and take their pattern from the transforming influence that honors outstanding scholars. Thus, in your abundant and dignified ranks, you are all those worthy men cherished by the ruler, those many scholars through whom peace is secured. How could you resemble Yan Yan and Chen Liang, who were merely worthy men of a declining age in distant lands…

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
text:
已哉諸士其能以無願乎否
則直凡民之不如耳有帝堯
以爲
君而士者不知自異於凡民其能
以無媿乎故文翰序是錄也
而爲諸士告焉
山東濟南府武定州陽信縣
===
儒學教諭趙文翰謹序
punctuated:
已哉！諸士其能以無願乎？否則，直凡民之不如耳。有帝堯以爲君，而士者不知自異於凡民，其能以無媿乎？故文翰序是錄也，而爲諸士告焉。
山東濟南府武定州陽信縣儒學教諭趙文翰謹序。
translation_en:
…and nothing more! Can you scholars have no aspirations? Otherwise, you would simply be inferior to the common people. With an Emperor Yao as your ruler, if you scholars do not know to distinguish yourselves from the common people, can you be without shame? Thus I, Wenhan, in writing the preface to this record, offer these words to you scholars.
Preface respectfully written by Zhao Wenhan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年福建鄉試錄
